Her contributions have supported a wide range of causes, including education, community development and initiatives aimed at improving opportunities for underserved populations.

headline: Trump set to unveil new tariffs after probe on excess factory capacity
content: The Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected. The results of the investigation are expected as soon as Tuesday afternoon, these people said. The US Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump's second term. The duties would partly replace tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The administration's tariffs have in part contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November's midterm elections showed 62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs. Tailored Tariff Rates It is unclear what tariff rates would be proposed. One of the people said that the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies. USTR has been investigating most of the US's largest trading partners under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 over what it called evidence of excess industrial capacity. The White House is expected to honour capped tariff rates that were included in finalised US trade deals with partner countries, this person said. These include duty caps of 15% on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19% for Malaysia. The US also is expected to honour the 20% cap on Trump's second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a trade truce due to expire on 10 January 2027 is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would rise to a higher level. The US Trade Representative's office and the White House did not respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement. Ryan Majerus, a former senior US Commerce Department trade official, said he expects a lengthy report that could include differentiated tariff remedies for each of the 16 trading partners. Majerus, a partner with King & Spalding, said the administration could propose high tariff rates of 15% to 25% on imports from countries deemed to have excess capacity in various sectors. Those levies would stack on top of existing tariffs of 10% or 12.5% imposed under a separate investigation into lax enforcement of anti-forced labour laws. However, he said the administration could also propose lower tariff rates with escalation clauses that would ratchet rates higher over time unless countries take steps to reduce excess production capacity. Replacement Tariffs The countries included in the probe are China, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia, along with the European Union. The Wall Street Journal reported earlier that the probe's results could be unveiled as soon as this week. USTR launched the excess capacity probe in March, along with a separate probe into weak or lax enforcement of anti-forced labor laws in 59 countries and the European Union. Together, the duties are meant to rebuild Trump's global "Liberation Day" tariffs that were struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The Trump administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity, which it says is flooding global markets with steel, aluminum, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. China has rejected the accusations, saying its exports reflect competitive advantages. The probe is also partly directed at Chinese investment into countries in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia, to manufacture goods for the US market and avoid prior US tariffs. Under a US-China trade truce due to expire on 10 January 2027, the Trump administration has capped second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, in addition to duties of about 25% imposed during Trump's first term. The US has already imposed a 12.5% anti-forced labor duty on all Chinese imports, leaving only 7.5% to reach the 20% cap. The US and China also are working to cut tariffs on $30 billion of non-strategic imports from each side.

headline: From Gokul To Latur: Congress Finds New Political Momentum In Maharashtra’s Cooperative Belt
content: For a political party that has struggled to retain its relevance in Maharashtra over the past few years, the cooperative sector is beginning to offer some encouraging signs. From Kolhapur to Sangli and Latur, recent developments in powerful cooperative institutions suggest that Congress is attempting to rebuild its political influence through local leadership, grassroots networks and alliances. These victories may not yet translate into an electoral revival, but they have certainly brought some of the party’s regional leaders back into the political spotlight. The first significant indication came from Kolhapur, where Congress MLC Satej Patil-led Samavichari Aghadi emerged as the largest group in the election to the board of directors of Gokul Dairy. The panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats, defeating the Mahayuti-backed panel, which secured 12. Taking on the combined political strength of the BJP, Shiv Sena and NCP was a significant achievement and underlined Satej Patil’s ability to mobilise local networks and bring different political interests together. However, the victory did not translate into control of the chairmanship. The Maharashtra government’s decision to give voting rights to four government-nominated directors changed the arithmetic, and the Mahayuti-backed candidate eventually secured the top post. While this was a setback for Satej Patil, the performance of his panel demonstrated that the ruling alliance could be challenged even in an institution where it enjoys considerable political influence. Gokul remains one of the most important cooperative institutions in western Maharashtra, and its electoral contest was as much about rural political influence as it was about the dairy business. The developments in Sangli have added another dimension to this emerging political narrative. After nearly 27 years, Congress has returned to the chairmanship of the Sangli District Central Cooperative Bank, with Mahendra Lad being elected unopposed. Shiv Sena’s Tanaji Patil secured the vice-chairmanship. The outcome is significant because of the political negotiations and understanding that made it possible. Congress MLA Dr Vishwajit Kadam played an important role in bringing together different political interests and ensuring that the Congress secured the chairmanship. The arrangement involved cooperation from leaders outside the party, including the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. In a district where cooperative politics has traditionally been influenced by powerful political families and established leaders, the outcome demonstrates Kadam’s ability to negotiate and influence local power equations. For Congress, securing the chairmanship after such a long gap is an important political gain, even though the bank’s new leadership reflects a broader, multi-party arrangement. Another encouraging development for Congress has come from Latur in Marathwada. The Sahakar panel led by former Congress MLA Dhiraj Deshmukh won 14 of the 19 seats in the Latur District Central Cooperative Bank election, defeating the BJP-backed Parivartan panel, which managed five seats. The victory is particularly significant for Dhiraj, son of former Maharashtra chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, as it comes two years after his defeat in the 2024 assembly elections. The result indicates that the Deshmukh family’s political and cooperative networks continue to have considerable influence in Latur. It also shows that Congress-backed local leadership can still put up a formidable challenge to the BJP beyond its traditional western Maharashtra base. These three developments need to be seen in the larger context of Maharashtra’s political geography. Western Maharashtra, particularly the districts of Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara, Pune and parts of Solapur, has historically played a decisive role in shaping the state’s politics. It is a region where Maratha political leadership, agricultural economics and the cooperative movement have remained closely connected. Sugar factories, district cooperative banks, milk federations and agricultural societies have never been merely economic institutions. They have also served as centres of political influence, leadership development and grassroots mobilisation. The cooperative movement played a crucial role in the rise of Congress in Maharashtra after Independence. Leaders such as Yashwantrao Chavan and Vasantdada Patil built their political influence through farmer networks and rural institutions. Over the decades, control over sugar factories, cooperative banks and milk unions became closely linked to electoral strength. The rise of the NCP under Sharad Pawar further transformed this political landscape, with cooperative institutions becoming important centres of influence for regional political leadership. Congress’s declining influence in western Maharashtra over the years was therefore not just an electoral setback. It also meant losing ground in the institutional structures that had once sustained its political strength. As the NCP expanded its influence and the BJP made inroads into the region, Congress gradually found itself pushed out of several traditional centres of power. The current political developments suggest that the party is attempting to reclaim some of that lost space. Satej Patil has demonstrated his ability to mobilise an opposition alliance in Kolhapur. Vishwajit Kadam has used political negotiation and consensus-building to secure a crucial position in Sangli. Dhiraj Deshmukh’s victory in Latur has reinforced the importance of local political networks and established leadership in cooperative elections. There is also a larger political calculation at play. The fragmentation of the NCP and changing equations among regional leaders have created opportunities for Congress to reassert itself. The party may not be in a position to challenge the ruling Mahayuti alliance across Maharashtra immediately, but regaining influence in cooperative institutions could help it rebuild its organisational base, particularly in rural constituencies. However, it would be premature to describe these developments as a full-fledged Congress comeback. Cooperative elections operate on a different political arithmetic from assembly and Lok Sabha elections. Local relationships, caste equations, family networks and institutional interests often determine their outcomes. Congress will have to demonstrate that the influence gained in these institutions can be converted into votes. It will also need to maintain unity among regional leaders and develop a stronger organisational structure beyond individual political strongholds. For now, the message from Kolhapur, Sangli and Latur is that Congress is far from irrelevant in Maharashtra’s rural political landscape. The party has leaders who can still mobilise people, negotiate alliances and challenge the ruling establishment in institutions that matter. Western Maharashtra, with its Maratha-dominated politics and deep-rooted cooperative network, could become central to this effort. In Maharashtra, political power has often travelled from sugar factories, milk unions and district banks to the corridors of Mantralaya. Congress appears to have recognised that rebuilding its electoral strength will require more than political speeches and alliances at the state level. It will have to regain its presence where rural influence is actually created and sustained. The recent cooperative victories offer an opening. Whether the party can turn that opening into a lasting political revival will depend on what its leaders do next.

headline: 'Stop Hebbal Tunnel': Bengaluru Environmentalist Takes Fight To Rahul Gandhi, Targets Shivakumar Govt
content: For a city struggling with congestion, shrinking green spaces and rising temperatures, the debate over the Hebbal tunnel is no longer just about traffic movement. It is also about the kind of Bengaluru the government intends to build. With regard to the proposed Hebbal short tunnel project, eminent environmentalist and former Indian Forest Service officer AN Yellappa Reddy has now taken the battle to the Congress high command, writing directly to Leader of Opposition and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and urging him to intervene and stop the Karnataka government’s proposed tunnel road and flyover projects. The growing public opposition to the projects, environmental concerns have been repeatedly raised through civic campaigns and social media, but that the government has remained unmoved. His appeal questions the Congress government’s infrastructure priorities, with the question being whether the city’s traffic problems can be addressed through more road infrastructure or whether the government needs to fundamentally rethink its approach to urban mobility without affecting the environment. Reddy, who once served as Secretary of the Department of Forests, Ecology and Environment in the Karnataka government, has questioned why the DK Shivakumar-led Congress government is pushing ahead with projects that, he believes, will neither solve Bengaluru’s traffic congestion nor justify the environmental cost. Yellappa addressed his letter to Gandhi saying he writes on behalf of more than two crore citizens in and around Bengaluru, where he urged Gandhi to step in, review the projects and direct the state government to explore alternatives centred on public transport. What makes the appeal significant is that Reddy is not merely questioning the environmental consequences of the project. He is challenging the very premise on which the government is pursuing it, arguing that Bengaluru has several other options to ease congestion which have not been adequately explored. In his letter, he describes the tunnel project as highly disruptive, futile and unsuitable for the city’s topography and geology, while accusing the government of overlooking what he calls the ‘low-hanging fruits’ of traffic management. “The Government has failed to speedily and effectively leverage all other available options – the low-hanging fruits – before going into this highly disruptive and futile project, which is most unsuitable for Bengaluru’s topography and geology,” the letter states. Reddy has also enclosed a Rapid Environmental Impact Assessment of the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project, prepared by ecologist Harini Nagendra and other researchers from Azim Premji University, Bengaluru. The assessment raises concerns over the environmental consequences of the proposed construction along the 2.3-km stretch, particularly the loss of more than a thousand trees. While the letter refers to 1,138 trees being endangered, the assessment identifies 1,128 trees proposed to be felled, of which 950 are estimated to store 77.54 metric tonnes of carbon. This is not the first time Yellappa Reddy has taken on the Karnataka government over the proposed tunnel road. He was among the leading voices in the campaign to protect Lalbagh gardens, where the proposed underground tunnel alignment and its entry and exit infrastructure had triggered fears of damage to the iconic botanical garden and its green cover and a pre-historic monolithic structure. In August this year, Reddy led thousands of citizens, environmentalists, regular walkers and civic groups in a protest march through Lalbagh, culminating in a human chain around the iconic Lalbagh Rock. Along with him in the protest, senior BJP MPs, including Tejasvi Surya, Shobha Karandlaje, CN Manjunath and PC Mohan, joined, amid growing outrage over the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, 2026. It sought to allow up to five per cent of parkland to be diverted for public infrastructure and utility projects. Environmentalists and citizens feared that the amendment could open the doors for infrastructure works inside Bengaluru’s limited green spaces. The same was the case with the Hebbal tunnel. The sustained public opposition eventually forced the government to reconsider its position. On September 4, the Cabinet withdrew the controversial Parks Amendment Bill. Days later, the government announced another significant change, stating that Lalbagh land would not be used for the tunnel road and that the alignment would be realigned. For Reddy, the issue of the Hebbal tunnel goes well beyond the number of trees that may be lost. In the letter, he describes the destruction of such many trees over a relatively short stretch as a serious environmental concern and calls for immediate corrective steps. He points out that Bengaluru’s remaining tree cover plays a critical role in controlling urban heat, absorbing carbon, reducing dust and air pollution and sustaining biodiversity. The trees also provide food and shelter for wildlife and help maintain ecological corridors connecting green spaces and water bodies. At a time when the city’s temperatures are rising and its green cover and water bodies are steadily shrinking, he argues that removing mature trees along the stretch would have consequences that cannot simply be offset through transplantation. Reddy’s letter is particularly dismissive of tree transplantation as a compensatory measure, arguing that its survival rate is extremely poor and that it cannot replace the ecological value of mature trees. But Reddy’s objection is not restricted to the environmental impact. He has also questioned the traffic logic behind the project, pointing out that the government is simultaneously proposing a flyover between the tunnel and Mekhri Circle. According to him, this effectively amounts to shifting congestion from one point to another, rather than addressing the underlying problem. He argues that the tunnel and flyover, when considered together, could actually increase congestion, a concern he says has also been raised by experts. “As an environmentalist, it pains me to see how the government I once served is hell bent on bulldozing invaluable trees and destroying scarce water bodies to promote projects which have no public demand or support,” he writes. Instead, Reddy wants the government to focus on strengthening the three major public transport options available to Bengaluru — buses, Metro and suburban rail. He has called for a concerted effort to ensure that at least 70 per cent of daily trips are made using these modes, thereby reducing the city’s dependence on private vehicles and freeing up existing road space. His argument is that people continue to buy and use private vehicles largely because an effective and extensive public transport network is yet to become a viable alternative for many commuters. He has also flagged the absence of adequate consultation with the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA), arguing that such major infrastructure decisions should not be taken without involving the statutory body mandated to coordinate urban transport planning. Reddy has called for greater emphasis on walkability, public transport and inclusive mobility instead of repeatedly turning to road expansion and flyovers. The appeal to Rahul Gandhi comes after, according to Reddy, repeated attempts to persuade the state government to reconsider the projects failed to yield results. He has invoked the Congress leader’s stated positions on environmental protection and public welfare, urging him to ensure that the Karnataka government reviews and cancels the proposed tunnel roads and flyovers and redirects its attention towards improving public transport. “Since all attempts to get the government to tread the needful path have failed, I am constrained to write to you with the ardent hope that you will stand by your stated views regarding the environment and will direct the government to review and cancel these projects and instead focus on quick and drastic improvements to public transport,” he writes in his letter and tells News18 that he hopes for a trouble from the senior Congress leader.

headline: Vijayasai Reddy demands abolition of toll collection on highways
content: VIJAYAWADA Parivartan Rajaniti Party (PRP) founder-president V. Vijayasai Reddy has demanded the abolition of toll collection, saying that vehicle owners already pay multiple taxes and charges, including GST, road tax, registration fees and various cesses. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/vijayasai-reddy-launches-parivartana-rajaneethi-party-vows-to-end-two-family-politics-in-andhra/article71688719.ece #Toll collection must be abolished. headline: ‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: SC agrees to hear contempt plea over Deepam row
content: NEW DELHI: The Madurai district collector has filed a status report before the Supreme Court informing it that the ceremonial lamp could not be lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram hills despite the court's November 20 order.The development came after a petitioner alleged that the state authorities had violated the Supreme Court's directions and sought contempt proceedings against them for failing to light the Karthigai Deepam at the designated location.The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications, assuring them that it would hear the matter.The Collector's report comes amid escalating tensions over the lighting of the traditional lamp at Thiruparankundram, where the Maha Deepam was lit at the Ucchi Pillayar temple instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar on Tuesday evening.The controversy has triggered protests by Hindu organisations and criticism from BJP leaders, who have accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of disregarding the Supreme Court's interim directions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Congress to hold nationwide ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches on Thursday; Kharge to lead from Lucknow
content: NEW DELHI: Congress will organise ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ Marches across all states on Thursday to mark Constitution Day, with party President Mallikarjun Kharge to participate from Lucknow.The party is stepping up its campaign ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.According to a statement quoted by ANI news agency, All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary KC Venugopal said every Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) would organise a march in its respective state.The marches will begin at statues of BR Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi. Congress workers and participants will pay tribute, read the Preamble aloud and take an oath to protect the Constitution, recalling its principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.Alongside the marches, party workers will visit every polling booth under the Vote Rakshak campaign to verify the names of voters deleted from electoral rolls and help them reclaim their right to vote.Venugopal appealed to students, youth, farmers, workers, women, Dalit, Adivasi, OBC and minority communities, as well as civil society members and other citizens who value the Constitution, to participate in the marches."The Constitution gave every Indian the vote. The Indian National Congress is duty-bound and committed to defend it," he said, as per ANI.The Congress also raised concerns over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Venugopal referred to Rahul Gandhi's allegations of "Vote Chori", citing fake and duplicate entries in Mahadevapura, attempts to delete thousands of genuine voters in Aland, and alleged irregularities in Haryana and other states.He alleged that the Election Commission of India had dismissed the findings instead of ordering an impartial inquiry, sought affidavits from the leader of opposition and failed to share information requested by investigating agencies.Venugopal also criticised the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which began months before the Bihar Assembly elections and has since been expanded to several states and Union Territories. He said the exercise, despite its stated aim of ensuring clean electoral rolls, had made citizens prove their eligibility.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Saffron stage, caste clout: Inside Kunda’s Rajput power play
content: Ghaziabad As the winds of the Assembly elections begin to stir across Uttar Pradesh, the saffron canopies of religious kathas are increasingly doubling as stages for political mobilisation and messaging. This alchemy was on display in Kunda, Pratapgarh, recently, where popular preacher Dhirendra Shastri’s Ram Katha became a theatre of Kshatriya-Thakur assertion, draped in the semantics of Hindutva. In the run-up to the Katha and at the event, the host, Rajput strongman and MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh (Raja Bhaiya), championed inclusive Hindutva slogans such as “Hum Sab Hindu Bhai-Bhai,” urging Islam-like unity beyond caste lines, and demanding Indian citizenship for Pakistani Hindu refugees. While the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik) president called the timing coincidental, political observers note that the gathering largely served as a cross-party consolidation of influential Thakur leaders. Prominent Rajput strongmen and leaders, including Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, Dhananjay Singh, Brijesh Singh, Dinesh Pratap Singh, Mayankeshwar Sharan Singh and rebel SP MLAs Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh shared the stage, projecting unified caste strength ahead of elections.

headline: Not Just 2 Seats: Can Saharanpur Make Or Break Congress-SP Alliance Ahead Of UP Elections?
content: The Samajwadi Party’s decision to announce candidates for Saharanpur and Behat even as seat-sharing negotiations with Congress continue has exposed a growing trust deficit between the INDIA bloc partners. The question of who commands political influence in western Uttar Pradesh and who is the big brother in the alliance in the state is back in the spotlight. What began as a disagreement over seat-sharing has now turned into a public show of resentment, with Congress MP Imran Masood questioning the manner in which SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is conducting negotiations. The immediate trigger was the Samajwadi Party’s announcement of its first list of five candidates on November 24, even as discussions with Congress were underway. Among those named were sitting MLA Ashu Malik from Saharanpur and Umar Ali Khan from Behat. Both constituencies are in Saharanpur district and are also among the seats Congress wants to contest. For Masood, who represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha, the move was more than an electoral announcement. It was a question of how much respect Congress was being accorded by its alliance partner. “Are we beggars? Will you treat us like this – that we aren’t even asking you for seats and you declared 26 seats? We didn’t even demand seats from you,” Masood told IANS, expressing his displeasure over what he sees as a unilateral approach by the SP. “When you have made this declaration against me, I don’t understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress, or the BJP? It has to be decided, doesn’t it, whether you want to fight the BJP or fight us? So, what can I say about this,” Masood questioned. The remarks have brought an underlying tension within the INDIA bloc into the open: Can two parties that need each other to take on the BJP agree on who gets to represent the same voters? Why Both Congress And SP Want Saharanpur Located in the state’s northwestern corner, bordering Haryana and Uttarakhand, Saharanpur occupies an important position in the politically sensitive western UP belt. Its electoral character is shaped by a diverse social composition, including a substantial Muslim population, Dalit communities, Jat voters, Gujjars and other backward communities. This makes it a constituency where electoral outcomes often depend on how effectively parties build social coalitions rather than rely on a single vote bank. The region has long witnessed competition between the Congress, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), the BJP and the Samajwadi Party, with the relative strength of these parties changing across elections. The BSP has historically enjoyed a significant organisational presence in the region, particularly among Dalit voters, while the SP has built its support base through its minority and backward-caste outreach. The BJP, meanwhile, has sought to consolidate Hindu voters across caste lines. Congress, which once enjoyed a wider political footprint in Uttar Pradesh, has been attempting to rebuild its organisation and reclaim constituencies where it believes it still has local influence. Saharanpur has therefore become an important test of whether Congress can independently negotiate from a position of strength or will have to accept the SP’s assessment of electoral winnability. Imran Masood’s Rise And Congress’s Claim Over Saharanpur The Congress’s claim over Saharanpur is closely linked to Imran Masood’s political journey and his electoral performance. A familiar face in western UP politics, Masood has moved across political formations, including the Congress, BSP and SP, before returning to the Congress fold. His victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections gave the Congress a much-needed foothold in a state where its electoral presence had weakened considerably. The result was significant for another reason. Saharanpur had voted for the BSP in 2019, the BJP in 2014 and the BSP again in 2009. The Congress victory in 2024 therefore represented a return to the seat after a gap, rather than an uninterrupted party stronghold. For Masood, this victory has strengthened the argument that Congress has a political base in the district that it cannot simply surrender during alliance negotiations. His position has also gained importance following the Congress’s organisational reshuffle in October, when he was appointed working president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee. The appointment was seen as part of the party’s effort to strengthen its presence in western UP and improve its bargaining position ahead of the Assembly elections. Masood and those close to him have previously made it clear that Congress does not intend to give up its claim over the region. Speaking about the party’s electoral ambitions in Saharanpur, his nephew Hamza Masood had said: “Hamara majboot jila hai, apna majboot jila thode hi chhod denge” (This is our strong district; why would we leave our own stronghold?). Why The Samajwadi Party Is Unwilling To Give Ground The SP, however, has its own reasons for refusing to concede Saharanpur easily. Unlike Congress’s Lok Sabha-level success, the Samajwadi Party can point to its established Assembly-level presence in the district. In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh elections, SP’s Umar Ali Khan won Behat, while Ashu Malik secured the Saharanpur Assembly seat. The party also emerged as a strong challenger in Saharanpur Nagar, where it narrowly lost to the BJP. The SP’s decision to renominate Ashu Malik and Umar Ali Khan is therefore rooted in its assessment of the two constituencies and the performance of its sitting legislators. There is also a larger political consideration. Akhilesh Yadav has repeatedly emphasised the party’s PDA strategy, which seeks to bring together Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities). The announcement of four Muslim candidates in the SP’s first list of five is consistent with this political outreach. Giving up constituencies with sitting MLAs, particularly in a region where the party believes it has a strong electoral base, could complicate that strategy. Akhilesh has publicly maintained that seat-sharing should be decided on the basis of electoral winnability rather than the number of constituencies each party demands. “Baat humare liye seat ki nahi hogi, jeetne wali seat ki hogi. Jo jite woh seat le le,” he had said earlier, arguing that the alliance should prioritise candidates capable of winning. In a public message to Congress on November 24, he also called for serious discussions based on political realities and the prospects of victory. “Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect,” he said, asking Congress to submit a wider list of potential constituencies beyond the 26 seats already discussed. The problem is that both parties appear to have different definitions of winnability. For Congress, its 2024 Lok Sabha victory and its historical presence in Saharanpur justify a claim over the region. For the SP, its sitting MLAs and Assembly-level performance make the constituencies difficult to relinquish. The Bigger Seat-Sharing Battle Beyond Saharanpur The disagreement over Saharanpur is unfolding against the backdrop of a much wider tussle over the number of seats each party will contest in the 2027 Assembly elections. Congress has reportedly brought down its demand from an initial 181 constituencies to around 130, while the SP has offered it 26 seats so far. The latest round of negotiations has seen Congress submit a fresh list of constituencies, but the gap between the two sides remains substantial. The SP’s announcement of candidates while discussions were still underway has added to the mistrust. For Congress, the concern is that the party could be left with little room to negotiate if the SP continues announcing candidates for constituencies on its wishlist. And Saharanpur is not the only point of friction. The Congress is looking to expand its footprint in western Uttar Pradesh, where several constituencies have a combination of Muslim and Dalit voters that both parties want to reach. The stakes are particularly high because the two parties have reasons to preserve their partnership. Their alliance performed strongly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, with the SP winning 37 seats and Congress securing six in Uttar Pradesh. Together, they dealt a significant electoral setback to the BJP in a state that sends 80 MPs to the Lok Sabha. But translating that parliamentary success into an Assembly alliance is proving more complicated. While the SP remains the larger Opposition force in the state, Congress wants to use its improved electoral performance to rebuild its independent political identity. For now, neither party has indicated that it wants to walk away from the alliance. But the Saharanpur dispute has exposed the difficulty of sustaining political unity when both partners are competing for the same constituencies and sections of voters.

headline: Delegation of political parties, civil society groups meets Delhi CEO over SIR deletions
content: A delegation of political parties and civil society groups that met Delhi’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) said he accepted their suggestions, including restoring voters deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) with original voter serial and Electors Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.The delegation included members of the Aam Aadmi Party, Communist Party of India, Communist Party of India (Marxist), Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist), and activists Anjali Bharadwaj, Amrita Johri, and members of the Voter Adikar Manch. It met the CEO on Monday to press for protecting every eligible voter’s right to vote.The delegation said the CEO issued directives and that a Standard Operating Procedure would be released shortly. “The responsibility for restoring every eligible citizen’s right to vote lies with the Election Commission, a duty it cannot absolve itself of,” the delegation said in a statement on Monday.An official said the meeting went well and the CEO’s office will work to streamline the suggestion. “Several suggestions were already in the pipeline. We will consider all demands which help make the process easier for ordinary voters,” the official said.The talks focused on implementing the November 6 order regarding another chance for voters under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, and Duplicate (ASDD) categories to get back on the roll, issued in light of the Supreme Court’s October 28 directions on the SIR, and on voters’ difficulties.For voters whose names were deleted and later placed in the ASDD list released on August 31, the CEO accepted a proposal that their voting rights can be restored by filling an enumeration form. They will retain their original voter serial number and EPIC number.The delegation said that voters who were deleted and have since applied for re-enrolment through Form 6, after August 31, should be given their original EPIC numbers. The CEO assured them this would be considered.On Form 7 applications seeking removal of voters, the delegation said verification must be sought from the BLA-2 (Booth Level Agent-2) who filed the form. It demanded that all Form 7 applications be made public, that notices go to affected voters, and that decisions be taken only after a fair and adequate hearing.The group flagged incorrect Form 7 filings in Mustafabad and said appropriate action must be taken. It urged that similar cases be brought immediately to the notice of the Electoral Registration Officer.The delegation said it was also agreed that cases where the ERO or Assistant ERO themselves filed Form 7 to remove a name would be re-examined.

headline: Bulls return to D-St! Sensex zooms 1,900 points intraday; key factors here
content: Sensex today, stock market today: Domestic equity markets staged a strong rally on Wednesday, with benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty 50 advancing amid broad-based buying. The Sensex surged more than 1,900 points, or 2.3 per cent, to hit an intraday high of 84,382. Similarly, the Nifty 50 rallied 550 points, or 2.2 per cent, to touch an intraday high of 25,917. On the sectoral front, the buying was broad-based, with the banking and financial services stocks leading the gains. The Nifty Financial Services index surged 2.4 per cent, while the Nifty Bank index climbed 1.9 per cent. Banking heavyweights HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank advanced more than 3 per cent each. The Nifty IT index also moved higher by 1.9 per cent. Analysts said that the dramatic change in the FII stance towards India, AI trade unwinding, rupee appreciation and better-than-expected impressive earnings growth have combined to boost market sentiments, strongly supported by fundamentals. "It is important to understand that India’s improving fundamentals, as reflected in the impressive 27% earnings growth of Nifty 50 in Q2 has the potential to support the increasing FII inflows and impart resilience to the market," VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said and noted that India has been the best-performing large market in the world this month so far. As of 10:40 AM, the BSE benchmark was up 1,672 points, or 2.03 per cent at 84,108. The Nifty 50 index traded 480 points, or 1.88 per cent higher at 25,825. CHECK Stock Market LIVE UpdatesStock market today, Sensex today rally: Key factors AI reverse trade: Analysts said that Indian equities advanced, even as a deepening tech rout swept through Asian markets. Cooling AI trade continues to lend support to the Indian IT by easing concerns over disruption to traditional services. Notably, Asian stocks tumbled as tech-led rally fizzled inthe US, with the region's chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of ‌the selloff. South Korea's Kospi cracked 5.7 per cent, while Taiwan's TAIEX fell 7 per cent, as the two key barometers of the AI trade came under pressure. Japan's Nikkei 225 was down 3.3 per cent. Overnight in the US, the Nasdaq fell 1.5 per cent. Nvidia surrendered some ​of its gains after Jensen ​Huang's return as CEO earlier ??this week, falling 5.9 per cent, while Anthropic lost 6.5 per cent to below its IPO price. According to a report by Deutsche Bank Research Institute, India's low correlation with other global indies is suddenly looking like a strength, helping to drive record inflows of foreign investment into Indian equities. FII activity: On Monday, FIIs bought shares worth Rs 5,457.28 crore. Analysts said that foreign investors have emerged as a major driver behind markets rally in the recent weeks, with net investments crossing the ₹1 trillion mark to reach ₹1.27 trillion in November so far, marking the highest-ever monthly inflow. "It is important to note that the vicious cycle of FII selling leading to rupee depreciation, triggering more FII selling, has turned into a virtuous cycle of FII buying leading to rupee appreciation triggering more FII buying," Vijayakumar said. The strong inflows in the month of November come after FIIs withdrew ₹34,843 crore in October and ₹35,861 crore in September. Strong earnings: Brokerages have turned optimistic about corporate earnings after listed companies posted strong Q2 results. The combined adjusted net profit grew by 30.4 per cent Y-o-Y, the fastest growth in 12 quarters. Net sales grew 22.4 per cent, the highest in 16 quarters. Post this, Motilal Oswal Securities has raised its FY27 Nifty 50 EPS estimate to ₹1,243. Elara Capital expects EPS growth of 9.9 per cent, 17.1 per cent, and 14.5 per cent in 2026-27, 2027-28, and 2028-29, respectively. According to HDFC Securities, this strong earnings delivery is extremely remarkable, given the uncertain economic environment due to global unrest and elevated crude oil prices. Aggregate YoY earnings growth in Q2FY27 has been the highest in the past three years after breaking out of the tight band of 2-12 per cent. READ MORE Oil prices fall: Oil prices fell modestly on Wednesday, paring some of the previous day's gains, as concerns over supply disruptions in West Asia were offset by rising supply and the prospect of a market surplus. Brent crude futures fell 0.5 per cent to $90.9 a barrel, while WTI crude slipped 0.6 per cent to $81.5. According to Mohammed Imran, research analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, President Donald Trump’s signal that talks with Iran could run through year-end reduced the immediate risk of renewed US strikes. "The price move suggests traders are betting on better supply availability and a more comfortable global balance into year-end and 2027. Middle Eastern supply also remains high." READ MORE Technical + recovery after Monday sell-off: Earlier on Monday, markets closed sharply lower after last week's strong rally. Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president, -research, Bajaj Broking, said that some consolidation is likely after a recent strong rally of more than 15 per cent in just 4 weeks. Nifty is likely to consolidate in the range of 24,800-25,800 in the coming sessions thus forming a base for the next leg of up move towards the previous all-time high of 26,373 levels in the coming weeks. The short-term support is placed at 24,800-24,600 levels being the confluence of the recent breakout area, 20 days EMA and the 38.2% retracement of last 4 weeks rally, he said. headline: 2 youths die of suspected drug overdose in Machhiwara within 3 days; BJP targets AAP government
content: The deaths of two youths due to suspected drug overdose in Machhiwara Sahib within three days have triggered a political attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, with BJP Ludhiana Rural district president Gagandeep Sunny Kainth questioning the police administration's action against drug traffickers.Kainth said the deaths were particularly disturbing as the police had claimed heightened vigil and patrolling across the area ahead of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's visit. Despite the heavy security deployment, he alleged, drug peddlers continued to operate openly.Referring to the two deaths, Kainth said Gagandeep Singh, a resident of Indira Colony who had returned from Dubai, died of a suspected drug overdose two days ago. Before the family could come to terms with the loss, the body of another youth, factory worker Bhupinder Singh, was found along with a syringe on a dirt track along the Machhiwara-Nurpur road.He said the statement of Bhupinder's father, Amardeep Singh, that his son had taken Rs 500 from him on the pretext of buying food but used the money to purchase a drug injection, was deeply distressing."Police personnel can be deployed in large numbers for the Chief Minister's security, but the government has failed to show the same resolve in pulling Punjab's youth out of the drug menace," Kainth said.He demanded a thorough investigation into the drug supply network in the area and action against the alleged kingpins rather than focusing only on small-time peddlers. Backing the victim's family, he also called for murder cases to be registered against those responsible for supplying drugs that led to the deaths.Kainth warned that if the government failed to take decisive action against drug traffickers in Machhiwara and the wider Ludhiana Rural constituency, the BJP would launch a public agitation against the alleged failure of the state government to tackle the drug menace.

headline: Miss Universe Jennifer Barreto Education Qualification: 3 Degrees, 2 Master's In Psychology And Social Work
content: Jennifer Barreto was crowned Miss Universe 2026 at the 75th edition of the international beauty pageant, held in San Juan, Puerto Rico, on November 24. Her victory marked Puerto Rico’s sixth Miss Universe title. She also made history as a mother winning the crown. But apart from the crown, the beauty queen has an impressive academic background, with qualifications in psychology and social work. (Image: Instagram/@jenniferbarretopr) The 27-year-old beauty queen holds a bachelor’s degree in psychology and two master’s degrees, one in psychology and another in clinical social work. Barreto completed her bachelor’s degree in psychology in Kentucky. She subsequently pursued postgraduate studies, earning master’s degrees in psychology and social work. (Image: Instagram/@jenniferbarretopr) Barreto has also completed specialised studies in several areas, including trauma intervention, child protection, domestic violence prevention, suicide prevention and community needs assessment. She is mother to a seven-year old daughter named Penelope. (Image: Instagram/@missuniverse) Beyond her academic achievements, Barreto has professional experience in prevention and crisis response. In 2021, she began working with the US Army’s Family Advocacy Program at Fort Cavazos, Texas. In this role, she worked as an educator and crisis responder, supporting military families affected by domestic violence and child abuse. (Image: Instagram/@jenniferbarretopr) She also provided training to leaders on prevention and intervention strategies. She later worked as a Prevention Specialist, focusing on identifying community needs, assessing risks and developing strategies to improve the well-being of military communities. Barreto has also volunteered at the Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center and continued to collaborate with the Pediatric Diabetes Association in Puerto Rico. (Image: Instagram/@jenniferbarretopr)

headline: Wedding turns into shootout in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh; one dead, another critical
content: A wedding celebration turned into a scene of panic and bloodshed late on Tuesday night when indiscriminate firing broke out inside a hotel located at DVC Chowk in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh, people aware of the development said on Wednesday.One person was killed instantly in the firing while another sustained critical bullet injuries. The injured person received first aid at the local hospital and was later referred to RIMS, Ranchi, where their condition remains serious.According to preliminary information, a marriage ceremony was underway at the hotel when a dispute broke out between the groom's side and the bride's side over an issue. The argument escalated within minutes and turned violent, with gunfire starting soon after.Chaos spread across the venue as soon as the sound of gunshots echoed, with guests, including women and children, running to save their lives. Tables were overturned, food was scattered, and the wedding atmosphere turned into fear and confusion.Upon receiving information about the incident, local police arrived at the scene and took control of the situation. The hotel was cordoned off, and the crime scene was secured for forensic examination.Police have started scanning the CCTV footage installed in and around the hotel to identify the shooter and reconstruct the exact sequence of events. Statements of the hotel staff, the wedding hosts, and the eyewitnesses are also being recorded.Confirming the incident, Hazaribagh SP Aman Kumar said that a licensed firearm was used in the crime, adding that the accused has been absconding since the incident and that police teams are conducting raids at possible hideouts to arrest him. The SP said the probe is ongoing and that all angles, including the reason for the dispute and the role of others present at the scene, are being investigated.Police said the identity of the deceased and the injured will be shared after informing their families and completing legal formalities. The post-mortem of the deceased will be conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death. The cops have appealed to the people not to pay attention to rumours and have assured that the accused will be arrested soon.

headline: Woman alleges gangrape at Delhi cafe, 3 held
content: Three people, including two women, have been arrested in connection with the alleged gangrape of a 22-year-old woman in East Delhi’s Preet Vihar area on Monday, police said. Three other accused are absconding, they added. According to the preliminary investigation, the woman and six others initially spent time together at a cafe where they allegedly drank and danced before leaving around 2 am on Monday. After leaving, the woman allegedly called her mother and informed her that she was going to a friend’s house in Mandawali. A male friend subsequently allegedly dropped three women, including the survivor, in Mandawali, police said. According to the police, the group then allegedly went to another cafe in the vicinity, which falls under the jurisdiction of Preet Vihar police station. The woman was aware that the keys to the cafe were hidden under a flower pot, officers said. She took the group there, following which they allegedly retrieved the keys, opened the cafe, which had already shut for the night, and held a party inside, police said. According to the police, all seven, including the woman, were present at the cafe, where they allegedly consumed alcohol. The group left the cafe around 3:30 am. At approximately 5:45 am on Monday, the woman, accompanied by another male friend, made a PCR call to the police, officers said. She was subsequently taken to the police station and sent for a medical examination. During the course of the investigation, she alleged that two men had sexually assaulted her while four others watched and did not intervene, police said. Police registered a case under the relevant provisions pertaining to gangrape and arrested three accused. Efforts are underway to trace the three other accused who are on the run, officers said.

headline: India warns against using tech for strategic one-upmanship, calls for inclusive AI governance
content: United Nations India has voiced concern over the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, calling out the tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers as it underscored that technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities. Addressing the Security Council’s high-level open debate on Maintenance of International Peace and Security on ‘Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change’, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni said AI systems can inadvertently perpetuate biases related to gender, language and socio-economic background. Delivered India’s statement at the UN Security Council high-level open debate convened by Latvia. Speaking on the theme, “Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change”, I highlighted four key considerations: 1️⃣ Technology must remain human-centric and an instrument of peace 2️⃣ The application of emerging technologies in conflict settings must be responsible, human-centric, respect sovereignty, and adhere to international law 3️⃣ We must address threats posed by misuse of emerging technologies such as AI 4️⃣ Technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities. We must address technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes. Countries of the Global South should not be tested as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, regulated and deployed.— Parvathaneni Harish (@AmbHarishP) November 24, 2026 “We note with concern the emerging medium- and long-term trends of technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, and a tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, are regulated and are deployed,” Mr. Parvathaneni said. “AI must not reduce human beings to mere data points or raw material. India supports inclusive international cooperation on technology governance, including through the United Nations, with due regard to national priorities and developmental needs,” he said. He emphasised that technology should serve humanity, strengthen international cooperation, and advance the cause of lasting peace. “Technology may inform human judgement but cannot and should not replace it,” he said. India also asserted that amid the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into military and intelligence spheres, responsibility for use of lethal autonomous weapons systems must always rest with humans. “Rapid technological advances are fundamentally transforming the nature of conflict and the international security landscape. Artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and emerging digital technologies present unprecedented opportunities but also introduce new vulnerabilities and risks across the entire conflict cycle,” Mr. Parvathaneni said. He added that the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into military, intelligence, and civilian spheres has fundamentally transformed the landscape of international peace and security. India stressed that the application of emerging technologies in conflict settings must be responsible, human-centric, respect sovereignty, and adhere to international law. “Emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems raise legitimate legal and ethical questions. India is committed to addressing these within the framework of the Convention on Prohibitions or Restrictions on the Use of Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), which seeks to balance military necessity with humanitarian considerations,” Mr. Parvathaneni said. He underscored that human judgement and oversight remain essential, taking into account the operational context and characteristics of the weapons system. “Responsibility for the use of such systems must always rest with humans,” the Indian envoy said, adding that leveraging technology for protection must be a cross-cutting and cross-sectoral measure. “It must be used for the protection of civilians and of peacekeepers and should be leveraged for the protection of humanitarian personnel.” India called on the international community to address threats posed by misuse of emerging technologies such as AI. “The risks associated with AI are real, and we must address them without any hesitation. The potential misuse of these emerging technologies by terrorists and non-State actors is a matter of grave concern. Incomplete, inaccurate, or deliberately manipulated data through AI can undermine decision-making,” he said. He told the Council that India has made robust advancements in digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies, reflecting a clear emphasis on protecting critical information infrastructure and ensuring the continuity of essential civilian services. Addressing the Security Council Open Debate, Secretary General Antonio Guterres voiced concern that today’s wars have become “proving grounds” for AI-enabled targeting. Asserting that killer robots must have no place in the world’s future, Mr. Guterres reiterated his call to urgently launch negotiations for a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems. “AI is driving greater autonomy across military functions. From intelligence gathering to target selection, it is reported that algorithms are increasingly shaping life-and-death decisions,” he said, adding that these capabilities are within the reach of both States and non-State armed groups. “And the potential integration of AI with nuclear command, control and communication systems is a recipe for catastrophe. As long as nuclear weapons exist, the decision to use them must rest with human beings alone,” Mr. Guterres said. “When civilians are killed, or human rights are violated, the answer must never be ‘the algorithm did it’,” Mr. Guterres said. The UN chief added that humans must always retain control over life-and-death decisions – guided by international law and ethical principles. “Technology companies must reckon with the legal risks they may face if their services contribute to violations of international law. And no country should design, develop, deploy, or use military applications of AI in armed conflict that violate international law, international humanitarian law, or international human rights law,” he said. Delivered India’s statement at the UN Security Council high-level open debate convened by Latvia. Speaking on the theme, “Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change”, I highlighted four key considerations: 1️⃣ Technology must remain human-centric and an instrument of peace 2️⃣ The application of emerging technologies in conflict settings must be responsible, human-centric, respect sovereignty, and adhere to international law 3️⃣ We must address threats posed by misuse of emerging technologies such as AI 4️⃣ Technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities. We must address technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes. Countries of the Global South should not be tested as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, regulated and deployed.— Parvathaneni Harish (@AmbHarishP) November 24, 2026

headline: Tamil Nadu government set to ink 70 MoUs for investments to the tune of over ₹50,000 crore
content: CHENNAI Tamil Nadu is set to sign over 70 memoranda of understanding (MoUs), entailing investments of over Rs. 50,000 crore, at the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave, scheduled to be held in Chennai on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Sources said the MoUs would cover sectors including manufacturing, clean energy, textiles, aerospace and defence. It is learnt that Royal Enfield will be signing a deal for EV motorbikes. Keppel-backed Cleantech Solar, a renewable energy developer with a portfolio of 1.2 MWp+ renewable energy projects, including over 400 MW in Tamil Nadu, is also signing a deal. This will be a five-year investment, integrating solar, wind and battery energy storage systems, designed to meet the evolving energy requirements of Tamil Nadu’s commercial and industrial sectors. Sources say the two South Korean automotive component manufacturers — Seoyon E-Hwa Summit Automotive India Private Limited and Hwashin Automotive India Private Limited — that recently expressed interest in investing in Tamil Nadu will also be signing MoUs. “Turning investment intent into working facilities and steady livelihoods is what matters most for our people. Our focus is on practical execution, responsive institutions, and balanced industrial growth across Tamil Nadu,” Industries Minister S. Keerthana said. Status report The TVK government will also provide an update on the MoUs signed since the party came to power, including the number of project proposals that have translated into actual investments. It will also present a status report on the remaining projects, detailing their progress at various stages, such as land acquisition and construction. At its first investors’ conclave held in August this year, the TVK government signed 97 MoUs, entailing more than Rs. 67,542 crore in investments.

headline: Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister
content: KALABURAGI The State government is examining a series of measures to address the growing problem of human-elephant conflict in Hassan district, including the installation of steel-rope barricades and fitting GPS collars on elephants to monitor their movements, Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy said on Tuesday. The Minister said residents of Belur, Sakleshpur and other parts of Hassan district have been facing difficulties owing to elephant movement, and the State government was taking their concerns seriously. The Minister was speaking to presspersons after inaugurating the new main entrance gate and various development works at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district. The works were taken up at a cost of ₹18 crore with assistance from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation and other sources. He also laid the foundation stone for additional works estimated to cost ₹3 crore. Pointing to the fragmented nature of forest areas in the region, he said nearly 13,000 acres of forest in Belur taluk were spread across nine separate patches, and the nearly one lakh acres of forest area in Sakleshpur were similarly divided into more than 80 patches. “This fragmentation made it difficult to regulate elephant movement and prevent human-elephant conflict,” he said. The proposal to relocate elephants to the Bhadra forest area had been under discussion for some time, and the government would also take into consideration the concerns expressed by local elected representatives, Mr. Reddy said. “The feasibility of installing steel-rope barricades to prevent elephants from straying out of forests is being examined, subject to financial constraints. A plan to fit GPS collars on elephants and continuously monitor their movements was also being implemented,” he said. Kamalapur zoo development Speaking on the development initiatives taken at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district, Mr. Reddy said that several facilities have been developed at the zoo with funding from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation, the Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation and contributions from mining companies. “Hampi is an important historical destination that attracts a large number of tourists. The government is committed to developing the zoo as an additional attraction,” he said. The Minister said that arrangements had been made to ensure an uninterrupted supply of water, fodder and food for the animals and birds. Solar-powered borewells had been installed to ensure a regular water supply and to meet emergency requirements. Shade had also been provided for the animals, while a sprinkler system had been introduced to maintain the plants. The zoo would be provided with additional animal species, with priority given to their health and conservation, he said. New open and closed jeeps and buses had also been arranged to facilitate safari tours. K.S. Basavanthappa, Vijayanagara district in-charge Minister; H.R. Gaviyappa, Hosapete MLA; E. Tukaram, Ballari MP; M.P. Latha Mallikarjun, Harapanahalli MLA; K. Rangaswamy, Karnataka Zoo Authority chairman; Kavita Mannikeri, Deputy Commissioner; S. Jahnavi, Superintendent of Police; and senior forest department officials were present.

headline: Garhshankar: Teachers protest Census duty on Parkash Purb  of Guru Nanak Dev
content: The Democratic Teachers Front (DTF), Punjab, staged a protest against the local administration for calling teachers for Census-related work on a holiday marking Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purb. The protesters burnt an effigy of the administration and demanded an end to what they termed unnecessary pressure on teachers.Addressing the gathering, DTF state joint secretary Mukesh Kumar and state publicity secretary Sukhdev Dansiwal alleged that although self-enumeration was meant to be undertaken by people themselves, the local administration was pressuring enumerators and supervisors to meet targets. They alleged that teachers were even being forced to facilitate the process through their mobile phones.The union leaders said teachers were already burdened with various non-academic duties throughout the year. Thousands of teachers had performed responsibilities related to BLO and SIR exercises and now they were also being assigned self-enumeration work.They said several teachers were facing dual duties of BLO and Census-related work, adversely affecting students’ studies in schools. The DTF leaders demanded that teachers should not be assigned door-to-door self-enumeration work and that the practice of seeking daily evening reports from enumerators and supervisors should be discontinued. They urged the administration to give priority to students’ education and stop putting unnecessary pressure on employees.Among those present were Hans Raj Garhshankar, Jasvir Singh, Satnam Singh, Subhash Chander, Husan Lal, Karnail Singh, Sandeep Kumar, Parjinder Singh, Kuldeep Singh, Rajesh Kumar, Vinod Kumar, Manjit Kaur, Inderjit Kaur, Mamta, Manjit Singh and Subhash Kumar.

headline: Amritsar: Faith blends with science, heritage at GNDU
content: Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU) celebrated its 57th Foundation Day on Tuesday, coinciding with Gurpurb celebrations. The celebrations highlighted the contemporary relevance of Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings of universal brotherhood, equality, humanity and selfless service through religious observance, academic discussions and cultural exhibitions.Addressing the gathering, Vice-Chancellor Prof Karamjeet Singh said the university’s founding vision extended beyond imparting education to promoting Guru Nanak Dev’s philosophy. He emphasised that academic excellence must go hand in hand with ethical values and social responsibility.Highlighting Amritsar’s economic potential, he said the university was preparing a research-based vision document to explore the city’s development as a hub for trade, cargo, logistics and international commerce, alongside its established religious and tourism identity. Consultations with experts from India and abroad were underway.He also outlined efforts to develop artificial intelligence (AI)-based Punjabi language learning tools, impart AI training to students and communicate scientific research in simple Punjabi. “University alumni have pledged Rs 5 crore towards the initiative,” he said.Former GNDU Vice-Chancellor Dr Jai Rup Singh, speaking on the conceptual relationship between Gurbani and modern genetics, said the 99.9 per cent genetic similarity among human beings underscored the commonality of humanity.Referring to Gurbani, he highlighted the importance of understanding human existence through spiritual and scientific perspectives. He clarified that while Gurbani and the Big Bang Theory were distinct concepts, both encouraged reflection on the origins of the universe.Dr Rajwant Singh, founder and global president of EcoSikh, spoke about Guru Nanak Dev’s vision of personal transformation and global harmony. Referring to Sri Japji Sahib, he emphasised truth, humility, compassion and harmony with nature as the foundations of a peaceful and inclusive society. He also announced plans to develop 450 forests in Amritsar to mark the city’s 450th anniversary.The celebrations featured Sri Akhand Path Sahib, Shabad Kirtan, Ardas and exhibitions showcasing Punjab’s traditional embroidery, Phulkari, Bagh, musical instruments and jewellery. A painting competition on ‘Amritsar 450’, along with exhibitions of rare books, manuscripts was held.
