headline: 1 MLA among 117: Alliance SAD’s only lifeline for survival
content: Between the two alliance partners, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which reunited on Tuesday after a gap of six years, the partnership is potentially the former’s only shot at political survival.The 2027 assembly elections are a make-or-break battle for SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, where a strong showing could mark the party’s resurgence, while another poor showing would inflict irreparable damage on its future.From being in power for two consecutive terms between 2007 and 2017, SAD has been reduced to the margins of state politics a decade later. It won 15 seats in the 2017 assembly elections, a tally which shrunk to just three in 2022.Its legislative presence has dwindled further, with two of its three legislators — Manpreet Singh Ayali (Dakha) joining Akal Dal (Waris Punjab De) and Dr Sukhwinder Kumar Sukhi (Banga) moving to the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Ganieve Kaur Majithia, representing Majitha, now effectively remains SAD’s lone face in the assembly.“The hard work Sukhbir Badal has put in during the past few months is commendable. It has led us to a partnership with the BJP, and the alliance will register a victory in the 2027 polls,” said SAD secretary general Balwinder Singh Bhundar, while maintaining that SAD was never desperate.BJP had also sensed the ground realities and realised that an alliance was necessary for the safety, security and growth of people in the state, he added.While a section of BJP leaders, including former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh and former state unit president Sunil Jakhar, had advocated an alliance, a majority of the leadership in Punjab and New Delhi had rejected the possibility and maintained that the BJP would contest all 117 assembly constituencies in the state.In contrast, the entire SAD leadership had pushed for an alliance, even as Sukhbir maintained a public silence on the negotiations. During recent media interactions, he had said he was “not an astrologer” when asked about the possibility of a tie-up, even as he held meetings with senior BJP leaders, including Union minister Amit Shah and national president Nitin Nabin, to work out the arrangement.“What options did SAD have to remain in the political contest other than an alliance with the party that is in power at the Centre?” remarked Jagrup Singh Sekhon, former head of the political science department at Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar.The SAD attempted to rebuild itself from the grassroots by seeking support directly from the masses, but remained unsuccessful, he added.Sharp decline in vote shareIn the 2007 assembly elections, SAD won 48 of the 117 assembly seats, with a vote share of 37%. In 2012, it improved its tally to 56 seats, polling 34.7% of the votes.However, the party’s fortunes reversed in 2017, when its seats slid to 15 and the vote share to 25.4%. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), then a new entrant in Punjab, won 20 seats.After a split from the BJP, in 2022, SAD contested the assembly elections in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), managing to win only three seats and its vote share falling to 18.5%.AAP swept the polls with a 42% vote share, gaining more than 23% points over its 2017 performance.SAD’s decline was also evident in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when it recorded its lowest-ever vote share of 13.4% and managed to win just one seat, Bathinda, through Harsimrat Kaur Badal.Deal clinched on November 13The final meeting that clinched the alliance was held in New Delhi on November 13. On returning the following day, Sukhbir hinted to party leaders that they should prepare for an alliance after the annual office-bearers’ election of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) on November 20. Subsequently, he was conveyed that a joint press conference would be held on November 24 for a formal announcement.Before that, Sukhbir had made frequent trips to New Delhi whenever summoned by the BJP leadership, with most of the meetings taking place at night.

headline: Old alliance, new dynamics: Decoding the SAD-BJP reunion
content: Six years after they parted ways over the Centre’s farm laws, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday buried the hatchet by reviving the alliance, resetting political equations in Punjab and setting the stage for a three-way battle in the high-stakes assembly polls due early next year.Between 1997 and 2017, the two parties fought five assembly elections side by side and won three. That partnership unravelled in September 2020 when fierce protests by farmers across Punjab and Haryana against the BJP government’s three agricultural laws forced SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal to resign from the Union cabinet. Days later, party chief Sukhbir Singh Badal pulled out of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). Even after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the laws on November 19, 2021, the two parties remained apart.Reviving the tie-up on Guru Nanak Jayanti carries unmistakable political symbolism in Punjab. Crucial milestones in Centre-Punjab outreach have repeatedly coincided with Gurpurb—from the inauguration of the Kartarpur Corridor on November 9, 2019, ahead of Guru Nanak’s 550th birth anniversary, to the 2021 farm law repeal announcement.As both parties prepare to face the electorate together again, the revived coalition brings together distinct advantages alongside vulnerabilities.Strengths: A time-tested social coalitionThe SAD-BJP tie-up draws strength from a proven electoral formula rooted in Punjab’s social structure. Together, the two allies delivered a landslide in 1997, winning 93 of the state’s 117 assembly seats, and later returned to power in 2007 and 2012, becoming the first alliance to secure consecutive terms in Punjab since the state’s reorganisation in 1966.According to political observers, the partnership bridges Punjab’s rural-urban and demographic divides, combining the SAD’s predominantly Sikh rural base with the BJP’s urban Hindu support. “It’s a time-tested alliance. Of the five elections they fought together, they have emerged victorious thrice,” said Amanpreet Gill, an associate professor of political science at Khalsa College, New Delhi.Describing the tie-up as a social coalition that factors in Punjab’s two principal communities, Gill added: “It has been the best coalition to resolve Punjab’s paradox of majority as minorities and minority as majority. It also serves the historical mission of Hindu-Sikh unity in Punjab. There is a political chemistry between the two parties, and both have benefited from each other.”That sentiment was echoed within the BJP’s state ranks following Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s press conference remarks after the tie-up announcement. “What Amit Shah told today in the press conference, that the alliance was important for Hindu-Sikh unity, carries weight. Akalis represent Sikhs, and Hindu leadership will also start getting importance,” a senior state BJP leader said.Weaknesses: Existential crisis & ground realitiesThe upcoming election will be the alliance’s first joint assembly test without SAD patriarch Parkash Singh Badal, who passed away in April 2023. It is equally a make-or-break polls for Sukhbir’s leadership. Out of power for a decade following back-to-back assembly poll defeats in 2017 and 2022, the 106-year-old SAD is facing an existential crisis, weakened by peasant resentment and a steep erosion of credibility in the Panthic arena. Compounding its woes, the party suffered a vertical split in 2024 that resulted in the formation of the breakaway faction SAD (Punar Surjit).For the BJP, the reunion marks a retreat from its stand of contesting alone. Even after Shah declared at a rally in Moga that the party would go solo in the 2027 polls, ground assessments failed to inspire confidence. “Even as a section in the BJP was bent upon convincing the high command that the party alone would make a grand entry, the high command knew the ground situation,” said a former minister, pleading anonymity. According to people familiar with the matter, the wake-up call was the tepid public response to the BJP’s anti-drug yatra, which exposed the limits of its standalone organisational reach.Opportunities: The ‘double engine’ pitch, strategic resetThe alliance opens a critical window of opportunity for both partners, say analysts. For the Akalis, it offers a much-needed lifeline back to mainstream relevance. For the BJP, reuniting with the NDA’s oldest constituent strengthens the Modi-led coalition nationally while handing the party a readymade rural organisational and social network in Punjab that it struggled to build on its own.The partners are essentially banking on the “double engine government” pitch stressing that political alignment between Chandigarh and New Delhi will push infrastructure development in the state. “The stage is set now. If the alliance is voted to power, Punjab will see development,” said former Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) president Manjit Singh GK.After the announcing the tie-up, Shah publicly termed the SAD “bada bhai” (elder brother), reposing faith in Sukhbir’s leadership and assuring that the chief minister’s post would go to the senior partner, a gesture made to reassure the Akali cadre.Challenges & threats: Seat-sharing formulas, farm anger, past baggageThe tie-up will come with its share of challenges both for the SAD and the BJP. The biggest change in the alliance equation is the seat-sharing arrangement. From 1997 to 2017, the SAD was the senior partner, contesting 94 of Punjab’s 117 assembly seats, while the BJP contested 23. The SAD largely focused on rural seats and the BJP on urban constituencies. That balance is now expected to change.According to functionaries in both parties, the BJP is likely to contest 47-48 seats in 2027, nearly double its earlier share. The broad division is expected to remain the same, with the BJP focusing on urban seats and the SAD on rural constituencies. In the new scenario, the SAD will have to yield more political space to the BJP, which will now act almost as an equal partner.Beyond seat numbers, the SAD faces an uphill task of pacifying farmer unions, whose fierce opposition to the farm laws triggered the 2020 split. Also, the Akalis must repulse stiff competition on their core Panthic turf from breakaway rivals such as SAD (Punar Surjit) and Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De).Old controversies also threaten to resurface as political rivals look for fresh fodder to target the alliance partners. The 2015 Bargari sacrilege incidents and subsequent police firing continue to haunt the SAD, while the drug menace, with senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia already facing vigilance heat, gives the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress a ready campaign ammunition. Having previously pitched itself as a cleaner alternative, the BJP will now have to share ownership of that past record.The reunion is also likely to create internal friction within the BJP’s state unit. Accommodating vocal SAD critics inducted into the saffron fold, such as Ravinder Singh Bittu and Kunwar Vijay Partap who investigated the Behbal Kalan case, will be a challenge.

headline: Mohali Phase 5 residents oppose vegetable market at cleared dumping site
content: Residents of Phase 5 and adjoining Shahi Majra have once again raised concerns over the use of vacant land near the resource management centre (RMC), this time over the resumption of the vegetable market.Located close to residential areas, Shahi Majra village and commercial establishments, it was earlier used as a dumping site, leading to concerns over the accumulated waste and foul smell.The issue intensified after a fire broke out at the site on October 1. The fire continued to smoulder for several days despite repeated efforts. The dump again caught fire on October 11.The recurring fires had triggered protests by residents, who demanded that the accumulated garbage be removed permanently and the land be developed into a park or green belt. The Municipal Corporation finally cleared the waste on October 31 this year.However, the Mohali market committee soon moved to resume the vegetable market at the cleared ground. Residents are now opposing the operation of the vegetable mandi on the same ground. They allege that the market, which traditionally operates every Monday and Friday, has led to fresh civic issues in the area. They have raised concerns over vegetable waste being dumped after trading hours, which is later scattered by stray cattle.SK Goyal, vice-president of the Green Park Residents Welfare Society, Park No. 49, Phase 5, said the mandi was affecting the daily lives of residents.“After vegetable sellers leave, they throw waste in the area. Traffic is also affected as customers park their vehicles on the road. Besides, residents are facing disturbance at night when vendors shout loudly,” Goyal said, adding that residents had suggested an alternative site near the mills to the mandi representatives.On the other hand, farmers and small traders have argued that shifting the mandi could affect their livelihoods.Mohali market committee chairman Govinder Mittal said the mandi was legally established under the relevant Act and had been operating for several years. He added that it was permitted under a Punjab government welfare scheme and its functioning was regulated by the market committee against user charges.The disagreement between residents and vendors escalated on November 3 when residents protested against the mandi and stopped a market committee truck carrying material to the site.After discussions between the two sides, the market was allowed to operate around 5.30 pm. However, the terms of the understanding remain unclear.Kuldeep Kaur Kang, municipal councillor from Ward 9, said that the vegetable market has been operational for the last four years. It was closed for two months, but resumed after the MC cleared the waste.Kang added that residents had signed a representation seeking relocation of the mandi and submitted it to the mandi board. “A suitable alternative site has been identified and discussed with the board secretary and chairman, but written approval for the relocation is awaited. We have also written to the chief minister, and a response is awaited,” Kang said.

headline: 6 booked for assault, stone-pelting over unpaid dues in Balongi
content: A family was attacked in Balongi over unpaid dues on November 10, with six residents allegedly assaulting them with stones and bricks. The victim has further alleged aerial firing before the accused fled.Balongi police registered a case against the accused.According to the complaint filed by 38-year-old Radha, her husband, Jai Singh owed money to three of the accused, Raman, Suman and Salma.Around 5pm on November 10, their nephew Abhay informed them that the group was assaulting his father, Raju, at his house in Rehmat Enclave.When Radha and Jai Singh reached Raju’s house and questioned the accused, the group allegedly attacked them too. The couple ran towards their house, but the accused chased them and pelted them with bricks and stones. Neighbours intervened after hearing their cries for help.Radha was later admitted to Kharar civil hospital until November 13. Her medical report recorded five blunt-weapon injuries, including two referred for an orthopaedic opinion. Jai Singh and Raju sustained minor injuries.Police booked Raman, Pawan alias Kallu, Sunny, Salma, Rajni and Suman under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 191(3) (rioting) and 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police said a spot inspection did not yield evidence of aerial firing so far, and they were probing Radha’s allegation.

headline: Chandigarh: PU’s  ₹118-crore multipurpose hall awaits mandatory clearance
content: Nearly 15 years after work began on Panjab University’s (PU) ₹118-crore Multipurpose Hall, the university is still awaiting the occupation certificate and other mandatory clearances for the facility.Despite having secured structural safety and fire safety certificates, the remaining approvals are yet to come through, with the hall’s formal inauguration now pushed to next year.In a telling contrast, PU will hold its December 5 convocation, with vice-president of India CP Radhakrishnan as chief guest, at the university’s Gymnasium Hall instead of its newly constructed 2,500-seater auditorium.The university has applied for the occupation certificate and is awaiting the remaining approvals, PU registrar said. “We have got some certificates like structural safety, fire, etc. We are awaiting the rest. It will be done in due course,” he said.The pending clearances come even as the facility has already been used for university programmes under phased operationalisation. However, its formal inauguration remains pending, with a portion of the construction work on the first floor also yet to be completed.The registrar said the hall was likely to be inaugurated next year, citing pending construction work, mandatory approvals and budgetary constraints.The project, initially estimated to cost around ₹60 crore, has seen its estimated cost rise to ₹118 crore. With a seating capacity of approximately 2,500, the Multipurpose Hall is PU’s largest auditorium and was envisioned as a dedicated venue for large-scale academic, cultural and institutional events.The facility includes a main auditorium, green room, rehearsal room, workshop room, VIP rooms, exhibition area, boardroom, cafeteria and basement parking.The project has missed several earlier expectations of completion and inauguration over the years. Once the remaining construction work and mandatory formalities are completed, the hall is expected to provide the university with a larger dedicated venue for major institutional functions.

headline: Mohali: Haryana govt employee duped of  ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad
content: A 53-year-old Haryana health department employee was allegedly duped of nearly ₹5 lakh by cyber fraudsters who lured her with a Facebook advertisement offering financial assistance.The complainant, who resides in Nayagaon, told police that she was in urgent need of money. So when she came across a Facebook advertisement offering assistance, she clicked on it and shared her phone number on the link.About a week later, a man identifying himself as Jagdish Singh called her and sought copies of her Aadhaar and PAN cards. According to the complainant, the caller later claimed that an inspector general of police had withheld the funds meant for her. Later, another person contacted her, alleging that her GST documents were incomplete and that a court had imposed a fine. She was asked to pay the amount to receive the promised financial assistance. Believing their claims, the woman transferred the money through multiple transactions. The accused later demanded another ₹4 lakh. She stopped responding to their calls after realised that she had been cheated.Based on her complaint, a case under Sections 318(4) and 319(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act has been registered against unidentified persons.Man cheated of ₹4 cr on pretext of goods supplyA Gujarat-based man allegedly cheated a city resident of ₹4 crore on the pretext of supplying goods ordered online.The accused, identified as Yash Panchal, has been booked under Section 318(4) (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Mauli Jagran police station.According to the complaint filed by Roha Partap Singh, a resident of Raipur Kalan, the accused received ₹4 crore through online transactions between November 26 and December 25, 2024, against an order for certain goods. However, he neither supplied the goods nor refunded the money.

headline: Biker killed as manjha slits throat in SE Delhi
content: A 27-year-old man on a motorcycle died on Tuesday after a stray kite string (manjha) slit his throat while he was near Barapullah on the newly inaugurated stretch of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway.Police identified the victim as Vikas Singh, a resident of Jaitpur area, who had recently become a father.The incident took place near Shaheen Bagh in southeast Delhi around 8.11 am. Police said Singh worked at a laptop repair centre in Delhi and was on the way back to his home from an overnight work trip.Deputy commissioner of police (southeast) Vineet Kumar said that police teams were informed about a “bike rider lying injured in a pool of blood on the road”.The string had caused Singh to lose control of his bike and fall onto the road. “He sustained a severe injury to his neck. He was sent to AIIMS Trauma Centre where the doctors declared him brought-dead.”His body has been preserved for a postmortem examination.According to Singh’s family, he also received injuries to his ankle and wrist because of the kite string. Delhi Police said they have initiated a probe in the case and are looking at nearby CCTVs to establish the exact sequence of events that led to the incident.A case under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita section 106 (causing death by negligence) has been lodged.Singh is survived by his wife Pinky and their three-month-old daughter. The family said the couple was married in 2025.Singh was a resident of. His family said his company had sent him for some work at night and he was returning home the next day when he died.Speaking to HT, his wife said, “He called me around 7am and asked about me and the baby. I scolded him and told him to come home soon. He apologised and said he was on the way. Around 8.20 am, I got a call that Vikas got injured. I rushed to the expressway in an auto and found he had already died.”Umesh Soni, Pinky’s father, said they had been informed of the incident around 8.30am and came to Delhi from Pratapgarh. “We have a baby and the father was killed because of someone’s nuisance. I went to the Mumbai expressway myself. It was not a small thread. It looked like multiple strings of manjha got stuck to his neck, hands and even leg. Isn’t it a new flyover? Why was so much Manjha lying around the edge there? Vikas had a helmet and was riding safely. But the kite string was long and sharp. There was blood everywhere on the road.”According to Delhi Police’s data, 3 deaths and at least 13 injuries have been reported due to manjhas this year.In May, a five-year-old boy died after his neck was slit by a manjha while he was travelling with his family on a motorcycle in northeast Delhi’s Usmanpur area. He was rushed to a hospital but succumbed to his injuries. HT found that no arrests were made in the case.Last year, on August 15, a 30-year-old bike rider sustained severe neck injury while travelling from Sarita Vihar to Faridabad.In June last year, a 22-year-old man died after his throat was slit by a manjha while he was riding his scooter near Bara Hindu Rao Hospital in north Delhi. He suffered a deep cut on his neck and collapsed on the spot.

headline: Notices sent to 6 Jamia students for organising canteen protest
content: Jamia Millia Islamia has served showcause notices to atleast six students over an alleged unauthorised gathering at the university’s central canteen to protest the Supreme Court’s recent ruling in the Bilkis Bano case.Saying that the protest was held at a non-designated location, the university administration has given the students two days to explain why disciplinary action should not be taken against them.The Congress-backed National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) had organised a protest on November 23, with around 100 students gathering at JMI’s central canteen in the North Campus to condemn the SC’s order regarding the release of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case. A poster about the gathering circulated on social media platforms, inviting students to join.“You along with a large group of other students associated with different political outfits assembled near the central canteen…for the solidarity gathering for Bilkis Bano against the recent order of the supreme court granting ball and suspending the life sentences of two convicts in her case…during the unauthorised gathering at the central canteen you also delivered a speech and raised slogans to cause disruption and disturb the normalcy of the campus,” the notice, also seen by HT, dated November 23 and issued to one of the students read. It was signed by JMI’s chief proctor professor Mohammad Asad Malik.A JMI spokesperson said that the university has designated a specific space for dissent to ensure that routine activities are not disrupted while also providing students with a democratic platform to exercise their freedom of expression. “The central canteen is not a designated site for protests. It is a place where our departments and teaching blocks are located. It disturbs classes and besides exams are due shortly,” the spokesperson added.In the notice, the administration reiterated that, through an order issued in October 2025, it had designated a specific location for students to hold protests within a democratic framework. Citing the order, the administration stated that the gathering at the central canteen violated the prescribed guidelines, allegedly undermining student discipline and disrupting the university’s routine functioning.The university has directed the students to submit their defence by 9pm on November 25 through an email to the university’s chief proctor.

headline: CJP’s Saurav Das accuses Centre of ‘blocking UK trip’
content: Cockroach Janta Party(CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Tuesday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led central government of using a show-cause notice over alleged discrepancies in his passport details to prevent him from travelling to the United Kingdom (UK) to deliver a lecture at Oxford Union.He called it an attempt to harass him and intimidate the youth.“The notice was sent just five hours before my flight, and its sole purpose was to harass me and send a message to other young people: look, this could happen to you too,” Das said.Das was scheduled to travel to the UK for an event at the Oxford Union on December 1, where he said he was invited to speak about the “Cockroach Movement”.The central government was yet to comment on the allegations, but people aware of the matter said that the address details and credentials of the CJP co-convener were under probe for the past few months.A person aware of the matter said, “If you remember, the Puducherry police team had also visited his house to verify the address he submitted in the court. The addresses he submitted were different from the place where he was living in south Delhi. There are discrepancies related to this place of birth in the passport and other details such as Aadhaar. This is why a notice was issued to Saurav Das by the Regional Passport Office of Chennai in which he was asked not to use the passport for any purposes, including travel,” a person aware of the matter said.On October 30, a bench of the Madras High Court issued a notice to the Regional Passport Officer, Chennai, seeking the RPO’s reply on a PIL alleging that Das was not an Indian citizen and that his passport should be cancelled.Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor, said, “Saurav Das, who has so far opposed the Government of India... wanted to slip out to defame India from abroad on the Constitution Day. He was going to a private body to spew anti-India venom.”CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also questioned the reasons behind the restriction. “What is the reason for stopping him from travelling abroad? What is wrong with an Indian citizen visiting renowned universities and speaking about a movement that gained international recognition? Is Saurav a criminal? Has he looted a bank?” Dipke said during a media interaction at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra on Tuesday afternoon.

headline: Dr Atul Mohan Kochhara named DGHS chief
content: Dr Atul Mohan Kochhara, a senior dermatologist, was appointed the new director general of health services (DGHS), according to an order by the Delhi government’s health and family welfare department.Previously, Dr Vinod Kumar, medical director of the GTB Hospital, had been holding the additional charge of the post.The order, dated November 21, said, “Pursuance to the approval of Lieutenant Governor, Delhi, Dr Atul Mohan Kochhar, NTS (Dermatology), SAG (senior administrative grade), is hereby posted as Director (DGHS), Government of NCT of Delhi, with immediate effect.”HT has seen a copy of the order.Kochhar served as chief executive officer of the National Accreditation Board for hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) from December 2019 to March 2026. Before that, he worked as a professor and consultant in dermatology at Maulana Azad Medical College and Lok Nayak Hospital.This is the fifth appointment to the post in two years. In May 2025, Dr Rati Makkar was appointed to the post but opted for voluntary retirement in August. Dr Vatsala Aggarwal succeeded her the same month. She was arrested by the anti-corruption branch and subsequently suspended over alleged irregularities in the procurement of medicines and medical equipment for Delhi government health services.Dr Sushma Jain, then medical superintendent of Jag Pravesh Chandra Hospital, was assigned the additional charge of DGHS director in June this year.Kumar was subsequently entrusted with the additional charge in July 30.

headline: Delhi traffic circles may be rejigged to handle infra works, increased area under new corridors
content: New DelhiThe Delhi Traffic Police are surveying overburdened traffic circles, covering large geographical stretches or areas with heavy traffic movement, for boundary realignment and possible creation of eight to ten more traffic circles to distribute the workload, two senior police officers said.The study started around a fortnight ago and is likely to be completed by mid-December, they said. A report on the current situation, required divisions or mergers of a traffic circle’s areas with the adjoining circles, and requirement for new traffic circles and districts will be sent to the police headquarters for approval.The proposal for the realignment of traffic circles’ boundaries will be sent to the Delhi lieutenant governor’s (LG’s), seeking official sanction.“After the LG’s nod, a notification would be issued from his office notifying the lot-line adjustment and creation of additional traffic circles and districts across Delhi. Accordingly, a fresh proposal demanding additional manpower in the traffic police unit would be moved to the concerned authorities,” said one of the two officers cited above.The plan comes in view of the opening of the Urban Extension Road (UER)-2, the Barapullah Corridor’s Phase-3, Dwarka and Delhi-Dehradun Expressways and the soft launch of the newly constructed Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, the officers said.Additional commissioner of police (traffic) Dinesh Kumar Gupta said, “The boundary realignment of the traffic circles was required for the redistribution of the workload. Our survey is aimed at identifying such traffic circles and examining whether they need to be divided to ensure more effective traffic management. We expect an addition of 8-10 circles and 3-4 traffic districts.”In south Delhi, the Lajpat Nagar and Sangam Vihar traffic circles are being considered, given the traffic management challenges posed by busy commercial and transport hubs and other factors. The Lajpat Nagar circle handles traffic congestion of roads around Sarai Kale Khan, such as the DND, Barapullah corridor, the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway and the Delhi-Meerut Expressway, in addition to high-footfall and heavy vehicular movement in and around the Lajpat Nagar market.The second officer cited above said, “After the restructuring, some parts of the Lajpat Nagar traffic circle may be added to the NFC and Tilak Marg circles, particularly the Ring Road’s stretch between Ashram Chowk and the Indraprastha (IP) flyover via Sarai Kale Khan that could be divided between the two circles.”Another under lens is the Sangam Vihar traffic circle, which covers areas from Greater Kailash to Asola Wildlife Sanctuary, near Delhi-Faridabad border. Due to high traffic volume and ongoing infrastructure projects, traffic personnel of the circle are daily handling multiple traffic congestion points on the Outer Ring Road, Mehrauli-Badarpur Road and in areas like Alakhnanda and Sangam Vihar.“Through boundary realignment, some portion of the Sangam Vihar traffic circle may be merged into its adjoining Saket and Badarpur circles,” the second officer added.Others under consideration are Shahdara and Madhu Vihar traffic circles in the trans-Yamuna belt, Najafgarh and Dwarka circles in southwest Delhi, and Samaipur Badli, Narela, and Aman Vihar circles in outer Delhi.Additional commissioner Gupta said the survey will examine multiple parameters, including the geographical area under each traffic circle, daily traffic volume, congestion hotspots, major roads and intersections, accident-prone stretches and the existing manpower.“Our focus is on creating smaller and more manageable jurisdictions based on traffic movement, congestion patterns and operational requirements,” said Gupta.

headline: Delhi’s political leaders celebrate Gurupurab
content: New DelhiChief minister Rekha Gupta, on the occasion of Guru Purab on Tuesday, called for an end to social discrimination and prejudices in society, offering prayers at the Gurdwara Nanak Piao Sahib in north Delhi.Besides the CM, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin, Delhi ministers and political leaders took part in celebrations at key gurdwaras across the Capital to mark the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.Gupta said that Guru Nanak Dev’s life and philosophy serve as a guiding light for all humanity. “At a time when society was plagued by social discrimination and various prejudices, Guru Nanak Dev Ji showed people the path of truth, love, equality and service to humanity. Through his teachings and conduct, he conveyed the message that God is one and all human beings are equal,” she said.“The year-long programmes (to commemorate the martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji) will culminate in a grand finale at the Red Fort from December 12 to 14. We invite the entire Guru Sangat, Sadh Sangat and the Gurdwara Management Committee to participate in the event,” she said.Nabin, who visited the Gurdwara Shri Rakabganj Sahib in New Delhi along with Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra and minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa, said, “The government is working to realise the mantra of Antyodaya by following the ideals of Guru Ji. I pray that the light of Guru Nanak Dev illuminates our lives with compassion, hard work, and selfless service.”At the same location, Delhi Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta said that Guru Nanak Dev’s vision of the welfare of all, carries a universal message that transcends religious boundaries.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, after visiting the Gurdwara Rakabganj, said in a post on X, “Today, on the auspicious occasion of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s sacred Prakash Purab, I had the good fortune to pay my respects and receive blessings at Gurdwara Sri Rakabganj Sahib. I prayed to Waheguru Ji for happiness, peace and prosperity for everyone.”

headline: Delhi govt to set up largest skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh
content: The Delhi government will set up its largest skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh, where young people will receive training in modern technologies and skills aligned with industry requirements and women will be equipped with skills to pursue employment and entrepreneurship, the chief minister’s office said on Tuesday.The centre will offer employment-oriented technical courses along the lines of Industrial Training Institute (ITI) programmes. In a statement, chief minister Rekha Gupta said, “The proposed centre in Shalimar Bagh is an important step towards fulfilling this vision. By aligning training programmes with market demand and industry requirements, the centre will prepare young people for modern workplaces.”Women, the statement further said, will have opportunities to acquire skills according to their interests, abilities and family circumstances, as well as explore avenues to start their own businesses.Gupta said that the centre is also proposed to offer flexible schedules, weekend batches and online and offline training facilities. “This will enable women who are unable to pursue training due to domestic responsibilities to upgrade their skills,” she added.An official from CMO said that Delhi has small-scale ITIs, kaushal kendra and skill centers, but no such skill development centers exist at large scale.A modern building for the centre will be constructed by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC) across approximately eight acres. Located near Desu Colony, the centre will have smart classrooms, 14 state-of-the-art laboratories and training centres, a library and learning resource centre, a multipurpose auditorium with a capacity of 250 people, and facilities for conferences and placements, among others.“Modern equipment will be made available for training in digital and IT, fashion and textiles, tailoring and handicrafts, beauty and wellness, baking and food processing, healthcare and other related fields,” said the official.The campus will further adjoin a horticulture training field spread over approximately two acres. “It will provide practical training in plant care, plant health and landscaping. Keeping in mind the needs of students coming from distant parts of Delhi and outside the city, there are also plans to develop hostel accommodation and modern sports facilities to provide trainees with a comprehensive and accessible learning environment,” the official added.To make the centre more accessible for working mothers, two crèche units, each with a capacity of 25 children, will be set up on the premises. A medical sick bay will also be established to provide first aid facilities.The academic and technical operations of the centre will be managed through the skill development centre of Dr B. R. Ambedkar University, which functions under the directorate of higher education.The training programmes will focus on industry-oriented practical skills in accordance with the standards of the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). Young people will receive training in fields such as digital services, IT support, artificial intelligence, retail and hospitality, the official said.

headline: Delhi govt kicks off technical review of duct setup for Chandni Chowk
content: The Delhi government has initiated a technical review of its proposed multi-utility duct (MUD) system for Chandni Chowk, with a committee examining the project’s feasibility, technical specifications and implementation framework at its first meeting on November 20, officials said on Tuesday.The Technical Convergence Committee (TCC), chaired by the district magistrate (Old Delhi) and Special Secretary (Power), reviewed the concept note and detailed project report (DPR) to assess the feasibility of accommodating multiple essential utilities within a common underground network.The government plans to develop underground corridors to house electricity cables, water and gas pipelines, fire-hydrant networks and other utilities at technically suitable locations. The initiative is aimed at reducing repeated road digging, minimising traffic disruptions and ensuring better coordination among agencies responsible for maintaining underground infrastructure.The project, approved by the Cabinet in August, will initially be implemented as a pilot across two stretches in Chandni Chowk — 310 metres along Esplanade Road and 560 metres along Mor Sarai Road.The November 20 meeting marked the first formal step towards advancing the project, which also seeks to shift overhead electricity wires underground while providing an organised system for other essential services. Under the proposed model, multiple utilities will share a common underground corridor, instead of agencies undertaking separate excavation and infrastructure work.The technical assessment assumes significance given the dense population, heavy commercial activity and complex network of existing utilities in Chandni Chowk, officials said. Coordinating the relocation and integration of these services will be a key challenge before the project moves to the execution stage.Following the committee’s technical assessment, the government plans to move towards awarding contracts and finalising execution timelines.“The first meeting of the Technical Convergence Committee took place on November 20. It was chaired by the District Magistrate (Old Delhi) and Special Secretary (Power). Members are reviewing the concept note and DPR for technical feasibility, specifications, and implementation,” Delhi Power minister Ashish Sood said in a statement shared by his office.Sood said shifting overhead electricity wires underground was an important part of the government’s efforts to make the city’s power infrastructure safer and cleaner. The multi-utility duct model in Chandni Chowk, he said, was intended to provide a coordinated and long-term infrastructure solution.

headline: Meet citizens on a mission to make Delhi’s roads safer, while earning rewards for it
content: Twenty-six-year-old Aftab Ahmed works at a private telecom company in north Delhi’s Roop Nagar. But for the past year, every free minute – even during his lunch breaks – armed with his mobile phone, he steps down from the office to photograph and record motorists jumping red lights, riding without helmets, driving on the wrong side and flouting other traffic rules. He then uploads the photos as evidence on Delhi Police’s Traffic Prahari app.Ahmed says he joined the app after a friend lost her life at the age of 28 in a road crash in west Delhi’s Paschim Vihar. He believes that the tragedy could have been averted had his friend, who was on a bike, been wearing a helmet. “Instead of remaining a silent witness to such dangers on Delhi’s roads, I decided to do something about it. Another friend of mine told me about the app,” said Ahmed.His efforts, aside from being a public service, have also yielded monetary benefits – till March this year, he says he has earned more than ₹2 lakh from the rewards received for reporting violations on the app.B.Tech student 21-year-old Mohammad Faizan had seen a number of accidents in his neighbourhood, northeast Delhi’s Bhajanpura, caused by wrong-way driving and riding a bike without a helmet. Faizan said he told traffic personnel deployed in the area multiple times about the violations. However, his complaints did not yield long-term results and he was often scolded by the personnel, and even locals.“In August last year, a traffic police official asked me to become a traffic crusader instead of just raising complaints about the problems in the area. My frequent reporting has resulted in a dip in traffic violations in Bhajanpura and Yamuna Vihar,” said Faizan, who has earned ₹15,000 from his time on the app.Becoming a traffic sentinelDelhi Traffic Police launched the smartphone-based app “Traffic Sentinel” in December 2015, allowing registered users to report 11 common traffic violations to the traffic police — driving against the flow of traffic, yellow line violation, parking on footpath, triple riding, defective number plate, driving without seatbelt, riding a two-wheeler without helmet, stop line violation, red light jumping, dangerous/zig zag driving, and using mobile phone while driving.The scheme was re-launched as “Traffic Prahari” on September 1, 2024.The aim, deputy commissioner of police (traffic) SK Singh said, was to empower citizens to inculcate road discipline among drivers.According to traffic police data, the app has more than a million (1,081,687) registered users as of October 31 and hundreds of challans are generated from their contributions every day.The process is relatively simple: a Traffic Prahari has to take a clear photograph or video of the vehicle involved in a traffic violation. They then have to upload it to the Prahari App, clearly mentioning the type of traffic violation being reported, date, time and place and exact location of the recorded violation, as well as the registration details of the vehicle.“Every reported violation is scrutinised by the Delhi Traffic Police personnel at the enforcement centre at traffic police’s headquarters in Todapur. If violation is found correct, then a notice and challan number is generated, otherwise violation is rejected with reason,” DCP Singh said.On their end, once traffic police receive a report, a notice under section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act is issued to the registered owner of the vehicle.“The alleged violator is provided the option to compound the offence within a stipulated time period. If the violator does not respond to the notice, a court challan is issued against the registered owner of the offending motor vehicle and sent to the court for initiating further legal proceedings under the relevant provisions of law,” said a senior officer.A traffic sentinel may be called in the court for testimony only where the offender challenges the reported traffic violation.“However, such types of cases are rare. A traffic sentinel cannot be summoned by any other authority,” the second officer added. There are no criminal or civil liabilities.A total of 2,46,842 traffic violations had been reported till October 31 this year, up from 1,18,249 last year in the same period.The rewardFor each successful report for a certain violation, the user is also awarded points. These points can be added up to earn cash prizes and commendation certificates.For instance, a wrong-side driving violation earns a user five points, while three points each is awarded for uploading a video of red-light jumping, dangerous or zig-zag driving, and using mobile phones while driving. Each Yellow line violation or parking on footpath report earns two points. One point each is given for the remaining five violations.The top four traffic sentinels who earn the most points every month get cash prizes of ₹50,000, ₹25,000, ₹15,000, and ₹10,000 depending on their position. The reward encourages public participation in policing the city’s roads and creating awareness among commuters, said additional commissioner of police (traffic) Dinesh Kumar Gupta.“I mostly focus on helmetless riding, wrong-side driving, triple riding, red light jumping and dangerous driving. I have earned more than 10,000 points on the app since I joined the initiative. The accumulated points earned me ₹2 lakh until March this year,” said Ahmed.The riskWhile the role is voluntary and the process is relatively simple, it has its own risks and threats.“A while back, a person claiming to be a Delhi Police head constable called me over a traffic challan that was generated because of the evidence I uploaded to the app. I don’t know how he found out about me. He was angry and threatened me,” recalled Ahmed, adding that the man disconnected the call after Ahmed threatened to report him to the police.A senior police officer said details of people registered as Traffic Praharis are not disclosed to anyone or anywhere. “There is a possibility that persons making the threatening calls impersonated police personnel,” added the officer.30-year-old Prince Bera, an IT consultant who lives in Uttam Nagar, said he too had faced threats and violence from commuters who spotted them recording their traffic violations, but did not share the details.People, he said, do not believe in the authority they get from the app alone since no identity cards have been issued to them. They also rarely get any assistance from police personnel when they are facing pushback in public.“Earlier public representatives were issued identity cards but they were widely misused, forcing the department to discontinue the scheme. However, any Traffic Prahari facing issues in public can approach a traffic police official or the local police for assistance,” the officer cited above said.Despite this, the sentinels continue to report violations. Atul Kumar Bhatia, 41, a corporate sales manager who joined six months ago, said he was motivated to do this by the news reports of various accidents. “Breaking traffic rules in Delhi is very common but the violators don’t realise that one bad decision can cause life-long suffering for loved ones.”

headline: All JJ Act offences to be tried by Children’s Court, irrespective of punishment: Delhi HC
content: The Delhi High Court has ruled that all offences under the Juvenile Justice (JJ) Act must be tried by the Children’s Court, irrespective of the term of imprisonment.In a judgment delivered on November 23, a bench of justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj held that the amendment to Section 86 of the JJ Act has retrospective effect, meaning the cases which took place before the amendment and are currently pending, will also be transferred to the said court.The amendment, which came into force on September 1, 2022, mandates that all offences under the JJ Act be tried exclusively by the Children’s Court, regardless of the punishment prescribed. Prior to the amendment, the jurisdiction to try such offences was determined by the term of imprisonment prescribed, with cases separately falling within the jurisdiction of the Children’s Court, a Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) or any other magistrate, depending on the nature of the offence.“By holding that Section 86(4) of the JJ Act, 2015 has a retrospective effect, meaning thereby, that even the trials which are pending before the JMFC under the unamended Act, shall be transferred to the Children’s Court by virtue of Section 86(4) of the JJ Act, 2015, post its amendment,” the court said.The ruling also has implications for the appellate process, as it would result in the state and the accused losing one tier of appeal, with challenges to the Children’s Court’s verdicts lying directly before the high court.The court delivered its verdict while adjudicating a reference made pursuant to the trial court’s order of January 24.The trial judge had sought the high court’s determination on whether the amended provision had retrospective or prospective effect and if offences under the BNS involving a minor victim would qualify as “offences against children” under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, and consequently be tried by the Children’s Court or by the court otherwise designated to try such offences under the BNS/IPC.The issue arose following the amendment to Section 86 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.The trial court judge, while making the reference, was concerned that transferring pending case s— instituted before the amendment to Section 86 of the JJ Act, 2015 and currently being adjudicated by a JMFC — to the Children’s Court could adversely affect the accused and the state’s right to a first appeal.The judge noted that under the earlier framework, an appeal against an order passed by the magistrate would lie before the sessions court. However, the appeal following the transfer of cases to children’s court would lie directly before the high court.In its 17-page verdict the court clarified that the amendment was only applicable to offences under that Act and does not extend to general offences under the BNS/IPC. “The offences under the BNS/IPC, even where one of the victims is a minor, unless otherwise provided by any other statute, is not exclusively triable only by a Children’s Court established under Section 25 of the CPCR,” the court held.

headline: Satya Niketan building collapse: Delhi court refuses bail to PG operator
content: New DelhiA Delhi court on Monday denied bail to the operator of a paying guest accommodation in south Delhi’s Satya Niketan, where a building collapse in September and left seven people dead, observing that the operator “prioritised his financial interests” over the lives and safety of the students living there.Additional sessions judge Dhirendra Rana of the Patiala House Courts, rejecting Shubham Tyagi’s bail plea, said that “he could have foreseen the danger posed by the unauthorised construction” and “should have ensured that the premises were vacated until the work was completed”.“He could have easily foreseen the danger on account of illegal construction activities but he prioritised his financial benefits above the life and safety of innocent students/labours,” the court observed.On September 6, the building where a PG accommodation under the banner of “Hostel Daze” was running collapsed due to work being undertaken in the basement. Five students and two labourers died in the incident, while five others were rescued with injuries.According to the prosecution, the building had undergone construction and structural alterations without obtaining the necessary permissions from the competent authorities. Investigators alleged that the work, which began around 10-12 days before the collapse, increased the load on the existing structure and weakened its load-bearing capacity.Tyagi and co-accused Sudhanshu Lovenish Kumar had taken the premises on rent from its owners, Urmila Gupta and her family, under a September 6, 2025, rent agreement to operate the PG. Tyagi has been in judicial custody since September 11, 2026.The court held that even if Tyagi was not directly responsible for the construction, he could not escape responsibility as the operator of the PG accommodation. “If construction work was not under his control and not on his instructions then he was duty-bound to get the property vacated from occupants till the time construction was going on,” the judge said, adding that Tyagi was also obligated to inform the residents about the potential danger.The court further noted that Tyagi, a lawyer by profession, was aware of the laws governing the operation of a PG accommodation but had failed to follow them. “The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of 7 valuable lives, are not entitled for the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” the order said.The prosecution alleged that the two operators failed to verify the building’s structural safety before renting it and did not take adequate precautions to protect residents despite the ongoing construction work.Tyagi’s counsel argued that he was merely a tenant occupying the second and third floors of the building and had no authority under the rent agreement to undertake structural modifications. He also contended that the investigation was complete, the charge sheet filed and his continued custody was unnecessary.Rejecting the argument, the court said his occupation and control of the premises placed an obligation on him to ensure the safety of the students.

headline: Delhiwale: To the ends of the earth
content: It could be our clothes, our balcony. It all feels like home. A pink sweatshirt is hanging upside down above the red Honda sign. Its sleeves dangling below the balcony railing. There’s washing out on another balcony, too. A safed tauliya is hanging above a sign for the Guru Jolly Institute of Astrology, which promises a solution to every problem.Actually, you see the shop signs first. Then you begin to notice the homes above them.The pink sweatshirt, for instance, is visible from right inside Krishna Park Extension metro station, through the glass beside the escalators at Gate No. 2–see photo. The Magenta Line ends here, in west Delhi. This is the third in our series on the last points of the Delhi Metro’s lines, and on what lies outside them.On the other side of the station, a narrow pavement runs between the glass wall and the traffic on the main road. A giant billboard dwarfs the scene. It offers 3 BHK homes starting from 3.52 crore rupees. A bird is perched atop the billboard.Now a bus pulls up outside the Metro station. The door opens. On the roadside, a scrap collector is sitting on his white sack, facing the open door. He makes no move towards the bus. He talks eagerly. He has been picking things up off the streets since early morning, he says. Now he is tired, so he is resting on his sack. He says he has no home. Then he turns to look at the station. He says he has never seen the inside of a Metro train.On a grey wall, a pink poster bears the words Dukh Nivaran Ashram. A place to give relief from sorrow. The poster says the ashram looks after people who have no one to look after them.The board at the Metro exit points to Guru Nanak Nagar. A few steps inside is a little grocery. It is clear that some of the residents here have come from foreign lands and made their home here. This shop is where they can pick up familiar things to eat. For in big yellow letters above the grocery’s door are two words. African Shop. In a way, the last stop of the Magenta Line is touching another continent.

headline: Delhi court seeks police report on complaint against influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj
content: New DelhiA Delhi court on Monday sought an action-taken report from the city police regarding a criminal complaint filed against self-styled influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj, accusing him of repeatedly circulating objectionable social media content targeting a particular religious community and their religious practices.Judicial magistrate Kautuk Bhardwaj of the Patiala House Courts, seeking the report from the Parliament Street police station, scheduled the next hearing for January 8, 2027.The complaint, filed by Mohd Shahid Gangohi, alleged that Bhardwaj had published and circulated posts, videos and comments on various social media platforms containing insulting references to Muslims and their religious practices. The complaint also objected to the alleged creation and circulation of vulgar, AI-generated images.The complainant claimed that such content had the potential to promote communal hatred, foster hostility between communities and disturb public peace and communal harmony.Advocate Feroz Khan Ghazi, appearing for the complainant, submitted that all available avenues to bring the alleged content to the police’s notice had been exhausted, leaving the complainant with no option but to approach the court.To be sure, Bhardwaj was arrested by Delhi Police on September 5 in a separate case relating to the alleged assault on the father of a teenage Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist during a protest at Jantar Mantar in July. The case drew attention after a video podcast surfaced in which Bhardwaj purportedly claimed to have attacked the protester’s father and boasted about causing him serious injuries. The FIR was initially registered under BNS provisions relating to causing hurt and wrongful restraint. Provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act were subsequently added after the complainant alleged caste-based insults.A separate FIR was also registered under provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and criminal intimidation following allegations that the teenage protester had received rape threats from Bhardwaj’s supporters.The court granted him regular bail on October 6 after noting that he had not violated the conditions imposed while granting interim relief.

headline: Aeravti Ventures launches ₹300 cr second fund, secures 50% at first close
content: Bengaluru-based venture capital firm Aeravti Ventures has launched its second fund, Aeravti Ventures II, with a target corpus of ₹300 crore. The Sebi-registered Category II alternative investment fund (AIF) has secured commitments for nearly 50 per cent of its target corpus at the first close, with the final close expected within the next six months. Fund II will focus on three core investment themes — food security, health infrastructure and physical security. The investments will span opportunities across agriculture and allied sectors, biosciences, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, waste management and energy. “As India continues to evolve, some of its most significant opportunities will emerge from businesses solving foundational challenges across food systems, healthcare and physical infrastructure. With Fund II, we want to back founders addressing these gaps early and help build businesses that can create lasting value for the Indian economy,” said Rishabh Singh, managing partner at Aeravti Ventures. Aeravti Ventures II plans to invest in around 9-10 startups across India, spanning pre-seed to pre-Series A stages, with a preference for leading pre-seed and seed rounds. The fund expects to write initial cheques of ₹6-10 crore per company and has the capacity to invest two to three times the initial amount in subsequent funding rounds. Shubham Jhuria, partner and chief financial officer at Aeravti Ventures, said participation from several existing investors reflected the relationships and conviction built through the firm's first fund. “With Fund II, we are building on that foundation with a more focused investment strategy, a stronger team and the ability to support our portfolio companies through follow-on investments as they scale,” he said. Aeravti's first fund achieved a final close of ₹76 crore and has been fully deployed across seven companies. The firm led the seed round in each of those companies. A few portfolio companies have subsequently raised follow-on funding, while three are currently profitable, according to Aeravti. Among portfolio milestones, Origin Fresh has scaled monthly revenue fourfold while remaining profitable. ONO expanded its lending footprint ahead of acquiring an NBFC licence, while East Ocyon has received positive feedback in its pre-clinical trials. The venture capital firm is also strengthening its investment team with the addition of senior members, including Anam Ajani and Aditya Siroya.

headline: Suvendu Promises Prime-Time Slots For Bengali Films, Construction Of Theatres To Promote Regional Cinema
content: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has directed cinema halls across the state to screen Bengali films during prime-time slots. The move aims to promote Bengali cinema, expand its audience reach, and strengthen the state’s cinema infrastructure. This directive was issued by the chief minister during a meeting with cinema hall owners and film producers. The meeting came following reports that the Bengali film ‘Sadhan Bamakhyapa’, based on the life of a Tantrik, had been dropped from several cinema halls to make way for Bollywood actor Salman Khan’s latest release. The decisions also include compulsory prime-time screening of Bengali films, construction of new theatres at 51 locations and conversion of 70 old halls into cinema halls, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA said, according to ANI. Speaking to the outlet, BJP MLA Rudranil Ghosh expressed confidence that the the decision would help preserved the dignity of regional Bengali culture. “Everyone thanked Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari today because for many years, there was only talk of prioritising Bengali films, but nothing had been done. Today, a decision was made regarding Bengali films: to preserve the dignity of regional Bengali culture, one Bengali film will have to be shown during prime time no matter what”, Ghosh said. He also pointed out to a sharp decline in the number of cinema halls in the state. “Care will be taken to ensure that Bengali films are not suddenly removed. Most importantly, new theatres will be built at 51 locations. 70 old halls will also be converted into cinema halls. There used to be 800 cinema halls in Bengal at one time; today, their number has dwindled to just around 100”, he said. BJP MLA and actor Rupa Ganguly told ANI that several long-standing issues concerning cinema halls were being addressed during the meeting with financial approvals granted for many halls. “There were many problems, and many of those problems are being resolved. Financial approval for many halls has also been given. The issue regarding the prime-time slot has also been addressed and solved. Now, Bengali films will be shown in the prime time slot,” Ganguly said.

headline: CM to open ‘Vision Koyilandy Conclave 2026’ on Nov. 27
content: KOZHIKODE Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will open ‘Vision Koyilandy Conclave 2026’, an event to chalk out future development plans for the Koyilandy Assembly constituency in Kozhikode district, on November 27. Koyilandy MLA and Kozhikode District Congress Committee president K. Praveenkumar told the media on Tuesday (November 24) that the event would be held at the Koyilandy stadium. He said that the aim was to conceive projects in sectors such as education, health, transport, agriculture, industry, tourism, and infrastructure development. Experts in various fields would discuss their ideas at the conclave. “We want to prepare a development plan for the constituency for 2040. A development blueprint will be prepared based on the suggestions raised at the conclave within a month after the event,” Mr. Praveenkumar said. A two-day exhibition showcasing the various development projects being taken up in the constituency would begin on Wednesday (November 25). Kerala Sahitya Akademi chairperson Kalpetta Narayanan would open the exhibition. Apart from the Chief Minister, Ministers such as N. Samsudheen, A.P. Anil Kumar, V.E. Abdul Gafoor, and T. Siddique, and Shafi Parambil and P.T. Usha, MPs, would attend the conclave along with elected representatives from municipalities, grama panchayats, district panchayats, and block panchayats, Mr. Praveenkumar said. Chairpersons of Payyoli and Koyilandy municipalities and grama panchayat presidents in the constituency were present at the press meet. Meanwhile, the Koyilandy MLA claimed that the United Democratic Front-led government had sanctioned at least 16 projects for the constituency in the past six months. Preliminary works have already begun. Apart from them, a proposal had been given to develop a mini cruise terminal at Kolavipalam. Asked about the poor condition of roads leading to Kappad, a historically important place in the constituency, Mr. Praveenkumar said that a project had been prepared to construct a breakwater between Kannankadavu and Kolavipalam. It would address the issue of roads getting damaged in the monsoon season, he added.

headline: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Saudi capital
content: Dubai Two Indians were among those injured in an attack on a financial district in Riyadh that triggered strong condemnation from New Delhi. India also denounced continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26 Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26 Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26 storyline 1 “Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said. The attack was carried out on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). Local authorities said the injured included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese and four Egyptian nationals. The MEA said India strongly condemns the attack in Riyadh as well as the continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. “These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks,” it said in a statement. India also reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed its unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity. “We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest,” the MEA said. There has been a sudden escalation in tensions in West Asia, especially after the Houthis carried out several strikes on Saudi Arabia. The West Asia conflict began in February following attacks on Iran by the U.S. and Israel. New Delhi has consistently called for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. India has been specifically voicing serious concern over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian infrastructure and economic assets, cautioning that such strikes undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
