headline: Nepal PM Balen Shah's India Visit Marks New Chapter In Ties, Says Brother-In-Law
content: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's maiden visit to India since assuming office was more than a diplomatic milestone for his family. It was an emotional moment and, according to his brother-in-law Harish Kumar Sejekan, the beginning of a potentially transformative chapter in India-Nepal relations. Speaking exclusively to NDTV Foreign Affairs Editor Aditya Raj Kaul after the two-day visit, Sejekan described the welcome extended to Balen Shah by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, including the ceremonial guard of honour and the warmth shared by the two leaders, as deeply moving. Recalling watching the visuals with his wife, Sejekan said the family was overwhelmed with emotion. "We had tears in our eyes," he told NDTV, reflecting on the journey of a young man who went from nurturing political ambitions to becoming Kathmandu's mayor and eventually Nepal's Prime Minister. Sejekan said Balen Shah's rise was particularly remarkable because he had neither an established political dynasty nor traditional political backing. His ascent, he said, was driven by hard work, conviction and a direct connection with ordinary Nepalis. The visit comes against the backdrop of Nepal's Gen Z-led political upheaval, which reflected widespread public frustration with corruption, established political parties and governance failures. Balen Shah emerged as a symbol of political change, carrying the expectations of a generation demanding accountability and effective leadership.

headline: CIA hit by cyberattack amid string of US government system disruptions: Report
content: An unclassified Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) system used to handle open-source intelligence was breached in a cyberattack, but no classified information was compromised, and the issue has since been resolved, The Associated Press reported citing sources familiar with the incident. The breach came to light on Tuesday, amid a series of recent technical failures and suspected cyber incidents affecting key US government agencies and major companies.The affected system handled open-source intelligence, the report said, citing an anonymous source. The person was not authorised to speak publicly about the matter.What was affectedThe compromised system was used to collect and analyse publicly available information. This includes data from the internet, commercial satellites and private data brokers.Although such information is generally public or semi-public, it can provide intelligence analysts with significant insights. Analysts can also combine it with information gathered through classified intelligence operations to build a more detailed picture.It was not immediately clear what specific information was compromised or who was responsible for the breach.The New York Times first reported the incident on Tuesday.CIA breach follows series of US system disruptionsThe incident comes after several technical failures and suspected cyber incidents raised concerns about the security of US government systems and critical infrastructure.An internal network used by the National Security Agency (NSA) to communicate classified information was offline for some time last week. The FBI is also investigating an apparent breach of a national law enforcement database maintained by the agency.These incidents followed a nationwide ground stop that disrupted air travel after air traffic controllers struggled to communicate with pilots.Several major companies, including Apple, JPMorgan Chase and Microsoft, also experienced system outages this month.The disruptions have raised questions about vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure, banking systems and digital services used by millions of people.Trump administration denies coordinated cyberattackThe Donald Trump administration has said the recent outages were not part of a coordinated cyberattack.Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton appeared on Sunday morning news programmes to reassure Americans following the disruptions.Clayton said the outages were largely linked to efforts to patch and upgrade systems to stay ahead of hackers. He warned that hackers now have access to sophisticated artificial intelligence tools, allowing them to carry out attacks on an unprecedented scale.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

headline: Old friends, but new political ground: SAD-BJP alliance faces tougher road this time
content: There was a sense of déjà vu as Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the Akali Dal-BJP alliance on Tuesday. Late five-time CM Parkash Singh Badal had famously described it as a “nau-maas da rishta”, a bond that he saw as a guarantor of communal peace in the state. While the partners may see the reunion as a winning proposition, replicating their past success of forming three governments together, beginning in 1997, will require hard work. The alliance has been out of power since 2017. Punjab presents a tough electoral battlefield as it heads to the polls early next year. The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is fighting a make-or-break battle as it seeks another term on the strength of its welfare record, while a resurgent Congress appears to have finally got its warring leaders to close ranks. While Shah has reassigned the title of “big brother” to the Akalis, saying that the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) would play the senior partner’s role and that the Chief Minister would be from the party, the BJP is unlikely to be content with playing second fiddle as it did in the past. The BJP nearly doubled its vote share to 18.56% in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, giving it a lead of over five percentage points over the Akalis, who polled 13.42%. Over the past six years, the BJP has tried hard to reinvent itself in Punjab. It has inducted several Jat Sikh leaders, many of them from the Congress, and sought to shed its earlier image of a party largely identified with Hindu traders. It has also made a sustained pitch for Dalit votes. Dalits account for over 32% of Punjab’s population, according to the 2011 Census. The Prime Minister’s visit to Dera Ballan, where he sought the blessings of its chief, Sant Niranjan Das, and the launch of a yatra earlier this week to mark the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Ravidas underline the importance the BJP is attaching to this constituency. The Akalis, meanwhile, are working hard to regain lost ground. There are some signs of revival, with veterans such as Prem Singh Chandumajra and former Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) chief Bibi Jagir Kaur returning to the party fold. The anger in the countryside against the now-repealed farm laws also appears to have abated, with two farmer organisations recently aligning with the Akalis. However, the emergence of the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), led by Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh, and the Akali Dal (Punar Surjit), under former acting Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Harpreet Singh, poses a challenge to the SAD’s claim over Panthic votes. Amritpal’s return to the state on three-hour custodial parole to attend his grandmother’s cremation demonstrated his support among sections of the youth and the Panthic constituency. The BJP, which has brought in not just Congress leaders but also their political ambitions, is unlikely to settle for the 23 seats it contested in the past. A new Punjab The political ground in Punjab has shifted after five years of AAP rule. The border state was among the first to embrace this “new” party in 2022. The Arvind Kejriwal-led party may not have transformed Punjab as it had promised, but it has taken welfare measures to a new high. Nearly 90% of households receive 300 units of free electricity every month. For the first time in the state’s history, eligible women have also begun receiving monthly financial assistance under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana, launched in July. Now it is going to the polls with a balance sheet of tangible measures instead of mere promises. While the war on drugs and corruption is the main plank of the revived alliance, voters are unlikely to be swayed by rhetoric alone this time. The Opposition has consistently blamed the alliance, the Akali Dal in particular, for the drug menace in the state. In 2017, Bhagwant Mann, then an AAP MP and now Chief Minister, made the anti-drug campaign deeply personal, targeting the Badal family with his popular ditty "Kikli". The alliance's biggest challenge is to convince voters that it has a workable remedy for the state's ills, many of which the Opposition lays at its door. And a mere manifesto will not do. It will have to walk the talk.

headline: Tamil Nadu runs Supreme Court contempt risk: Lamp lit, but not at pillar on Madurai hill
content: Hours after it assured the Madras High Court that it would comply with the Supreme Court order, the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday left the deepathoon, the contested stone pillar atop Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, unlit on the Karthigai Deepam festival. On November 20, the top court, in an interim order, had permitted lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the stone pillar on the hilltop as a one-time arrangement. By 6 pm, the festival flame burned at its customary place near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple at the foothill, not on the pillar atop the hill. Caught between the court and allies who keep him in office, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay chose his allies, and the risk of contempt. Earlier in the day, the Madurai bench of the Madras High Court held an urgent hearing to ensure compliance of the Supreme Court order. District Collector Nishant Krishna, who was appointed by the SC as the nodal officer to ensure lighting of the deepathoon, made a personal appearance and assured that the SC order will be given effect. “We deem it necessary to remind the District Collector that he is a public servant who is answerable only to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in this case. He shall ignore any contra advice given by any other authority. We are sure that no law officer worth his salt will counsel him to act in contravention of the order…” the High Court noted in its order. The High Court also recorded senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan’s submission that he was “on instructions from the state officials” to clarify “that the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court would be complied with,” and that there was no need for the HC to entertain these writ petitions. For Vijay, whose TVK fell short of a majority in its first Assembly election, the question was how much political risk he could afford for a ceremony the court had authorised for one evening. The IUML, the VCK, the CPI, the CPI(M) and the Congress had taken a firm stand against lighting a second lamp at the contested site. Their support is crucial to his government. The Left parties had urged him to preserve the existing practice. VCK minister Vanni Arasu had publicly taken much the same position. Karthigai Deepam is an evening when families across Tamil Nadu light rows of lamps outside their homes. At Thirupparankundram, the day began with a temple car procession. Later, a copper cauldron, a cotton wick and ghee went up the hill under police escort. About 6,000 police personnel had been deployed across Madurai and around the hill. Even the airspace was accounted for – police had banned drones. At the foot of the hill stands the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple, one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan. Near the summit is the Sikandar Badusha Dargah, a Muslim shrine. The stone pillar stands about 50 metres from the dargah. Hindu organisations have long sought an additional flame there. That distinction matters in a town where, three decades ago, four temple priests put in writing what they understood the tradition to be. The annual lamp, they said, had been lit at Uchi Pillaiyar for as long as anyone could remember. On November 20, Supreme Court Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi stayed the findings of a January 6 Madras High Court judgment, but directed the authorities to permit a small team authorised by the temple to light the pillar lamp this year. The public could not accompany it. The arrangement settled neither ownership of the site nor any customary right to worship there. The Madurai Collector was to report on compliance within three days of the festival. #WATCH | Thiruparankundram, Tamil Nadu | Police deployment at the Deepathoon stone pillar, where the Supreme Court had given an interim order to light the lamp today at 6 pm. At a distance from it is located the Ucchi Pillayar Temple, where the Maha Deepam has been lit as part of the annual Karthigai Deepam festival. Visuals from Annamalai Hills in Thiruparankundram where both locations are. — ANI (@ANI) November 24, 2026 The state's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Commissioner sought a review on Sunday. The petition turned on a practical difficulty with a one-time ritual. Once performed, the state argued, it could never again be said that it had never taken place. The festival arrived before the state could secure a hearing and a stay. Vijay's predecessor, M K Stalin, had faced much the same decision last December and personally instructed his administration to hold its position despite the risk of contempt. After officials failed to carry out Justice G R Swaminathan's order to light the pillar lamp, the judge authorised petitioners to go up with a Central Industrial Security Force escort. Police blocked access. Protesters and police clashed, and the DMK government faced contempt proceedings. A division bench subsequently upheld the direction to light the lamp, setting the stage for the state’s appeal. On Tuesday, some of the policing took place a considerable distance from Madurai. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran had been on the road for 40 minutes when police detained him at Thatchanallur, on the outskirts of Tirunelveli, at 3:15 pm. Former Union minister L Murugan was stopped at Annur in Coimbatore district. He asked how a prohibitory order issued in Madurai had come to apply to him in Coimbatore. Shortly after 6 pm, CTR Nirmal Kumar, the state's law minister and Thirupparankundram's MLA, announced that the flame had been lit at the traditional spot. At the foothills, police removed devotees protesting over the unlit pillar. Five days before the festival, the death of Kolathur MLA V S Babu left Vijay's TVK with 108 seats in an Assembly with 228 sitting members, seven short of a majority on its own. The Congress holds five seats, while the IUML, the VCK, the CPI and the CPI(M) hold two MLAs each. Together, those 13 MLAs take the government's tally to 121.

headline: Food meets art, books greet readers at Iranian Mehfil Cafe, once a library storage
content: Through the glass window, the ceramics are a little blurry, but the colours catch the eye. Behind it, a group of people sit at a table. The books on the shelves behind them are stocked in order, and the lights on the ceiling reflect on the paintings. At Irani Mehfil Cafe, there are white concentric circles on the ceiling. A vivid ring of green traces the outer edge, while another illuminated red circle sits at the core. Separated by the white plaster of the inner rings, the colours of the Iranian flag glow above the tables. “In Iran, everything is artistic,” says the owner and founder of the cafe, Mehdi Shirmohammadi, and this ceiling and the decor of the cafe are proof. Six tables are widely spread, enough to navigate through the space comfortably. A hot Persian herbal saffron tea sits on the table occupied by two young men with its wispy steam condensing on the glass pot. The cafe is located at the Iran Culture House, inside the cultural wing of the Embassy. Close to the India Gate, the Supreme Court, and the Delhi College of Art, it witnesses a steady stream of tourists, lawyers, students, and government officials. The space is small and intimate. The chef, Viketou, stands at the kitchen counter, making a cheesy chicken burger. “We get orders for a lot of continental dishes. Among the Iranian items, the herbal teas are the most ordered. The Iranian falafel as well,” he says, adding that Sholeh Zard, which is only available on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, is the most favourite dessert. Sholeh Zard is one of Iran’s most iconic saffron rice puddings, with a silky texture. There are still limited Iranian dishes on the menu. Continental dishes were added on the request of customers who frequent the cafe. “I want to expand the cafe and introduce a lot more Iranian dishes. But for that, we need a proper kitchen as the cuisine’s preparation time is quite long,” says Shirmohammadi. With roughly 600 books lining the shelves and a small archive of rarer volumes, the cafe opened about 14 months ago. Before this, the room held only books. It was a book storage, a part of a much larger library that was run inside the Iran Culture House. It was a closed space, and one requires permission to enter. About two years ago, Dr Fariduddin Faridasr, the Cultural Counsellor for the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India and Head of the Iran Culture House in New Delhi, was looking for a way to introduce people to Iranian culture. Shirmohammadi, who had come to India to start a dry fruit business, was pulled into the conversation. He had two plans, but was too busy with his own business to execute those. But there was no one who could work on the plans. Two months later, Shirmohammadi was ready to invest. But he had a condition: the cafe should be open to the public and the security policies should be changed. What was once a sealed storage space became Irani Mehfil — a place where people can read and buy books, and eat. Shirmohammadi holds a PhD in economics, and his family runs a dry fruit business — a popular trade in Iran. He came to India to start his own brand, Shiro, and built packaging and cold storage facilities for it. He also runs a travel agency. But the cafe allowed him to bring a different side of his culture to the city. “Mehfil,” Shirmohammadi says, “in Farsi, means a place for a warm gathering.” He aims at dispelling the propaganda built around his country, “Iran, like India, is a big country with different religions, different cultures, different languages. The North of Iran is a lush, green region filled with rice farms, while the Northwest is a cold, mountainous region where temperatures drop down to -26°C,” he says, sitting at the cafe with a blueberry shake. The war and sanctions in his country, however, have weighed heavily on his life and business. A direct flight from Delhi to Tehran no longer exists, forcing him to travel through Moscow with an 11-hour layover just to see his family. Importing and exporting goods, on which his dry fruits business relies, is now a hassle. When the war began, instead of fleeing, the Iranian diaspora — including Shirmohammadi and his wife — tried desperately to find a way back. “When the war started, all of us wanted to go back to Iran,” he says. “Our parents are there … All of our people are our family.” For him, the political divisions fade when the country is under attack. “If you ask any Iranian, we die for our country,” he says. “Iran is our main brand.” Irani Mehfil Cafe also plans to host storytelling events that explore Iran’s diverse culture — highlighting distinct foods, architecture, clothing, and agricultural traditions across regions. “We will also be looking at putting some Iranian handicrafts for sale,” Shirmohammadi adds. While currently, rugs collected by Shirmohammadi hang above the bookshelves — some draped from the ceiling like tents — the walls are lined with framed Persian calligraphy. Inside glass cabinets, turquoise-inlay plates and brightly coloured vases catch the light. A favourite of Shirmohammadi is a half-silk rug painted by Mahmoud Farshchian, an artist whose works are considered a pinnacle of Persian art. There is also a heavy, richly illustrated book of Farshchian’s paintings. Many books in Farsi also occupy the shelves. The Culture House holds weekend Farsi classes, and students from Delhi University and Jamia who attend often come looking for Persian books.

headline: After 5-month gap, Arvind Kejriwal returns to Punjab rally stage
content: After a five-month hiatus from Punjab’s major public rallies, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener Arvind Kejriwal will return to the state on November 26, with his address at ‘Khushhaal Punjab Rally’ expected to signal the start of the campaign for the upcoming Assembly elections.The event, being organised on AAP’s 14th foundation day, has been designated as a state-level government function, as the state government will also launch its smart ration card initiative on the occasion.Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and other senior party leaders will share the stage with Kejriwal at the gathering.The party is likely to use the platform to showcase the Bhagwant Mann government’s performance, highlight its welfare initiatives and outline its political roadmap for the elections. Kejriwal and Mann are also expected to send a strong message to Opposition parties that AAP has stepped up its preparations for the Assembly polls.AAP has already named 71 candidates for Punjab’s 117 Assembly constituencies. The Moga rally is expected to provide further momentum to the exercise. Kejriwal had last addressed a major public gathering in Punjab in Amritsar during the ‘Ek Shaam Bhagwan Shiv Ke Naam’ programme on June 27.His absence from the state’s major political rallies over the past five months had drawn attention. AAP spokesperson Neel Garg, however, said Kejriwal had been occupied with political engagements in other states, including Gujarat and Goa, and would now join the Punjab leadership at the Moga rally.Notably, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) has also announced a massive rally to mark the birth anniversary of former Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in Moga on December 8, which is likely to be attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Elaborate arrangements are being made for the AAP’s November 26 rally, with a massive venue spread across nearly 116 acres at Matwani village on the Moga-Ludhiana highway in Moga district being readied.The organisers are expecting a gathering of over one lakh people, with AAP leaders mobilising workers and supporters from across the state.A large ‘pandal’, stage, seating arrangements, drinking water, food, toilets and other basic facilities are being put in place. Separate parking arrangements are being made for vehicles to arrive from different directions. A number of ministers and senior party leaders have been regularly visiting the rally venue to take stock of the preparations.Besides, constituency in-charges and MLAs have been asked ensure participation in the rally, with each unit arranging at least 25 buses.

headline: Zero e-auto and 37 goods carrier applications: Why is Delhi’s EV push stuck?
content: Nearly five months after Delhi's ambitious Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 came into effect, there is little interest in availing subsidies to buy electric auto-rickshaws and goods vehicles, which are meant to replace some of the city's most polluting vehicles. Under the policy, from January 1, 2027, only electric auto-rickshaws can be registered in the city. With just about a month left before that deadline, no applications have been received for the purchase incentive for electric autos, government data show. Just 37 applications have come in for electric goods carriers. There are virtually no takers for the government’s scrapping incentives either. No one has applied for the Rs 25,000 incentive for junking a conventional-fuel three-wheeler. A single application has been received for the Rs 50,000 incentive for scrapping goods carriers. The buying and scrapping incentives were meant to push fossil fuel-run autos and LCVs off Delhi’s streets and gradually replace them with EVs. Autos and light goods vehicles stay on the road for longer, logging a high mileage every day, and have a disproportionately higher contribution to Delhi’s urban air pollution, says the EV Policy 2026. “Accordingly, prioritised electrification of these vehicle segments is essential to achieve sustained improvements in air quality,” it says. The contrast with two-wheelers is stark. The purchase incentive for electric two-wheelers has drawn 12,584 applications so far, according to government data. The Rs 10,000 incentive for scrapping an old two-wheeler has seen lower interest – only 237 applications so far. Two-wheelers are more than two-thirds of the total vehicle stock in Delhi. The transport sector is the biggest contributor to the city’s air pollution load. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has told the Supreme Court that vehicular emissions make up 23% of Delhi’s winter air pollution. Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh said the data on subsidies suggest there is interest in electric commercial vehicles. “The cost of electric versions of these vehicles is very high. But even then, people have started showing interest. As soon as the charging infrastructure ramps up, uptake will rise much faster,” Singh told The Indian Express. The response to the subsidies for commercial vehicles is poor even though the government’s offer is currently the best. To encourage early adoption, the policy offered the biggest benefits in its first year. The current Rs 50,000-subsidy for buying an EV auto will come down to Rs 40,000 in the second year, and Rs 30,000 in the third year. For electric goods vehicles, the incentive in the first year is up to Rs 1 lakh, which will come down in later years. Scrapping incentives are paid only if a new EV is bought within six months of scrapping the old vehicle. Reasons behind low uptake Industry executives said a key reason for the low uptake is technical issues at the backend of the Delhi EV portal. To qualify for the subsidy, electric goods carriers – which fall in the ‘N1’ category of light four-wheeler goods vehicles, must meet localisation requirements adopted from the Centre’s EV schemes. Major components of the EV model have to be made or assembled in India. “The Delhi EV Policy portal is not showing some models which are certified under the central schemes. Customers have come to us complaining about their applications not being eligible, so we are now in touch with the government,” a senior executive at an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) said. Sources in the government said, however, that there are few options in the market that meet localisation requirements. Transport operators pointed to the high cost of buying and maintaining EVs, and the inadequate charging infrastructure as reasons to hold back. Even the subsidy does not appear that attractive to transporters. “These vehicles are too expensive, and they are not widely used. If I can sell my old vehicle in the market at a better price, why would I choose to scrap it?” Shyam Sundar, general secretary of the Delhi NCR Transport Ekta Manch, said. For auto-rickshaw drivers, the main concerns are charging time and the lack of charging points, apart from the fact that the Rs 50,000 purchase incentive does not seem enough to go for a switch. “It takes 5-10 minutes to fill a CNG auto. How long will charging take? There is no charging infrastructure. EVs are more expensive to maintain. The subsidy should have been at least Rs 1.5 lakh,” said Rajender Soni, general secretary of the Delhi Auto Rickshaw Sangh.

headline: ‘Family church’ vandalised, Odisha man approaches police. Next day, excavator shows up
content: On November 21, Durjan Harijan of Odisha's Koraput district approached the police against a group of youths for allegedly vandalising a church near his house in Patraguda village. The church, he said, was built by him for the family – the only Christian household in a predominantly tribal village of 900 under Kotpad tehsil. The land belonged to his father, he claimed. Police registered a case against the group of tribal youths who were allegedly behind the vandalism. However, a day later, the structure was brought down in the presence of local authorities and police. While officials said Durjan voluntarily undertook the demolition since the church was built on government land, the villager said he was forced into razing the structure. Durjan, who converted to Christianity around a decade ago, built the church-cum-prayer hall next to his house three years ago, where he held worship services every Sunday. There are seven members in his family who frequented the church. Speaking to The Indian Express, Durjan said a group of youths from the same village suddenly entered the church premises on Saturday and started the vandalism, following which he approached the police. Based on his complaint, the Kotpad police lodged an FIR against seven persons of the village under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including mischief, obscene acts and songs near public places, and common intention. “Some villagers had started visiting the church over the past few months. Hence, the villagers accused us of converting people to Christianity, which is not true. They abused me and my family before vandalising the church,” Durjan said. He said the local authorities and police visited the site the following day and the church was demolished in their presence. Even though he claimed the Pentecostal Beersaheba Church was built on land belonging to his father, officials said it was constructed on government land, without the requisite permission. The officials admitted that the villagers, too, were opposing the presence of the church and had urged the authorities to demolish it. “Following reports of vandalism at the church and the subsequent police FIR, we visited the village and held the peace meeting. As the villagers alleged that the church was built on government land, we issued a show-cause notice to the person concerned asking why the structure wouldn’t be demolished,” Kotpad tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra told The Indian Express. He said after getting the show cause notice, the “person concerned” demolished the structure. When contacted, inspector-in-charge of Kotpad police station Runu Majhi also stated that the structure was demolished by Durjan. To queries whether police have made any arrest on the complaint of Durjan, Majhi said the matter is still under investigation. Responding to the officials’ claims, Durjan alleged that he had been pressured into arranging an excavator to demolish the structure. He said he is now seeking legal opinion to take the matter to the court.

headline: ‘Papa’s security removed on purpose to get him killed,’ says Rahul Gandhi
content: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi has said that the removal of the security cover of his father and former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was not an “accident and that it was removed on purpose so that he got killed”. Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by an LTTE suicide bomber during a campaign trail in Sriperumbudur near Chennai on May 21, 1991, sending shockwaves across the world. Indira Gandhi, Rajiv’s mother, had been gunned down by her own bodyguards at her residence just seven years earlier in 1984. During an interaction with his mother and CPP chairperson Sonia Gandhi, days after the launch of her memoir ‘Belonging: A journey of love’, along with his sister and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said an atmosphere was created for the former PM to get killed. A video of their reminiscences was shared by them on social media platforms Tuesday. “Papa’s security was removed so that he got killed. Papa’s security removal was not just an accident; it was done on purpose so that he got killed. And the atmosphere was created for him to get killed. It was obvious what was going on,” said Rahul Gandhi. Sonia Gandhi recalled the security threats her husband Rajiv Gandhi faced after losing power in the 1989 elections. The then V P Singh government withdrew Rajiv Gandhi’s SPG cover. “Rahul had come back and just so happened that my husband was going on a tour. This particular one to Bihar. During the trip in Bihar, Rajiv ji was the Leader of the Opposition. First of all, they were in an open jeep, and there were stones, rocks thrown at them,” said Sonia Gandhi. “And what happens if you don’t have security, proper security, and if you go to a state where the government is of the BJP or Opposition, then by and large whoever is in charge there, they will not be particular about the security. They say ‘haan aa raha hai, theek hai’, do your normal thing,” Sonia Gandhi is heard saying in the video. If the government is of BJP or any other rival party, they are not going to give special attention to security, she said. “So it was quite a horrible tour. Rahul was with his father throughout and he witnessed the rocks being thrown and all the shouting and screaming against his father. And when he came home he told me, ‘Mama, if we don’t do something about Papa’s security, I know I am going to come back for his funeral very soon’,” she said. Rahul then talks about how the Bihar trip was the “final straw”. “The Bihar trip was the final straw but I was saying it from before. And my position on it was very clear. I told my father also. I told my mum also. I had an argument with my father about it,” he said. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra then points out how after Indira Gandhi’s assassination, her mother had become paranoid about “Papa’s security” and would go around “checking the barbed wires” and whether the guards were sleeping. “I knew as my room was in the front of the house,” said Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, adding that she would not sleep until she heard her father’s footsteps. “Rahul’s deductions” about the father’s security situation were logical, she said, while her own response was “completely emotional”.

headline: ‘Wadde’ Badal’s 99th birth ann rally: As SAD returns to its ‘lucky charm’, why Moga matters in Punjab’s politics
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend an event in Moga on December 8 to mark the 99th birth anniversary of former Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal said Tuesday, soon after his party and the BJP restitched their alliance in the run up to the 2027 Assembly elections. “Wadde Badal saab and Modi ji shared a beautiful bond. Modi saab has expressed his wish to attend the huge gathering we are organising in Moga on December 8, Wadde Badal saab's birth anniversary,” Sukhbir said at a joint press conference in Delhi. For the SAD, which has been out of power in Punjab since 2017, Moga has long been a preferred venue for launching election campaigns and holding major political rallies, particularly on Badal's birthday and the party's foundation day on December 14. The Moga “charm” worked for the party, especially in 1997, 2007 and 2012 Assembly elections, though its rallies failed to translate into electoral victories in 2017 and 2022. The choice of Moga is significant as this time, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), is also set to kickstart its election campaign from the district with party's national convenor Arvind Kejriwal set to address a 'Khushaal Punjab' rally on November 26, the party's 14th foundation day. While the SAD's rally will be held at the Anaj Mandi in Moga, the AAP event is scheduled at the border of Matwani and Nathuwala Jadid villages. Neither party has chosen village Killi Chahlan, traditionally a favourite venue for major political gatherings in the district. Moga has already hosted two major political rallies this year. On February 16, the AAP held a massive anti-drug rally at Killi Chahlan, followed by the BJP's 'Badlav Rally' on March 14, addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. At the latter, Shah announced that the BJP would contest the 2027 Assembly elections on its own and promised an anti-conversion law and a drug-free Punjab by 2029. Why Moga matters The preference for Moga cuts across party lines, with the SAD, Congress, AAP and BJP all using the district to mobilise workers and launch political campaigns. Its central location makes it accessible to party workers from all three regions of Punjab — Majha, Malwa and Doaba. The district is also a hub of farm activism and farmer union activities. “Moga is the heart of Punjab. It is convenient to travel from all districts in less time. The prime reason to choose Moga is the location,” said veteran Akali leader Prem Singh Chandumajra. Another Akali leader and former minister Sikander Singh Maluka, meanwhile, said, “Moga has always been lucky for the SAD-BJP”. Moga's significance for the SAD dates back to February 1996, when the party held its 75th anniversary conference, popularly known as the 'Moga Convention'. The gathering marked a watershed moment for the party, with the Akali Dal broadening its political appeal beyond the Sikh community and the Panth to position itself as a party representing all sections of Punjab. The party adopted the slogan 'Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat' and sought to reach out to Hindus and other communities after years of Khalistan extremism. A year later, the SAD-BJP alliance - then anchored by Atal Bihari Vajpayee - swept to power in 1997, with Badal becoming Chief Minister. The alliance subsequently launched its campaigns from Moga ahead of the 2007 and 2012 Assembly elections, winning both. On December 8, 2006, Badal's 79th birthday, a rally at Killi Chahlan was attended by BJP leaders LK Advani, Arun Jaitley and Rajnath Singh, besides Navjot Singh Sidhu. Ahead of the 2012 elections, the alliance held a 'Maha Vikas' rally at the same venue on December 18, 2011. When the Moga factor failed The district, however, could not help the SAD-BJP alliance overcome growing public anger in 2017 over the sacrilege incidents and the drug menace. At least two years before the polls, and soon after the sacrilege incidents and subsequent police firing on protesters, the Akali Dal had held a 'Sadbhavna Rally' at Dana Mandi in Moga on November 28, 2015 to “promote communal harmony and peace”. Then, on Badal's 89th birthday on December 8, 2016, the party organised a 'Paani Bachao, Punjab Bachao' rally at Killi Chahlan amid the escalating dispute with Haryana over the Sutlej-Yamuna Link canal. The rally sought to project Badal as the “saviour of Punjab's waters”. The SAD-BJP alliance, however, suffered a crushing defeat, with the Congress coming to power. After parting ways with the BJP in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws, the Akali Dal returned to Moga ahead of the 2022 elections, holding its 100th foundation day rally at Killi Chahlan on December 14, 2021. Addressed by Badal, the gathering failed to revive the party's fortunes. The Akali Dal eventually won just three Assembly seats. Congress and AAP too turn to Moga Moga has also served as a launchpad for the Congress and AAP in the run-up to previous elections. Ahead of the 2022 Assembly polls, the AAP announced its third pre-poll guarantee — a monthly assistance of Rs 1,000 for women — at Moga on November 22, 2021. Prior to that, on March 21, 2021, it had held a 'Kisan Maha Sammelan' at Baghapurana to mobilise farmers. The Congress, too, chose Moga to reach out to farmers during the agitation against the Centre's three farm laws. On October 4, 2020, Rahul Gandhi, accompanied by then Chief Minister Capt Amarinder Singh, led a 'Kheti Bachao Yatra' and rode a tractor with farmers. Gandhi was also scheduled to launch the Congress campaign for the 2022 elections with a rally at Killi Chahlan in January that year, but it was cancelled due to Covid restrictions. Prior to that, ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, Gandhi addressed the Congress's 'Mission 13' rally at Killi Chahlan. The party went on to win eight of Punjab's 13 Lok Sabha seats. Moga had also figured in the Congress's preparations for the 2017 Assembly elections, when rebellion was brewing in the party with a section rallying behind Amarinder Singh as its chief ministerial face. At a 'Captain Liyao, Punjab Bachao' rally in Baghapurana, then Leader of Opposition Sunil Jakhar had declared: “The writing is on the wall and Capt Amarinder Singh is going to be the next CM.” Amarinder subsequently led the Congress to power. The AAP had earlier launched its 'Kisan Manifesto' for farmers at a rally in Baghapurana on September 11, 2016, followed by Amarinder Singh's 'Kisan Yatra to woo the farming community.

headline: Dancing Girl and Nizam jewels to be displayed at Yuge Yugeen museum
content: The ‘Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro’ from the National Museum in New Delhi, the Nizam’s jewellery collection from the vaults of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), and the gemstone ornaments found at the Taxila excavation site — these will be among the rare displays at the first gallery of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, titled ‘Adornment’. The gallery, set to open on the lower level of the North Block by August next year, will house over 1,000 priceless pieces sourced from museums and sites across the country, The Indian Express has learnt. It is intended to offer visitors a view of the sophistication and aesthetic character of the Indian civilisation, said officials. “Since the Dancing Girl is the first image that we have of various adornments that women wore during the civilisational journey of that time, we need to start from there,” Union Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal said. Besides the 4,500-year-old bronze statue of the 'Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro', which will showcase India's ornamental traditions, there will be other Harappan jewellery found during various excavations, currently housed in the National Museum and other site museums under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), officials said. Then there will be the Nizam's jewels - a priceless collection which is currently housed in the RBI's vaults in Mumbai, and has been displayed only thrice since the government acquired it in the 1990s. The collection has about 173 royal heritage pieces, dating back to over seven generations of the Asaf Jahi dynasty, or the Nizams of Hyderabad (1724-1948), including the 184.75-carat Jacob Diamond, the 465-pearl Satlada necklace, turban ornaments (sarpech), emerald pieces, and heavy diamond polkis. However, not all the pieces are likely to be displayed at Yuge Yugeen. According to officials, an assortment of ancient gold and silver ornaments, from the 4th century BCE to the 1st century AD, unearthed from archaeological sites like Bhir Mound and Sirkap in Taxila, now referred to as the Taxila jewellery collection, will also be moved from the National Museum in the Capital to Yuge Yugeen. Recently, a mock gallery was created at the Yuge Yugeen for scenographers to get an idea of the showcase. Officials said an advisory committee will look at the selection of objects and their descriptions. Meanwhile, several sculptures and figurines representing the theme of adornment are being sourced from various museums and galleries, including the Indian Museum in Kolkata and the Allahabad Museum; miniature paintings and the Gandhara sculpture collection are being sourced from the National Museum in Delhi. Aggarwal said many objects will be sourced from the National Museum in Delhi, which will then be “re-curated”. On the fate of the 35,000-square metre National Museum on Janpath, he said: “A decision has been taken by the government that this museum will stay as the National Museum”. Aggarwal said while the National Museum will “remain the national museum and will remain a museum of history, Yuge Yugeen will be a museum of civilisation”. The displays for the Yuge Yugeen Museum will come from museums across the country, including the National Museum, he said. At a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 11, the Union Cabinet approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Museum through adaptive re-use of the North and South Block complex, at an estimated project cost of Rs 3,230 crore. Billed to be the largest museum in the world, it will have eight thematic segments, telling the story of India spanning over 5,000 years, officials had said earlier. The ambitious museum project will be implemented in a phased manner by 2031. Other galleries are being developed on themes such as architecture and cityscapes, mathematics and astronomy, languages and scripts, faith and spirituality and Bharat connects - trade and ideas.

headline: Personal attack, veiled dig: Rift between two Kerala Congress MPs plays out in open
content: Alleged infighting within the ruling Congress in Keralam took an ugly turn with party MP Rajmohan Unnithan unleashing a verbal attack on fellow Parliamentarian from the state, Shafi Parambil. Unnithan, who represents the Kasaragod Lok Sabha seat, on Tuesday alleged that Shafi's followers were behind the recent online campaign against him. Addressing the media in Kasaragod, Unnithan said, “Cyber attacks against me are orchestrated from a house in Adoor. I understand that the disciple is doing it for his mentor. The disciple is now resting after impregnating four girls.’’ Unnithan was referring to former Youth Congress state president and ex-MLA Rahul Mamkootathil who has a house in Adoor. Last year, multiple allegations of sexual misconduct, including rape and forcing the victims to terminate their pregnancies, had surfaced against the former legislator after which he was removed from the primary membership of the party. In Keralam's political circles, Shafi had been known as Mamkootathil’s mentor. When the former Palakkad MLA faced the allegations, then ruling CPI (M) had termed Shafi and Rahul as “guru” and “disciple”. Shafi, who is reportedly one of the contenders for the post of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president, was not available for reactions. Unnithan, however, went on questioning the political stand of Shafi. Questioning the general impression that Shafi had been close to late Chief Minister Oommen Chandy and his 'A’ group in the party, Unnithan said, “If Shafi is part of the A group, that would be the eighth wonder in the world.’’ As the controversy snowballed, late Chandy’s wife Mariyamma Oommen joined the issue saying, “Chandy had loved Shafi, but it is not known whether he (the latter) had reciprocated that. Chandy had suggested J S Akhil as the president of the Youth Congress, but I am not the person to say who had worked against Akhil’s prospects.” Notably, Mamkoottathil had succeeded Shafi as the state president of the Youth Congress and continued in office till his removal from the post in the wake of the alleged misconduct against women. Cultural Affairs Minister P C Vishnunadh, though, came to Shafi’s defence, describing him as a committed Congress worker whom he had known since their student days in the Kerala Students Union. What is the cyber controversy Youth Congress leaders had earlier circulated a cartoon video, apparently taking a dig at Unnithan, after he criticised the appointment of an additional public prosecutor in Kasaragod. A section of Youth Congress leaders had accused Unnithan of being a leader who lands the party in difficult situations. Meanwhile, Unnithan's son Amal questioned the role of senior Congress leaders in the controversy. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, Amal alleged that attempts were being made to weaken CM VD Satheesan and create a situation favourable to a change in leadership. The latest confrontation comes against the backdrop of growing differences over the distribution of political appointments and authority between the government and the Congress organisation. A section of leaders close to MP K C Venugopal has reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with Satheesan's style of functioning, while the CM supporters have accused some leaders of attempting to portray the government as being in crisis.

headline: From Instagram reel to political corridors, how row over excavator at Sheshnag has snowballed
content: It started with an Instagram video. An earthmover is seen digging the soil near a pristine blue water body. The person inside the machine and another filming the act seem to be having their own bit of fun with it, moving the excavator's arm round and round while smiling into the camera, and then putting the video up on social media with a trending song playing in the background. The sight of the heavy machine against the alpine lake was enough to raise eyebrows but as it turned out to be the much-revered Sheshnag lake, the issue snowballed with political leaders, climate activists, and concerned citizens weighing in on the matter. The video has since been deleted but the controversy around it continues to escalate. While political leaders have termed the explanation of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), that it was carrying out post-Amarnath yatra stabilisation work on an existing track, “unconvincing”, many have also questioned the “silence” of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on the issue. Mehbooba’s trek On Tuesday, former Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti tried to trek up to the Himalayan lake before she was stopped, some 12 kms away at Chandanwari, citing “security reasons”. “My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder,” Mufti said. “What is being concealed today could become a man-made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath Cave, Yatra and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole,” said Mufti, accompanied by PDP legislators Waheed Para and Aga Muntazir Mehdi. Since Monday, new videos have emerged showing large-scale use of excavators in rocky as well as snow-covered mountains. A viral video showing excavators operating near Kashmir’s Sheshnag Lake on the Amarnath Yatra route has sparked concerns over environmental damage. PDP leader Mohit Bhan called it a “crime against Hindu faith”, while Mirwaiz Umar Farooq questioned the impact on the fragile Himalayan ecosystem. Read: — The Indian Express (@IndianExpress) November 23, 2026 On Tuesday, Hurriyat leader and Valley's chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq asked people to sign a petition to stop the “plunder”. “We all have to collectively raise our voice to stop the mindless destruction of our ecology at its most fragile places. Why is our Chief Minister mute? As peoples' elected representative, it is his duty to speak up and do the needful to ensure this plunder is stopped,” Mirwaiz said. “I have signed this petition and urge all those who want to save Kashmir’s fragile ecology (to) do so. Stop construction around Kashmir's alpine lakes.” ‘Govt should come clean’ J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra has asked the government to come clean on the project. “In the video, the JCB (excavator) can be seen dumping the soil into the lake. It seems they are fiddling with it,” Karra said. “(The) government should come clean on what is a JCB (excavator) doing in Sheshnag and for what?” Though CM Omar is yet to speak up on the issue, a legislator of his party, the National Conference, has termed the explanation by the BRO “unconvincing”. “If you have to stabilise a track, why is the bulldozer needed?” asked Hasnain Masoodi, who is a retired High Court judge. “Himalayan ecosystem is fragile and already under stress. This is a disturbing incident.” Communist leader M Y Tarigami said that questions raised over the use of excavators should not be treated as interference with yatra. “If the work is only on the existing track, why are heavy earthmovers needed?” he asked. Earlier, in its clarification, the BRO had said, “The works are confined to the existing tracks.” Said Tarigami, “This work cannot be seen apart from the Khanabal-Baltal highway, NH-501. The project's design report, prepared by NHIDCL in January 2024, proposes 2- or 4-laning about 90 km of road from Khanabal to Baltal. It includes a new stretch from Chandanwari to Baltal along the traditional Yatra route, through Pissu Top, Zojibal, Sheshnag and Panchtarni. The authorities must say clearly how the work under way relates to this alignment.” Tarigami said the government must publicly answer three questions. “Has any independent expert body assessed whether the slopes around Sheshnag can take this excavation? Have environmental and forest clearances been sought or obtained? If so, why have they not been made public? And how does this work relate to the NH-501 alignment, which passes through Sheshnag? Where the excavated material is being dumped, and who chose those sites, must also be made public,” he said. “Until these answers are on record, the work near the lake must stop.”

headline: Want to book a DDA park for an event? Here’s how to do it
content: Want to hold a poetry reading or a yoga session or a school picnic at a venue operated by the Delhi Development authority? As it opens 17 park locations and eight amphitheatres to events, the DDA has introduced a policy for booking the venues that it operates. Schools can book a space for just Re 1. The policy follows several meetings chaired by Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu on rationalising and upgrading services in DDA parks, according to officials. The entire booking process — from checking available sites, capacities and charges to applying and paying — will move to a single-window online portal linked to the DDA website, bringing bookings onto one common digital platform, said officials. Weddings and political functions are not allowed at the venues. Venues at a glance The open lawns include Swarna Jayanti Park and Chitragupta Park in Rohini, G-8 Lake Park in Hari Nagar, District Park in Paschim Vihar, Sandesh Vihar and Lake Park in Pitampura, District Parks in Dwarka's Sectors 11 and 17, Indraprastha Park, Sanjay Lake, Coronation Park, Astha Kunj and Hauz Khas Park. The event areas range from about 1 to 3 acres. Baansera, Asita and Mehrauli Archaeological parks have separate lawnwise rates. Amphitheatres at Indraprastha Park, Astha Kunj, Utsav Ground, Vasant Udyan, Tughlaqabad Recreational Park, Sanjay Lake, Coronation Park and the Commonwealth Games Village, with recommended capacities of 150 to 750, can also be booked. The cost Open lawns are classified by expected peak crowd, ranging for up to 200, 200 to 500, and more than 500 people. A small gathering costs Rs 3,000 to Rs 9,000 a day, a medium one Rs 5,000 to Rs 15,000, and a large one Rs 6,000 to Rs 18,000, depending on the area. The refundable security deposit is twice the total cost for small events and three times for bigger ones. Amphitheatres cost Rs 3,000 for a half-day slot and Rs 5,000 for a full day for non-ticketed events, and Rs 10,000 and Rs 15,000 for ticketed ones. The riverfront and heritage venues cost more. For non-commercial events, rates run from Rs 5,000 a day for a 450 sq m lawn at Baansera to Rs 3 lakh for the Charbagh near Quli Khan's Tomb in Mehrauli. Events with branding or sponsorship pay 1.5 times the rate. Schools pay Rs 1 plus GST for non-ticketed activities such as picnics, painting and debates, and get 50% off for other events. Recognised higher educational institutions, government departments and PSUs also get 50% off booking charges. How to apply Individuals, RWAs, NGOs, firms and institutions can apply at least five working days before the event with a plan. Payment is to be made upfront but the booking is confirmed only when DDA issues an allotment letter, which it aims to do within three working days, according to officials. Cancellation made more than 30 days in advance ensures a full refund; but if the event is cancelled within 10 days before the scheduled date, the organisers get nothing. To get their deposit back, organisers must upload GPS-tagged photographs of the site before and after the event. Events in Ridge areas must be held between sunrise and sunset, officials underlined.

headline: Family of ailing Navy veteran jailed in Qatar seeks Indian mission’s help for his release
content: A WEEK after his emergency hospitalisation in Doha, the family of former Naval Commander Purnendu Tiwary, who has been incarcerated in Qatar since 2022, has written to the Indian mission in Doha, seeking help in securing his release on humanitarian grounds. Tiwary had to be rushed to hospital on the night of November 17, for an undisclosed medical procedure. His sister Meetu Bhargava told The Indian Express that they have not been made aware by the prison authorities about the nature of his sudden illness. Even as they were informed that he had returned to prison after an emergency medical procedure two days later, the family says they are extremely concerned about his health condition, and wrote to the Indian Embassy in Doha on Monday, seeking “urgent intervention” to secure his immediate repatriation on humanitarian grounds. Last week, as Tiwary was hospitalised, Bhargava had put out an appeal in a post on X, seeking Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar’s intervention to facilitate his return to India, “before it’s too late”. According to the family, the 67-year-old Naval veteran is suffering from various physical and psychological ailments, including Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, which they attribute to his prolonged solitary confinement in Qatar. On November 20, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that New Delhi has contacted Qatari authorities to verify Tiwary's well-being, seek further details on his medical condition, and ensure he receives proper medical attention. When asked at the media briefing, Jaiswal said, “We have gotten in touch with the Qatari authorities so as to ascertain his well-being as also to impress upon them that if there is a requirement of him getting proper medical attention, that should be given to him. We also understand that he was recently hospitalised, and we are seeking further details in regard to his medical condition.” “We remain committed to doing our best for Commander Tiwary, and we are in touch with his family members as also with the Qatari authorities,” he said. Tiwary was among eight former Indian Navy personnel arrested in Qatar in 2022. While the other seven officers were released and returned to India in February 2024, he remained in custody serving a six-year sentence in a separate legal case. The Ministry of External Affairs maintains that Tiwary could not return because he became entangled in a separate financial case and investigation in Qatar tied to his former employer, even after receiving a pardon in an alleged case of espionage.

headline: Karnataka government to procure 674 GPS rovers: Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah
content: Bengaluru: The government has decided to procure 674 GPS rovers to ensure greater accuracy and technology-driven surveys of plots, supporting the process of converting B-Khata properties to A-Khata, Urban Development Minister Dr Yathindra Siddaramaiah said on Tuesday.

headline: Government to set up skill centre for youth, women: CM Rekha Gupta
content: New Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Tuesday said that the Delhi government will establish an eight-acre “state-of-the-art” skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh where young people will be trained in emerging technologies and industry-oriented skills, including digital services, IT support, artificial intelligence, retail and hospitality. Designed specially for Class 12 graduates, the centre will offer employment-oriented technical courses along the lines of ITI (Industrial Training Institute) programmes, as per the Chief Minister’s office (CMO). “Women will have access to short-term courses in baking, beauty, fashion, tailoring and other practical skills. The objective is to ensure that training goes beyond certificates and becomes a source of financial independence,” the CMO said in a statement. The centre has also proposed to offer flexible schedules, weekend batches along with online and offline training facilities which will enable women, bound by domestic responsibilities, upgrade their skills. “The centre will not only emerge as a major hub for skill development among young people but will also bring women into the mainstream by making them economically self-reliant,” the statement said. The CMO has not specified a timeline for the Centre to be operational, but sources said it could take at least a year. “The government plans to construct the primary building in a year and launch the programme. Construction of the entire campus may take another year or two. We are also exploring the possibility of starting the programme at any existing ITI or polytechnic,” an official said. Employment opportunities Ms. Gupta said providing better employment opportunities to Delhi’s youth and economically empowering women were among her key priorities and the proposed centre was an important step towards fulfilling this vision. In the Budget presented in March, the CM had stressed the importance of skill development and employment-oriented training. Last month, while speaking about The Industrial Policy, 2026, approved by the Cabinet, she said that women and young people will receive special attention under skill development programmes. “By aligning training programmes with market and industry requirements, the centre will prepare young people for modern workplaces. Women will have opportunities to acquire skills suited to their interests, abilities and family circumstances, as well as explore avenues to start their own businesses,” the CM said. The entire campus will be constructed by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC) across eight acres in Desu Colony. The centre will have smart classrooms, 14 state-of-the-art laboratories and training centres, a library and learning resource centre, a multipurpose auditorium with a capacity of 250 people, and facilities for conferences and placements. Modern equipment will be provided for training in digital and IT, fashion and textiles, tailoring and handicrafts, beauty and wellness, baking and food processing, healthcare and other related fields. A horticulture training field, spread over approximately two acres adjoining the campus, will also be developed. It will provide practical training in plant care, plant health and landscaping, the statement said. Focus on women After completing their training, women will be able to seek employment or start their own ventures, such as boutiques, beauty salons, bakeries, tiffin services and other businesses, the CMO said while adding that the proposed entrepreneurship and incubation facility will provide guidance, mentorship, market linkages and access to financial assistance to help women set up their businesses. To make the centre more accessible to working mothers, two crèche units, each with a capacity of 25 children, will be set up on the premises. A medical bay will also be established to provide first aid facilities. According to the CMO, there are also plans to develop a hostel and modern sports facilities to create an accessible learning environment to suit the needs of students coming from distant parts of Delhi and outside the city. The academic and technical operations of the centre will be managed through the Skill Development Centre of Dr B. R. Ambedkar University which functions under the Directorate of Higher Education of the Delhi government. The training programmes will focus on industry-oriented practical skills in accordance with the standards of the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

headline: DDA rolls out park booking policy; schools can book spaces for Rs. 1
content: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on Tuesday announced a new booking policy for its parks allowing citizens, institutions and organisations to book designated spaces in 17 parks across the city for cultural, educational, recreational and community events. The bookings will be processed through a single-window online portal linked to the DDA website, the authority said in a statement. Under this policy, schools can book designated park spaces for educational and recreational activities including picnics, painting, photography, debates and competitions, for Rs 1. Schools booking parks for other purposes will also get 50% concession. Permitted activities include yoga sessions, nature walks, workshops, exhibitions, cultural performances, book fairs and community gatherings. Political events and marriage ceremonies, however, are not permitted. The policy divides open park spaces into three categories based on the number of people expected to attend. For gatherings of up to 200 people, the daily booking charge starts at Rs 3,000 for an area of up to 4,000 square metres. It increases to Rs 5,000 for gatherings of 201 to 500 people and Rs 6,000 for events with more than 500 people. For spaces measuring between 8,000 and 12,000 square metres, charges go up to Rs 18,000 for a day. The 17 identified locations include Swarna Jayanti Park and Chitragupta Park in Rohini, District Park in Paschim Vihar, Indraprastha Park, Sanjay Lake, Asita-Yamuna River Front, Coronation Park, Hauz Khas Park, Bansera and Mehrauli Archaeological Park. Activities at ecologically sensitive sites will be subject to additional restrictions. The DDA may also ask applicants to modify their event layouts or put in place additional environmental and safety measures depending on the site. Special facilities such as amphitheatres and other designated venues will have a separate tariff. For non-ticketed events, the charges will be Rs. 3,000 for a half-day slot of up to six hours and Rs 5,000 for a full day. For ticketed events, the charges are Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 15,000, respectively. Applicants will have to submit their applications at least five working days before the proposed event, along with an event plan. The booking will be confirmed only after approval by the competent authority and issuance of an allotment letter, as per the policy accessed by The Hindu. Organisers will be responsible for crowd management, safety, waste disposal and restoring the allotted area after the event.

headline: Chinese doctors’ delegation visits Hyd to build medical ties
content: Hyderabad: A 16-member delegation from China’s Guizhou Medical University (GMU) province visited Hyderabad as part of the seventh Dr Kotnis Memorial Joint Medical Mission, organised by the India-China Friendship Association (ICFA), to explore avenues for medical cooperation and strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries.The visit was aimed to help the Chinese doctors understand India’s healthcare delivery system while facilitating exchanges in medical technology, research, treatment practices and traditional medicine, including traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and acupuncture. The delegation comprised 10 doctors and six public health dept staff.“This is primarily an effort to promote friendship and exchange between the two countries through the medical profession. We want to take the message of cooperation to people and improve mutual understanding,” said Dr Mohan Reddy, national secretary of ICFA.The association is also exploring a memorandum of understanding between the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Chinese Medical Doctors Association (CMDA) to facilitate future exchanges, conferences, continuing medical education programmes and student training.“We want doctors from both countries to interact, learn from each other and eventually develop training and exchange programmes,” Dr Reddy added.During a presentation on TCM, a Chinese doctor spoke about its long history, training methods and role in China’s healthcare system. Explaining its holistic approach, the doctor said, “The focus is on the balance of the whole person, rather than a single condition. Treatment is based on the individual’s needs and aims to prevent disease before it occurs.”The mission had remained suspended for four to five years amid border tensions and Covid-related restrictions. “The revival of the mission is expected to provide fresh momentum to medical and cultural exchanges between the two countries,” said Hu Xiao, vice-president and cheif physician, GMU. headline: ECI rejects Yuga Thulasi Party’s name change plea
content: Hyderabad: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has rejected the Hyderabad-based Yuga Thulasi Party’s request to rename itself the ‘Gau Matha Rashtra Matha Party’ (GMRMP), ruling that the proposed name does not conform to its guidelines.Party founder K Shiva Kumar, however, has decided to challenge the decision and seek a review from the ECI, arguing that the proposed name has no religious connotation and does not conflict with that of any recognised political party.“I will continue to fight for ECI approval for change of my party’s name. My party’s proposed name GMRMP is completely distinct and is not a translated version of any existing recognised national or state political party in India. The title of the party is not in conflict with any existing party,” Shiva Kumar said.He maintained that the proposed name did not represent or advocate any particular religion, but signified agricultural prosperity, rural livelihoods, animal welfare and eco-friendly farming practices.Shiva Kumar, a former TTD board member who has been campaigning for cow protection and runs a goshala on the outskirts of Hyderabad, has also demanded measures for cow protection and sought allotment of 1,000 acres for a goshala.The Yuga Thulasi Party had attracted attention during the previous Telangana assembly elections after it was allotted the road roller symbol, which resembled the BRS’ car symbol. The similarity had sparked concerns in the BRS that it could confuse voters and split its votes. The BRS had also sought to persuade Shiva Kumar not to field candidates.The party also contested from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Varanasi Lok Sabha constituency in the previous elections to highlight its cow protection campaign.Seeking a review of the ECI’s decision, Shiva Kumar argued that the terms “Gau Matha” and “Rashtra Matha” had significance beyond religion.“Prominent Muslim organisations and community leaders, including the All-India Muslim Jamaat and various regional religious heads, have repeatedly issued public appeals advocating for the cow to be recognised as India’s national animal to foster social harmony and rural economic strength. This universal support across communities establishes beyond doubt that the reference to ‘Gau Matha’ and ‘Rashtra Matha’ transcends religious boundaries and holds unifying national, agrarian, and socio-economic significance,” Shiva Kumar said in his appeal to ECI for review of its decision.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Congress MP Accuses BRS Leaders of Misinformation on Telangana Irrigation
content: Hyderabad: Congress MP Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy on Tuesday accused BRS leaders T Harish Rao and KT Rama Rao of spreading misinformation over Krishna river water allocations and irrigation projects, including Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme and Palnadu Water Grid.He alleged that the previous BRS govt had compromised the interests of farmers in southern Telangana through its decisions on major irrigation projects. Questioning BRS govt’s handling of the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme, the Bhongir MP said its decisions had caused serious damage to the interests of farmers in southern Telangana.According to him, GO 72, issued in 2013, had originally proposed drawing water for the project from Jurala. However, the subsequent GO 105, issued in 2015 during the previous BRS govt tenure, shifted the source to Srisailam, necessitating additional lifts and pumping infrastructure. As a result, the estimated project cost escalated from over Rs 30,000 crore to more than Rs 80,000 crore, while the project remained incomplete, he alleged.He further accused the previous government of neglecting several important irrigation projects, including SLBC, Kalwakurthy, Nettempadu, Bhima and Koilsagar. “Following meetings held at Pragathi Bhavan with YSRCP leader Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy in 2019 and 2020, Andhra Pradesh govt issued GO 203 for the Rayalaseema Lift Irrigation Scheme,” he alleged.He also referred to GO 56 concerning the Palnadu Water Grid, issued on February 16, 2022, and said the relevant decisions and records were already available. Against this backdrop, he accused BRS leaders of misleading people by creating a false impression that these projects were only now being initiated.The Congress government, he said, had been consistently demanding national project status for the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme. Advising BRS leaders to stop their criticism, Chamala alleged that those who had themselves exploited irrigation projects for political purposes were now attempting to spread false propaganda against the Congress government.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
