headline: Ferozepur man nets Rs 2.5L per acre from fish farming
content: While many farmers continue to grapple with rising input costs and shrinking returns from the conventional wheat-paddy cycle, Gurmeet Singh of Kahan Singh Wala village in Guruharsahai subdivision has charted a different course for himself. Moving away from the traditional cropping pattern after 2015, he ventured into fish farming and piggery, turning an unconventional choice into a rewarding source of income.Today, he is practising fish farming on 10 acres of his own land while earning a net profit of around Rs 2.5 lakh per acre of pond after meeting all expenses. His success has also emerged as an example of how diversification can offer farmers a viable alternative to conventional agricultural practices.Talking to The Tribune, Gurmeet said before 2015, he used to cultivate wheat, paddy and vegetables. However, he eventually decided to explore a different line of work and took up fish farming. Initially, he operated on leased land and had fish ponds spread over 18 acres. He has now shifted the activity to 10 acres of his own land. His ponds produce six varieties of fish, including Murakh, Rohu, Catla, Silver Carp, Grass Carp and Common Carp.Explaining the economics of the venture, Gurmeet said maintaining water quality, regular cleaning of ponds and ensuring proper fish feed were essential for good production. “Normally, an acre of pond yields around 20 to 22 quintals of fish, but while taking care of these aspects, I achieved a record production of 28 quintals per acre,” Gurmeet said. “I believe farmers should supplement conventional agriculture with allied occupations to improve their income,” he added.The harvested fish fetch between Rs 140 and Rs 150 per kg. “The returns from fish farming on 1 acre can be higher than what a farmer earns from cultivating wheat or paddy on 3 acres,” Gurmeet said, adding that he regularly sought training and technical guidance from the department to improve production.It is pertinent to mention here that Kahan Singh Wala has emerged as a fish-farming hub, with fish farming being undertaken on nearly 250 acres in the village. Across the district, fish farming is being practised on 1,194 acres through 467 ponds.The Fisheries Department is also encouraging farmers by providing fish seed, training and technical guidance. Assistant Deputy Director Manjot Kaur said 559 people from the district had registered with the department through the National Fisheries Digital Platform.“Those interested in starting fish farming are provided five-day training, technical assistance, subsidy and insurance facilities. The subsidy provision is 40 per cent for the general category and 60 per cent for SC, ST and women beneficiaries,” said Manjot.However, despite promoting fish farming as an alternative livelihood, the department itself is facing a shortage of resources. Fish seed is produced in ponds spread over nearly 7 acres of departmental land. However, after 3 acres were allotted for the PGI Satellite Centre, several ponds used for fish seed production had to be closed, reducing the area and water availability for the purpose.Notwithstanding these constraints, departmental officials and staff continue to guide farmers and facilitate access to government schemes, as fish farming gradually gains ground as an alternative source of income in the district.

headline: Health dept orders safety audit of govt hospitals
content: Thiruvananthapuram: The health department directed superintendents of all govt hospitals to carry out an immediate and comprehensive inspection of all buildings to assess their structural condition and fitness. The department asked superintendents under the directorate of medical education (DME) and the directorate of health services (DHS) to pay particular attention to old and dilapidated structures and buildings sporting cracks, leakage, ceiling damage or other signs of deterioration. Buildings housing patients, operation theatres, ICUs, wards and labs have been given the highest priority.If any building or part of it is found unsafe, the superintendent must immediately report it to DME or DHS, without waiting for routine reporting channels or further instructions. The circular directed precautionary steps, including restricting access to unsafe areas and shifting patients and staff wherever necessary without delay.Where structural defects are suspected, superintendents must arrange a technical inspection by competent engineering authorities and submit detailed reports with recommendations for repair, renovation or reconstruction.DME and DHS have been made responsible for monitoring compliance and following up on the reports they receive. They must furnish a consolidated status report on the structural condition and safety of hospital buildings to govt within a month. Additional chief secretary (health) APM Mohammed Hanish had issued a circular in this regard.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. Download the TOI App.

headline: Israel’s Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
content: JERUSALEM Israel’s Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) it agreed to ​sign a coalition pact with a right-wing Opposition party as it ‌seeks to form a government following last month’s election. Gadi Eisenkot | Netanyahu’s challenger storyline 1 Also read | A guide to Israel’s elections https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/the-view-from-india-newsletter-a-guide-to-israels-elections/article71627046.ece Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, earlier on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) and they agreed on a deal afterward, the first such alliance since the election. Israel’s ‌Parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government, after the election on October 27 stripped ‌Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority but left ‌others ⁠with no clear path to power. Analysis | Benjamin Netanyahu: A Prime Minister always at war storyline 1 Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government storyline 1 President Isaac Herzog has ⁠tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, while Mr. Netanyahu remains caretaker Prime Minister. Mr. Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its ​majority. It now holds 53 ‌of the Knesset’s 120 seats. Mr. Eisenkot’s center-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners — including Mr. Lieberman — hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold ‌19 seats and are aligned with Mr. Eisenkot in their ​vehement opposition to Mr. Netanyahu. The agreement between Mr. Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Mr. Lieberman, whose party ⁠won 7, was something of a surprise, since Mr. Lieberman had been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from ‌Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu. Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents storyline 1 Mr. Lieberman has also said his main goal is to oust Mr. Netanyahu from power. Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, but he could ask for a 14-day extension. If he fails, Mr. Netanyahu would get a shot. If ‌no one is able to form a government, another election will be held ​next year. Talks are also ongoing between Mr. Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a ⁠unity government. Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government Isaac Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government storyline 1 The left-wing Democrats party, which won 8 parliamentary seats, separately said ⁠it was suspending talks with Mr. Eisenkot because of progress in his talks with Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible ‌unity government and “given with the deadlock in negotiations to form a ‘change government.’ Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, has said he ​prefers a government without Mr. Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

headline: Falls emerge as No. 1 injury threat in India, surpass road crashes
content: Hyderabad: India is becoming safer from many major injuries when measured by population-adjusted rates, but its growing and ageing population is keeping the actual burden of death and disability stubbornly high, with falls becoming the single largest contributor to age standardised injury burden in India, overtaking road injuries.An analysis of Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data, published in ‘The Lancet Regional Health–Southeast Asia’, found that age standardised injury disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates fell across nearly all major categories between 1990 and 2023. Yet total injury numbers did not decline at the same pace as population growth and ageing added to the burden.The study, ‘Trends, demographic drivers, interstate inequalities, and projected burden of injuries in India, 1990–2023: A population-based observational analysis using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023’, examined eight major injury categories across states and Union Territories.DALYs measure the overall health burden by combining years of life lost to premature death with years lived with disability.In 2023, falls had the highest age-standardised injury burden nationally at 958.7 DALYs per 100,000 population, followed by road injuries at 831.1 and self-harm at 671.9.Falls are emerging as a particular concern as India ages. Their age standardised DALY rate declined by an estimated 0.85% annually between 1990 and 2023, but population ageing contributed 2.57 million DALYs to the net increase of 4.66 million fall-related DALYs over the period.By 2047, the age standardised rate for falls is projected to decline by 30.6%. Even so, falls are expected to remain India’s largest injury burden as the population aged 60 and above is projected to roughly double between 2021 and 2050.Road injuries present another major challenge. Their age standardised DALY rate fell by just 0.26% annually between 1990 and 2023, the slowest decline among the major injury categories studied.The researchers linked the sluggish improvement to rapidly rising motor vehicle and two-wheeler ownership outpacing safety-engineered road infrastructure and enforcement, along with mixed traffic, vulnerable road users and limited pre-hospital care.Road injury deaths reached 1,68,000 in 2022, up 9.4% from the previous year, despite road injury numbers plateauing in national data. The study said this could point to greater crash severity, higher speeds or slower trauma response along highways.Overall, road injuries recorded a net increase of 4.90 million DALYs between 1990 and 2023 as population growth and ageing outweighed epidemiological improvements. Their age standardised burden is projected to decline by 23.9% by 2047, but road injuries are expected to remain India’s second largest injury burden.Other injuries recorded much sharper improvements. Age standardised rates declined annually by 3.25% for drowning, 2.69% for exposure to mechanical forces, 1.82% for interpersonal violence and 1.27% for burns.But the national improvement conceals widening disparities between states.Burns recorded an age standardised rate of 146.1 DALYs per 1,00,000 in 2023. Although their national rate declined, interstate inequality widened sharply. The study linked burns to household energy poverty, unsafe cooking with solid fuels and kerosene, inadequate housing, occupational exposure and domestic risks.Interstate inequality also increased for road injuries, while disparities narrowed for self-harm, falls and drowning.The researchers said national age standardised rates alone can therefore understate the volume of trauma and disability that India’s health system must handle as the population grows and ages.The disparities are reflected in wide state-level differences in road injuries between Uttarakhand and Delhi, burns between Odisha and Mizoram, and poisonings between Haryana and West Bengal in 2023. Such variations, the study noted, show how national averages can conceal pockets of high risk and unequal access to prevention, emergency care and rehabilitation.The study was conducted by researchers from AIIMS Madurai, Karpaga Vinayaga Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre in Chengalpattu, Sri Manakula Vinayagar Medical College and Hospital and Sri Venkateshwara Medical College Hospital & Research Centre in Puducherry, and PGIMER Chandigarh.For policy planning, the researchers called for trauma care, rehabilitation services and health workforces to be planned using demographic and population projections rather than relying only on historical injury-rate trends. They also stressed expanding rehabilitation, particularly in rural and resource-poor areas, to tackle long-term disability after discharge.The authors recommended integrating fall prevention and post-fall rehabilitation into the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly. Suggested measures include home hazard modifications, strength and balance programmes, vision and medication reviews, and hip-protection and recovery pathways.For road injuries, the study called for road-safety and trauma-financing initiatives to be coupled with stronger pre-hospital care, trauma registries and state-specific interventions. It also stressed targeting risks such as solid fuel cooking through clean fuel programmes, including the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: 1st privately built PSLV set for launch early next year: Isro chief
content: NEW DELHI: The first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-N1) is ready for a maiden launch in the "first quarter of next year", Isro chairman V Narayanan said on Tuesday. He also said govt is fast-tracking satellite launches in collaboration with startups "in a big way" as Isro currently has only 56 space assets in orbit.Talking about foreign collaboration, the Isro chairman said, "India is collaborating with 64 countries... At least 434 satellites for 34 countries have lifted off from Indian soil during the last 12 years."Gaganyaan in final phase, says Isro chiefSpeaking on the sidelines of the 5th India International Space Conference in Delhi, Isro chief V Narayanan said, “Earlier, it was only Isro that built PSLV with the support of industry. Now, an L&T and HAL consortium has been given five PSLVs (to build). So, the first rocket PSLV-N1 is getting ready and we are targeting to launch it by the first quarter of next year.” Isro’s arm NSIL signed a contract with the consortium in Sept 2022 for Rs 860 crore for five PSLV rockets.Narayanan said, “We need to build a lot of space assets for communication, navigation and earth observation. This can’t be done by govt sector (alone). Isro and INSPACe are hand-holding private companies and you will see its benefit five years from now. Today, from one startup, their number has come to 440+.”Pointing out that “Gaganyaan is not late”, he said, “It is a technology-intensive activity. We are in the final phase. The rocket and other items are ready. We’re working on the orbital module. At the earliest opportunity, it will be launched.” He said, “Isro and Semiconductor Lab in Chandigarh have developed a Vikram processor. Vikram-32 chip has come out, and we are going to induct it.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: SAD-BJP tie-up reunites cousins Sukhbir, Manpreet after 16 years
content: The SAD-BJP reunion ahead of the upcoming Assembly elections has not only changed Punjab’s political equations but has also brought the political journeys of the two Badal cousins – Sukhbir Singh Badal and Manpreet Singh Badal – closer once again, after 16 years of rivalry.While Sukhbir is the president of the SAD, Manpreet is currently the national vice-president of the BJP. Both belong to Badal village in Muktsar district. The two cousins parted ways politically in 2010 following differences over economic policies and the functioning of the SAD. Manpreet was expelled from the party in October 2010.He later floated his own party, the People’s Party of Punjab (PPP), and openly criticised the SAD leadership and its policies. The 2012 Assembly elections, however, proved disappointing for Manpreet.His PPP failed to win even a single seat, and he lost from both Gidderbaha, his traditional constituency in Muktsar district, and Maur in Bathinda district. His father Gurdas Singh Badal also lost the contest against elder brother Parkash Singh Badal from Lambi in the same election.Manpreet joined the Congress in January 2016 after merging his PPP with the party. He won the Bathinda Urban seat in the 2017 Assembly elections as a Congress candidate and became Finance Minister in the government led by Capt Amarinder Singh.In the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, Manpreet had unsuccessfully contested against his sister-in-law and Sukhbir’s wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal from Bathinda.After leaving the Congress, Manpreet joined the BJP in January 2023. The party fielded him from Gidderbaha in the 2024 Assembly byelection, but he lost. In August 2026, he was appointed the BJP national vice-president.With the revival of the SAD-BJP alliance on Tuesday, the two cousins could soon be seen sharing the stage at political events.Interestingly, their personal ties had improved over the past few years, especially after the death of their fathers. Both cousins have been seen attending each other’s family functions, including weddings.Meanwhile, Manpreet Badal refused to speak on his personal and political relations with Sukhbir, but said, “The renewed bond between the BJP and the SAD is more than an alliance. It is a celebration of the eternal, unbreakable unity of Hindus and Sikhs, woven together by centuries of shared sacrifice, love, and brotherhood. Today, we begin a new chapter for Punjab, where every home knows peace, every hand finds prosperity and every citizen walks tall with dignity and honour.”Divide that even Badal Sr, Chautala could not bridgeFormer Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal wanted to see cousins Sukhbir and Manpreet together again in the SAD, but his wish remained unfulfilled. The late SAD patriarch had even tried to bring the two together.The appeal for reconciliation was also made publicly by senior SAD leaders Balwinder Singh Bhunder and Prem Singh Chandumajra at a prayer meeting for Parkash Singh Badal in May 2023.Former Haryana Chief Minister Om Parkash Chautala, too, had personally attempted to reconcile Sukhbir and Manpreet.

headline: ‘Killer string snatched happiness’: Biker dies as banned Chinese manjha slits throat
content: Vikas Singh recently had his first child with his wife. On Monday, the 26-year-old man's life was cut short when a stray Chinese kite string (manjha), which is banned, allegedly slit his throat near Barapullah on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway while he was returning home from work on Monday, according to his family members. Vikas, who worked at a repair centre, allegedly lost control of his motorcycle after the string allegedly got entangled around his neck, inflicting a deep wound. He died on the spot, according to police. His wife, Pinky, said she rushed to the spot in an auto. “I had told him to come home early then he called me around 7 pm and said he was late and that he would be home soon. He even apologised. He asked if me and our daughter were doing well. Later, I got a call around 8:15 pm that he had met with an accident. Umesh Soni, Pinky's father, said he too rushed to the accident site after receiving her distress call. “She told me that my son-in-law had met with an accident. When I reached the spot, I found him lying in a pool of blood, with severe injuries to his neck. The police personnel told me that his neck had been caught in Chinese manjha and he had died on the spot,” Soni said. He added, “He and my daughter were so happy after they became parents. Their child is barely three months old. This killer string has snatched away all their happiness,” he said. After the incident, Singh’s body was taken into police custody and sent for a postmortem examination. His father-in-law said his daughter and Singh had solemnised their love marriage in court around two years ago. He also questioned how the banned kite string had reached the expressway and called for strict action against those involved in its sale and use. At the family’s home, Singh’s wife was inconsolable on Tuesday as relatives and neighbours gathered to offer support. The couple’s infant son is now left without his father. The latest death comes amid a series of fatal and serious accidents involving banned Chinese manjha in Delhi over the past few years. Despite restrictions on its sale and use, the sharp kite string has continued to endanger commuters, particularly two-wheeler riders.

headline: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
content: NEW DELHI: Congress politician Rahul Gandhi said the security of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, was removed deliberately to get him killed, making a sensational charge years after the former PM was assassinated by a suicide bomber in Tamil Nadu.In a video interaction with his mother Sonia Gandhi and sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said, "Papa's security was removed so that he got killed. Papa's security removal was not an accident. It was done on purpose so that he got killed." "An atmosphere was created for him to get killed. It was obvious what was going on. I told papa and mom, and had an argument about it with my father," he said.Act passed by Rajiv government offered SPG cover only to PM, not former PMsRahul Tuesday posted a video featuring the family discussing Sonia Gandhi’s recently released book ‘Belonging’, in which his charge came just after his mother spoke about the lax security arrangements during Rajiv Gandhi’s visit to Bihar as leader of the opposition, where he faced stone pelting. Rahul had accompanied his father on his Bihar visit.Even though Rahul alleged there was an “intention” behind withdrawing his father’s security in 1988, the Special Protection Group Act, passed in 1988 by the then Rajiv government, restricted SPG cover strictly to the PM and not to former PMs. Thus, Rajiv lost the protection after being voted out in 1989. V P Singh replaced him as PM. When Rajiv was assassinated at a rally in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, the Chandra Shekhar government was in office.Following the assassination, the PV Narasimha Rao government amended the Act, extending protection to former PMs and their immediate family members for five years after leaving office. This brought Sonia, Rahul and Priyanka under its cover. It was further amended in 1994 to prolong the duration to 10 years.Rahul also said Sonia has not written about how she was treated by some people. He said she was “humiliated, abused” in politics, adding he may talk about it someday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 6 years after split, Akalis & BJP tie up for Punjab assembly polls
content: NEW DELHI: After six years of separation marked by AAP's rise in Punjab, BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal on Tuesday renewed their alliance ahead of assembly polls, with home minister Amit Shah recognising the regional party as the "big brother" in the tie-up and claimant to the chief minister's chair in case NDA returns to office after a decade.Shah was joined by SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the announcement, timed to coincide with Guru Nanak's birth anniversary, exuding confidence in their victory and the governing AAP's wipeout in the polls to be held early next year.The Akalis had broken away from NDA over the now-scrapped farm laws.The revival of the alliance after a period which saw SAD's fortunes nosedive and BJP achieve limited success in expanding its base outside its influence in urban areas brings NDA right back into the reckoning in a state where AAP and Congress were being seen as the main election contenders.BJP and SAD are banking on the revival of the social compact between the former's base among Hindus and the latter's once-formidable farmer constituency. Much will depend on whether their renewed chemistry will enthuse their traditional voters in a crowded battlefield.Amit Shah: BJP-SAD pact not merely political, it’s an emotional bondPM Modi, whose meeting with Badal in Parliament complex on Aug 7 was the first clear indication of the tie-up, was emphatic in his endorsement of what he called a "natural alliance"."Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first. I am extremely delighted that Shiromani Akali Dal returns to NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," home minister Amit Shah said. Modi will be in Moga on Dec 8 to attend a rally to mark Parkash Singh Badal's birth anniversary. Shah said, "The alliance between BJP and SAD is not merely political; it is an emotional bond rooted in mutual trust and Punjab's history. NDA is now complete with Akali Dal's return.""A tidal wave has started today," SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal said, claiming the alliance would bag 100 seats in the 117-member assembly.Shah was quick to emphasise the alliance's emotive symbolism of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood in the border state with a history of social tensions and spells of militancy; Nabin too described it as a "natural alliance", and Badal invoked his father's description of their ties as "nau-maas da rishta" (together like nail and flesh). Jana Sangh, BJP's political predecessor, had allied with Akalis too. Shah's announcement that SAD will be the senior partner - Badal being the obvious CM face even though no such announcement was made - despite its shrinking base, underscores BJP's recognition that its Sikh ally should lead the alliance and look like a credible contender for office. The BJP, however, is expected to contest a bigger number of seats than the 23 it used to in the alliance.Akali's 10-year stint in office, with BJP as junior partner, ended in 2017 with their massive defeat at the hands of Congress as a big chunk of its core voters revolted over the government's alleged mishandling of sacrilege incidents and issues of drug abuse and corruption, creating a fertile ground for AAP's rise and its subsequent sweep in 2022.Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot said, "It's a compromised alliance, a desperate alliance. BJP and SAD have not revealed why they parted ways six years ago, what were the reasons that SAD and BJP left each other. Have the GoI and BJP given any assurance to the country on MSP, have they apologised for the three black farm laws, and what is the SAD view on the hundreds of protesters who died on the Delhi border in the farmers' protest? Both parties had no political space left in the state, and they have chosen to join hands."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review
content: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah said Tuesday that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, which allows pilgrims to travel visa-free to a holy site associated with Guru Nanak across the border in Pakistan, will be opened as soon as national security concerns are resolved.Responding to a media query at a news briefing, where he announced the BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal alliance ahead of the Punjab polls, he said national security should not be politicised, noting that it is the Modi government which built it.Government had closed the corridor after Operation Sindoor over security concerns. Shah said Kartarpur went to Pakistan after India's partition due to Congress' carelessness."As soon as this (national security) issue is completely resolved, we will immediately reopen Kartarpur Sahib with full honour," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Tamil Nadu To Sign 'Over Rs 50,000 Crore' In Fresh Deals Across 70 Pacts At Chennai Investor Meet
content: Tamil Nadu is gearing up to unveil around 70 investment agreements worth more than Rs 50,000 crore ($5.38 billion) across diverse industrial sectors during a major investor conclave in Chennai, Reuters said while quoting sources. Designed to accelerate industrial expansion and convert earlier pledges into active ground-level projects, the fresh commitments span manufacturing, clean energy, electronics, industrial infrastructure, engineering, and textiles. Key Investors and Sectoral Push Hosted under the second edition of the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave, the event brings together global corporations and domestic industry leaders looking to establish or scale up operations in the southern state. Among the prominent names expected to ink fresh memoranda of understanding are Brazilian electric motor giant WEG, two-wheeler major Royal Enfield, and German industrial firm Vautid. Alongside signing new pacts, the Vijay-led state government is scheduled to lay foundation stones for projects valued at roughly Rs 8,000 crore ($860 million) and inaugurate six completed facilities. Crucially, project activity is slated to extend beyond traditional metropolitan hubs around Chennai into emerging industrial corridors across the state. Turning Pledges Into Capital Expenditure The push reflects Tamil Nadu’s sharper focus on execution—ensuring that headline announcements translate swiftly into land allotments, factory construction, and jobs. In August 2026, the state had already secured nearly 100 agreements valued at Rs 67,452 crore ($7.25 billion) with global players including Saint-Gobain and Super Micro Computer. More recently, official figures released ahead of the Chennai conclave showed that Tamil Nadu finalised 112 investment pacts worth Rs 1,14,812 crore (roughly $12.35 billion) across 23 sectors between May and November 2026, projected to generate over 1.32 lakh jobs—with 83 of those projects already reaching the land confirmation stage. Fierce Interstate Race for Global Supply Chains The latest investment drive comes amid intense competition among southern Indian states to capture global supply chain shifts. Earlier this month, neighbouring Andhra Pradesh announced major commitments including a Rs 42,600 crore ($4.59 billion) coal-to-gas project by Reliance Industries and a Rs 18,600 crore ($2 billion) second manufacturing plant from Kia India. Anchored by its reputation as the “Detroit of Asia” and home to manufacturing giants such as Hyundai, Renault, Foxconn, and Tata Electronics, Tamil Nadu is banking on this multi-billion-dollar wave of fresh capital to safeguard its industrial lead and strengthen its export ecosystem.

headline: ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic
content: NEW DELHI: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic, while nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in vitamin B12, pointing to a wider nutritional challenge that goes beyond iron deficiency, a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has found.The findings fill a key data gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which did not include anaemia estimates. Government had subsequently said these would be drawn from an independent ICMR survey based on venous blood samples.The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition's SAMPADA survey for 2023-25 found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years. NFHS-5 reported a prevalence of 57 per cent among women in the same age group. The figures, however, are not directly comparable because the surveys covered different groups of women and used different testing methods.State-wise estimates showed sharp regional disparities, with Andaman and Nicobar recording the highest prevalence at 81.2 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years.The burden was also high in other groups. Anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19 years. Among children, 41.8 per cent of those aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent of those aged 5-9 years were anaemic. The prevalence was 43.6 per cent among pregnant women and 58.1 per cent among lactating women. Among adult men aged 20-59 years, it stood at 22 per cent.B12 deficiency was more widespread among adolescents, affecting 65.4 per cent of girls and 66.1 per cent of boys. It was found in 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of adult men aged 20-59 years. The prevalence stood at 63.1 per cent among pregnant women and 51.8 per cent among lactating women.Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, despite anaemia affecting 46.3 per cent and 55.9 per cent of these groups, respectively. Iron deficiency itself remained common, affecting 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age, 29.6 per cent of pregnant women and 23 per cent of children aged 12-59 months, compared with 10 per cent for adolescent boys."Not all anaemia is caused by nutritional deficiencies such as iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, chronic kidney disease, tuberculosis and cancer can also cause anaemia. Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," said Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology, AIIMS."We have been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme to develop simple algorithms to identify such cases," Seth added.The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories, drawing data from over 81,000 households and analysing over 1.7 lakh blood samples.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Young People Hand Their Plan For A Climate-Ready Meghalaya To The Government.
content: Shillong, 24th of November, 2026 : Young people from across Meghalaya presented 15 recommendations today on how the State can keep health care, schooling and mental wellbeing within reach as floods, landslides and heat become more common. Drawing on what they have seen in their own communities, they also designed practical solutions of their own, from landslide warning lights to cooling curtains woven from pineapple leaves. The report, Young People’s Action Group: A Youth-Led Agenda for Meghalaya, was presented at the State Guest House, Taragarh, Shillong. UNICEF Assam hosted the event with the Department of Sports & Youth Affairs (DSYA), Government of Meghalaya, and partner Centre for Policy. “This session is designed so that young people’s recommendations have somewhere to go,” said Dr Madhulika Jonathan, Chief of Field Office, UNICEF Assam. “What we heard today is the first advice from YPAG as an advisory platform, and we will take it forward with the Department through the work plan.” The Young People’s Action Group (YPAG) aims to give young people aged 15 to 29 a regular role in policymaking, public decisions and community action in Meghalaya, with a focus on climate change. UNICEF Assam and NE States presented the concept to the Hon’ble Chief Minister in 2023. It has since rolled it out with support from the Government of Meghalaya and civil society partner Centre for Policy, Meghalaya (Living Roots Foundation). In July 2026, a State Government review chaired by the Additional Chief Secretary & Development Commissioner named YPAG a youth advisory group, to carry young people’s ideas to Government across departments. YPAG was launched in May 2026. In total, 138 young people helped choose its focus, and more than 72,000 were reached online. Then 105 young people from 11 districts took part in workshops in Shillong, Nongpoh, Tura and Jowai. “Distance should not decide whether someone survives,” one participant said. headline: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
content: NEW DELHI: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval called on Maldives defence minister Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting and discussed ways to strengthen defence and security cooperation between the two countries.This was the first high-level contact between the two countries after President Mohamed Muizzu's visit to Pakistan recently. That visit raised eyebrows here as Maldives signed 20 MoUs with Pakistan, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation. Muizzu had also called for the resumption of the Saarc summit process during his visit.Doval is in Male for the CSC, which was formed to promote closer cooperation between member states on vital matters of security and to strengthen partnerships for enhancing regional security in the Indian Ocean Region.Originally launched in 2011 as a trilateral maritime security dialogue involving India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, the grouping later inducted Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles into its fold.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: PM Modi, Merz say India-EU FTA will unlock new opportunities
content: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi spoke to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday and reviewed the growing momentum in the India-Germany Strategic Partnership, while discussing ways to unlock new opportunities in trade and investment, defence and advanced technologies."Had a productive conversation with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. India and Germany will continue to work closely together to address global challenges and promote peace, stability and a rules-based international order," PM Modi wrote on X (formerly Twitter).The talks took place ahead of PM Modi's visit to Brussels next month -- on his way back from G20 in the US — to sign the India-EU FTA. The government has not yet confirmed if PM Modi will have a stopover in Berlin.PM Modi and Merz noted in their talks that the agreement would unlock several new opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment."As India and Germany celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across key sectors, including defence and advanced technologies," an Indian readout said. According to the readout, the leaders exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest."They agreed to continue working closely together to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order. They also emphasised the importance of continued cooperation at multilateral forums in addressing contemporary global challenges," it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Akali Dal-BJP alliance a necessity, not compulsion: Avinash Rai Khanna
content: Describing the SAD-BJP partnership as a reflection of Punjab’s social and political aspirations, senior BJP leader and former MP Avinash Rai Khanna on Monday said the alliance was not merely a political compulsion, but a continuation of deep-rooted historical and social ties between the two parties.Interacting with industrialists, traders and members of the public in Amritsar to gather suggestions for the BJP’s 2027 Assembly election manifesto, Khanna said the renewed understanding between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal was a demand of people, who wanted to rid Punjab of the AAP and the Congress.“Our continued public interactions during ground campaigning have strongly brought out the demand for this alliance. The SAD-BJP alliance is a public demand, not a political compulsion. The people of Punjab want the two parties, bound by deep historical and social ties, to come together and offer an alternative to the AAP and the Congress,” he said.Khanna’s remarks assume significance as the renewed SAD-BJP understanding is likely to reshape the BJP’s organisational approach in Punjab. Party workers, who have spent the past six years building an independent political base following the 2020 split, will now have to adjust to a changed political equation involving renewed coordination with their former allies.Though senior leaders, including Khanna, avoided commenting on the changed poll pitch by party — which until recently was set to contest on all 117 seats in Punjab independently — he did mention that seat-sharing and other political equations will be cleared in coming days.The alliance has united two former partners at the leadership level, but its acceptance among party cadres, farmer organisations and different sections of Punjab’s electorate remains a question to be tested.He maintained that the relationship between the two parties went beyond electoral calculations, drawing strength from decades of shared history, social bonds and mutual understanding. Leading the preparation of the party’s election manifesto and public consultations, Khanna along with Shwait Malik, Ashwini Sekhri and senior party leadership from Amritsar held meetings with industrialists, traders and other members of civil society. They also launched toll-free mobile numbers for the public to share and drop suggestions for the drafting of election manifesto. Emphasising the BJP’s priorities for Punjab, Khanna identified the fight against drug addiction, quality education and accessible healthcare as key focus areas.

headline: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
content: To linger in Banaras is to linger in another era, an era which one cannot quite date by century," wrote Harvard scholar Diana L Eck in 'Banaras: City of Light'. The inaugural CII Banaras Biennale, which opens on Nov 27 and is on view till Dec 31, gives art lovers a new excuse to linger in one of India's oldest cities.Despite its noisy, crowded lanes and walls with their own artwork of paan stains, the city is more than the Instagram reels of Ganga aarti and sunset boat rides suggest. Aptly themed 'Kashi/Light; City as Sensorium', the biennale seeks to put Banaras on the cultural map, but without treating it as a mere backdrop. "The biennale is envisioned as a long-term commitment to positioning Banaras as a global capital of living culture," says Madhav Singhania, chairman of the steering committee of CII Banaras Biennale 2026. The Biennale spans visual art, textiles, craft, music, performance and scholarship, with events spread across ghats and galleries.That approach is rooted in the idea that the city's past and present need not be kept apart. At the centre of the exhibition is Bharatiya Kala Bhavan (BKB) inside the Banaras Hindu University campus, where lead curator Gayatri Sinha has chosen to place contemporary work among the museum's extensive collection of more than one lakh objects. "Can we make the ancient and the contemporary conversational?" she asks.The question is the aesthetic thread that ties the biennale together. There is a more literal dhaga, too - of silk and zari. Pramod Kumar KG, who is curating the textile and craft section, is looking to connect Banaras's mastery of the loom with contemporary fashion and design.BKB's collection began with art historian Rai Krishna Das, who started collecting in 1920. Its present building was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1962. The main gallery houses Sinha's exhibition, 'The Cycle of Life: Samsara', which looks at life, death, livelihood and renunciation in Banaras. "If you visit Varanasi, sooner or later, this integration between life and death, between life, livelihood and renunciation, between the appropriation of a certain sensibility and the letting go of your human education becomes very important."Sinha draws from BKB's impressive collection of terracotta sculptures, miniature paintings, textiles and coins, and makes connections with contemporary art. Terracotta heads, some nearly 2,000 years old, are shown alongside a contemporary work in the medium by Ravinder Reddy. Manu Parekh, whose artistic practice has repeatedly returned to Banaras, also features in the exhibition. An 11ft-by-11ft tapestry based on his work, woven by Karishma Swali's Chanakya School of Craft, evokes the city at night.Biennales in India have usually been led by artists, curators or foundations, but this one brings industry and cultural institutions such as the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and Sunil Munjal's Serendipity Arts together. "This is sort of curatorially led, but industry-driven," says Tarana Sawhney, chairperson of the CII Art & Culture Committee.The intention is not simply to parachute a festival into the city and leave. "We didn't want to create a festival that just went in, kind of engaged with the city and left," Sawhney says. Skilling and textile development initiatives are part of a larger effort that will continue after visitors have gone. For Sinha, the work is ultimately about bringing objects, histories and artistic practices together without erasing their differences. In Banaras, where the old and the everyday share the same streets, that conversation is already part of the city.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Turning the pages of glorious past in Amritsar
content: History came alive through rare books, old newspapers and precious manuscripts at the Bhai Gurdas Library inside Guru Nanak Dev Univeristy during an exhibition, “Amritsar 450: Exhibition of Rare Books and Manuscripts”.To commemorate the 450th foundation anniversary of the holy city, which falls in October 2027, the university is hosting a series of cultural events.For visitors, it was more than an exhibition of old publications — an opportunity to travel through time and discover Amritsar’s rich past through the written records that have survived generations, documenting its religious institutions, historical personalities, political movements and cultural evolution.Among the fascinating exhibits were a series of publications and historical records on Maharaja Duleep Singh dating back to 1890, History of the War in Afghanistan (1843), a historical account concerning the First Anglo-Afghan War (1839–1842), fought between British India and Afghanistan and Religious Magazine (1835).Publications such as Guide to the Darbar Sahib (1905), Report Shri Darbar Sahib (1929) and Tawarikh Shri Amritsar, authored by eminent Sikh historian Giani Gian Singh, documenting the foundation of Amritsar and the historical and religious significance of Sri Harmandir Sahib.The collection also featured the Punjab District Gazetteer: Amritsar District (1947), historical accounts of Gurdwara Shahid Ganj Sahib and Gurdwara Panja Sahib, and literature documenting important chapters of Punjab’s political history. Particularly significant were the dated editions of Gadar Hindustan newspaper (1930), a Punjabi newspaper associated with the Ghadar Party, the revolutionary organisation founded by Indian expatriates in the United States to campaign for India’s independence from British rule. It was published from San Fransisco. It carried political commentary, news and patriotic poetry.Another historically significant exhibit was Khoon de Sohile (1920), a 306-page publication brought out by Akal Agency, Lahore, documenting events and atrocities during the Martial Law period in Punjab in 1919. The rare publication offers an important archival glimpse into one of the most turbulent chapters of Punjab’s colonial history.Registrar Prof (Dr) KS Chahal inaugurated the exhibition and appreciated the library team for bringing together an impressive collection of historical literature. He encouraged students, researchers and visitors to explore these invaluable resources and understand their significance.The university’s Amritsar 450 celebrations will also showcase Punjab’s living heritage through a folk art exhibition featuring phulkari, jewellery, folk costumes, household articles and traditional crafts. Products made by students from the departments of apparel and textile technology.

headline: Govt plans multi-year motor insurance for cars, bikes; no insurance, no fuel pilot at 10 petrol pumps in NCR
content: NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry is proposing a series of measures to address the problem of uninsured vehicles on roads, including introducing a single premium for four- and six-year insurance policies for cars and two-wheelers, respectively.Separately, the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has asked road transport and petroleum ministries to launch a pilot of the ‘no insurance, no fuel’ initiative at five petrol pumps each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh which have automated number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that can identify vehicles and help verify their insurance status.TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry is also working on the plan to link premiums to traffic offences recorded against vehicle owners in the previous year.The proposed changes are aimed at encouraging more vehicle owners to maintain valid insurance coverage and improving compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act. Under the proposal, insurance premiums could increase based on specific traffic violations recorded against a vehicle in the preceding year, making repeated offenders pay more for insurance.The ministry is also examining options to revise the base insurance rates for specified vehicle categories, including electric vehicles, as part of a broader review of the existing premium structure.Insurance data show that nearly 25 crore active vehicles have valid insurance, which is around 81% of the vehicles that are currently running across the country. While over 90% of heavy commercial vehicles have valid insurance, it’s around 88% in the case of cars. The compliance is least at around 57% in case of three-wheelers and it’s around 80% in case of two-wheelers.Supreme Court had earlier issued directions to govt to examine measures to ensure that vehicles plying on roads have valid insurance coverage. Third-party motor insurance is mandatory under the Motor Vehicles Act. Vehicles without valid insurance pose a serious risk in case of crashes, leaving accident victims and their families vulnerable to inadequate compensation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Dalai Lama, office allotted bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi
content: NEW DELHI: The Centre has allotted a Type-7 government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama and his office, Gaden Phodrang, providing a permanent base for his visits to the national capital. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile Tuesday described the move as a significant gesture of support towards the spiritual leader and the Tibetan community.Though housing and urban affairs ministry officials did not respond to queries, it is learnt that the ministry had transferred the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane to the ministry of external affairs last year after receiving a request. People aware of the development said usually, such transfers of accommodation are initially for three years and can be extended.According to news agency ANI, speaker of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile Dolma Tsering described the development as "very welcome news". She said the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital more convenient and provide greater comfort during his stay in Delhi.Welcoming the decision, Tibetan parliament-in-exile member and standing committee member Choedak Gyatso said, "government of India has given us refuge when we had no country. We lost our country, and it gave us Dharamshala when we had no land and gave us schools and many institutions that can preserve our culture."Recalling his recent official visit to Delhi, during which he met MPs, Gyatso said he had personally visited the bungalow along with the Tibetan deputy speaker and described the opportunity as a great honour.Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011 after he voluntarily relinquished political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership. The trust is responsible for preserving the institution of the Dalai Lama and supporting his spiritual and humanitarian work.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Health minister seeks vigilance inquiry into sale of illegal cosmetics
content: Kozhikode: Health minister K Muraleedharan on Tuesday said that he sent a letter to the home department seeking a vigilance inquiry into spurious fairness creams and cosmetics entering the market. Addressing reporters, he stated that the probe was requested amid growing suspicions and complaints about fake cosmetics.When asked about reports that the fairness cream which led to a 17-year-old girl from Malappuram suffering renal complications was manufactured in Pakistan, he said that no concrete evidence had been received to substantiate the claim. The information was so far limited to reports aired by television channels, he added.The minister said that the health department wants a comprehensive investigation to trace the origin of the products and determine whether they were being manufactured or marketed without valid licences.“No unauthorised products or cosmetics without govt approval will be allowed to be sold, irrespective of the brand name under which they are marketed,” he said.The drugs control department has been directed to intensify inspections, and strict action would be taken against any violations brought to govt’s attention, Muraleedharan said.Meanwhile, Areekode police has found that the customer care number linked to the Ftune fairness cream, allegedly laced with mercury, used by the 17-year-old, belonged to a woman in Kasaragod.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kozhikode | Silver Rate in Kozhikode | Bank Holidays in Kozhikode | Public Holidays in KozhikodeStay updated with the latest Kozhikode news. Download the TOI App.

headline: Punjab Assembly polls: Jaggu Bhagwanpuria’s wife is family pick
content: With the family backing her, Dr Amandeep Kaur, the wife of incarcerated gangster Jaggu Bhagwanpuria, is set to contest the Assembly polls as an Independent from the Dera Baba Nanak seat.A US returnee and former dentistry student, Kaur has now made politics her sole focus. She tells supporters to address her husband as Jagdeep Singh Athwal, seemingly oblivious to the fact that a change in name does not necessarily guarantee a change in fortunes. “When someone calls him Bhagwanpuria, my heart sinks. He is Jagdeep Singh Athwal. Nobody is born a gangster. He wants to start life afresh. Let us give him a chance at redemption,” Kaur said.She commands a significant following. Elders from neighbouring villages bow in reverence, touch her feet and take pictures with her. She is also at the centre of all discussions, be it financial or political.Dera Baba Nanak comprises nearly 250 villages. Kaur has already reached out to a majority of sarpanches, seeking support for “better healthcare, education facilities, employment generation and eradication of drugs”.“I want to improve the life of the villagers,” Kaur said with the poise of a seasoned politician. Fresh out of her teens, she is already looking at the long run: “I am not thinking of the next elections, but far, far beyond that.”

headline: Akali Dal, BJP reunite: Punjab ex-CM Capt Amarinder Singh’s absence raises eyebrows
content: Senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader and former Punjab CM Capt Amarinder Singh’s absence during the announcement of the alliance between his party and the Shiromani Akali Dal in Delhi has raised eyebrows.The leader was initially among the strongest votaries of the alliance. He even argued in its favour when the BJP’s entire rank and file was batting for a solo fight. Whether he was informed about or invited to the event could not be confirmed.His absence comes in the backdrop of his recent displeasure with the BJP for not having kept him in the loop on any political discussion. In a recent interview with The Tribune, the former CM candidly disclosed he had expressed his reservations on not being consulted by the party leadership despite his six decades of political experience in Punjab during a meeting with PM Narendra Modi.In the run-up to the alliance this week, the former CM had changed his stance and expressed his doubts that the alliance, if it were to materialise, would make any headway as the Akali Dal had fragmented into many splinter parties. His changed stance has set off speculation about his future course of action.

headline: India’s space economy projected to rise to $40-45 billion by 2036: Minister Jitendra Singh
content: NEW DELHI: India's space economy is set for a major expansion, with its value projected to rise from nearly $9 billion at present to $40-45 billion by 2036, as private companies will be the key drivers of this growth, space, science and technology minister Jitendra Singh said on Tuesday.Addressing the 5th India International Space Conclave 2026 here, Singh said from a handful of startups some years ago, their number has gone up to nearly 400-500, showing the scale of expansion and transformation in the space sector over the past few years. He attributed the growth to a series of space reforms initiated under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi.The minister said the establishment of New Space India Limited (NSIL), the creation of the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), and the decision to open the space sector to private players marked a turning point in India's space journey. He cited Skyroot Aerospace's maiden launch vehicle flight, its multi-mission launch agreements and attainment of unicorn status, alongside advances by firms such as Agnikul, which are developing indigenous propulsion systems, rocket engines, earth-observation solutions and satellite imaging technologies.Singh called for greater corporate participation in scientific research, urging businesses to make better use of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding and develop a stronger culture of philanthropy for science. “What you spend on research is also a worship,” he said, stressing that scientific research should receive greater support from private businesses.During a question-and-answer session at the event, the minister pointed out that India must continue to strengthen indigenous capabilities, with the guiding approach centred on indigenous sources, indigenous technology and indigenous projects, while remaining open to mutually beneficial international partnerships. “Investments from domestic private players have taken some time to pick up initially. So we need to scale them up,” Singh said, urging industry participants to take a more active role in bringing capital into the sector.Fearless legend or grounded realist?
