headline: Hit by vehicle, brick-kiln worker rescues injured owl at Hisar village
content: A brick kiln employee rescued an injured barn owl from stray dogs on the outskirts of Kirtan village in the district after it was hit by an unknown vehicle.According to information, Jagdish Verma, a superviser at a brick-kiln spotted the injured bird lying on the roadside when stray dogs were barking at it and trying to attack. He took the injured owl to his office and looked after it for several hours. He also offered it an egg and chicken, but the injured bird did not eat anything.Verma later informed the Wildlife Department officials in Hisar. The Wildlife Department Inspector Dinesh Jangra took the owl and safely rehabilitated in the Deer park in Dhansu village.The barn owl is a nocturnal bird of prey commonly found in agricultural areas and semi-urban settlements across Haryana and other parts of North India.

headline: Himachal’s Navodaya Vidyalayas alumni felicitate Kangra DC Hemraj Bairwa
content: Former students of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas from Kangra and Hamirpur districts organised a farewell-cum-felicitation ceremony in honour of Kangra Deputy Commissioner Hemraj Bairwa at McLeodganj.Bairwa has recently been appointed Deputy Secretary in the Union Ministry of Power. A former student of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Dausa, Rajasthan, he was warmly welcomed by members of the Navodaya Alumni Association.The gathering was attended by former students from Kangra and Hamirpur, including several professionals serving in administrative, medical and academic fields. The alumni lauded Bairwa’s tenure as Kangra Deputy Commissioner and appreciated his people-centric initiatives and contributions to public welfare.Kangra’s art fraternity bids farewell to DCThe art and culture fraternity of Kangra also organised a farewell for the outgoing Deputy Commissioner, expressing gratitude for his support in preserving and promoting the district’s rich cultural heritage. Members of the fraternity appreciated his encouragement for initiatives aimed at showcasing Kangra’s distinctive artistic traditions and cultural legacy.

headline: Over 600 students take part in youth festival at Khanpur Kalan university
content: The three-day UNIFEST-2026, organised by Bhagat Phool Singh Mahila Vishwavidyalaya (BPSMV), Khanpur Kalan, from November 21 to 23, concluded on Sunday amid great enthusiasm, vibrant cultural performances and a celebration of Haryana’s rich cultural heritage.Government Girls College, Madludha won the overall trophy, while BPSMV, Khanpur Kalan, secured the runner-up position. Professor (Dr) Ram Pal Saini, Vice-Chancellor, Chaudhary Ranbir Singh University (CRSU), Jind, attended the valedictory ceremony as the chief guest. In his address, he highlighted the importance of the Haryanvi culture, folk art and traditions, and encouraged young people to remain connected with their cultural heritage.Addressing the gathering, Dr Ram Pal Saini said the Haryanvi culture is a symbol of identity and pride. It represents a rich legacy of folk songs, ragnis, traditional arts and cultural values. He encouraged the students to take pride in their language, culture and traditions. His deep attachment to Haryanvi culture was evident when, despite holding the position of Vice-Chancellor, he presented a beautiful Haryanvi ragni on stage. His performance enthralled the audience and added a special charm to the ceremony. He further said that India is a young nation and every young citizen has a responsibility to contribute towards the country’s progress. He also emphasised that Haryanvi culture and its rich traditions can play an important role in this journey. Professor Anjana Garg from Maharshi Dayanand University (MDU), Rohtak, attended the ceremony as the guest of honour. In her address, she said that art is a powerful medium of human expression and sensitivity. She encouraged young people to remain connected with art, literature, music and cultural activities alongside their academic pursuits, as these activities help develop creativity and enable students to recognise their hidden talents.Haryanvi folk artist Sombir Kathurwal also enthralled the audience with his impressive performance, adding vibrant colours of folk culture to the ceremony. Professor Sudesh, Vice-Chancellor, said the enthusiastic participation and outstanding performances of students during UNIFEST had once again demonstrated that young women possess immense talent. What they need is the right platform, encouragement and opportunities to showcase their abilities. The Vice-Chancellor announced that special workshops would be organised for students who demonstrate exceptional talent in various competitions. These workshops would help them polish their skills, identify their interests and explore opportunities to pursue art and cultural activities as a career.On this occasion, the Dean of Students’ Welfare (DSW) also appreciated the active participation, creativity and enthusiasm of students. More than 600 students participated in 35 cultural and literary competitions during the three-day UNIFEST, held from November 21 to 23. The participants showcased their artistic abilities and creativity through various events including dance, singing, theatre, ragni, mimicry, debate, elocution, painting, mehndi, rangoli, collage and poster making.UNIFEST-2026 concluded with a renewed commitment to identifying and nurturing the hidden talents of young women, promoting Haryana’s rich folk culture and inspiring the younger generation to remain connected with their cultural roots while contributing towards nation-building.

headline: Chandigarh: Town Planning Department orders removal of DG sets from DLF Phase I parks
content: The Haryana Town and Country Planning Department has directed the removal of heavy diesel generator (DG) sets installed in parks, green belts and open spaces in DLF Phase I, Gurugram, citing violations of the approved layout plan of the 589-acre residential colony.In an affidavit filed before the National Green Tribunal (NGT), District Town Planner (Enforcement), Gurugram, Amit Madholia, stated that field officials had found DG sets installed at locations not earmarked for such facilities.Through a communication dated November 3, the department directed DLF Ltd and the DLF City Residents Welfare Association to remove the installations and restore the affected areas in accordance with the approved layout plan.It warned that non-compliance within the prescribed timeframe could invite coercive action under Section 3B of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, including removal and confiscation of the DG sets wherever legally permissible.The action follows an application filed by the DLF Phase I A Block Residents Welfare Association before the NGT's Principal Bench in New Delhi.The department told the tribunal that the matter involved not merely the installation of generator sets but also violations of the sanctioned land-use pattern. Parks, green belts and open spaces cannot be used for purposes not permitted under the approved layout plan.DLF Phase I is a plotted residential colony spread across 589.57 acres and developed under 24 licences. The department also placed the approved layout plan before the tribunal, marking the locations where DG sets had allegedly been installed without authorisation. The latest revised layout plan for DLF Phases I to III was approved on July 19, 2018.In its response, DLF Ltd denied responsibility for the installation, operation or maintenance of the alleged 30 generator sets. It stated that DLF Utilities Ltd was responsible only for horticulture and cleaning as part of the general upkeep of parks, while DLF Ltd was the developer of the colony.

headline: Kapal Mochan mela concludes, 7 lakh devotees take dip in sarovars
content: The five-day inter-state Shri Kapal Mochan-Adi Badri mela concluded peacefully with about seven lakh devotees taking dip in holy sarovers in Kapal Mochan mela, near Vyaspur town of Yamunanagar district on the occasion of Kartik Purnima on Tuesday with a belief to attain moksha.Pilgrims from Punjab, Haryana and other states arrived at Kapal Mochan mela and took dip in Kapal Mochan, Rin Mochan and Surajkund sarovars soon after 12 am on Tuesday.After taking bath, the pilgrims also performed the religious ritual of lightening earthen lamps on the banks of the sarovars and offered prayers at temples and gurdwara on the mela premises.This mela is considered as a symbol of unity and integrity of the people of different religions. The shopkeepers associated with the trade of stainless steel and brass utensils did brisk business on this occasion as most of the pilgrims bought utensils from here as a symbol of good omen (shagun).Chief Minister Nayba Singh Saini also visited the mela and Deputy Commissioner Preeti presented him a portrait of Guru Nanak Dev.“This year, the mela was held from November 20 to 24, 2026. Under the guidance and supervision of Deputy Commissioner Preeti, extensive arrangements were made for smooth conduct of the five-day Mela. The mela went off peacefully and devotees felt satisfied and praised the arrangements made for the devotees,” said Yamunanagar DIPRO Dr Manoj Kumar.He said despite the massive crowds, there was no inconvenience anywhere due to the elaborate arrangements made by the district administration. “Every devotee bathed thoroughly in all three sarovars and performed the rituals with full rites,” said Dr Manoj Kumar.After 12 am on November 24, when the devotees began bathing in the holy sarovars, Superintendent of Police Kamaldeep Goyal, SDM Vyaspur-cum-Mela Administrator Dr Kuldeep Singh, along with other officers personally visited the three sarovars and inspected the arrangements. The SP asked the police personnel and volunteers deployed on all roads and sarovars to be more vigilant.According to information, since ancient times, people from various religions and sects have had a special faith in visiting the Kapal Mochan Tirtha Raj, a land of gods, goddesses, sages, sufi saints, and gurus.

headline: Guru Nanak’s teachings remain guiding light for humanity: Governor
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta on Tuesday said that the timeless teachings of Guru Nanak Dev were a guiding light for humanity, inspiring generations to uphold the values of equality, selfless service, universal brotherhood and social harmony. He interacted with mediapersons after paying obeisance at Gurdwara Singh Sabha at Saproon in Solan district on the auspicious occasion of Parkash Purb.The Governor extended warm greetings to people, particularly the Sikhs, and said that Guru Nanak Dev’s three fundamental principles — ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhako’ — provided a meaningful foundation for building a compassionate, equitable and harmonious society.He said that the unparalleled sacrifices of Sikh Gurus and the immense contribution of the Sikh community to the freedom struggle, national security and nation-building would continue to inspire generations.He highlighted the initiatives taken by the Central Government and said that the opening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor in 2019 fulfilled a decades-old aspiration of the Sikh community.He said that the institution of Veer Bal Diwas on December 26 to commemorate the supreme sacrifice of the Sahibzadas and the initiatives such as the Hemkund Sahib ropeway project, Seva Bhoj Yojana and efforts to secure justice for the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots reflected the Centre’s commitment towards preserving the glorious Sikh heritage, respecting religious sentiments and ensuring the welfare of the community.The Governor said that Hindu and Sikh communities shared a profound cultural, spiritual and historical legacy. He cautioned against forces attempting to create divisions among people on religious lines and urged citizens to remain vigilant against such designs and collectively safeguard the unity, integrity and social fabric of the nation.

headline: Akhilesh Yadav's Open Letter, Then A Move That Overlaps Congress Wishlist
content: In the seat-sharing arrangement, the Congress wants a hundred seats, Samajwadi is reluctant to spare more than 26, and the gap between these two numbers tells you everything about the alliance dynamics.

headline: Guru Nanak Parkash Purb observed with zeal in Sirsa
content: The Parkash Purb of Guru Nanak Dev was celebrated with great devotion and enthusiasm in Sirsa, with religious programmes and a tree plantation drive highlighting his teachings of love, equality, brotherhood and selfless service.Baba Sarsainath Sewa Trust organised a tree plantation drive at Sirsa Railway Station. Saplings were planted at the Government Railway Police Station and the Indian Railways parcel office.GRP SHO Ranbir Singh Bhatia and Commercial Superintendent Umesh Verma said Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings continue to guide humanity. They stressed that planting trees and protecting the environment are important responsibilities for everyone. Trust president Ravinder Saini urged people to serve humanity and protect nature.Meanwhile, a prabhat pheri was organised at Dera Baba Bhuman Shah in Sanghar Sadha village under the leadership of Baba Brahm Das. A large number of devotees participated in the procession, singing Gurbani and chanting ‘Satnam Sri Waheguru’. A beautifully decorated Palki Sahib was the main attraction.Addressing the devotees, Baba Brahm Das highlighted Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings of ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhako’, urging people to remember God, earn honestly and share with the needy

headline: ACME Foundation distributes nutritional kits to TB patients in Kangra, Himachal
content: Emphasising the importance of nutrition in tuberculosis (TB) treatment and recovery, the New Delhi-based ACME Welfare Foundation distributed 37 nutritional kits among TB patients from Fatehpur, Shahpur and Nurpur blocks of Kangra district under the Nikshay Mitra initiative.A workshop on ‘Nutrition and TB’ was also organised at the Conference Hall of the Chief Medical Officer’’s office in Dharamsala. Health officials, representatives of the Inner Wheel Club Dharamshala, TB patients and community members participated in the programme.Seven patients received nutritional kits from Chief Medical Officer Dr Omesh Bharti and other dignitaries, while the remaining 30 kits were delivered to beneficiaries through health department staff.A special session highlighted the nutritional benefits of millets, including ragi, bajra, jowar, kodo and kutki, and their role in maintaining a balanced diet. Sadhvi Pandey, Director of ACME Welfare Foundation and Tashvika India Food Private Limited, explained the nutritional value of millet-based products and demonstrated how they could be incorporated into everyday meals.Dr Bharti appreciated the foundation’’s initiative and said community participation was crucial to achieving the goal of a TB-free India. District TB Officer Dr RK Sood also urged voluntary organisations and citizens to come forward as Nikshay Mitras and extend nutritional support to TB patients throughout their treatment.

headline: Poll pact hits hurdle in Uttar Pradesh as Congress seeks over 100 seats, SP offers just 26, names 5 candidates
content: Sharp differences emerged between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on Tuesday, with the Congress staking claim to over 100 seats in the 403-member House and the Akhilesh Yadav-led party offering it just 26.Even as the talks remained inconclusive, the SP released its first list of five candidates. The party fielded Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mehboob Ali from Amroha and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur.The Congress, dissatisfied with the offer, maintained that its share should not be less than what it was allotted in the 2017 elections. Uttar Pradesh Congress working president Imran Masood asserted that the party was not “begging” for seats from anyone.The differences surfaced during the second round of seat-sharing talks between the two INDIA bloc allies in the national capital on Tuesday. The meeting, which lasted around three and a half hours, saw discussions on the electoral equations in nearly half of the 403 Assembly constituencies.Sources said of the 26 seats offered by the SP, the Congress had won only two, Rampur Khas and Pharenda, in the 2022 Assembly elections. Of the remaining 24 seats, the BJP had won 23 and its ally Apna Dal (S) one.The Congress had finished second in four of these constituencies— Mathura, Kheragarh, Jagdishpur and Kidwai Nagar. Its candidates had polled fewer than 3,000 votes in constituencies such as Baghpat, Modinagar, Hapur, Jewar, Syana and Khurja.Senior SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav maintained that in 20 of the proposed constituencies, the SP had secured between 60,000 and 70,000 votes in the previous Assembly elections, while the Congress had managed around 2,000 votes. The SP believes its voter base could help the Congress win these seats. The Congress, however, has been negotiating on the basis of the 2017 seat-sharing arrangement and the 2024 LS election results.Party sources said the SP, despite being in power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017, had allotted around 105 seats to the Congress. The party sees little reason to settle for a smaller share this time, particularly after its improved performance in the 2024 LS elections, when the SP won 37 seats and the Congress six. The Congress has handed over a list of over 100 constituencies to the SP, including Assembly segments falling under the parliamentary constituencies it contested in 2024. The party has also cited its organisational expansion in the state to justify its demand.Speaking after the meeting, AICC Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said discussions were being held on each of the 403 constituencies and that nearly half of them had been covered. He said further meetings would be held in the coming days. Besides Gautam, UP Congress president Aradhana Misra-Mona and Masood participated in Tuesday’s deliberations. The next round of talks is likely to be held after two days owing to the engagement ceremony of Misra-Mona’s daughter.Meanwhile, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav asked the Congress to identify potentially winnable constituencies beyond the 26 seats discussed on Tuesday, saying the two parties should focus on electoral arithmetic rather than the number of seats each contests.“This is not about seats, but about victory,” Yadav said, describing the exercise as “seat adjustment” rather than seat-sharing. He proposed that the two parties jointly assess at least two candidates in constituencies with difficult electoral equations and select nominees by consensus to ensure mutual transfer of votes.Yadav said candidates should be projected as INDIA bloc or PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) nominees rather than those belonging to individual parties.Acknowledging the Congress’ support for the PDA in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Yadav said the combined organisational strength of the two parties would be equivalent to preparations for 806 seats in the 403-member Assembly. He also urged prospective candidates to accommodate adjustments, saying the larger objective was to form governments in Uttar Pradesh and subsequently at the Centre.

headline: ‘Navankur’ welcomes freshers at Sonepat’s Puran Murti Vidyapeeth
content: Puran Murti Vidyapeeth hosted its grand freshers’’ festival, “Navankur-2026’’, to welcome new students and provide them with a platform to showcase their talents. The event featured a spectacular blend of music, dance, fashion and entertainment. Live performances by popular Haryanvi artistes Aman Jaji, Ruba Khan and Vishwajeet Chaudhary added to the grandeur of the celebrations. Students danced to the artistes’’ performances late into the night, while the entire campus was filled with excitement and enthusiasm.The programme was inaugurated with the lighting of the ceremonial lamp by the institute’’s Chairman, Dr Vijaypal Nain, his mother, Murti Devi, and Vikram Singh, District Youth Coordinator and Principal of a Government Industrial Training Institute (ITI).Speaking on the occasion, Dr Nain said that the freshers’’ ceremony was a memorable occasion in every student’’s life. Such events provide newcomers with an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the institute’’s environment, develop mutual understanding and showcase their talents. He added that, alongside academics, cultural and creative activities play an important role in the overall development of students.During the ceremony, students showcased their talent, confidence, style and personality through a spectacular ramp walk as part of the title competitions.BTech student Pari was adjudged ‘Star of the Event’, while Akash from the Law Department won the ‘Mr Fresher’ title and BTech student Ananya was crowned ‘Miss Fresher’. Diploma student Daksh was named ‘Mr Energetic’, while Ananya won the ‘Miss Energetic’ title. BTech student Dhruv was adjudged ‘Mr Personality’, while Vani won the ‘Miss Personality’ title. Ankit Sharma from BTech was awarded the ‘Mr Handsome’ title, and Megha from the Law Department was crowned ‘Miss Diva’.The ceremony was attended by institute secretary Gautam Nain; treasurer Bhopal Singh; Managing Director Kapil Bhatia; MD Engineer Sanghdeep Shakya; Director Academics Dr Sweety; Campus Director Kuldeep; Registrar Kanwaljit Singh Sandhu; Director of Puran Murti College of Law Prof TC Rana; Dean Academics Dr Sonia; Principal of Pharmacy Dr Sunita; and Dr Sumita, Principal of Puran Murti Global School Himani Dahiya; and Vice-Principal Varun, along with several other dignitaries.

headline: Sarpanch’s husband shot at in Tarn Taran
content: Sukhbir Singh, husband of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch Manjit Kaur, was shot at and injured allegedly by two brothers on Tuesday. Manjit Kaur is the sarpanch of Nawan Pind Daleke village here.The accused, identified as Mangal Singh and Udam Singh, alias Uday, both residents of Palasaur Kalan village, allegedly intercepted Sukhbir Singh and his wife while they were travelling on a motorcycle from their village to Tarn Taran.According to the police, the accused suspected that Sukhbir Singh had informed the police about Amritpal Singh, a villager allegedly involved in drug peddling. They claimed that Sukhbir Singh had opposed Amritpal Singh’s alleged drug-selling activities, following which the police arrested him.The Sadar police have registered a case against the two accused under Sections 109, 304, 324(4) and 351(B) of the BNS, along with Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act.Sadar SHO Inspector Baljit Singh said a search operation had been launched to arrest the accused.

headline: Ludhiana: Old civic woes, new political equations heat up contest
content: Little has changed for residents of Atam Nagar, who continue to grapple with crumbling roads and parks, overflowing sewage and garbage dumps, traffic congestion and micro industries operating in the mixed land-use spaces.Aam Aadmi Party’s Kulwant Singh Sidhu wrested the seat from then Lok Insaaf Party (LIP) president Simarjit Singh Bains in 2022 with the promise of transforming the region into a model civic hub — a vision that still feels distant.A visit to Dugri exposes the ground reality. The stretch between Gill road and the Dugri police station is in a dilapidated state. The busy section is riddled with potholes or encroached upon by impounded vehicles, as is Gill road, with a 24-year-old motorist even losing his life after his bike skidded off the road on November 4.Garbage dumps near Dugri bridge, the bus stand flyover, Shimlapuri make for both eyesores and health risks.Nidhi Behl, a resident of Model Town, said the AAP government has failed to deliver on its promises. “Roads are in a pathetic condition across the board. Several industrial units operate from private residences in Shimlapuri, New Janta Nagar and Dashmesh Nagar,” she lamented.Another resident, Manjit Singh, said the residents dreaded the monsoon as overflowing sewage and traffic snarls made life miserable. Singh asserted that the civic body’s newly laid storm water pipes to drain rainwater were connected to sewers, which overflow after the slightest of rain.A railway overbridge on the Ludhiana-Dhuri track also remained on paper.Speaking to The Tribune, Avtar Singh Bhogal, a member of the United Cycle and Parts Manufacturers Association (UCPMA), also rued the AAP government’s failure to promote industry. “There are more than 10,000 micro industrial units operating in the mixed land-use areas but their future is uncertain. The government has not found a solution for them. They just keep extending deadlines. There is an urgent need to declare the mixed land-use areas as industrial zones and provide subsidised plots to residents elsewhere.”Contrary to the sentiment on ground, AAP has reposed faith in Sidhu, who had defeated Congress candidate Kamaljit Singh Karwal by a comfortable margin of over 16,000 votes in the last elections.“I have delivered on the promises, be it sports infrastructure or improving the road network or ensuring the smooth functioning of Aam Aadmi Clinics,” he said.The Congress is sensing an opportunity but before it can get to work, it has internal issues to address of its own. Two-time MLA Simarjit Singh Bains, who merged his LIP with the Congress, and Kamaljit Singh Karwal are both strong claimants for the ticket.Their friendship goes back to their time at the Guru Nanak High School in Janta Nagar. They were business partners as well.Bains tasted electoral success as an Independent from Atam Nagar in 2012 with Karwal still by his side. The two, however, parted ways following a rift and Karwal joined the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in 2015. Bains founded the LIP a year later and won from the seat again in 2017.The two have since returned to the Congress — Karwal in 2016 and Bains in 2024.Karwal is a close confidant of former minister Bharat Bhushan Ashu and also enjoys a good rapport with former CM Charanjit Singh Channi. Bains, on the other hand, shares a better equation with former Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring.While neither has spoken out openly against the other, practices like holding parallel events and skipping each other’s rallies are commonplace. Bains was missing from Channi’s recent ‘Jawani Sambhal Yatra’ as well.“I secured more than 28,000 votes in the last elections. Since then, I have stood with the people and questioned the government’s apathy. I will definitely get the ticket again,” a confident Karwal said.With the SAD formalising its alliance with the BJP, the pool of ticket claimants has grown considerably. “Can the AAP MLA even list one project that he brought to the constituency? He has spent his entire term like an area councillor, bragging about road patchwork and transformer installations,” BJP claimant Parvinder Lapran said, taking on a combative stance.SAD halqa in-charge Jagbir Singh Sokhi too was quick to claim that all development projects in the area were carried out by the Akali government. The two face stiff competition for the ticket from Hira Singh Gabria’s son, Rakhwinder Singh Gabria, and BJP industrialist Mukesh Sahni.

headline: Hisar cops urge people to stay alert against cyber frauds, sextortion
content: With incidences of cybercriminals trapping gullible persons to commit frauds on the rise, the Hisar police have issued a series of advisories for the people about staying alert against attempts of sextortion, digital arrest scams, fake government notices, fraudulent WhatsApp money requests and the misuse of bank accounts for illegal transactions by unscrupulous persons.Hisar SP Siddhant Jain stated that while the police had been constantly vigilant and taking immediate cognisances of the incidents reported to it. It was also necessary for the residents to be vigilant against such attempts to lure them. The SP also urged people to use Haryana Police’s digital security applications, Abhedya and Abhedya 2.0, to guard against suspicious calls.The SP cautioned about falling prey to sextortion rackets as fraudsters threatened to circulate private photographs, videos or chats on social media to extort money. He said cybercriminals contacted people through social media platforms or messaging applications before recording video calls or using morphed and fake videos. Their aim was to threaten their targets with defamation and then blackmail them by threatening to share the content with family members, acquaintances or on social media.Jain also alerted people on another mode of fraud in which fraudsters impersonating relatives, friends or acquaintances on WhatsApp seek urgent financial assistance. In another advisory, the SP warned people against allowing others to use their bank accounts in exchange for commissions or easy money.“Cybercriminals try to lure people with promises of fast earnings and use their accounts to route money obtained through online frauds. Such accounts are commonly referred to as ‘mule accounts’,” he said, adding that account holders can also face police scrutiny if fraud proceeds are routed through their accounts.The SP said that details of the ATM or debit cards, PINs, OTPs, UPI details, net banking passwords or SIM cards must not be shared with anyone, or receive and transfer money on behalf of strangers.Similarly, there is growing threat of fraud in which criminals send fake government notices, court summons, arrest warrants and other legal documents to frighten people into transferring money. “The fraudsters impersonating as police officers, court officials or investigating agency personnel, approach and threaten victims with arrest or legal action and demand money in the name of settling cases or preventing arrest”, he said and urged people not to fell prey to such persons and report the incidents to the police.The SP has urged people to download Haryana Police’s Abhedya and Abhedya 2.0 applications in their mobile phones which provided security against suspicious WhatsApp calls while Abhedya 2.0 is meant for regular mobile or telephone calls. In case of financial fraud, victims should immediately call 1930 and inform their banks or financial institutions to help prevent further loss of money, he said.

headline: SAD alliance will bolster Panthic party, check radicals in Punjab: BJP leader Sunil Jakhar
content: Former Punjab Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Sunil Jakhar today said the party’s alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) would strengthen the state’s principal Panthic party and check the rise of militancy and radicalism in the border state.Speaking to The Tribune after Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the tie-up, making it clear that the Chief Minister’s position would remain with big brother Akali Dal, Jakhar said, “Home Minister’s remarks about CM-ship are about enhancing the credibility of the panthic party.”“I am not bothered about posts. The Home Minister has graciously said the CM-ship will be with ‘bade bhai’ (big brother) Akali Dal. Look at this from Punjab’s point of view. It is about granting credibility to the Panthic party. The BJP has accepted them as the big brother.”“If a credible Panthic party is pushed aside, militant elements can rise again. The BJP has given a signal that Punjab is one. It has once again gone back to 1996 when the alliance with Akali Dal was first formed as a social arrangement for Hindu-Sikh unity,” he added.The leader said the move would significantly alter Punjab’s political scene, forcing “even Congress leaders to look for greener pastures.”“The Congress is on its way down and there’s bickering all around. With this alliance, people will send a clear message to politicians — if they want to be in service in the Punjab Assembly, they must look for better options,” said Jakhar.Asked what delayed the alliance, Jakhar said, “Certain issues needed to be discussed. A common minimum programme, on how to address Panthic issues, and check the rise of militancy, is now ready. The Bandi Sikhs issue will also be resolved.”“A credible Panthic party which has sanction from the Akal Takht and credibility with the Sikh sangat is the need of the hour as it acts as a release on the pressure cooker of radicalism. Whenever Panthic parties go down, militant elements rise. This is not conducive and the ISI is always looking for trouble. The alliance will give strength to the Akali Dal and help check the money-making machine of the Aam Aadmi Party,” Jakhar said, expressing hope that PM Narendra Modi would address issues of the Panth, drugs and farmers when he visits Moga on late Parkash Singh Badal’s birth anniversary.Jakhar also described seat sharing talks as a minor issue, saying, “There will be concessions from both sides. What is important is that a change will be visible with the finalisation of this alliance.”

headline: Sai Baba’s teachings of peace remain relevant, says Himachal’s minister Yadvinder Goma
content: The 101st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Sri Sathya Sai Baba was celebrated with religious fervour and devotion at Sai Temple, Lanj, in Kangra district on Monday. Ayush, Youth Services and Sports, and Law Minister Yadvinder Goma attended the celebrations as the chief guest, while Deputy Chief Whip and Shahpur MLA Kewal Singh Pathania was the special guest.After offering prayers, Goma said Sai Baba’s life and teachings embodied the ideals of love, compassion, humanity and selfless service. He said the spiritual leader’s message of brotherhood, peace and social harmony remained highly relevant, particularly for the younger generation. He urged youngsters to draw inspiration from Sai Baba’s ideals and contribute towards nation-building.Appreciating the cultural performances presented by children, the minister announced an incentive of Rs 51,000 for the participants. He also listened to the demands raised by local residents and assured them of appropriate action.Pathania said Sai Baba’s teachings continued to inspire people to uphold the values of love, peace and service. He added that such celebrations helped strengthen social bonds and familiarise younger generations with India’s rich cultural and spiritual heritage.A grand procession was taken out from the temple, with devotees singing bhajans and chanting prayers. The celebrations also featured devotional programmes, cultural performances and distribution of prasad. Individuals who had made notable contributions in various fields were also honoured on the occasion.

headline: Public sentiment drove tie-up with SAD: BJP’s Punjab leadership
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has acknowledged the strength of an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), with the party’s state leadership accepting the fact that public sentiment in Punjab favoured the reunion of the two former partners ahead of the Assembly polls.“Like me, thousands of BJP workers were opposed to any alliance with the SAD after we parted ways in 2020. After interacting with the public, we have realised that under the current situation, only our alliance can lead Punjab out of the quagmire created by successive Congress and AAP governments over the past decade,” state vice-president Subhash Sharma said.Speaking to The Tribune, Sharma said the alliance announced in the national capital could reshape Punjab’s political landscape, altering public expectations and the calculations of all political parties. “I am flooded with calls from people across sections, including Sikh leaders, assuring us of their support,” he said.Former working president Ashwani Sharma echoed the sentiment, saying, “The coming together of the former allies once again brings renewed hope for Punjab’s progress and prosperity.”Will ensure state’s peace, prosperity, says DhillonPunjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon also welcomed the announcement, describing the alliance as a historic step towards ensuring progess of the state.“Restoring law and order in Punjab will be the top priority, and strict action will be taken against gangsters and criminal networks,” the leader added.

headline: Rohtak arts varsity participates in IFFI
content: Dada Lakhmi Chand State University of Performing and Visual Arts (SUPVA) has made an impressive presence felt at the Indian International Film Festival (IFFI) in Goa.For the first time, SUPVA has set up a stall at the international festival being held in Panaji. The stall was formally inaugurated by untying the ribbon knots by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) Chairman and Malayalam film actor G Krishna Kumar and SUPVA Vice Chancellor Amit Arya.During this, the university’s EC member and National Award-winning film director Atul Gangwar, Academic Council member and advisor to the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Satyanarayan, National Award-winning film directors Manish Saini and Kamlesh Mishra were also present.The guests also launched the university’s debut poster. NFDC Chairman Kumar said that presenting the university’s academic achievements, creative activities, art and culture, and the accomplishments of students studying film and television here to filmmakers, artists, delegates and cinema enthusiasts from India and abroad through this stall is truly a commendable step.SUPVA Vice Chancellor said that the objective of participation was to establish the university’s distinctive identity at the national and international levels and to familiarise the global community with the innovations.

headline: Amritsar: In Rafi’s birthplace, cherished memories still await museum
content: Residents of Kotla Sultan Singh village have demanded a museum to preserve the legacy of legendary playback singer Mohammed Rafi. Every month, Rafi’s fans from across the country and abroad visit his native village, with many turning up on his birth and death anniversaries. They come in search of his roots, belongings and memories, hoping to feel a connection with the singer whose voice has been a part of their lives for decades.Their search for Rafi’s ancestral house leads them to the residence of Gurbir Singh Samra, a government schoolteacher posted at Tarpai village, a few kilometres away.An advocate of setting up a museum in the village, Gurbir said Rafi’s original house comprised a single room spread over barely one marla. Before Partition, Rafi’s family sold the house to his great-grandfather. A much larger house now stands at the site.Drawing on stories passed down through generations, Gurbir said Rafi was a close friend of his grandfather, Mula Singh. “Rafi, Mula Singh, Bakshish Singh and Kundan Singh were close friends who studied together at the Government Primary School,” he said.An old red-brick block still stands on the school premises, preserving a link with the singer’s childhood. Amid the newer school buildings, the structure continues to attract the attention of visitors.Pointing towards the building, Gurbir said the four friends studied there together until Rafi’s family moved to Lahore in the late 1930s. All four childhood friends have since passed away, with Rafi being the first to die in 1980.Gurbir also recalled a family anecdote about Rafi carving his name on the trunk of a mango tree before leaving for Lahore. The tree, which stood in a mango orchard spread over nearly two acres, was subsequently felled.Like other village children, the friends would visit fairs in neighbouring villages, spend time in the fields, help prepare jaggery from sugarcane and play hide-and-seek. Rafi, inspired by a fakir (ascetic) in the village, would often hum and sing. Nazeer Ahmed was their teacher, while Urdu was the primary medium of instruction at the time.According to Gurbir, Rafi never returned to his native village after Partition. However, during a stage performance in Amritsar in 1956, the singer called out to his childhood friend Kundan Singh by name over the microphone.Vinod Sharma, principal of Sri Dasmesh Senior Secondary Public School, said a bust of Rafi had been installed and a memorial hall constructed on the school premises, where his fans pay floral tributes. He recalled that some visitors even carried soil from the village back to their homes as a keepsake.“The government or the film industry could take the initiative to establish a museum in the village where his belongings, photographs and other memorabilia could be preserved,” Sharma said.Gurnam Singh, a tailor, said Rafi’s son Shahid had visited the village twice and interacted with residents. He felt the village had yet to fully recognise the significance of the singer’s legacy, otherwise a museum would have been established long ago.He said organising annual fairs was a traditional way of commemorating prominent personalities in Punjab’s villages. However, no such fair had been instituted in Rafi’s memory. It was only the gathering of fans on his birth and death anniversaries that lent the village a festive atmosphere.Lakhwinder, the son of a daily-wage labourer who runs a barber shop in the village, shared another anecdote about Rafi’s father, Mohammad Ali, who belonged to the traditional barber community and also cooked at weddings.According to accounts passed down by village elders, Rafi’s father was known for his culinary skills, his ability to prepare rice in seven differently coloured layers in a single degh (large cauldron) during wedding celebrations.For residents, these fading memories and oral accounts underline the need for a museum to preserve Rafi’s association with the village.

headline: Coalition, facts & effects: All eyes on seat-sharing  in Gurdaspur, Pathankot
content: The SAD-BJP coalition has changed the political permutations and combinations in all the 10 Assembly seats of the twin districts of Gurdaspur and Pathankot to the extent that senior Congress and AAP leaders have admitted that their ambitions are sure to go in for a hit if they do not immediately end their ongoing infighting.Things looked comparatively easier for both the Congress and the ruling dispensation until the SAD, having a stronghold in rural Punjab, and the BJP, known for wielding a strong influence in urban areas, decided to join hands today.“We have to change track and fall in line if we have to stay in the reckoning,” said a sitting AAP MLA.The Assembly segments going to the polls in Gurdaspur and Pathankot districts are Bhoa, Pathankot, Sujanpur, Dinanagar, Gurdaspur, Dera Baba Nanak, Fatehgarh Churian, Qadian, Batala and Sri-Hargobindpur. In certain seats of Gurdaspur and Pathankot district, the alliance will barely have an effect. Sources revealed that Dinanagar was sure to go to the BJP like it had been happening in the past several elections. However, the SAD is on a sticky wicket in the area hence the alliance will not affect either the Congress or the AAP. Aruna Chaudhary of the Congress and Shamsher Singh of the AAP will be seen in a direct contest. During the old seat sharing agreement, the Gurdaspur city seat used to go to the SAD, with ex-MLA Gurbachan Singh Babbehali being their candidate. However this time, the BJP is trying to wrest the seat from the SAD with senior leaders citing the performance of the party in the 2024 general elections when the SAD and the BJP had contested separately. Ex-Sujanpur MLA Dinesh Babbu, who was the BJP candidate, had surpassed the Akali candidate’s tally by more than 10,000 votes from Gurdaspur city. “This piece of statistics is more than enough to convince the SAD to let the BJP candidate contest,” said a senior RSS leader. Senior BJP leaders say this time, their party will lay claim to the seats in which their candidates had got more votes than the SAD in the 2024 general elections. All eyes are now on how the 10 seats of the two districts will be divided between the BJP and the SAD.

headline: ‘Learnt our lesson’: JJP shuts door on future BJP alliance
content: The Jannayak Janta Party (JJP) has ruled out any possibility of a future alliance with the BJP, with its youth state president Digvijay Chautala expressing regret over the party’s decision to join the BJP-led government in Haryana after the 2019 Assembly elections.Addressing a press conference in Bhiwani, Digvijay, younger brother of former Deputy Chief Minister Dushyant Chautala, said the party’s four-and-a-half-year association with the BJP had dented its clean and honest image.“Doodh ka jalaa, chhachh ko bhi phoonk maar ke peeta hai,” he said, suggesting that the party had learnt its lesson. He maintained that nobody could question Dushyant Chautala’s integrity, hard work or style of functioning, but the alliance had forced the party to defend itself before the public.Referring to his father and JJP national president Ajay Chautala, Digvijay said the party leadership had also ruled out any future understanding with the BJP. While the possibility of alliances with other parties could be explored, he asserted that the decision against joining hands with the BJP was final.The JJP had won 10 seats in the 2019 Assembly elections and extended support to the BJP after it fell short of a majority. Dushyant Chautala was subsequently appointed Deputy Chief Minister in the Manohar Lal Khattar-led government and given charge of several key departments.However, the alliance triggered resentment among sections of the JJP’s support base. The party faced further criticism during the farmers’ agitation, with farmer leaders targeting its leadership for remaining part of the BJP-led government.The BJP snapped ties with the JJP ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The regional party subsequently suffered electoral setbacks, with all its candidates losing their security deposits in both the Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.The JJP is now attempting to revive its political fortunes ahead of the next electoral cycle in Haryana. Seeking to invoke the legacy of former Deputy Prime Minister Devi Lal, the party has planned a rally in Mahendergarh on December 6 to demonstrate its organisational strength.

headline: Why are sugarcane farmers protesting in Haryana?
content: While the sugar mills in the state are ready to start their crushing operations, the sugarcane farmers are holding demonstrations and have refused to deliver the produce to the mills. The farmers have been expressing unhappiness over the Haryana Government’s decision to increase the sugarcane prices by Rs 35 per quintal over the next two years.What triggered the protest?The Haryana Government announced to give Rs 430 per quintal during the 2026-27 crushing season and the price will subsequently rise to Rs 450 per quintal in the 2027-28 season. However, farmers’ organisations rejected the increase, arguing that it is insufficient in view of the rising cost of production. The sugarcane farmers received Rs 415 per quintal last year. They have been demanding Rs 600 per quintal for the current season. According to the protesting farmers, the increase of Rs 35 per quintal over two years does not address their financial concerns.Why are farmers demanding Rs 600 per quintal?Farmers argue that the cost of sugarcane cultivation has increased due to rising expenses on agricultural inputs, labour and other farming operations. They also claim that the prices being offered for sugarcane are not providing adequate returns, affecting the profitability of cultivation. As per the farmers, the cost of production is over Rs 455 per quintal, while the government is offering Rs 430 per quintal.What do the farmer leaders say about the situation?Vinod Rana, president of the Ganna Kisan Sangharsh Samiti, questioned the government’s decision to increase the price by only Rs 15 per quintal for the current season. He said the government needed to explain the basis for such a small increase, particularly when farmers were struggling to recover their production costs. BKU (Charuni) Ambala spokesman Rajiv Sharma pointed out that the area under sugarcane cultivation had been declining because farmers were not receiving remunerative prices.What appeal has been made by farmer unions?The farmer unions have appealed to the sugarcane farmers across Haryana to not harvest their crops and deliver sugarcane to sugar mills until their demand for higher prices is accepted. In the absence of sugarcane, the mills haven’t been able to start their crushing season.How will the agitation affect sugar mills?The protest has already started affecting the crushing season. Naraingarh sugar mill and Shahabad sugar mill failed to receive sugarcane stocks to begin crushing operations amid the farmers’ agitation. Sugar mills depend on a continuous supply of sugarcane to operate their crushing units. If farmers continue withholding their produce, the mills could face a shortage of raw material, potentially delaying the start of crushing and affecting sugar production.What happens next?Various farmer unions in the state have joined hands and have decided to intensify the protests under the banner of Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha. They have also decided to hold a massive protest in Kurukshetra on December 2 and gherao the CM’s residence. The farmers have made it clear that they intend to continue withholding sugarcane supplies until their demand for Rs 600 per quintal is accepted. For the Haryana Government and sugar mills, the challenge will be to ensure that the crushing season proceeds without prolonged disruption while addressing the concerns raised by farmers.

headline: ‘Thag jod’ aimed at protecting political interests: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on SAD-BJP alliance
content: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday described the newly announced BJP-SAD alliance as a “thag jod”, alleging that the two parties had joined hands to protect their political interests and regain power rather than safeguarding Punjab’s interests.In a video message addressed to Punjabis, Mann questioned the political consistency of the two parties, citing their differences over the three farm laws, the transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab, the state’s river waters dispute and control over Sikh institutions.He said the Badals had initially supported the farm laws but changed their stand after the farmers’ agitation gained momentum. “As many as 750 farmers had lost their lives during the agitation,” he said.Referring to the BJP’s positions on Punjab-related issues, Mann alleged that the party had sought control over Panjab University, proposed a separate Assembly building in Chandigarh and advocated sharing Punjab’s river waters with Haryana and Rajasthan. He also accused the BJP of interfering in the management of Sikh institutions, including Takht Hazur Sahib and Patna Sahib.Questioning the Akali Dal’s decision to ally with the BJP, Mann recalled SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal’s earlier statements alleging that the BJP and RSS were taking control of Sikh institutions. He also referred to developments in December 2024, when Badal was awarded a “tankhah” (religious punishment). Mann alleged that Badal had subsequently accused the Sikh high priests of acting at the BJP’s behest.Mann said the SAD and BJP could not escape responsibility for their 10-year rule from 2007 to 2017. He alleged the drug menace and incidents of sacrilege, including those in 2015, had occurred during their tenure.

headline: Punjab Congress revisits election strategy, plan centralised campaign
content: Hours after the SAD and BJP revived their alliance, the Congress leadership decided to present a united front ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. At the first meeting of its state election committee, the party resolved to work on a common platform, particularly to counter the NDA.The meeting, chaired by Punjab Congress affairs in-charge Sachin Pilot, saw senior leaders express concern that multiple party yatras were projecting the Congress as a divided house rather than a united force. Leaders were advised to set aside their differences ahead of the Assembly elections.All 42 committee members shared their views on the possible impact of the SAD-BJP alliance on the Congress’ prospects of returning to power. A senior leader said the party had begun discussions on revisiting its political and electoral strategy for the 2027 poll.Among those present were CLP leader Partap Singh Bajwa, former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, former PPCC chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, former ministers Brahm Mohindra and Dr Raj Kumar Verka, and ex-Speaker Rana KP Singh.“The focus of the strategy against the SAD-BJP alliance would be to project both AAP and the SAD as parties dependent on ‘outsiders’ to run Punjab’s affairs. Both parties have a lot to explain to Punjabis, and this will work against the alliance,” a senior leader said.Several leaders also expressed concern over the declining representation of Hindu leaders, particularly amid fears that the BJP could eat into the Congress’ vote bank. Sources said Pilot informed committee members that a centralised campaign and strategy would be rolled out in the coming days to counter the SAD-BJP alliance and the AAP.Members were asked to submit three-four recommendations for each of the 117 Assembly constituencies in sealed covers. The party would discuss each suggested candidate with the respective committee members. However, they would also be held accountable if their recommended candidates worked against the party after being denied the ticket.The Congress has reportedly identified 40-50 probable candidates, but the first list will be released only after detailed deliberations. Pilot also assured members that adequate representation would be given to youth in ticket allocation, sources said.Congress leader and Amethi MP Kishori Lal Sharma on Tuesday facilitated a meeting between Warring and former minister Bharat Bhushan Ashu at the Congress Bhawan. Sources said the meeting was arranged at the intervention of Pilot to resolve differences between the two leaders. Another round of talks was expected to be held in Delhi.

headline: Five-year delay in four-laning project chokes traffic at Mataur in Kangra district
content: Commuters travelling on the busy Pathankot-Mandi National Highway are facing mounting difficulties as the proposed Rajol-Tanpuri four-laning project remains stalled, making traffic management increasingly challenging, particularly at Mataur Chowk.Despite repeated assurances from the authorities, the project has witnessed little progress over the past five years. The prolonged delay has worsened traffic congestion, with long queues of vehicles becoming a routine sight. Besides local residents and daily commuters, tourists visiting Kangra district are also bearing the brunt of the bottlenecks.The lack of an effective traffic management system has further aggravated the situation. Heavy vehicles arriving from the Palampur side contribute significantly to congestion at Mataur, while motorists heading towards Pathankot, Dharamsala and other destinations struggle to navigate the crowded stretch.Traffic snarls intensify during peak hours when vehicular movement increases sharply. Emergency services, including ambulances, often face delays in negotiating the jam-packed roads.Residents say traffic jams have become a daily ordeal. They allege that traffic personnel are finding it increasingly difficult to manage the rising volume of vehicles, while the existing road infrastructure is inadequate to cope with the pressure.Kangra MP Rajiv Bhardwaj said the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) had submitted three alternative alignments for the Rajol-Tanpuri four-laning project to the state government. One of the proposed routes extends from Rajol towards Salangari, passing near the IT Park and Ichhi before reaching Mataur and connecting with the existing highway at Kachhiari. However, none of the proposals has seen any significant progress so far.The delay has placed additional pressure on Mataur Chowk, where vehicles frequently remain stuck for extended periods. Residents say the situation has become increasingly frustrating, especially during rush hours.The proposed four-laning project remains a major concern for people across the region. With construction yet to begin, commuters continue to grapple with recurring traffic congestion and uncertainty over the project’s future.Kangra MLA Pawan Kajal said completion of the project would significantly ease traffic movement in the area.However, uncertainty over the alignment and continued delays have dimmed hopes of an early resolution.Residents have urged the state government, the NHAI and the traffic police to work in coordination, finalise the highway alignment at the earliest and introduce immediate traffic management measures to provide relief to commuters.Both the MP and the MLA maintained that unless the long-pending project is taken up on priority, traffic congestion at Mataur and adjoining areas is likely to worsen further.

headline: Poor flight connectivity, high fares hit Kullu-Manali tourism
content: Poor air connectivity and high airfares at Bhuntar airport in Kullu district have emerged as major concerns for the tourism industry in Kullu-Manali, with tourism stakeholders urging the state and central governments to strengthen flight services to attract more high-end domestic and international tourists to the Himalayan region.Tourism stakeholders said that the limited frequency of flights and expensive air tickets were discouraging tourists who prefer air travel, particularly those looking for convenient and time-saving access to popular destinations such as Manali and other tourist attractions in Kullu district.They stressed that improved air connectivity was essential to position Kullu-Manali as a preferred destination for high-end tourism.Alliance Air was earlier operating flights on the Delhi-Kullu, Kullu-Dehradun and Kullu-Amritsar routes. However, the airline suspended its flight service between Delhi and Kullu from November 3. Similarly, flight service has also been suspended on the Kullu-Dehradun and Kullu-Amritsar routes.Hira Lal Rana, president of the Himachal Pradesh Travel Agents Association, said tourism was the backbone of the economy of Kullu district and provided employment opportunities to a large number of local youth in the private sector.He said there was an urgent need to improve air connectivity at Bhuntar airport to attract high-end tourists to Kullu-Manali. The low frequency of flights and high airfares were major setbacks for the tourism industry, which depended heavily on tourist arrivals from different parts of the country and abroad.Rana stressed that better flight connectivity and affordable air travel would make the region more accessible to tourists and help strengthen the local tourism economy.Budhi Prakash, another tourism stakeholder from Manali, stated that despite four BJP MPs from Himachal in the Lok Sabha, two BJP MPs from Himachal in the Rajya Sabha and Union Minister JP Nadda, who also hails from Himachal, the state could not focus on the development of tourism in the state. Air services could not be strengthened without the intervention of the Centre. So, all these BJP leaders should collectively take up this issue with the Centre as well as with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as he always talks about the promotion of tourism in Himachal.Roshan Thakur, president of the Hoteliers Association Manali, said tourism stakeholders had repeatedly raised the issue of inadequate air services with both the state and central governments.He said representatives of the tourism industry had also met Rajya Sabha MP Dr Sikander Kumar and requested him to take up the matter with the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation to ensure better air connectivity at Bhuntar airport.

headline: SAD-BJP tie-up ‘alliance of hearts’, will give Punjab new direction: Saini
content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Tuesday termed the SAD-BJP tie-up an “alliance of hearts”, saying it would strengthen Punjab and give the state a new direction.Hailing the re-alliance between the SAD and the BJP, he described it as a significant step in the interest of Punjab.The BJP and the SAD had parted ways in September 2020 following differences over the Centre’s three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed following a year-long farmers’ agitation, with thousands of protesters camping at Delhi’s borders in 2020-21.The development comes ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, scheduled for early 2027.Speaking on the re-alliance, Saini said the partnership was not merely a political arrangement but an “alliance of hearts” and a natural coming together of like-minded forces committed to Punjab’s progress and the aspirations of its people.He credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP National President Nitin Nabin with taking the initiative to revive the alliance in the interest of Punjab’s welfare.Saini said the move carried forward the long-standing relationship between the BJP and the SAD, which dated back to the era of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and senior BJP leader LK Advani.The Haryana Chief Minister said the alliance would work jointly to address key challenges facing Punjab, including gangster activities and the drug menace. B‘To protect farmers’ interests’ BHe added that the partnership would focus on protecting farmers’ interests, ensuring the safety and dignity of women and working for the welfare of economically weaker sections.Calling for public participation, Saini urged the people of Punjab to unite and contribute towards strengthening the state and putting it on a new path of development. BTo rid state of AAP’s jungle raj: Vij BMeanwhile, Haryana Minister Anil Vij claimed that the SAD-BJP alliance would form the next government in Punjab, asserting that the two parties had come together to rid the state of what he termed AAP’s “jungle raj”.Vij also declared that the AAP’s political presence in the country had come to an end.“The BJP has defeated AAP’s guru, Arvind Kejriwal, in Delhi, and now what chance does his disciple (Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann) have of surviving?” he said.Vij said the SAD-BJP alliance reflected the voice of the people of Punjab.“It was essential for the BJP and the SAD to come together to free Punjab from the AAP’s ‘jungle raj’,” Vij said, adding that the alliance was announced on the auspicious occasion of Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purb.

headline: Punjab and Haryana High Court orders release of car seized without FIR
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has expressed dismay over the police taking possession of a car that was not involved in any FIR and the subsequent refusal by a magistrate to release it, despite recording that no case was registered in connection with the vehicle.Allowing a petition filed against Haryana and other respondents, Justice Vikram Aggarwal set aside the August 26 order passed by Jagadhri Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate and directed the car’s release to the petitioner forthwith.Justice Aggarwal recorded that the car was not involved in any FIR and that the police had taken its possession “only on account of some financial dispute” between the present petitioner and another person.The petitioner, in turn, had approached the magistrate seeking the vehicle’s release.“Keeping in view that the FIR is not registered with regard to the vehicle and the report of the SHO concerned reveals that the vehicle is a matter of some financial dispute between the registered owner and the applicant, therefore, the present application is dismissed being misconceived,” the court had ruled.Taking note of both the police action and the magistrate’s refusal to release the vehicle, Justice Aggarwal observed, “This Court is indeed appalled firstly on account of the action of the police, for having taken possession of the vehicle without it being involved in any FIR and secondly on account of the order passed by the Court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jagadhri…”The State counsel, who appeared after receiving advance notice, also “fairly conceded” that the vehicle should have been released on superdari “since it is not involved in any FIR”.

headline: Now, truth will come out: Rao Narender on SAD-BJP tie-up
content: Taking a dig at the SAD-BJP pre-poll alliance in Punjab, Haryana Congress president Rao Narender Singh on Tuesday said his party was “actually excited” about the tie-up, claiming it would expose the political claims of its constituents.He asserted that the Congress had an “alliance with people” and would return to power in Punjab.He said the alliance would help the people of Punjab distinguish between political claims and reality.“The alliance is good and we are excited about it. Now, the truth will come out,” Singh said in response to a question from mediapersons on Tuesday on the sidelines of a “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” chaupal at Uchana village in the district.Singh said the people of Punjab had already witnessed the tenures of the SAD-BJP alliance, the AAP and the Congress.“People have realised that only the Congress knows how to take everyone along. A Congress-led government will be formed in Punjab. The people of Punjab will never vote for the BJP,” he added.He said that no matter how many alliances were formed in Punjab, the Congress had an “alliance with the people”, who had already made up their minds to bring the party to power.Commenting on the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance in Uttar Pradesh, he said there was no deadlock and discussions were continuing.He expressed confidence that the Congress-SP alliance would emerge victorious in the upcoming elections and form the government in the state.Earlier, as part of the party’s ongoing programmes to safeguard voting rights and constitutional values, Singh and AICC in-charge for Haryana Sanjay Dutt chaired the chaupal and urged party leaders and workers to reach Panchkula on November 26 to participate in the ‘Save the Constitution March’.They held detailed discussions with district presidents, block presidents and organisational office-bearers, urging them to make the march a success.“To save the Constitution, we will hold a march in Panchkula on November 26. Preparations are underway. A large number of party workers and members of the public are expected to participate in the state-level march,” Singh said.Dutt said, “This march will be historic. Every Congress worker will participate in it with complete unity and strength. The present government is misusing power and striking at people's right to vote through unfair tactics.”“Arbitrarily deleting names from electoral rolls and depriving people of their democratic rights is against the basic spirit of the Constitution. The Congress will not tolerate any attack on this right of the people,” he added.Dutt said that until Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was removed from his post, electoral rolls were prepared in a transparent and impartial manner, and the names of voters improperly deleted were restored, the Congress's struggle would continue.He called upon all workers to treat it as their responsibility to take the message of the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign to every home and village.

headline: Amritsar: Some fall prey to drugs in the land of melodies
content: Decades after legendary playback singer Mohammed Rafi rose to fame, few youngsters in his native village are pursuing performing arts. For many youngsters in Kotla Sultan Singh, aspirations revolve around settling abroad and pursuing a comfortable lifestyle, while some have fallen prey to drug abuse.After Rafi, Hardeep Gill is perhaps the only native of the village to have carved out a career in cinema. A theatre artiste and actor, Gill has made a name for himself in the Punjabi film industry.He made his acting debut with the 2008 film ‘Hashar: A Love Story’. His film ‘Nabar’ went on to win a National Award. His other notable films include ‘Mitti’, ‘Panjaban’, ‘Punjab 1984’, ‘Mr & Mrs 420’, ‘Judge Singh LLB’, ‘Dakuaan Da Munda’, ‘Shadaa’, ‘Singham’ and ‘Chal Mera Putt 2’.Hardeep Singh, a village resident, said the trend of migrating abroad gained momentum among youngsters in the early 2000. He recalled that one of the earliest residents to migrate overseas belonged to his extended family and had moved to Canada between 1990 and 1995.“I no longer remember his name, but his father’s name was Ajaib Singh. He belonged to an agricultural family,” he said.According to him, shrinking employment opportunities have prompted youngsters to migrate overseas in search of better prospects. Though some enterprising residents have opened shops, limited footfall in rural areas restricts business growth. The village currently has around 30 shops catering to the daily needs of residents.Located near the boundary of Gurdaspur district, Kotla Sultan Singh is situated over five km from Majitha town and is connected by a narrow road.Discarded injections and syringes in the village have raised concerns over drug abuse. Village elders lament that few youngsters have drawn inspiration from the life of ‘Fiko’, as Rafi was affectionately called by his family and childhood friends. They recalled that opportunities for professional growth were scarce during Rafi’s childhood, with limited means of communication, transport and career guidance. Despite these constraints, he went on to become one of India’s most celebrated playback singers.Meanwhile, Kotla Sultan Singh is undergoing a socio-economic transformation. Modern houses and shops have come up in the village, while several families have chosen to build houses in nearby Majitha town.

headline: How NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index is rewiring India's federalism
content: Consider two states. Tamil Nadu runs a near-universal food distribution system that predates the national food security law by nearly five decades, funds one of the world's largest school-meal programmes entirely from its own budget, and maintains public health infrastructure among the densest in India. Its maternal mortality ratio, infant mortality rate, literacy, and poverty headcount place it closer to a high-middle-income country than to the Indian average. Keralam's record is comparable: a social pension architecture built over decades, near-universal primary health coverage, and human development outcomes that have long served as a reference point in global comparisons.
