headline: North Karnataka could become a separate state in 5-10 years: BJP MLA Balakrishna Jarkiholi
content: The demand for a separate state of North Karnataka could become a reality in the next five to 10 years, BJP MLA Balakrishna Jarkiholi has said.His remarks come a week ahead of the Karnataka Legislature's winter session in Belagavi, scheduled to begin on December 2, when regional development and the long-pending demands of North Karnataka are expected to come into focus.The North Karnataka region, particularly Belagavi, witnesses heightened political activity ahead of the annual legislature session, with the Maharashtra Ekikaran Samiti (MES) renewing its decades-old demand for the separation of Belagavi from Karnataka and its merger with Maharashtra.Recalling former Minister Umesh Katti's advocacy for a separate North Karnataka state, Arabhavi MLA Jarkiholi on Tuesday said, "Sometimes, we too felt that it might be a good idea. He used to say that if North Karnataka became a separate state, Belagavi would become its capital and the region would witness tremendous development."Also Read | Karnataka HC lets cops probe BJP MLA in Form 7 case but protects him from arrestSpeaking to reporters, the former minister said the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha was constructed in Belagavi with the objective of benefiting the region, but development had not taken place to the desired extent."Development has taken place, but not to the extent that it should have. If comprehensive development is to take place, we need to consider what he used to say about having a separate state of our own," he said.Jarkiholi said the BJP would take up the problems of North Karnataka seriously and fight to secure relief for the people.Responding to a question on whether there was support for the separate state demand, he said, "Perhaps, after five or ten years, things may move in that direction. It could definitely happen. Let us see what happens then."On the demand for devoting the entire winter session to issues concerning North Karnataka, the BJP MLA said he would raise the matter with the party's state president and at the meeting of its legislators.Also Read | Karnataka's DK Shivakumar Travels On Japanese Bullet Train Ahead Of Toyota Factory Visit"If it is not possible to devote all nine days to North Karnataka, we will at least try to ensure that five days are set aside for discussing issues concerning this region," he said.He said issues concerning Bengaluru and other regions could be discussed when the legislature meets there, while the Belagavi session should focus on North Karnataka.Jarkiholi said the discussion should cover irrigation, farmers' problems and drought, adding that political differences should be set aside to collectively fight for the region's development."We will set aside our differences within Belagavi district and forget the political differences prevailing in the state. We will all come together and fight for the development of North Karnataka," he said.Claiming that successive governments had contributed to the region's development through infrastructure, roads, irrigation projects, educational institutions and other facilities, he said much more needed to be done.Also Read | Karnataka Congress MLAs oppose elephant relocation; Motamma submits resignationReferring to the Nanjundappa Committee report, which identified several taluks as backward, he said there were no backward taluks in the region today, though some might continue to figure in official records."Development has taken place. However, we will continue to make efforts to ensure that it happens on a much larger scale," he said.Jarkiholi also said people from North Karnataka should come together, irrespective of political affiliations, to strongly raise their concerns during the legislature session.The Arabhavi MLA is one of the five Jarkiholi brothers who hold sway in Belagavi.

headline: Supreme Court 'inclined' to stay Calcutta HC order deferring Kolkata civic polls till decision on ward delimitation
content: New Delhi Stating that it shouldn't postpone pending elections "unreasonably", the Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order deferring the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) polls till the issue of ward delimitation is decided. A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the issue by November 30. Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided The West Bengal government, through a delimitation, has increased the number of wards of KMC from 144 to 209. The petitioner argued that the State government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering in order to secure partisan advantage to the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results. Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided storyline 1 The KMC has undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the next civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144. The High Court had restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing a notification for the KMC election till a single bench disposes of a plea on ward delimitation. "We are inclined to stay the impugned order for the reason that the factual and legal issues which have been highlighted, the division bench will pass a fresh order, an appropriate order. "The writ petition before the single judge will be directed to be transferred to the division bench. And till the division bench forms a view the polls can be held off," the Bench observed. West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari storyline 1 During the hearing, Justice Bagchi said,""We shouldn't postpone pending elections unreasonably." The division bench of the High Court had directed the State Election Commission (SEC) to not issue a notification for elections to the KMC till the disposal of a petition pending before a single bench. Challenging the delimitation exercise, the petitioner, a former CPI-M councillor, sought a declaration stating that the entire exercise of determination of the number of KMC wards is void and the quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards is bad in law. Dipu Das alleged that the delimitation exercise has been undertaken based on electoral rolls instead of the actual population, thereby excluding a substantial number of residents from consideration. The petitioner claimed that the civic body had no elected council, and the corporation's former chairperson Smita Pandey had been appointed its administrator after the House's dissolution on June 8. He also sought an interim order of stay of operation of the delimitation notification and to restrain the SEC from issuing any notification calling an election to the KMC. The single bench on October 29 refused an interim stay. West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar This announcement comes as the Kolkata Corporation election remains stalled by the Calcutta High Court; Mamata-Trinamool says why not hold elections and appoint elected representatives West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar storyline 1 Aggrieved by the refusal, Mr. Das moved the division bench. The State government, the order had said, could empower its chosen administrator to make a tailor-made recommendation and then be bound by it, effectively allowing the government to recommend amendments to itself and undermining the provision's independence. "Such puppetry cannot be compatible with the scheme of the KMC Act. The key feature of Section 601 of the KMC Act is the institutional autonomy vested in the Corporation in making a binding recommendation to the state government, which confers authority on the Corporation, an autonomous institution, to decide the delimitation of its own wards, in other words, its electoral constituencies," the order said. It stated that the manner in which the corporation was dissolved mid-term, and an administrator was appointed, followed by "the hasty chronology of events thereafter" lent substance to the appellant's arguments "that there might have been a method in the madness". The observations made in the division bench order came with a rider that they were "tentative in nature insofar as the final disposal of the writ petition is concerned."

headline: Indian Ocean must connect nations, not divide them: NSA Ajit Doval at Colombo Security Conclave
content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Wednesday emphasised the shared maritime and civilisational ties among Indian Ocean littoral states, saying the seas must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them.Addressing the 8th National Security Advisors' Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male, Doval called for sustained cooperation among countries in the region to ensure maritime security, regional stability and economic prosperity.“We the littoral states of the Indian Ocean region share a common maritime space and are connected by civilisational heritage shaped over a long period of history,” Doval said. Recalling the legacy left by previous generations, he said the seas had historically connected communities and countries, and urged participating nations to preserve this tradition for future generations.Also Read: NSA Ajit Doval reviews bilateral defence cooperation with Vietnam's deputy PM in Hanoi“As was mentioned by the National Security Advisor of Maldives that the generations before us left the legacy for us that the seas connected us. Let us leave for our progeny also a heritage, a tradition that will bind them together and not divide them through these seas,” he said.Doval said the formation of the Colombo Security Conclave in November 2020 was guided by a collective vision to ensure the safety, security and stability of the Indian Ocean Region.“The formation of the Colombo Security Conclave in November 2020 was anchored by our collective vision for a safety, security, and stability of the Indian Ocean region,” he said, adding that the grouping had made considerable progress but still had a long journey ahead.He also underlined India's commitment to strengthening the regional grouping, linking the CSC to New Delhi's neighbourhood-first policy and its broader MAHASAGAR vision.“For India, the Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our neighbourhood-first outlook and the Mahasagar vision, which stands for mutual and holistic advancement in security and growth areas. We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges,” Doval said.Assuring participating countries of India's continued support, he said New Delhi would extend necessary assistance to achieve the common objectives of the conclave.“I assure all of you here that India, as one of the partner countries here, as one of the Speaker countries that initiated the idea of the Colombo Security Conclave, will give its best and will try to give all necessary help and assistance, and we assure you of our fullest commitment to achieve our common objectives,” he added.Expressing appreciation to the Maldives for hosting the meeting, Doval said the CSC had evolved from an initial idea about the strategic importance of the Indian Ocean into a structured regional platform.“It is indeed a very proud moment for me to be here and enjoy the great hospitality of the Government of Maldives. I am particularly grateful to the NSA of Maldives for the excellent arrangements that he has made for this conference and for giving us an opportunity to share our thoughts and opinions,” he said.He noted that the Indian Ocean was important not only for the national security and economic prosperity of countries in the region but also for safeguarding the interests and welfare of their people.“We started as a very rudimentary idea that the Indian Ocean is important for our national security; it is important for our economic prosperity; it's also important for the human dimension, looking after the interests of the people who are in this region,” Doval said.He credited the participating countries for the development of the conclave, pointing out that it now had a secretariat and a Secretary General to strengthen its institutional framework.“And the idea subsequently developed; it was with the cooperation of all of you that today now we have got a secretariat, we have got a proper Secretary General, and we do hope that in the coming months, we will be able to carry it forward,” he added.Doval also highlighted the adoption of the CSC Charter and the Memorandum of Understanding on the establishment of its secretariat in August 2024, welcoming the progress made in institutionalising the grouping.He praised Admiral Ghormade, who is associated with the leadership of the CSC Secretariat, describing him as one of the most outstanding professionals he had known during his career.The CSC Member States signed the Charter and the Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment of the Secretariat on August 30, 2024. The signing ceremony was hosted by the Government of Sri Lanka in Colombo. Doval, Maldives National Security Advisor Ibrahim Latheef, Mauritius High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Haymandoyal Dillum and Sri Lanka's National Security Advisor Sagala Ratnayake signed the documents on behalf of their respective countries.The CSC aims to promote regional security by addressing transnational threats and challenges of common concern to its Member States. Its five pillars of cooperation include maritime safety and security; countering terrorism and radicalisation; combating trafficking and transnational organised crime; cybersecurity and protection of critical infrastructure and technology; and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.Earlier on November 24, Doval met Maldives Minister of Defence and National Service Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the meeting. The two sides discussed ways to strengthen bilateral defence and security cooperation and exchanged views on matters of mutual interest.The 8th CSC Council of National Security Advisers meeting is being held in the Maldives from November 24 to 26, bringing together participating countries to discuss regional security cooperation in the Indian Ocean Region. The participating countries include India, Bangladesh, Maldives, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Seychelles. (ANI)

headline: CJP’s Saurav Das moves Delhi High Court over being stopped from flying to U.K.; hearing on November 26
content: New Delhi Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an Oxford University event, where he was slated to speak on the "cockroach movement." https://www.thehindu.com/topic/cockroach-janta-party/ CJP’s Saurav Das claims he was stopped at Delhi airport from travelling to U.K. storyline 1 The rise of the Cockroaches: Timeline storyline 1 The plea was mentioned for urgent hearing on Wednesday (November 25). A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said the matter would be listed on Thursday (Novembre 26). CJP leader Saurav Das says ‘coward government’ flagged passport, stopped UK trip CJP leader Saurav Das says ‘coward government’ flagged passport, stopped UK trip CJP leader Saurav Das says ‘coward government’ flagged passport, stopped UK trip shorts 1 Mr. Das has alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London. "I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are," Mr. Das's counsel submitted. He said the flight is on Thursday (November 26). "Let it be (heard) tomorrow," the bench responded. On Monday (November 23), in a series of posts on X, Mr. Das criticised the central government after being prevented from boarding his 1:00 a.m. flight to London. "I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford. This cowardly government did not allow me to board my flight to London, where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE and Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement," Mr. Das said. Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport Saurav Das was served the notice at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before his flight; the government has not issued any statement on the reasons for stopping him at the Delhi airport Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport storyline 1 "Indian students put their heart and soul into organising the events, but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" he added. Mr. Das said he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion. "And that's why I was going to London. But as soon as I went to the immigration check, I came to know that my passport has been flagged," he said. "Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion? I wish I was Nirav Modi. I wish I was Vijay Mallya. I wish I had looted thousands of crores from the banks..." he said.

headline: JioStar starts fresh layoffs as television business faces mounting pressure
content: JioStar has reportedly begun another round of layoffs as its television broadcasting business faces pressure from a decline in pay-TV subscribers and a slowdown in television advertising. The latest workforce reduction is part of a broader restructuring exercise as the company looks to rationalise its broadcasting operations and shift investments towards digital businesses, including JioHotstar, according to a report by The Economic Times. The latest round is expected to affect around 150 employees across departments, including marketing, production, studios and operations, Exchange4Media reported on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the development. Industry sources told the publication that the final number could be higher. The exact number of employees affected has not been officially disclosed. The Economic Times reported that the phased layoffs could affect more than 10 per cent of JioStar's workforce, which is estimated to exceed 5,000 employees.JioStar offers severance package to affected employeesEmployees affected by the latest restructuring exercise are being offered at least six months' salary as severance, along with a pro-rata bonus for the current financial year, according to the media reports. ALSO READ: Cipla gets USFDA nod for first generic version of Flovent asthma drug JioStar has confirmed that the restructuring will affect some employees. Responding to a query about the layoffs, a company spokesperson told Inc42: "We are rebalancing our portfolio to focus our investments on the businesses where we see the strongest opportunity for long-term growth. This is a strategic decision aimed at strengthening our competitive position in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry." The spokesperson added that the company recognised the impact of the decisions on employees and was committed to treating them with respect and providing support during the transition.Television business faces pressure as JioHotstar growsThe layoffs come as JioStar's television broadcasting business faces challenges from a shrinking pay-TV subscriber base and slower television advertising growth. The company operates a portfolio of 120 entertainment and sports television channels. While its broadcasting operations face pressure, JioHotstar has reported growth in advertising and subscription revenue, according to The Economic Times. The restructuring also includes plans to shut television channels that are incurring costs without generating meaningful revenue. The company intends to rationalise its broadcasting portfolio and redirect investments towards businesses with stronger growth prospects, the report said. Exchange4Media also reported that the prolonged suspension of television audience ratings has added to the pressure on broadcasters. The absence of regular, independent audience measurement has affected how broadcasters assess channel performance and negotiate advertising deals.Second major workforce reduction since mergerThe latest exercise is the second major round of workforce reductions since Viacom18 and Disney's Star India merged to form JioStar in November 2024. The merger brought together the companies' television broadcasting, digital streaming and sports businesses. JioStar subsequently undertook a restructuring exercise in 2025, with more than 500 employees leaving the organisation across functions, according to The Economic Times. Inc42, in its report, put the number of exits in the earlier exercise at more than 1,000. The latest cuts come amid a wider reduction in employee strength across the television industry. Zee Entertainment's employee count fell from 3,434 in FY25 to 3,007 in FY26, while Sony Pictures Networks India reduced its workforce by more than 10 per cent, The Economic Times reported.

headline: HUMTA promises space in Hyderabad for pedestrians, other road users by 2050; identifies 120 locations for skywalks, FoBs and other infra
content: HYDERABAD Hyderabad is set to become a pedestrian friendly city by 2050. This was the plan laid out by B. Jeevan Babu, Managing Director of the Hyderabad Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority during the four-day Indian Roads Congress. For that date on the horizon, 120 locations have been identified for skywalks, Foot over Bridges (FoB) and other pedestrian infrastructure facilities. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/in-telangana-the-right-to-walk-derailed-by-design/article71147816.ece Gaps in pedestrians infrastructure being examined “The Comprehensive Mobility Plan for 2050 is nearing completion. Its scope includes assessing pedestrian infrastructure gaps and demand, walking access to [Hyderabad] Metro, MMTS, bus stops and terminals, road safety and pedestrian crashes, links to land use and activity centres, and investment priorities. The final report is expected in one or two months,” said Mr. Jeevan Babu, showing a presentation that showed the gaps and fixes proposed. A few corridors for initial changes “We have road space, but that is not properly used. The usability is divided. Pedestrian issues with roads are not properly addressed and vehicular movement is dominating the road. So, we are planning to have space for all. This will create development of roads hierarchy and usage. We have identified a few corridors for the initial changes,” he said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/more-than-50-population-uses-pedestrian-spaces-why-focus-on-cars-asks-panellist-at-irc/article71728849.ece A few locations which are nightmare for Hyderabad pedestrians He shared two locations that are a logistical nightmare for pedestrians in Hyderabad: the Secunderabad Station and Rathifile Bus Station area, and another at JNTU and Lulu Mall area. Two other locations where skywalks are planned include the coaching centres zone in Dilsukhnagar and the IT workplaces in Hitec City. 1-km skywalk to connect Metro, railway and bus stations in Secunderabad The intervention in Secunderabad — a 1-kilometre skywalk — will bring about an integration of the Secunderabad East and West Metro Station, the railway station and the three bus stations of Secunderabad, Rathifile and the Uppal bus station in the area. It will provide a continuous elevated pedestrian corridor reducing the number of people crossing the road and risking their lives. “So, this is a concept of multimodal integration. This is to actually encourage people to use pedestrian infrastructure to reach from the railway station to their destination. And we are restricting people from spilling over onto the roads through design intervention,” he said giving an outline. 2.63 km intervention in Kukatpally Similarly, the intervention in Kukatpally, albeit a longer one at 2.63 km, will connect the JNTU Metro station, JNTU campus and the neighbourhood commercial zones of Rythu bazaar and Lulu Mall. “Rapid urbanisation and increasing vehicle ownership have created significant pedestrian safety and congestion challenges at major commercial and office zones like L.B. Nagar, Dilsukhnagar, Hitec City and Ikea Hyderabad. Existing pedestrian infrastructure is inadequate, resulting in unsafe at-grade crossings, traffic conflicts, and poor first-and-last mile connectivity,” said Mr. Babu. Along with these interventions, new parking police, street design guidelines, multi-modal integration guidelines are also on the anvil. “Ultimately, the vision and goal is to transform Hyderabad into an economically competitive, world-class, quality city with public transport-first approach and appropriate non-motorised transport facility for everyone,” said Mr. Jeevan Babu.

headline: Deficient monsoon leaves Udaipur’s lakes shrinking; raises fears of tourism slowdown, water crisis
content: The shimmering lakes that have long defined Udaipur’s identity and drawn tourists from across the world are witnessing declining water levels following a deficient monsoon, raising concerns over the city's tourism-dependent economy.According to the Rajasthan Water Resources Department’s (WRD) reports, Fateh Sagar and Swaroop Sagar, which were filled to capacity in November last year, have witnessed a significant decline in water storage. The picture is starkly different from the usually brimming lake by August or September, which attracts residents and tourists to witness the opening of its overflow gates. With the peak tourist season underway, restaurant owners and boating operators fear that further depletion of water levels could adversely affect tourist footfall, as well as businesses and livelihoods dependent on the city's lakes. Residents are also apprehensive about a potential drinking water crisis in the coming months.What the reports sayAccording to the reports, the water level in Fateh Sagar, which has a designed gauge level of 13 feet, declined from 5.51 feet in October to nearly 4 feet in November. The lake, which was filled to capacity in October last year, held only 60.83% of its total water storage capacity in November this year.Similarly, Swaroop Sagar, which has a full gauge level of 11 feet, recorded a water level of 7 feet in November, with its storage declining from 100% last year to 63% this year. Udai Sagar, at a full gauge of around 24 feet, recorded a water level of 21 feet, with storage declining from 91% last year to 80% this year. Meanwhile, Goverdhan Vilas, which has a full-gauge level of around 9 feet, recorded a water level of 6 feet, holding only 47% of its total storage capacity.The WRD reports also showed that the combined water storage of 15 medium and small reservoirs in Udaipur district declined by 42% year-on-year in November, from 271.48 million cubic metres (MCM) to 151.43 MCM.Several reservoirs, including Badgaon, Vallabhnagar, Aakodra and Ghasa, which were filled to capacity last year, held only 38.17%, 50.34%, 7.60% and 19.59% of their respective storage capacities in November this year. Meanwhile, Sei Dam held 24.31% and Mansi Wakal 49.53% of their storage capacities.Across the larger Udaipur water resources zone, comprising 178 reservoirs, water storage declined by 43.18% year-on-year in October, from 1,531.74 MCM to 870.25 MCM. By November, it had further declined to 814.99 MCM, accounting for just 44.04% of its total capacity, against the statewide average of 61.71%.The department’s rainfall data showed that between June and early October, Swaroop Sagar received 236 mm of rainfall, while Nai, an important catchment area for Pichola, received 272 mm. Udaipur city recorded 327 mm of rainfall, while Girwa received 315 mm, Dewas 355 mm, Sei Dam 392 mm and Udai Sagar 393 mm.The fearsUdaipur’s lakes play a significant role in the city's tourism economy, supporting hotels, restaurants, boating services and several other lake-dependent businesses.Vipul, a local restaurant owner, said, “This is usually the peak tourist season in Udaipur, but inadequate rainfall and low water levels in the lakes are affecting business.”Boating operators at Lake Pichola also expressed apprehension over the receding water levels, saying that a further decline could increase operational costs and difficulties. If the situation worsens, they may even have to suspend boating services.Environmentalist Anil Mehta said inadequate rainfall across the catchment areas of Udaipur’s lakes had affected the entire network of interconnected water bodies.“Udaipur’s lakes are part of an interconnected water system. Fateh Sagar is primarily fed by the Chhota Madar and Bada Madar reservoirs through the Madar Canal. It also receives water from Badi Talab through the Upli Badi and Hawala Kalan canals. Once Pichola fills to capacity, its surplus water flows into Fateh Sagar through a link canal after the Kala Kiwad gates are opened. Similarly, excess water from Fateh Sagar flows into Udai Sagar through the Ayad River,” he said.“Areas such as Nai, Bujhra and Kodiat are important catchment areas for Pichola. Normally, adequate rainfall in these areas feeds the Sisama River, which carries water to Pichola through the Nandeshwar channel. However, this year, inadequate rainfall in the catchment areas has resulted in insufficient water flowing into the rivers and streams feeding the lakes,” Mehta added.While deficient rainfall has emerged as an immediate challenge, human interventions, including encroachments, unregulated construction, and the disruption of natural drainage channels, have also raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of Udaipur’s historic lake system.On June 5 this year, the Rajasthan high court took suo motu cognisance of growing ecological threats to Udaipur’s lakes, flagging concerns over encroachments, unregulated construction, pollution, degradation of catchment areas and disruption of natural drainage channels.The court directed authorities to undertake comprehensive inspections and submit detailed reports on the ecological condition, geographical extent, catchment areas, hydrological connectivity and conservation status of the water bodies.The order covers several prominent lakes, including Pichola, Fateh Sagar, Swaroop Sagar, Rang Sagar, Roop Sagar, Doodh Talai, Goverdhan Sagar, Badi and Udai Sagar.Apart from the potential impact on tourism, declining water reserves have also put pressure on the city's drinking water supply.Ravindra Kumar Chaudhary, superintending engineer of the Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), said inadequate rainfall had resulted in negligible inflows into surface water sources, causing problems with drinking water supply.Geeta Devi, a local resident, recalled the water crisis of 2005, when several of the city's prominent lakes were on the verge of drying up.“Earlier, water supply was available on alternate days. Now, the interval between water supplies has increased in some areas. The water level in borewells has also declined. If this situation continues, we will face a situation like 2005, when the city's major lakes were almost on the verge of drying up,” she said.However, a senior PHED officer, speaking to HT on condition of anonymity, said, “Yes, the situation is concerning, but it is not as severe as it was in 2005. Fortunately, Udaipur has not been declared drought-affected so far, unlike several other districts in the state. All necessary measures are being taken to address the situation.”

headline: Where is the accountability: Mallikarjun Kharge slams Modi government on anaemia report
content: New Delhi: The Congress on Wednesday attacked the Centre over a report on malnutrition and anaemia in the country and asked where is the accountability after 12 years of the Modi government. .Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked how can India realise its demographic dividend when millions of its women and children continue to suffer from malnutrition. ."The Modi Govt's own ICMR-SAMPADA report reveals that 55.9% of women of reproductive age are anaemic. Nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in Vitamin B12. 42% of children aged 1-4 years are anaemic. In Gujarat, 66% of women of reproductive age and 57% of young children are anaemic," Kharge said on X. .The Modi government's emphasis on "mild" anaemia cannot obscure the fact that nearly 30% of women of reproductive age suffer from moderate or severe anaemia, the Congress chief said. .Mallikarjun Kharge targets Prime Minister Modi on price rise, says progress will not be measured by length of his speeches.The latest NFHS-6 also reveals that nearly one-third of children are underweight and one in five suffers from acute malnutrition, Kharge said. ."Consider the Government's own financial records. Over Rs 1.13 lakh Cr released under Saksham Anganwadi, POSHAN 2.0 and predecessor schemes in six financial years. Over Rs 2,500 crore gap between funds released and utilised under POSHAN 2.0 in just four years. Nearly 44% of funds released under the original POSHAN Abhiyaan remained unutilised," he pointed out. .Kharge further said the share of Women and Child Development in the Union Budget has nearly halved -- from 0.96% in 2015-16 to 0.50% in 2025-26. .After 12 years of the Modi government, multiple nutrition schemes, fortified rice and iron supplementation programmes, where is the accountability?" Kharge said. .The Congress on Tuesday cited an official report that showed Gujarat faring poorly in terms of anaemia prevalence in 2023-25, and asked whether Union Health Minister J P Nadda would survive the release of this "damning report". .Congress general secretary in-charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh, had pointed out that the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has just put out a report titled "Anaemia and Micronutrient Deficiencies Across the Life Course in India". .In Gujarat, 61.4 per cent of adolescent girls (10-19 years), 63.8 per cent of adult women (20-59 years) and 66.2 per cent of women in reproductive age (15-49 years) were found to be suffering from anaemia during 2023-25, Ramesh said on X. ."Only Chhattisgarh fared worse. The corresponding figures for the best performing state Kerala were 21.4 per cent, 28 per cent and 29.1 per cent, no doubt high but nowhere near the levels prevailing in Gujarat, which for some years has been propagated as a model state by the prime minister and his cheerleaders," Ramesh said. .Why are we becoming 'vishwaguru' in air pollution: Mallikarjun Kharge targets Modi govt.In fact, for children in the age group of 12-59 months, Gujarat had the highest anaemia prevalence (56.5 per cent) while Kerala had the lowest (14.5 per cent), he said. ."Will the genial Union Health Minister survive the release of this damning report?" Ramesh asked. .Prevalence of anaemia in India is lower than reported in previous national surveys, with severe anaemia accounting for less than 2 per cent of cases across most age groups, according to findings of the Indian Council of Medical Research's SAMPADA survey released on Monday. .SAMPADA -- or the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry -- conducted during 2023-25, covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 states and Union Territories. .More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex and physiological groups. .The findings also showed that most cases of anaemia were mild, indicating an opportunity for early intervention, the Department of Health Research said.

headline: Before ‘Arohara’ for Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, two eminent musicians composed ragas in praise of Jayalalithaa
content: CHENNAI The chanting of Arohara in praise of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay during the ‘Soorasamharam’ celebrations earlier this month (on November 15, 2026) drew criticism from opposition parties and several Hindu organisations, as the chant is traditionally a devotional invocation to Lord Murugan. Folk singer Velmurugan later expressed regret over the incident and assured he would not repeat it. However, this is not entirely unprecedented in Tamil Nadu. The State has witnessed similar instances of musical adulation during the tenure of former Chief Minister Jayalalithaa, when prominent musicians composed ragas and performed them on stage in her praise. One of them even equated her with the presiding deity at Tirumala Tirupati.

headline: Wakf Board chairman Hafiz Syed Muhammad Ali Al-Hussaini unveils KBN Gold Cup trophies
content: KALABURAGI The cricket and hockey trophies of the Khaja Bandanawaz Gold Cup 2026 sports tournament, organised by the KBN House of Sports under the Khaja Education Society, were formally unveiled on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) by Hafiz Syed Muhammad Ali Al-Hussaini, Sajjada Nashin of Dargah Hazrat Khaja Bandanawaz (RA), chairman of the Karnataka State Board of Auqaf, Vice-Chancellor of Khaja Bandanawaz University and president of the Khaja Education Society. Addressing the players, Mr. Al-Hussaini said that victory and defeat were two sides of the same coin in sports and should be accepted with equal grace. He wished all the participating teams success in the tournament. The chief guest at the toss ceremony, Mr. Shivaranjan Satyampet, editor of Pramatha Vani and vice-president of the Kalaburagi District Working Journalists’ Association, appreciated the educational and sporting opportunities being provided by the Khaja Education Society in the region. The KBN Gold Cup 2026 sports tournament, being held from November 3 to December 4, features football, cricket and hockey competitions. The football tournament has already concluded, while the cricket tournament is currently under way. The trophy unveiling ceremony was held on the 10th day of the cricket tournament in the presence of several dignitaries, including Khaja Education Society general secretary Prof. A.M. Pathan, KBN University Pro-Vice-Chancellor Prof. Syed Ashfaq Ahmed, Registrar Mir Vilayat Ali, society secretary Benny Kuriakose, M. Jeelani and Sohail Munshi. Following the ceremony, the players of Al-Barkat School and Just Cricket Academy, who were to face each other in the 10th-day match, were introduced to the dignitaries. The national anthem was then rendered, following which Mr. Satyampet formally inaugurated the match by conducting the toss.

headline: Devotees barred from Thirupparankundram hill for second day as police restrict public entry
content: Devotees and the general public were barred from ascending the Thirupparankundram hill here for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, with heavy police personnel deployed near the entrance of the Palani Andavar temple.Police have erected barricades along the pathway leading to the hill and are restricting entry strictly to local residents. Those living on Kottai Street, which leads to the Palani Andavar temple, are being permitted access only after verification of their address through Aadhaar cards.Also Read: Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran held ahead of ‘Karthigai Deepam’ lighting in Madurai The Supreme Court had permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the disputed hilltop Deepathoon (stone) pillar located near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah on November 24, strictly by an authorised team, while barring the general public, processions, and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.Also Read: Karthigai Deepam lit at Madurai hilltop temple, not atop sacred pillarHowever, the TVK government on Tuesday defied the Supreme Court order, and the festival lamp was lit only at its customary place at Thirupparankundram.Security was tightened around the entire hill from Monday night, and the ban on devotees and the public ascending the hill has been in force since 6 pm on November 23.Also Read: Hindu outfits protest, BJP slams Vijay govt after Karthigai Deepam not lit at SC-approved spotHeavy police deployment continued near the Palani Andavar temple entrance on Wednesday as the restrictions remained in place.

headline: Nainar Nagenthran, Annamalai condemn use of ‘Arohara’ chant to praise Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, Minister
content: CHENNAI We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai on Monday (November 16, 2026) condemned a member of a committee under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department for allegedly chanting ‘Arohara’ in praise of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and HR&CE Minister during the Soorasamharam festival at Tiruchendur on Sunday (November 15). Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran also expressed his disapproval, saying it hurt devotees’ sentiments. Tiruchendur witnesses grand Soorasamharam amid chants by lakhs of devotees storyline 1 In a social media post, Mr. Annamalai said Velmurugan, a member of the HR&CE Department committee, had raised ‘Arohara’ chants for the Chief Minister and the Minister during the festival. Describing the act as condemnable, Mr. Annamalai said the “sacred devotional chant,” traditionally raised by devotees in praise of Lord Murugan, should not be used to glorify political leaders. Such an act would undermine spiritual traditions and hurt the sentiments of millions of devotees, Mr. Annamalai contended, and urged the Chief Minister to advise those concerned against using religious festivals and devotional expressions for political praise. Separately, interacting with journalists at the Chennai airport, Mr. Annamalai welcomed the communication from the National Commission for Women to Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police calling for an inquiry and a report into allegations that the Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh (TVK) had sent “obscene messages” to the District Collector. T.N. BJP chief demands apology Mr. Nagenthran also condemned the chants praising the Chief Minister and the HR&CE Minister. In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran alleged that the Tiruchendur temple was being turned into a political platform to glorify the Chief Minister and asked whether devotees had gathered at the temple to hear praises of Mr. Vijay. He also criticised the appointment of Velmurugan, a film personality, to the HR&CE trustees selection committee, alleging a lack of spiritual understanding. Mr. Nagenthran demanded that Mr. Velmurugan tender an immediate public apology for hurting devotees’ sentiments. AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran also found fault with the use of the chant and wondered “who authorised commentators of the event to praise the Chief Minister.”

headline: Maharashtra teachers to launch digital non-cooperation movement from December 1
content: Teachers’ organisations across Maharashtra have decided to launch a digital non-cooperation movement from December 1 to protest against the growing burden of online work and mobile applications, which they say is affecting classroom teaching.The decision was taken at a meeting of representatives of various teachers’ organisations held at Shikshak Bhavan in Pune on Tuesday.As part of the first phase of the protest, teachers will quit WhatsApp groups created by Block Resource Centres (BRCs), Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs) and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). They have also decided not to cooperate with the use of various additional mobile applications and online activities assigned to them.Vijay Kombe, state president of the Maharashtra Rajya Prathamik Shikshak Samiti, said, “Teachers are being burdened with an increasing number of online tasks, which are affecting their primary responsibility of teaching students. A single principal is part of more than 20 WhatsApp groups and is expected to follow instructions received through them. Teachers are also being asked to download and use several applications developed by government departments and NGOs. We have decided to launch a digital non-cooperation movement from December 1.”Also Read: Punjab: Unemployed teachers, cops scuffle outside CM’s house in SangrurHowever, Kombe clarified that the teachers would continue to use applications and digital platforms directly related to students and essential school activities.“We will continue working on student-centric applications and digital tasks such as uploading student attendance, mid-day meal data and UDISE information. Our main objection is to the enforcement of additional applications developed by NGOs and government departments, for which teachers are repeatedly asked to download and feed information. These activities add to our workload and take away time from teaching,” he said.The teachers’ organisations said that repeated requests to the government to reduce the online workload had not led to any positive decision. They said that instructions and demands for information were being sent through WhatsApp groups at all hours, affecting teachers’ personal time and mental well-being.Also Read: Ludhiana: Salary of 33 teachers withheld over BLO duty, union objectsThe organisations are also planning to submit representations to the concerned authorities at the state, district and taluka levels, seeking relief from unnecessary online work.Meanwhile, senior education department officials said they had not received any official communication from the teachers’ organisations regarding the proposed protest.“We have not received any official correspondence from the organisations yet. Once we receive it, we will look into the matter and take appropriate action,” a senior education department official said.

headline: SC refuses interim bail for Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam, says will await UAPA ruling
content: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to entertain pleas for interim bail for former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam in the larger conspiracy linked to the 2020 Delhi riots case and said that a decision on their release will have to await a decision by a three-judge bench on whether delay in trial can be a ground for bail under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA).Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddharth Dave, appearing for Khalid and Imam, urged the court to consider granting them interim bail pending the three-judge bench decision.A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “We will not hear it today…We will have to constitute a larger bench in light of the observations made in the order dated May 22, 2026 passed in Tasleem Ahmed v State of NCT of Delhi.”Sibal noted a two-judge bench on May 22 granted 2020 Delhi riots accused Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi interim bail while referring whether delay in trial should be a ground for grant of bail under UAPA to a larger bench. He said both Khalid and Imam should be considered for interim bail on similar lines.Sibal said that by allowing Khalid and Imam’s matter to be heard with the bench hearing the larger issue, the accused will remain inside jail as the January 5 Supreme Court order denying them bail said they could reapply after a year or once protected witnesses are examined. “Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing.”The bench said, “We are aware of everything. We have done our homework and have gone through the January 5 judgment.”The January 5 order said that the role attributed to Khalid and Imam stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. The Supreme Court granted bail to five other accused in the riots case.In May, a bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan granted bail to a narco-terror accused, saying that constitutional courts cannot permit Section 43D(5) of the UAPA, the provision imposing stringent conditions for bail, to eclipse the guarantees of liberty and speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution.The two-judge bench, which decided the bail plea of Ahmed and Saifi, cited the May 18 judgment and decided to place the matter before the CJI for an authoritative decision.Khalid and Imam approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi high court’s dismissal of their bail on September 30. Imam said that the case is at the stage of arguments on charge and the trial has not proceeded.In such a scenario, he said that “continued detention is no longer process-oriented and becomes punitive by reason of unreasonable and unjustified delay.”

headline: Jharkhand Assembly’s special session starts; Finance Minister moves resolution against SIR
content: Ranchi A two-day special session of the Jharkhand Assembly got underway on Wednesday (Novermber 25, 2026), with state Finance Minister Radha Krishna Kishore moving a resolution against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking its immediate halt. During the session, the House will deliberate on the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise and the amended mines law that was passed in Parliament in August. Moving the resolution against SIR, Kishore said voters were facing difficulties due to procedural complexities and technical shortcomings in the voter list revision process. "Of Jharkhand's 2.21 crore voters, 27 per cent were deemed suspicious and sent notices," he said. Alleging that the Election Commission of India was "working as the Centre's puppet", the minister said that removing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was "necessary to protect the Constitution". "There is an urgent need to halt the SIR exercise immediately and to issue a fresh standard operating procedure to ensure transparency in the process," Mr. Kishore said. The Assembly is scheduled to discuss challenges associated with SIR, following which the resolution is expected to be put to vote. Once approved by the House, the resolution will be forwarded to the Centre and other competent authorities, an official said.

headline: TVK committed ‘biggest constitutional affront’, says BJP amid Deepam row; Cong hits back
content: The lighting of a ceremonial lamp atop a temple instead of a sacred but disputed stone pillar in Tamil Nadu sparked a fresh political slugfest on Wednesday, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accusing the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and ally Congress of committing the “biggest constitutional affront” and “showing contempt for the Constitution”.There was no immediate comment from the TVK but the Congress hit back, alleging the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) were “spreading fake news” and “politicising” the matter.The developments came a day after the Karthigai Deepam was lit atop a temple on the outskirts of Madurai and not at the Deepathoon, the pillar, triggering allegations that the state government violated a Supreme Court order that last week allowed the lighting on the pillar as a one-time measure. The dispute centres on the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop location and the state authorities' objections to implementing the direction, citing law-and-order restrictions and customary practices.Also read | In Madurai's Karthigai Deepam row, SC asks parties to file contempt applications, says will pass appropriate orders“Today, I want to draw your attention to what we consider the biggest constitutional and cultural affront committed by the INDI alliance (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) and the Tamil Nadu government. On the occasion of Kartik Purnima yesterday, the Tamil Nadu government did not comply with the Supreme Court's order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam for just one day, subject to certain conditions,” BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said at a press conference in the Capital."I think this is the biggest and dastardly example of contempt against the Constitution by the so-called self-proclaimed Pioneers of the constitutional defence..,” he added.On November 20, top court justices Aravind Kumar and VM Pancholi had permitted the lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day as a restricted, one-time measure only. The court had also stayed the operative portions of the Madras high court’s January 6 judgment while clarifying that its permission will not establish any customary right to perform the ritual at the site in “subsequent years”.Also read | 'Age-old customs': Temple board defends lighting of Karthigai Deepam at usual spot despite SC orderOn Tuesday, the temple board said it had unanimously resolved to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam, located directly above the main deity, and protect the temple’s age-old customs. “Such long standing continuous practices, religious traditions and rituals and the Agama rules are considered the unique religious identity of the temple,” a detailed press note signed by temple Board of Trustees chairperson V Shanmugasundaram said.BJP leader CR Kesavan hit out at the “discriminatory” behaviour of the TVK-Congress government. "The TVK-Congress government, which defied the Supreme Court order, has betrayed the people of Tamil Nadu and backstabbed countless devotees of Lord Muruga. This discriminatory TVK-Congress government has insulted the sentiments and faiths of crores of Hindu devotees by humiliating and demeaning them as second-class citizens,” he said.“The TVK Congress government is nothing but a bigoted clone of the erstwhile DMK (Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam( government. The people of Tamil Nadu and the countless devotees of Lord Muruga and Hindu devotees will never forgive nor forget this TVK Congress government, led by Joseph Vijay, for perpetrating the very divisive and dangerous politics of polarisation,” he added.Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore accused the BJP and the RSS of attempting to turn the matter into a "political" issue. He also accused the opposition party of "spreading fake news", saying the state government had implemented the top court’s order.“We all know that the Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance always respects the Supreme Court. For some other reason, the Sanghis and RSS people want to turn it into a political controversy,” he said.“They (opposition) can do whatever they want, but the Tamil Nadu government under Vijay's leadership has fully implemented the Supreme Court's orders. This kind of fake news is unacceptable. The BJP and RSS are spreading such fake news. Tamil Nadu is a state where communal harmony prevails, and we will not allow this kind of division in the state,” he added.HT reached out to TVK for a comment but did not get one immediately.In a post on X on Tuesday, state law minister CTR Nirmalkumar said: “The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram.”

headline: Operation Gaja in Karnataka: People protest in Mudigere, observe bandh
content: Mudigere Residents of Mudigere taluk in Chikkamagaluru district staged protests and called for a bandh on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) against Operation Gaja, the Forest Department’s drive to move wild elephants from Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary. Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary vast enough to accommodate more elephants, says APCCF storyline 1 The bandh call has continued received a good response so far. A majority of the shops remained closed. They raised slogans against the Forest Department, Excise and Hassan district minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda for the drive. One more killed in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk; protests intensify storyline 1 Mudigere MLA submits resignation over elephant operation Mudigere MLA submits resignation over elephant operation Mudigere MLA submits resignation over elephant operation storyline 1 About 39 elephants have already reached Mudigere taluk, in two herds near Dunduga and Makonahalli. headline: Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati Thomas Menamparampil dies at 90 in Hyderabad hospital
content: Guwahati, Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati Reverend Thomas Menamparampil died at a hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday following a brief illness. He was 90.The current Guwahati Archbishop, John Moolachira, said Menamparampil passed away at 5:40 am and described the death as an immense loss to the Church and all who experienced his pastoral care.He also expressed heartfelt gratitude to everyone who accompanied Archbishop Menamparampil with prayers, affection, and support during his illness.Condoling the death, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma described Menamparampil as a man of deep faith and a tireless champion of peace who worked selflessly for reconciliation among communities."Deeply saddened by the passing of Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati, Most Rev. Thomas Menamparampil," Sarma said in an X post. A man of deep faith and a tireless champion of peace, he worked selflessly for reconciliation among communities and for the education of youths across Assam and the northeast, he said."My heartfelt condolences to the Catholic community and all who mourn him. May his soul rest in eternal peace," the chief minister added.Born on October 22, 1936, in Keralam's Pala, Menamparampil joined the Salesians of Don Bosco and was ordained a priest on May 2, 1965. He was appointed the bishop of Dibrugarh in 1981.In 1992, Menamparampil became the first Bishop of Guwahati. Following the elevation of the diocese, he was appointed the first archbishop of Guwahati in 1995, a post he held until his retirement in 2012.For over four decades, Archbishop Menamparampil was at the forefront of grassroots peace missions in Northeast India's most sensitive ethnic flashpoints, including Kokrajhar, Churachandpur, Haflong, Diphu, and Udalguri.In 2011, he was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his sustained efforts to foster dialogue, harmony, and peace among conflicting ethnic and tribal communities in Northeast India.The nomination, which drew international attention to grassroots reconciliation in the region, highlighted his quiet mediation across recurring communal fault lines, Moolachira said.Menamparampil received the Dr J Abdul Kalam World Peace Award in 2023 and the Peace Award in 2026.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Congress to hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across States on Constitution Day, Kharge to join programme in Lucknow
content: New Delhi The Congress will hold Samvidhan Raksha Marches across the country on Thursday (November 26, 2026) to mark Constitution Day, stepping up its campaign against alleged electoral roll manipulation and the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) failure to protect the right to vote. In a statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), AICC general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal said all Pradesh Congress Committees (PCCs) would organise the marches, with party president Mallikarjun Kharge participating in the Lucknow event. Beyond ‘vote chori’, Congress needs a broader strategy to take on Modi government Beyond ‘vote chori’, Congress needs a broader strategy to take on Modi government Congress and the wider Opposition bloc may need to recalibrate their strategy on the alleged ‘vote chori’ campaign, which has overshadowed issues that affect voters’ everyday lives News Analysis Beyond ‘vote chori’, Congress needs a broader strategy to take on Modi government storyline 1 Mr. Venugopal cited the allegations of “vote chori” raised by Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, including fake and duplicate entries in Mahadevapura, attempts to delete genuine voters in Aland and irregularities in Haryana. He accused the ECI of failing to order an impartial inquiry. What is the Aland voter fraud case? | Explained storyline 1 He also alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls had put millions of voters at risk, claiming that deletions across its three phases were believed to exceed 13 crore. The marches will begin at statues of Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi, followed by a reading of the Preamble and an oath to protect the Constitution. The party will also run its ‘Vote Rakshak’ campaign, with workers visiting polling booths to identify deleted voters and help them reclaim their voting rights. Mr. Venugopal appealed to citizens, including students, youth, farmers, workers and members of marginalised communities, to join the marches. “The Constitution gave every Indian the vote. The Indian National Congress is duty-bound and committed to defend it,” he said. The party’ communications chief Jairam Ramesh also recalled the speech delivered by B.R. Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly on November 25, 1949, a day before the draft Constitution was adopted. Quoting Ambedkar’s warning that “Bhakti in religion may be a road to salvation of the soul. But in politics, Bhakti or hero-worship is a sure road to degradation and to eventual dictatorship”, Mr. Ramesh said, “This magnificent speech is for the ages. It is ever relevant”. Ends

headline: ‘Well played, Namit Malhotra’: Ramayana VFX artist calls out DNEG over layoff after 4 years without a hike
content: While Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi’s Ramayana: Part 1 continues to dominate headlines for its record-breaking box office run—crossing ₹1,735.15 crore worldwide and closing in on the ₹1,000-crore mark in India—a former crew member has painted a starkly different picture of life behind the scenes.A visual effects artist, Rahul Dhanwe, who worked on Ramayana, criticised Namit Malhotra-owned DNEG in a LinkedIn post, alleging that he was laid off after 4.6 years with the company without receiving a single salary increment for over four years.Dhanwe, who claimed that he spent the last two years working on the mythological film, questioned the treatment of artists in the visual effects industry and urged fellow professionals to treat DNEG as their “last option”.'Feels like we worked for charity'In his post, Dhanwe said that senior management repeatedly asked employees to stand by the studio during a difficult period, and that he did so in the hope that conditions would improve.“Well played, Namit Malhotra and The Ramayana World. Really well played! I spent 4.6 years at DNEG, including the last two years working on Ramayana. Senior management repeatedly asked us to support the company during difficult times. We did,” he wrote. “For over four years, I worked without a single rupee of salary increment, hoping things would eventually improve. But what did we get in return? A layoff!”He added, “I never expected a special reward for supporting the company. But after investing 4.6 years of my career, this is certainly not the treatment I expected. We gave two years of hard work, skills, and dedication to Ramayana.” He said, “In a way, our personal sacrifices became part of our contribution to the film. We won't share in its future success or profits. It honestly feels like we worked for charity.”Warning to fellow artists and concern for ‘Ramayana Part 2’ teamDhanwe said his biggest regret was spending 4.6 years at the studio, adding that he believed he could have grown further professionally, financially and creatively elsewhere.“I understand companies are businesses, but does that mean artists should be treated as disposable resources?” he asked."My biggest regret is that I wasted 4.6 important years of my career at DNEG. Had I spent those years elsewhere, I genuinely believe I could have grown much further professionally, financially, and creatively. I am also concerned about the artists currently working on Ramayana Part 2. I sincerely hope they don't face a similar situation," he wrote.Calling his stint at the company the worst studio experience of his career, Dhanwe advised other VFX artists to weigh their options carefully."Honestly, DNEG has been the worst studio experience of my professional life. Such a big name, yet such a disappointing experience when it comes to treating artists," he wrote.He also flagged concerns for the artists currently working on Ramayana: Part 2.“To fellow artists: Think carefully before joining DNEG. If you have another good offer, consider it first. Keep DNEG as your last option. I wasted 4.6 years. Please don't waste yours. Artists are not disposable resources. They deserve respect, stability, and fair treatment,” he said.Neither Malhotra nor DNEG had issued an official response to the allegations at the time of publication.In a follow-up comment on the same post, he shared an update on his settlement, writing, “I have received a gratuity now. Thank you, guys.”

headline: Relocation of wild elephants does not solve human-elephant conflict in Keralam’s Chinnakkanal, finds study
content: IDUKKI Amid growing demands from residents and farmers groups to relocate wild tusker Chakkakompan from Chinnakkanal in Idukki, a four-member expert panel has found that removing or translocating wild elephants does not solve human-elephant conflict in the region. Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy says steel-rope barriers and GPS collars are among options to address the issue Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister storyline 1 District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt had constituted the panel in September to find ways to address the rising human-elephant conflicts in Chinnakkanal. The panel includes P.S. Easa, former Director of the Kerala Forest Research Institute and a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Asian Elephant Specialist Group; Rajan Pilakandy, a scientist at the institute; Jomy Augustine, a retired Professor and former Head of the Department of Botany at St. Thomas College, Pala; and Murukesan, a tribal community member from Chinnakkanal. According to sources, the panel’s report noted that authorities previously translocated a tusker known as Arikomban from Chinnakkanal to reduce conflict. Later, concerns arose over another tusker named Murivalan, who died while traveling its traditional path toward Suryanelli. Groups to prevent human-elephant conflict linked to more elephant deaths Groups to prevent human-elephant conflict linked to more elephant deaths Anti-depredation squads were formed in villages to incentivise communities to join hands with the Forest Department to respond to elephants together. However, the searchlights and firecrackers the squads used to drive elephants away possibly created a ‘landscape of fear’, forcing elephants to stray into more dangerous situations Groups to prevent human-elephant conflict linked to more elephant deaths storyline 1 ‘Not a solution’ “The removal of these two ‘problematic’ elephants did not alleviate human-elephant conflict in Chinnakkanal,” the report stated. “This indicates that removal of elephants is not a solution to the human-elephant conflict in the landscape.” Instead, the panel recommended attaching a radio transmitter to any identified “problematic” elephant to monitor its movements. According to the panel, though elephants frequently visit Mathikettan Shola National Park, a rapid habitat assessment revealed a shortage in food. It recommended planting reeds in the valleys as a restoration measure to encourage elephants to spend more time inside the park. To reduce disturbances, the panel called for regulating high-intensity lighting at resorts in Chinnakkanal, specifically naming Mahindra Serene, Club Mahindra and Sterling resorts. “Frequent night safaris should be banned. Noise-making activities in the tourist facilities should be regulated,” the panel recommended. Speed limits Regarding road safety, the panel found that elephants cross the Gap road stretch of the national highway at specific locations. It recommended implementing speed limits in those zones and installing advanced warning systems to prevent highway accidents. The experts also criticised the Rapid Response Team’s current practice of driving elephants away from an area based on public demand. The panel advised against scaring wild elephants at any time, urging teams to focus on monitoring the animals and alerting residents instead. Human-elephant conflict: Crop loss, property damage caused by tuskers highest post-monsoon, says study Human-elephant conflict: Crop loss, property damage caused by tuskers highest post-monsoon, says study Human-elephant conflict: Crop loss, property damage caused by tuskers highest post-monsoon, says study storyline 1 To ensure unimpeded elephant movement, the panel recommended removing fences around the Thachangari estate, which block passage from the Anayirankal reservoir to upper Suryanelli via the 60-acre shola. It also noted that solar fences are being installed indiscriminately along plantation boundaries and urged officials to prioritise protecting human settlements instead. The report stated that encroached and degraded lands in the Anayirankal reservoir catchment area, along with leased tribal areas and revenue lands, must be cleared of encroachments and restored to keep them accessible to elephants. In its ecological assessment of the Anayirankal area, the panel identified food species in the area and found that grass lands in the area provide the highest peak grass biomass followed by eucalyptus plantations, pine plantations and shola forests, while cardamom plantations yield the least. Operation Gaja: Herds regroup, 39 elephants are 3.5 km from Tatkola forest Operation Gaja: Herds regroup, 39 elephants are 3.5 km from Tatkola forest Operation Gaja: Herds regroup, 39 elephants are 3.5 km from Tatkola forest storyline 1 According to Forest department data cited in the report, wild elephant attacks have killed 34 people in the area since May 2010. Since the 2021-22 fiscal year, the department has spent heavily on solar fencing and allocated ₹17,565,490 to the Rapid Response Team for wages, equipment, vehicle maintenance and camp rations — yet elephant attacks and fatalities continue.The panel suggested contextual analysis of all death incidents in Chinnakkanal so that such incidents can be avoided in the future.

headline: Every South film industry is a new learning experience for me: Prashant Bajaj
content: Actor Prashant Bajaj, who made his television debut with Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah, and also shared screen space with Sunny Deol in Gopichand Malineni’s Jaat (2025), is now exploring opportunities across the Telugu, Kannada and Tamil film industries.While television gave him his first opportunity, Prashant was keen to explore films. “Television is good, but I’ve been meaning to try something different. I want to explore the larger canvas of films,” he says.The actor, who played Randeep Hooda’s character’s younger brother in Jaat, describes the film as a major breakthrough. “I got to work with some of the industry’s biggest names. I learnt a lot about fight sequences, acting and reacting on screen, and understanding the scale of a big commercial film,” he says. He also credits director Gopichand Malineni for making him feel comfortable on set. “Despite being such a big director who has delivered several hits, he treats everyone equally. He is a master at what he does and knows exactly what he wants to achieve,” he adds.With projects across three South Indian industries, the actor sees the transition as an opportunity to challenge himself. “The South Indian film industries are completely new to me, but I love challenging myself. Once you get on the sets and put your energy into the work, everything eventually falls into place,” he says.I enjoy being part of different industries.
