headline: TVS succession battle: Lakshmi Venu moves Madras HC against Venu Srinivasan
content: The succession dispute within Venu Srinivasan's branch of the TVS family took a legal turn on Wednesday, with his daughter Lakshmi Venu moving the Madras High Court seeking partition of the branch's joint family assets and allotment of what she says is her rightful share. The suit follows a partition notice issued by Lakshmi on November 16, in which she called upon her father, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary responsibilities and give effect to a fair and lawful division of the assets. The dispute centres on whether the wider TVS family restructuring carried out in 2020, along with a subsequent memorandum of understanding signed by members of Venu Srinivasan's immediate family in 2024, also settled the economic interests within his branch of the family. Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan Venu have maintained that a settlement has already been reached, while Lakshmi and her mother Mallika Srinivasan contend that no comprehensive partition of the family's economic interests has taken place. On Tuesday, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for Venu Srinivasan, had said there was nothing left to mediate because the family members had already entered into an agreement. A statement issued on Lakshmi's behalf on Wednesday said Srinivasan's response reflected no change in his position and did not recognise what she described as her lawful rights. The Madras High Court is likely to take up the matter on Friday. Mallika Srinivasan backed her daughter's decision to move the court. “It is unfortunate that the response to Lakshmi’s notice has not recognized her lawful rights and no progress has been made towards an amicable resolution. In these circumstances, she has been compelled to approach the Court to protect her rights,” Mallika said. The dispute is within the four-member family branch comprising Venu Srinivasan, Mallika Srinivasan, Lakshmi Venu and Sudarshan Venu, representing the third and fourth generations of TVS Group founder T V Sundaram Iyengar's family. “As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of Sudarshan’s,” Mallika added. Lakshmi has maintained that she approached the court after exhausting efforts to reach an amicable resolution and that the legacies of her great-grandfather and grandfather belong to her as much as to her brother. In the suit, Lakshmi has sought partition of the joint family assets and allotment of her claimed share. The assets include interests held through the VS Trust and other holding structures and encompass businesses allocated to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement, including interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton. Lakshmi has also sought the court's assistance in obtaining documents and information that she says have been withheld despite repeated requests. She has maintained that the 2020 restructuring of the wider TVS family did not amount to a partition of assets within Venu Srinivasan's immediate family. Her position is that no settlement or partition of those underlying economic interests was ever completed. The March 2024 memorandum of understanding among the four family members has emerged as a central point of disagreement. Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan regard it as part of a broader family settlement, while Mallika and Lakshmi argue that it largely dealt with issues such as trademarks, brand usage and non-compete arrangements rather than a division of family wealth. Lakshmi has clarified that the suit concerns ownership of joint family assets and is not directed at the operations of any company. She has said she has an interest in the continued strength of the businesses and believes that any partition should be implemented in an orderly manner and in accordance with law. The legal dispute could have implications for the beneficial ownership of assets held through the family's trust and holding structures, although the extent of any impact on the listed companies would depend on the court's findings regarding the nature and ownership of the assets in question.

headline: Nearly 9 in 10 women, girls feel unsafe walking to metro, bus stops in Delhi: Study
content: New Delhi, For many women and girls in Delhi, the journey to a metro station or bus stop itself is a source of fear, with nearly nine in 10 feeling unsafe making their way to the nearest public transport stop, a study by a gender equality organisation has found.The study, conducted by the Centre for Equity and Inclusion , found that 87.5 per cent of those surveyed felt unsafe walking to the nearest metro station or bus stop, while 88.9 per cent felt unsafe in their nearest public park after dark. More than three-fourths reported poorly lit footpaths, and 60 per cent said the footpaths were broken or missing.According to a statement by CEQUIN, the findings, based on responses from 1,588 women, girls and LGBTQ people, point to a safety concern that extends beyond the threat of sexual violence to the conditions in which people navigate the city every day.For nearly 80 per cent of those surveyed, men's behaviour including staring, passing comments and following them made everyday journeys unsafe. The study also found that 80.5 per cent could not identify the civic authority responsible for addressing their concerns, leaving a question mark over where they can turn when public spaces fail them.The study, titled 'Everyday Journeys: Women's and Girls' Access to Footpaths and Public Parks in Delhi', examines how infrastructure, social behaviour and institutional failures shape women's access to public spaces.CEQUIN, which works on gender-based violence and women's rights, has submitted its recommendations to the Supreme Court, the statement read.The findings come against the backdrop of a spate of rape and sexual assault cases reported across Delhi-NCR, including the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park. At least 13 such cases were reported in the first three weeks of September, prompting the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance on September 28 and direct authorities to identify vulnerable public spaces and strengthen safety measures.According to the statement, the study was undertaken in response to this intervention and draws on CEQUIN's 17 years of work on gender-based violence and women's rights. It looks beyond individual crimes to examine how the design and upkeep of public spaces, along with social behaviour and gaps in institutional accountability, can limit women's ability to move freely, the statement further read."When over 80 per cent of respondents cannot even identify which civic authority is responsible for addressing these gaps, exclusion becomes built into the city itself," Lora K Prabhu, co-founder and managing director of CEQUIN, said, adding that the organisation hoped its recommendations would drive measurable, gender-responsive urban reform.The report also cites National Crime Records Bureau data showing that Delhi recorded 13,396 crimes against women in 2024, the highest among India's 19 major metropolitan cities.It further points to the disparity in workforce participation, with Delhi's female Labour Force Participation Rate standing at 14.5 per cent in 2023-24, compared with 54 per cent for men. The report argues that safety fears and restricted mobility affect women's access to employment, though the figures do not establish a direct causal relationship.The study is set to be released on Wednesday at CEQUIN's annual event, 'Hain Haq Hamara Hissedari', marking the start of the '16 Days of Activism' against gender-based violence, the statement read.Founded in 2009, CEQUIN works across Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Rajasthan and Bihar to prevent and address gender-based violence through community mobilisation, advocacy and institutional engagement, with a focus on women, adolescent girls and gender-diverse people from marginalised communities.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Infant denied birth certificate in West Bengal after father’s name deleted in SIR
content: Kolkata A two-and-a-half-month-old infant in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar has been denied a birth certificate after her father’s name was found deleted from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/special-intensive-revision-of-electoral-rolls/ On September 9, Amina Khatun, a resident of Cooch Behar’s Khatamari village, delivered a baby girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital. Following the birth, Ms. Khatun and her husband, Abdul Habib, approached the hospital and the concerned Panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. However, they were reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the Panchayat Pradhan or MLA. When Mr. Habib approached the MLA of the Dinhata constituency, Ajoy Roy, for such verification, the MLA’s office refused the request. Mr. Habib was told that the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the electoral roll during the SIR process. “An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth. My house in Khatamari was built by my grandfather. I have shown them all the documents, but they still refused,” said Mr. Habib. A similar request was also refused by the Block Development Officer (BDO) of Sahebganj on the same grounds, he said. Hear pleas by deleted voters first, Supreme Court directs Bengal SIR tribunals Hear pleas by deleted voters first, Supreme Court directs Bengal SIR tribunals The court directed the ECI to increase the number of tribunals and relocate them to central hubs of Kolkata to facilitate expeditious disposal of the backlog of pending appeals Hear pleas by deleted voters first, Supreme Court directs Bengal SIR tribunals storyline 1 Mr. Habib is not the only one in his family whose name was deleted during the SIR. Three of his sisters’ names were also deleted. The Election Commission of India (ECI) called them for a hearing, citing a ‘logical discrepancy’ that six other persons also claimed his father as their own. Appeal before tribunal However, the names of Mr. Habib’s parents, wife Ms. Khatun, and elder sister were included in the voter’s list. He has now appealed before a tribunal to include his name in the voter’s list but the application is awaiting a decision. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) has strongly objected to the alleged administrative obstruction to issuing the infant’s birth certificate. “Birth registration is a statutory obligation, and every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). The child’s right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents. An administrative dispute concerning SIR cannot become a barrier to a newborn child’s fundamental rights,” said the APCR in an official statement, demanding that the government immediately provide her with a birth certificate. West Bengal CEO office postpones SSR due to unavoidable circumstances West Bengal CEO office postpones SSR due to unavoidable circumstances The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The State government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata. West Bengal CEO office postpones SSR due to unavoidable circumstances storyline 1 There have been several instances in Bengal in the last few months in which residents were denied basic facilities or access to a government scheme after their names were deleted in the SIR. The SIR held before the Assembly polls in West Bengal saw the removal of 91 lakh names from the electoral rolls of the State. Earlier in June, Umme Salma, a resident of Cooch Behar district, had to approach the Calcutta High Court after a local fair price shop dealer told her that her entitlement was likely to be discontinued unless she could show proof of an appeal concerning her electoral status after her name was deleted under SIR. The court had directed that the West Bengal government should not take any coercive steps against the petitioner with regard to her monthly ration entitlement without its permission.

headline: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
content: New Delhi India remains committed to working closely with key Indian Ocean nations to enhance their collective capacities to deal with evolving security threats, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The Indian Ocean as cradle of a new blue economy opinion 1 story Ajit Doval | The spy who came in from the cold In his address at the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male, Mr. Doval listed various pressing challenges facing the region and called for deeper strategic cooperation to address them. The Colombo Security Conclave as a much-needed security dimension opinion 1 Also read | India joins global ocean alliance, pledges to double Indian Ocean monitoring https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/india-joins-global-ocean-alliance-pledges-to-double-indian-ocean-monitoring/article71727999.ece The CSC has emerged as a key regional security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states, comprising India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles. It has largely been focusing on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, and transnational security cooperation. "The Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighbourhood First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision," Mr. Doval said. Visit to Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand will further strengthen India's Act East Policy: PM storyline 1 "We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges," he added. Last March, during his visit to Mauritius, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR, or 'Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, for India's engagement with the Global South. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi/ Mr. Doval said he was confident that the CSC will become an effective instrument in the Indian Ocean region to provide collective security and look after common interests. Maritime safety and security is of primordial importance to Indian Ocean Region: Secretary-General Maritime safety and security is of primordial importance to Indian Ocean Region: Secretary-General Any disruption in the Indian Ocean will have a deep impact on the economy across the region, says Sanjiv Ranjan, Secretary-General of the Indian Ocean Rim Association; war in West Asia overshadows India’s agenda for IORA summit next year, marking 30 years of the grouping Maritime safety and security is of primordial importance to Indian Ocean Region: Secretary-General storyline 1 "India has been trying to work very closely with Sri Lanka, with the Maldives and other countries, and we want to see that this cooperation is further extended," the NSA said. "I assure all of you that India, as one of the countries which had initiated the idea of the Colombo Security Conclave, will give its best and will try to give all necessary help, assistance. I assure you of our fullest commitment to achieve our common objectives," Mr. Doval added. India’s vision is to make Indian Ocean an Ocean of Opportunity: PM Modi in Seychelles India’s vision is to make Indian Ocean an Ocean of Opportunity: PM Modi in Seychelles Seychelles confers the title of ‘Guardian of the Blue Horizon’ on PM Modi; Delegation-level talks held by PM Modi with Seychelles President Herminie to deepen bilateral ties India’s vision is to make Indian Ocean an Ocean of Opportunity: PM Modi in Seychelles storyline 1 The Colombo Security Conclave was established in 2020 when India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives agreed to expand the scope and membership of their trilateral meeting on maritime cooperation. Cooperation under the CSC focuses on the five pillars of maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime and cyber security, protection of critical infrastructure, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

headline: Punjab elections: 30 years after 1996 Moga declaration, PM Modi to revive SAD-BJP alliance from same town
content: In 1996, Shiromani Akali Dal patriarch Parkash Singh Badal announced a decisive shift in Punjab politics from Moga by forging an alliance with the BJP, describing the partnership as essential for Hindu-Sikh amity after the painful years of militancy.Thirty years later, on December 8, Prime Minister Narendra Modi would return to the same politically significant town in the Malwa belt to announce the revival of that alliance, which suffered a setback after the Akalis walked out of the BJP-led NDA in September 2020 over the farm laws.Modi's visit, coinciding with the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal, will be keenly watched for the reasons he cites for the reunion of the estranged partners. Equally significant will be the parallels he draws with the late Akali leader's vision of the alliance, as articulated in the historic Moga Declaration adopted at the Shiromani Akali Dal's 75th anniversary conference on February 24 and 25, 1996.The Moga Declaration described the Akali-BJP alliance as rooted in the principles of Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat. It also envisaged the Akali Dal evolving into an inclusive regional force by expanding its reach among Punjabi Hindus and moving beyond its predominantly panthic image.Union Home Minister Amit Shah invoked the same sentiment while announcing the SAD's return to the NDA on Monday."This alliance will become a symbol of Hindu-Sikh unity in Punjab, India and the world," Shah said, echoing the vision of Parkash Singh Badal.SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, too, described the partnership as "emotional rather than political". Invoking his father's description of the relationship, he said the BJP and SAD shared a "nau-maas ka rishta" (a relationship akin to nail and flesh), portraying the renewed alliance as a coming together of families.The 1996 political shift paved the way for the first-ever pre-poll alliance between the BJP and SAD for the 1997 Punjab Assembly elections. The partnership brought together the BJP's urban support base and the Akali Dal's rural cadres and traditional support base.The alliance won 93 of the 117 Assembly seats in 1997, with the SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. It remains the highest tally recorded by any alliance or party in Punjab. The AAP won 92 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections.The two parties subsequently contested several elections together and remained a significant political force in the state. Their alliance also delivered two consecutive terms in government in 2007 and 2012, a first in Punjab's electoral history.Their separation in 2020 altered the state's political equations, with both parties contesting elections independently thereafter. The December 8 announcement will mark their formal return to a partnership that shaped Punjab politics for nearly a quarter of a century.Whether the revived alliance can recreate, or even come close to, its 1997 electoral performance remains to be seen.But when Modi arrives in Moga on December 8, the historical significance of the town will be difficult to overlook. It was here that Parkash Singh Badal and then BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee helped script a major realignment in Punjab's panthic and regional politics in 1996. The same town is now set to witness another chapter in that political relationship.

headline: CJP's Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being stopped from travelling to London over passport row
content: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London over alleged discrepancies in his passport details, particularly his place of birth.Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union on December 1. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.The development followed a show-cause notice issued to Das by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, on Monday evening, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his birth-related documents within seven days. The notice warned that his passport could be impounded under the Passports Act, 1967, if he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation.According to government sources, inconsistencies in details such as his date of birth and father's name were flagged across documents, including his Aadhaar card, passport and school certificate. The authorities initiated a fresh verification of his documents and information recorded in his passport application.The passport was originally issued to Das on August 21, 2019, following the verification process.Why was Saurav Das stopped from travelling?According to government officials, a passport holder issued a show-cause notice over allegedly incorrect particulars cannot use the passport for international travel until the matter is resolved.An official told TOI, "As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of."Another government officer said Das had time until November 30 to respond to the notice. The official added that he could resume international travel using the same passport once the RPO completed its re-verification and cleared the documents.However, Das said he became aware of the notice only after reaching the airport, claiming that it had been issued just hours before his scheduled departure.Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Das questioned the timing of the notice and the discrepancies flagged by the authorities, pointing out that his passport had been issued in 2019 after police verification and that he had undertaken several international trips since then.“How was I issued the passport which was given after police verification?” he asked.Alleging that the action was linked to his association with the CJP, Das said, “I was scheduled to talk in various prestigious universities in London on their invitation. That trip couldn’t be completed because the coward govt has flagged my passport citing some discrepancies...”UK engagements cancelled amid controversyApart from the Oxford Union panel discussion, Das said he was scheduled to participate in engagements involving Cambridge University, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.The Oxford Union event was scheduled for December 1, with Das and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke listed as key panellists on the organisation's website.Explaining the purpose of his proposed engagements, Das said he intended to discuss the growth of the CJP movement and its use of non-violent methods.“The Indian students studying there wanted to understand what CJP movement is and how it grew. I would have spoken about how this movement without violence could become successful. How the world’s Gen Z could learn from us,” he said.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh, who was also scheduled to travel to the UK, said her visa had been rejected a few days earlier. Dipke said he had also received an invitation but was scheduled to attend a CJP programme in Nagpur on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.The London School of Economics Students' Union Amnesty International Society subsequently announced that its event featuring Das had been indefinitely postponed. In a statement, it condemned what it described as an “arbitrary obstruction” and the “apparent targeting of an individual seeking to engage in academic dialogue and public discussion”.The society expressed solidarity with Das and said it would share updates if the event could be rescheduled.CJP questions action against DasCJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the decision to stop Das from travelling, drawing comparisons with the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi.“Is he (Das) a terrorist, a criminal? Why was he stopped?” Dipke asked at a separate press conference.Meanwhile, a public interest litigation has also been filed in the Madras High Court concerning alleged inconsistencies in Das's birth and parentage documents, while also questioning his citizenship.The passport authorities' re-verification process is pending, with Das required to respond to the show-cause notice by November 30.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: NIELIT brings a talent boost to Amaravati Quantum Valley
content: AMARAVATI The National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) will develop skilled professionals for India’s artificial intelligence, quantum technology and semiconductor sectors, with a goal of supporting 500 startups, its Director General, Madan Mohan Tripathi, has said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/indias-first-ai-quantum-university-campus-inagurated-in-guntur-of-andhra-pradesh/article71728573.ece Speaking to The Hindu at the launch of NIELIT’s Amaravati transit campus at Acharya Nagarjuna University on November 21, Mr. Tripathi said the institute would build a talent pipeline spanning technicians, equipment operators and researchers. From policy to talent: Amaravati Quantum Valley’s innovation blueprint From policy to talent: Amaravati Quantum Valley’s innovation blueprint To put Amaravati among the top five global quantum hubs by 2030, competing alongside established centres in Chicago, Munich, Singapore, and Australia, Andhra Pradesh started with regulation From policy to talent: Amaravati Quantum Valley’s innovation blueprint storyline 1 NIELIT would initially operate from the university before moving to a permanent campus in Amaravati Quantum Valley. The campus would support AI and quantum technology training and research, including quantum computing, sensing, materials and cryptography, he said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/inside-amaravatis-pioneering-leap-to-quantum-frontier/article71692735.ece The institute plans skilling programmes ranging from 30 to 1,000 hours, alongside proposed diploma, B.Tech. and M.Tech. programmes. Training would cover AI, machine learning, advanced computing, quantum communication and cryptography, semiconductor design and testing, with practical exposure to platforms and simulators. India’s first AI, Quantum University campus inaugurated in Guntur of Andhra Pradesh India’s first AI, Quantum University campus inaugurated in Guntur of Andhra Pradesh National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology transit campus on the premises of Acharya Nagarjuna University to commence training programmes on December 1, 2026 India’s first AI, Quantum University campus inaugurated in Guntur of Andhra Pradesh storyline 1 NIELIT would support the National Quantum Mission and the State Quantum Mission by supplying trained personnel. Addressing technological and materials-related challenges, Mr. Tripathi pointed to India’s existing expertise in cryogenics, vacuum technologies, magnet design and superconductivity. Materials research and the India Semiconductor Mission would further strengthen domestic capabilities, he said. During his inaugural address, Mr. Tripathi said the Tirupati centre would focus on semiconductor skilling, while Amaravati would host the proposed institution, envisaged as India’s first university dedicated to quantum technology and AI. Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier The first major test vision of building an indigenous premier deep tech hub arrives soon as an IBM Quantum System, already en route from the U.S., will be installed on February 3, 2027, at Amaravati Quantum Valley; homegrown breakthroughs are already emerging from Amaravati 1Q and Amaravati 1S labs, led by Q SHIVA and NAADA InFocus Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier storyline 1 He praised Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s vision of developing Amaravati Quantum Valley as a full-stack ecosystem, saying that talent development was an important dimension of building capabilities in AI and quantum technologies. The initiative is expected to help Andhra Pradesh develop the skilled workforce required for frontier technologies. By connecting education, research and industry needs, NIELIT could emerge as a key institution within Amaravati Quantum Valley, said C.V. Sridhar, Director, A.P. State Quantum Mission. Amaravati builds indigenous quantum tech stack Amaravati builds indigenous quantum tech stack Amaravati-based companies, universities and startups develop the NAADA chip, Q-SHIVA cryogenic platform, Q-CoRE electronics and Q-CODE software, laying the foundation for building quantum computers locally Amaravati builds indigenous quantum tech stack storyline 1

headline: Solar battery explosion sets thatched hut ablaze, kills five-year-old boy in Andhra Pradesh’s Nandyal
content: A five-year-old tribal boy was burnt alive after a fire, triggered by an explosion in a solar panel battery, gutted his thatched house in Andhra Pradesh’s Nandyal district on Tuesday, police said.The incident took place at around 1pm at Balapalathippa hamlet, under Erramatam gram panchayat in Kothapalli mandal.The deceased was identified as Dharma Teja, the younger son of an agricultural labourer. The family belongs to the Chenchu tribal community.Kothapalli police inspector R Jayashankar told HT that the boy was sleeping alone inside the house when the fire broke out. “The elder son had gone to his grandfather’s place nearby, while the father had gone to the agricultural fields for work and the mother was washing clothes outside the hut,” he said.According to a preliminary investigation, the fire was triggered by an explosion in the battery connected to a solar panel installed on the roof of the thatched house. The flames quickly spread through the structure, trapping the sleeping child inside, Jayashankar said.Bharathamma and some local residents tried desperately to rescue the boy but could not enter the burning house because of the intensity of the flames. “Despite their efforts, Dharma Teja was charred to death,” the inspector said.Jayashankar said the entire hamlet had no electricity connection until recently and most of the houses had installed solar panels on their rooftops with government assistance for power supply. “Some of the houses have recently got the electricity connections, but this family is yet to get the connection and has been using only solar power,” he said.The fire completely gutted the hut, destroying rice stocks and other household belongings worth around ₹1 lakh. Kothapalli Tahsildar Usharani visited the affected family and provided immediate financial assistance of ₹5,000 to help them cope with the tragedy.

headline: Fifty-three hospitalised after eating shawarma in Bhiwandi
content: Thane Fifty-three persons, including 17 children, have been hospitalised for suspected food poisoning after consuming shawarma from a roadside eatery in Bhiwandi town in Maharashtra’s Thane district, an official said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Bhiwandi sees second case of outbreak linked to shawarma storyline 1 The patients, being treated at the state-run Indira Gandhi Memorial (IGM) Hospital, also include 25 women, they said. According to Dr. Sandeep Gadekar, Medical Officer of Health at the Bhiwandi-Nizampur City Municipal Corporation, the patients are currently stable. Bhiwandi food poisoning: 79 people still hospitalised; FDA cracks down on eateries Bhiwandi food poisoning: 79 people still hospitalised; FDA cracks down on eateries Patient samples have been sent for microbiological, chemical, and culture analysis to determine the exact cause of the illness Bhiwandi food poisoning: 79 people still hospitalised; FDA cracks down on eateries storyline 1 The affected persons had consumed shawarma at an eatery in the Vanzarpatti Naka area of Bhiwandi on Monday night and subsequently developed vomiting and diarrhoea, the official said. On Tuesday, officials said that 11 people had been hospitalised due to suspected food poisoning. The number has now risen to 53. Case filed against eatery; owner absconding Dr. Gadekar told PTI that a case has been registered against the eatery owner under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations at the Nizampura police station. The accused is absconding, he said. FDA Assistant Commissioner Santosh Shisodia said they have urged the municipal corporation to designate specific areas for selling street food so they can be properly monitored, pointing out that vendors are currently scattered across Bhiwandi. Mr. Shisodia said the drinking water supplied to residents in the town appeared yellow, adding that only laboratory tests could confirm whether the reported ailments were linked to food poisoning or any other factor.

headline: ED raids house of SAD leader Ravinder Singh Khera in Kharar
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Wednesday raided the residence of Ravinder Singh Khera, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) halqa in-charge of Kharar.Khera is among the frontrunners for the SAD ticket from the Kharar Assembly constituency.However, the recent announcement of a SAD-BJP alliance in Punjab ahead of the upcoming elections has added uncertainty to the political prospects of candidates in the constituency.Khera, who owns Guru Kripa Rice and Agro Industries, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in January 2023 in a bribery case along with an FCI official.As recently as November 18, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal held a meeting with traders and businessmen in Kharar, including grocery store owners, property dealers, pesticide sellers, small traders and commission agents. Khera played a key role in organising the meeting.The Badal family has also held several major rallies in Kharar and adjoining areas, with Khera playing an instrumental role in mobilising support.

headline: Get govt to announce Parliament schedule, CPI MP Sandosh Kumar asks RS chairman
content: Communist Party of India (CPI) leader Sandosh Kumar P on Wednesday asked Rajya Sabha chairman CP Radhakrishnan to intervene and push the government to finalise the schedule for Parliament’s winter session, saying its continued silence on the matter was “deeply concerning”.“Such a lack of clarity is not merely an administrative inconvenience; it reflects a larger problem of the government’s reluctance to maintain transparency and take stakeholders into confidence on matters of parliamentary importance,” the Rajya Sabha MP from Keralam said in the letter.The letter comes amid continued uncertainty about the winter session of Parliament, which began on December 1 last year. Both Houses were adjourned sine die on August 13, but neither has been prorogued.Kumar said the winter session is traditionally held around November and December, and its schedule is usually communicated well in advance so members can prepare for legislative business.The uncertainty, he said, has practical costs for MPs who must plan travel, constituency programmes and other engagements around the parliamentary calendar.“Keeping elected representatives in a state of uncertainty, without any formal communication or consultation, is neither fair nor conducive to the effective functioning of Parliament,” the letter said, lamenting that the lack of consultation had “become an unfortunate norm under the present regime”.Kumar asked Radhakrishnan to step in, underlining that he was the guardian of the privileges and institutional dignity of the House,“Parliament is not an institution that can be convened or managed at the government’s convenience alone,” he wrote, describing it as the people’s supreme representative forum that must function with regard for established conventions and transparency.There has been speculation that the government is still considering calling a special session to pass bills implementing delimitation and women’s reservation. Congress leaders have suggested that the government might offer a constitutional guarantee of a 50% increase in the seats of all states.

headline: Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning
content: CHANDIGARH The reunification of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the crucial 2027 Punjab Assembly election has put both parties back in the reckoning, even as the State’s political landscape looks headed for a four-cornered fight, with the old partners joining hands to make it more competitive. In the run-up to the election, due in early 2027, the political positioning of the parties appeared increasingly vulnerable, and political observers felt that the logical way to overcome it was to forge an alliance.

headline: Tamil Nadu investment commitments hit ₹1.73 trillion under TVK govt
content: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday signed 78 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) involving proposed investments of ₹58,214 crore at the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave, taking total investment commitments secured since the C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government took office to about ₹1.73 trillion. The latest agreements have the potential to create 65,786 jobs, taking projected employment from the 190 MoUs signed since May 2026 to 198,557, according to the state government. Amid growing competition among Indian states for manufacturing and other investments, Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce S Keerthana said Tamil Nadu was focused on competing with the world's leading manufacturing economies rather than other states. “Our real competition is not another state, but the world's leading manufacturing economies,” she said. “With nine new trade agreements, our real competition is not another state. It is the world's leading manufacturing economies,” she added. The conclave coincides with the completion of around 200 days of the government's investment-promotion programme. The state has signed 190 MoUs involving about ₹1.73 trillion of proposed investments and nearly 199,000 potential jobs during the period. Keerthana said the government's focus was not merely on attracting investment commitments, but on converting them into operating projects, sustainable employment and longer-term economic growth. Of the 112 MoUs signed before Wednesday's conclave, 83 had progressed to land allotment or beyond, translating into a conversion rate of 74.1 per cent in a little over six months. “Every investment conclave in India ends the same way. Folders are exchanged, cameras flash, a big number is announced. And then the cameras leave. This conclave is also about what happens after the cameras leave,” Keerthana said. She also acknowledged that 25.9 per cent of the earlier MoUs had not yet reached the same stage. “Politicians usually tell you only where they are winning. I am telling you where the work is left. That is what a transparent government looks like,” she said. The government also presented a project-wise status report to the chief minister, aimed at monitoring investment commitments and identifying bottlenecks in project implementation. The first VETTRI conclave, held in August, had added 97 MoUs worth ₹67,452 crore, while the tally before Wednesday's event stood at 112 MoUs involving ₹1.15 trillion and 132,771 potential jobs. Keerthana highlighted regulatory changes aimed at accelerating investment execution, including amendments enabling industrial approvals within 21 days or less. The government has also introduced more than 25 reforms through 23 government orders across 11 departments and extended the validity of trade licences from three years to 10 years. She pointed to the Semiconductor Special Incentive Scheme launched in October and the establishment of the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission, which held its first meeting within 10 days of being formed. “For the first time, delay has an owner,” Keerthana said, stressing the role of institutional accountability in resolving investor concerns. The state is also working with the Greater Chennai Corporation to improve social infrastructure around the Global Capability Centre corridor, recognising that attracting talent requires housing and other urban amenities alongside industrial infrastructure. Keerthana cited the example of Brazilian engineering company WEG Industries, which chose Dharmapuri for a proposed ₹2,000 crore integrated manufacturing facility for electric vehicle motors, industrial drives and power-generation equipment. The project could generate around 3,000 jobs. She said state government teams had proactively approached the company, shown its leadership multiple potential sites and addressed its queries before the investment decision was made. Keerthana also referred to a recent meeting with the leadership of German company Vautid, which subsequently progressed to an MoU signing. The minister said global investment should also generate business opportunities for local suppliers and smaller companies. “When a global company chooses Tamil Nadu, it is choosing you. Every large factory we bring in must mean bigger orders for you,” she told local micro, small and medium enterprises and suppliers.

headline: Prey and water may be why tiger Explorer has stopped exploring in Andhra’s NTR district
content: VIJAYAWADA: The tiger, known as ‘Explorer’, which has been moving through the forest areas of NTR district, Andhra Pradesh, has remained in the Kanumuru area of Gampalagudem mandal for the past four days. The availability of a good prey base and small water bodies on the hill is believed to be among the reasons for the animal staying in the same location. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/explorer-returns-to-east-godavari-after-roaming-telangana-landscapes-on-the-other-side-of-river/article71276919.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/tiger-explorer-reaches-mylavaram-forest-near-vijayawada-four-villages-on-alert/article71723383.ece According to Forest Department officials, the tiger is currently in the A. Konduru forest block near Kanumuru and has not shown any significant movement from the area in recent days. Officials said the animal’s behaviour and movement could not be determined in advance. Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert GPS-enabled collar helps forest officials track the movement; no attacks on cattle or human habitations reported so far Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert storyline 1 Spotted deer, wild boars, porcupines and sambar deer are available on the hills, providing a natural prey base for the animal. The presence of small water bodies is also believed to be an attraction. Villagers have reportedly informed officials about cattle that strayed into the forest and have been living there for nearly 20 to 30 years. These animals could potentially provide another source of prey for the tiger. However, officials said it was difficult to establish whether the availability of prey and water was the reason for the animal remaining in the area. NTR District Forest Officer (DFO) Satish Reddy said that the Forest Department was closely tracking its movements but was unable to predict whether it would move towards the neighbouring hill ranges or remain in the present location. Tadoba tiger ‘Explorer’ returns to Andhra Pradesh in search of mate, territory Tadoba tiger ‘Explorer’ returns to Andhra Pradesh in search of mate, territory Now a fully grown adult, the tiger has returned to the Jangareddigudem forests months after its remarkable cross-country journey, prompting the State to pursue the relocation of female tigers and the establishment of a breeding population Tadoba tiger ‘Explorer’ returns to Andhra Pradesh in search of mate, territory storyline 1 The tiger was midway between the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) and Tadoba in Maharashtra, and it was difficult to guess which way it would move, he said. There were no tigresses in the block where it was currently moving, and the tiger would have to go back to Tadoba or the NSTR if it was looking for a mate, he said. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/tiger-population-in-nagarjunasagar-srisailam-tiger-reserve-pegged-at-76/article69364890.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/human-wildlife-conflict-escalates-in-chandrapur-as-five-more-fall-victim-to-big-cats/article70070110.ece A team from the Pune-based tiger rescue unit and the Rapid Rescue Team (RRT) from Rajamahendravaram have been deployed to monitor the animal. Around eight personnel from the two teams are currently involved in the operation. The teams are coordinating with the local Forest Department staff to keep track of its movements. The tiger, named ‘Explorer’ because of its extensive movement across different forest landscapes, is believed to have originated in Maharashtra’s Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve. It travelled more than 650 km through parts of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh. The young male tiger was captured near Kurmapuram village in Rayavaram mandal of Konaseema district on February 6, 2026, after it strayed into human-inhabited areas. It was fitted with a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar and released into the forests of Papikonda National Park on February 14. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/adult-male-tiger-released-in-papikonda-national-park/article70632548.ece Operation Stripes: Adult male tiger released in Papikonda National Park Operation Stripes: Adult male tiger released in Papikonda National Park Named ‘Explorer’, the big cat has been fitted with a satellite collar and transmission of data regarding its movements has commenced; special teams have been deployed to monitor its movements in the wild until it establishes its own territory Operation Stripes: Adult male tiger released in Papikonda National Park storyline 1 The radio collar enables the Forest Department to track the animal’s movements through satellite signals. Since its release, Explorer has continued to move across forest landscapes in the State, including parts of the Godavari region and Eluru district, before reaching NTR district. Its extensive movements have posed challenges to tracking teams, as it continues to explore unfamiliar territory rather than settle in a particular habitat. Its presence in the Kanumuru forest block is being closely monitored to ensure the safety of the animal as well as people in neighbouring villages. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/tiger-explorer-spotted-in-fields-near-lingapalem-in-andhras-eluru-district-villages-on-alert/article71710818.ece Tiger ‘Explorer’ spotted in fields near Lingapalem in Andhra’s Eluru district; villages on alert Tiger ‘Explorer’ spotted in fields near Lingapalem in Andhra’s Eluru district; villages on alert A rescue team from Pune is on its way to tranquilise and capture the tiger, the Forest Department says Tiger ‘Explorer’ spotted in fields near Lingapalem in Andhra’s Eluru district; villages on alert storyline 1

headline: LPST protest: Keralam CM Satheesan rules out lowering teacher-student ratio
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM Even as protests by the Lower Primary School Teacher (LPST) rank-holders are continuing in front of the Secretariat, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday said that lowering the teacher-student ratio from the sanctioned 1:30 to 1:25 is “impractical” as the ratio is already down to 1:19 in government-run LP schools in the State. The matter was discussed unofficially in Wednesday’s Cabinet meeting, the Chief Minister said. The government had already agreed to four of the five demands raised by the LPST rank-holders despite the additional financial burden involved. However, the fifth - lowering the ratio - is impractical since many districts have one teacher for every 11, 12 or 13 students, he said. Government lower primary schools in Keralam has 3,49,000 students and 18,856 teachers at present. In Malappuram, the ratio is down to 1:25, in Pathanamthitta and Kottayam 1:11, in Idukki 1:12 and Kannur 1:14. “Therefore, we cannot under any circumstances increase the number of teachers even if we bring down the official ratio to 1:25,” Mr. Satheesan said, attributing the fall in ratio to a dip in students enrollment. The Chief Minister also blamed the Kerala Public Service Commission for conducting interviews and publishing rank-lists for non-existent vacancies. The government has taken up this matter very seriously and has tasked a committee led by Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha to examine it. “No government can make appointments to non-existent vacancies,” he said, adding that the government also has the responsibility of protecting existing teachers who are threatened by a fall in the number of divisions. The four demands agreed upon by the government included not preparing a new rank-list without making appointments from the existing one, extending the validity of the rank-list and ensuring job security for appointments made through the PSC. The LPST rank-holders have been protesting in front of the Secretariat for more than 140 days now. On the agreed-upon four demands, Mr. Satheesan said government orders will be issued once the rank-holders call off their stir.

headline: CM Mann, Kejriwal to stay in Ludhiana ahead of AAP’s Moga rally
content: The Ludhiana district administration and police are on high alert ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) ‘Khushhal Rally’ in Moga on Thursday, with Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and party national convener Arvind Kejriwal scheduled to arrive in Ludhiana this evening and stay overnight before proceeding to the rally venue.A senior district administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the rally would mark the formal launch of the AAP’s election campaign in Punjab.“We cannot take it lightly. Chief Secretary KAP Sinha and DGP Gaurav Yadav had already visited Moga on November 23 to review the arrangements. Village Aitiana, near Halwara airport, has been designated as the helipad for the Chief Minister’s chopper. Officials are, therefore, on high alert,” the official said, adding that the heightened activity would continue until the imposition of the Model Code of Conduct.According to the schedule, Chief Minister Mann will reach the helipad at village Aitiana and receive Kejriwal, who is scheduled to arrive at Halwara airport on an Air India evening flight from Delhi. After receiving Kejriwal and other dignitaries travelling from Delhi, the VVIPs will proceed to Ludhiana, where they will stay overnight. They will leave for Moga the following morning to attend the mega rally.Heavy police deployment at Halwara airportMeanwhile, a large number of police personnel and officials were deployed at Halwara airport from early morning as security arrangements were stepped up ahead of the VVIP arrivals.An airport official said security had been strengthened in and around the airport, with the entire staff put on alert.“Since Kejriwal is arriving on the evening flight and Chief Minister Mann will be there to receive him and other VIPs from Delhi, elaborate arrangements are being made. The entire airport staff is on alert,” the official said.

headline: RR Initiative’s 4th blood donation camp collects 50 units
content: The District Red Cross Society, Mohali, facilitated the fourth blood donation camp organised by RR Initiative on the occasion of the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. The camp collected more than 50 units of blood, with donors participating enthusiastically in the initiative aimed at meeting the needs of patients and promoting voluntary blood donation.Rainrita Dachalwal, Pro-President of the Indian Red Cross Society, Mohali, was the chief guest. Representatives of political parties, social organisations and institutions attended the event and appreciated the organisers' initiative.Dachalwal said Sri Guru Nanak Dev had given the message of serving humanity, equality and selfless service. Blood donation was a meaningful expression of these values, as it could help save lives, she said.She urged people to donate blood regularly and participate in social welfare initiatives.Navneet Kaur, founder of RR Initiative, expressed gratitude to the Gurudwara Management Committee, District Red Cross Society, Mohali, Vishwas Foundation and Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital, New Chandigarh, and all other organisations for their support in organising the camp.Rajinder Singh, president of the Gurudwara Management Committee, welcomed the guests by presenting them with siropas.

headline: Who Is Justice GR Swaminathan, Judge At Centre Of Tamil Nadu Deepam Row?

headline: In Madurai's Karthigai Deepam row, SC asks parties to file contempt applications, says will pass appropriate orders
content: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused verbal requests to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the Tamil Nadu government over the lighting of a ceremonial lamp atop a temple on the outskirts of Madurai in Tamil Nadu instead of the disputed stone pillar on Tuesday evening. The Madurai district collector filed a status report informing the court that the lamp could not be lit at the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi asked the parties to file the necessary applications and said it would pass appropriate orders after examining them. This came after it heard an urgent mention by the original petitioners, Rama Ravikumar and others.ALSO READ | Century-old dispute over stone pillar ‘deepathoon’ returns to spotlight in Tamil Nadu as Karthigai Deepam litSenior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the collector, told the bench: “As the Collector, I have traced out all the steps I was supposed to comply with.” Senior Advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the petitioners who sought the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon, termed the collector’s attempt to place the status report before the court an anticipatory mentioning in response to the breach.Krishnakumar said the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at the disputed spot was most unfortunate. He alleged a deliberate attempt to circumvent the Supreme Court’s November 20 order. The Supreme Court last week allowed the lighting on the pillar as an interim measure.Krishnakumar told the bench that a statement was issued in the name of the temple’s Board of Trustees asserting that the lamp should be lit at the Ucchipillaiyar temple, as customary practices did not permit the ceremony at the Deepathoon. He alleged the temple’s sthanikars denied issuing such a statement.ALSO READ | Madras HC threatens officials of contempt charges over Deepathoon curbs“Deliberate attempt to non-comply with the order. They have succeeded by stratagems and devices. This is a complete infraction of the rule of law. They kept telling the high court till the last minute that they will comply with the order. They refused to comply,” Krishnakumar said.He urged the court to direct the authorities to take the flame, which was still burning at the Ucchipillaiyar mandapam, and place it at the Deepathoon as a matter of rule of law.The district administration maintained it made all arrangements in accordance with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order. It said the temple was asked in writing and reminded to authorise a team to carry out the exercise. The administration said the temple did not authorise any team until the last moment.Another counsel appearing for the petitioners alleged that the temple’s Board of Trustees was used to circumvent the Supreme Court’s directions and said they would move a contempt petition. The bench expressed its disinclination when the petitioners’ counsel urged it to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged non-compliance.The Bharatiya Janata Party and Hindu groups protested against the administration and said they would file a contempt petition.State minister CTR Nirmalkumar said the Karthigai Mahadeepam was lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram.

headline: Miranda House introduces professional certificate courses for the AI, creator economy
content: Miranda House, University of Delhi (DU), has launched a portfolio of professional certificate courses to equip university students with practical, industry-oriented skills for the evolving creative, media, and technology economy. This initiative, introduced in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Eros AIVidya, is aimed at helping participants understand how they can integrate creative technology and AI skills into practical learning opportunities. The initial portfolio offers University of Delhi students 15 six-month professional certificate courses, co-certified by the collaborating partners. The list of programmes includes AI Filmmaking, Influencer and Creator Business, Avatar and Digital Human Creation, Animation, Video Blogging, AR/VR Production, VFX Editing, Script Writing, Acting, Music Production, Music Composition and Direction, Sound Editing, Editing and Art Direction. The launch of these professional certificate courses on AI and the creator economy follows India's increased emphasis on skills and infrastructure for its creative and digital economy, as stated by the institute. Admission process and fees structure Admissions for these programmes are currently open to eligible DU students, irrespective of their gender. Candidates applying for the courses are required to possess a valid Class 12 pass certificate or mark sheet, while the selection process is strictly based on merit. The course fees range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,50,000 depending on the programme chosen by the candidate. As notified by the institute, a loan facility is available for interested students, subject to valid documentation and applicable terms and conditions. What will participants get? Through the AI Filmmaking course, participants will be introduced to emerging AI-enabled approaches to content creation, while the Influencer and Creator Business course will help them learn the professional and commercial skills relevant to the creator economy. Avatar and Digital Human Creation programme will take students through the emerging forms of virtual identity and digital media. These courses are offered alongside creative disciplines such as animation, VFX, acting, script writing, editing, music and sound, enabling students to develop capabilities across both creative craft and emerging technologies. On completion of these courses, 15 high-performing students will receive support through the collaboration to start their own businesses, as announced by the institute. The opportunity will also be extended to students who demonstrate noteworthy performance during their courses.

headline: SC refuses interim bail to Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam, asks Delhi Police to respond
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined, for now, to grant interim bail to activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots "larger conspiracy" case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).The two had challenged a Delhi high court order denying them bail.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response on their pleas.During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail while the matter was pending. Senior advocate Siddharth Dave, representing Imam, also sought similar relief, citing his prolonged incarceration.However, the bench refused to grant immediate relief, saying, "Not today". It said the Delhi Police would be heard before any decision was taken on the interim bail pleas.The Supreme Court also directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for the constitution of a three-judge bench to hear the case.In their petitions, Khalid and Imam have sought bail, arguing that the prosecution has yet to examine protected witnesses and that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.The case relates to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots, which broke out during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) and the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC).Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Haryana CM Saini plans 500-acre C&D waste facility, 10 storage sites in Gurugram
content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Tuesday directed the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) and the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) to work in mission mode to improve sanitation, manage construction and demolition (C&D) waste and expedite pending infrastructure projects.Chairing a review meeting, Saini examined sanitation, waterlogging prevention and pending projects related to road connectivity, drinking water supply and sewerage. He said there was no shortage of funds and the government expected visible results on the ground rather than progress reports.GMDA CEO DK Behera told the meeting that, after consultations with citizens, a plan had been prepared to identify 10 sites, each measuring one hectare, for the temporary storage of C&D waste. The sites would be secured with boundary walls or fencing to stop waste from spreading and causing pollution.For long-term disposal of C&D waste, the Chief Minister asked officers to identify about 500 acres near the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway. The facility would handle waste generated from Gurugram, Manesar and Faridabad. He also asked officials to fix the accountability of the companies concerned.Gurugram Police Commissioner Sibash Kabiraj informed the meeting that 12 vehicles allegedly transporting C&D waste illegally from Delhi have been seized. FIRs have been registered.CM Saini directed officers to put CCTV surveillance on the routes used for illegal transportation and at vulnerable spots, and to impose heavy penalties on offenders. He said there would be no compromise on the city's cleanliness.The Chief Minister also directed officers to ensure that dust does not rise anywhere in Gurugram. He asked for grass to be planted in roadside green belts with regular maintenance, and durable slabs instead of tiles on footpaths.He further directed officials to regularly monitor the attendance and performance of sanitation staff, with a designated officer assigned responsibility for each major road. Cleanliness, he said, must become part of routine civic management and not remain confined to campaigns.Saini asked the GMDA to complete missing links in the main drinking water supply network, road connectivity and sewerage system on priority. Where land availability is the hurdle, he said, officers should explore options, such as land exchange. He added that infrastructure planning should take into account Gurugram’s growing population.Municipal Commissioner Dr Pankaj informed the meeting that more than 250 stray cattle had been shifted to gaushalas. After hearing of assaults on rounding-up teams, the Chief Minister directed the police to act strictly against those obstructing officials.

headline: Madhya Pradesh teacher arrested for sending obscene messages to Class 12 student, threatening poor marks
content: A government school teacher in Madhya Pradesh's Guna Cantt area has been arrested for allegedly sending obscene and inappropriate messages to a Class 12 student and pressuring her to meet him alone.According to the complaint, the accused, identified as Narendra Kushwah, had been repeatedly messaging the student for some time, urging her to meet him privately and accompany him outside the school. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to give her poor marks in examinations and adversely affect her studies.The student further alleged that the teacher claimed he controlled everything in the school, including examination marks, and insisted that she would have to obey him. She also accused him of pressuring her to sit and talk with him in an area inside the school that had been partitioned with a curtain.ALSO READ | Rajasthan teacher arrested after refusing to marry 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on dating appDistressed by the continuous messages and threats, the student informed her mother, following which complaints were submitted to the district education officer (DEO), the school principal and the superintendent of police (SP).Based on the complaint, police registered a case against the teacher under relevant provisions of the POCSO Act and took him into custody.ALSO READ | ‘Harassment over fee payment’: Azamgarh Class 8 girl consumes poison, dies, teacher arrestedSchool principal Sanjay Kumar Jain said the student and her mother approached him with the complaint and submitted copies of the WhatsApp chats. He said the student alleged that the teacher had been communicating with her since after Children’s Day. The matter has been referred to the DEO for investigation.

headline: Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being allegedly stopped from flying to UK
content: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das on Wednesday moved the Delhi high court challenging what he claims was a decision by government authorities to stop him from travelling abroad. His lawyer sought an urgent listing of the matter, but the court said it would hear the plea on Thursday.The matter on Wednesday was mentioned before Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma. The plea, filed through advocate Krishnaraj Bapat, will be argued by senior advocate Akhil Sibal on Thursday.Das has alleged that he was stopped at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport from boarding a London-bound flight, where he was scheduled to attend an event at the University of Oxford. He claims he was invited to speak on the "cockroach movement".Why does Saurav Das claim he was stopped from flying to London?Das alleged that the Centre used a show-cause notice over discrepancies in his passport details to prevent him from travelling to the United Kingdom. Das claimed that the notice was sent around five hours before his scheduled flight and sought an explanation over discrepancies in his place of birth. He alleged that immigration officials stopped him at the airport and asked him to check the notice.The notice reportedly asked why his passport should not be impounded and gave him seven days to respond.The CJP co-convenor called the alleged action an attempt to harass him and intimidate young people associated with the movement. The government was yet to publicly respond to his allegations.Das said he was invited to speak at the Oxford Union about the “Cockroach Movement”. He also claimed that students had invited him to speak at the London School of Economics, the University of Cambridge and the University of Edinburgh.

headline: Over 70 MoUs likely to be inked as second edition of investors' summit in Tamil Nadu starts today
content: Over 70 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) are expected to be signed with multi-national companies during the second edition of the VETTRI Investment and Conversion Conclave 2026 in Tamil Nadu on Wednesday, officials aware of the details said.The business meet is scheduled to be held at a luxury hotel in Mahabalipuram, about 60 km from Chennai.According to the officials cited above, 78 MoUs worth 58,214 crore of investments are likely to be signed in the presence of chief minister C Joseph Vijay. “These investments across multiple sectors are expected to create 65,786 jobs in the state,” one of the officials said, seeking anonymity.“Over the past six months, Tamil Nadu has made significant strides in attracting investments. But for us, the real measure of success is what happens after an MoU is signed,” minister for industries S Keerthana said.“Are the investment commitments moving forward, are the investments translating into factories, production and jobs and are we creating meaningful employment opportunities? These are the questions we are focused on,” she added.She said that under the leadership of the chief minister, the commitment of the government is to build an industrial ecosystem where businesses can invest with confidence, projects can move forward with certainty and investments translate into opportunities and prosperity across Tamil Nadu.The developments come even as the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) alleged investments meant for Tamil Nadu are going to Andhra Pradesh.Former BJP Tamil Nadu president Tamilisai Soundararajan said the government should respond to the above concerns before signing any fresh MoUs."What concrete steps has the government undertaken to retain industrial companies already operating in Tamil Nadu," she said earlier on November 22.Of the MoUs announced so far, she added, the government must declare how many of them have materialised into operational factories and how many have led to the creation of new jobs.Ninety-seven MoUs worth ₹6,7542 across various sectors, including manufacturing, electronics, renewable energy, aerospace and life-sciences, were signed during the first edition of the summit in August.

headline: SpiceJet Q400 crew flags ground holds, crew fatigue and unpaid dues
content: SpiceJet’s missed payments to third-party vendors, including fuel suppliers and airport operations control centres, have triggered frequent ground holds and operational delays, according to an unsigned representation by a section of the airline’s Bombardier Q400 crew.The November 21 representation to the SpiceJet management warned that this had led to unpredictable disruptions, extended duty hours and prolonged salary delays, which were “directly eroding flight safety margins”. To be sure, several service providers have moved the airline to cash-and-carry terms.HT has reached out to SpiceJet for its comments.The letter cited an incident on the night of November 18-19 when the airline’s Q400 aircraft was denied departure clearance at Mumbai airport over its pending dues to airport and service agencies, leaving its cockpit crew stranded for hours without accommodation or return travel arrangements.Also Read: SpiceJet’s flight cuts put spotlight on global 80/20 rule for airport slotsAccording to the crew, two sets of cockpit crew had been asked to operate separate Delhi-Mumbai-Delhi rotations at short notice that night. While the second flight was cancelled after the crew reported for duty in Delhi, the first aircraft landed in Mumbai but was unable to depart because of the airline’s pending financial dues.While cabin crew members were provided tickets to return to Delhi, the representation alleged that the cockpit crew were left stranded at the airport for hours into the early morning, with repeated calls and emails to SpiceJet’s rostering team, travel desk and senior operational leadership going unanswered.“Ultimately, the Captain was offered an inadequate sum of ₹4,000 to arrange his own accommodation in Mumbai,” the letter said, adding that “no arrangement or financial provision whatsoever was made for the First Officer”.To be sure, several service providers have moved the airline to cash-and-carry terms.The crew members also alleged that protracted ground holds across Q400 operations had a cascading impact on duty schedules. “Due to these protracted holds, operating Captains and cockpit crew frequently exhaust their prescribed Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) and experience acute physical fatigue prior to departure or mid-rotation,” the letter said.Along with operational concerns, the representation flagged five months of pending salaries since July 2026, alleging that Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) contributions had not been deposited since October 2025 and Form 16 for the financial year 2025-26 had not been issued.The representation further alleged that they continued to operate flights despite financial hardship because of a six-month notice period and threats that the company would withhold their salary arrears, gratuity, and mandatory regulatory clearances if they stopped flying.SpiceJet’s fleet has shrunk to about seven operational aircraft, according to PlaneSpotters.net as of Nov 24. Its share of India’s domestic market fell to 0.6% in September from 3.9% in January, as monthly domestic passenger volume dropped to roughly 73,000 from nearly 592,000. On Nov 17, DGCA issued a notice to the airline, warning that most of its fleet remained grounded and that the carrier had failed to submit a credible plan to return the planes to service.
