headline: Centre, state remain committed to preserving Sikh Gurus’ legacy: Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini
content: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini said the Haryana and Central governments had undertaken numerous initiatives to honour the memory of the Sikh Gurus.Addressing a state-level function held on the eve of Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purb on Monday night at the sacred land of Kapal Mochan in Yamunanagar, he said that a Sikh Museum was being built near the Sixth Patshahi Gurdwara in Umri, Kurukshetra, and this museum would be the first such museum in the state, showcasing the Sikh history, culture and the contributions of the Gurus.“The holy land of Haryana has a deep connection with the Sikh Gurus. Lakhnaur Sahib in Ambala district was the maternal home of Guru Gobind Singh, and he spent his childhood there. The holy land of Kurukshetra also witnessed the visits of Sikh Gurus from time to time,” said the Chief Minister.On this occasion, the Chief Minister bowed his head at the Gurdwara Sahib and received blessings by doing ardaas. He also reached Shri Kapal Mochan, Shri Rin Mochan and Shri Suraj Kund sarovars and offered prayers with chanting of mantras in Kapal Mochan mela. He also wished everyone on Kartik Purnima.The Chief Minister said that Lohgarh, located a short distance from Kapal Mochan, also holds special significance in the Sikh history.“Baba Banda Singh Bahadur made it the capital of the Sikh state. A trust has been established in Lohgarh in the name of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur, which is working to preserve the historical, religious and cultural heritage of the area,” said Saini.He said a Baba Banda Singh Bahadur memorial and theme park was being constructed in Yamunanagar district at a cost of Rs 244.51 crore.On this occasion, he also announced a grant of Rs 2 crore to the shrine board for the development of 32 dharamshalas located in the Mela Shri Kapal Mochan-Adibadri complex.He further said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the memory of Sikh Gurus received national honour. “Sultanpur Lodhi is being developed as a heritage city. Dera Baba Nanak to Shri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor in Gurdaspur, Punjab, was developed with an allocation of Rs 120 crore,” he said.He further said that it was decided to celebrate ‘Veer Bal Diwas’ on December 26 every year, commemorating the sacrifice of the Sahibzadas.On this occasion, Haryana Education Minister Mahipal Dhanda, Yamunanagar MLA Ghanshyam Dass Arora, Sadhaura MLA Renu Bala, Ratia MLA Sardar Jarnail Singh, former Minister Kanwar Pal, BJP district president Rajesh Sapra, Special Officer to Chief Minister Bhopal Singh Khadri, DC Preeti, SP Kamaldeep Goyal, ADC Naveen Ahuja, mela administrator and Vyaspur SDM Dr Kuldeep Singh, Jagadhri SDM Vishwanath, Chhachhrauli SDM Jaspal Singh Gill, DPRO Dr Manoj Kumar along with BJP leaders and administration officials, lakhs of devotees were present.

headline: 12,000 guest teachers still await regular jobs: MP Kumari Selja
content: MP Kumari Selja has criticised the BJP government in Haryana over the delay in regularising guest teachers, saying nearly 12,000 teachers who have been serving in the government schools for around 21 years are still waiting for permanent jobs. In a media statement on Tuesday, Selja said thousands of teaching posts remain vacant in government schools, but the state government has failed to ensure regular recruitment. She said keeping experienced teachers uncertain about their future was unfortunate, especially when they had been educating children across the state for years. She urged the government to frame a clear policy for regularising eligible guest teachers in accordance with High Court directions and existing legal provisions.

headline: Bulldozers roll over standing crops in Jind, farmers clash with police, several detained
content: Dariawala: Farmers in Jind district of Haryana expressed strong resentment on Tuesday after the administration deployed JCB machines to clear standing crops in their fields for a high-voltage transmission line project. The action triggered a confrontation between farmers and police, following which several farmers were detained. The project involves laying a high-voltage transmission line from Sikar in Rajasthan to Jind and further towards Sonipat. The government is acquiring land from farmers for the project, but a dispute over compensation rates remains unresolved. Farmers alleged discrimination in the compensation process, claiming that some landowners are being offered compensation exceeding Rs 1 crore, while others are being offered only a few lakh rupees.According to farmers, a large solar power plant is being established in Bikaner, Rajasthan, to generate electricity for distribution to different locations. A high-voltage transmission network is being laid from Sikar towards Sonipat and Jind and other locations in Punjab. Wherever transmission towers are to be installed, approximately half an acre of land will be acquired. However, farmers alleged that the administration has failed to clarify the compensation structure. Sushil Kumar, a resident of Dariawala village, whose standing crops were damaged by JCB machines on Tuesday, said the government was acting unfairly towards farmers. He said farmers had worked hard to cultivate wheat and mustard crops, but the administration destroyed their produce without taking them into confidence. He added that farmers were helpless and were left distressed after seeing their hard work destroyed. According to him, the administration should have consulted farmers before taking such action.A large police force, including personnel from neighbouring districts, was deployed at the spot. Around 50 farmers were taken in buses to the police lines. They were reportedly released later in the night. Farmers have warned that they will launch a larger agitation if their demands are not addressed.They maintained that compensation rates should be finalised through meetings with farmers before any land acquisition or clearance work begins. They alleged that the government was forcibly taking over their land and said they would not accept such action without fair compensation.Meanwhile, officials maintained that compensation was being provided to farmers as per the prescribed rules. They said the farmers were adamant about their demands, which led to their detention. Officials also stated that farmers have the right to appeal before the Commissioner if they are dissatisfied with the compensation.Similar stir in SonipatSimilar protests are also underway in Sonipat district, where farmers have alleged discrimination in compensation rates for the same transmission line project. Farmers are staging a sit-in protest in Sohati village, demanding fair and uniform compensation for their land.

headline: Food safety backlog leaves nearly half of Haryana samples collected since April awaiting lab results
content: Gurgaon: Nearly half of the food samples collected by Haryana’s food safety department since April are still awaiting test results. Of the 4,490 samples collected, only 2,310 have been analysed, leaving 2,180 pending for examination.Of the samples tested so far, 507 — nearly 22% — failed to meet prescribed quality standards, while 1,803 were found to be compliant. Hisar recorded the highest number of failed samples at 38 out of 169 tested, followed by Gurgaon at 36 of 145, Faridabad at 30 of 106, Panipat at 30 of 84, and Karnal at 29 of 192. A total of 243 samples from Gurgaon and 245 from Faridabad were sent for examination.The department has also destroyed around 50,000 kg of adulterated sweets and other food products during its ongoing enforcement drive, highlighting the scale of violations detected during inspections. Paneer, khoya and sweets have remained a major focus because of their high consumption during the festive season.The campaign involves all 27 food safety officers (FSOs) and six designated officers (DOs), who have been deployed for inspections across districts. However, with fewer than 52% of the collected samples analysed so far, the quality of a substantial portion of the food products sent for testing is yet to be established.Food safety commissioner Manoj Kumar has been monitoring the campaign and directed officials to take strict action against adulteration and ensure that prescribed quality standards are maintained. Joint director Prithvi Singh has also been participating in field inspections and monitoring enforcement activities.The department said the drive is aimed not only at collecting samples but also at preventing substandard food from reaching consumers, identifying those responsible for adulteration and initiating action against them. The extent of violations will become clearer once the pending samples have been analysed.Under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, food businesses found violating prescribed safety and hygiene standards can face action depending on the nature and severity of the offence. This may include improvement notices, monetary penalties, suspension or cancellation of licences, and closure of premises. In cases involving substandard, misbranded or unsafe food, authorities can seize products, prohibit their sale and initiate prosecution. Repeated or serious offences specified under the Act can also attract imprisonment.

headline: Haryana to get its 1st Sikh museum in Kurukshetra: CM Saini
content: Chandigarh: Haryana will get its first Sikh museum at Umri in Kurukshetra, while a memorial and theme park dedicated to Baba Banda Singh Bahadur is being developed at Lohgarh at a cost of Rs 244.51 crore, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini said on Tuesday.Addressing a state-level celebration on Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s Prakash Parv at the sacred Kapal Mochan in Yamunanagar, Saini said the museum would showcase Sikh history, culture and the contributions of the Sikh Gurus. He said Lohgarh, situated near Kapal Mochan, holds a special place in Sikh history as Baba Banda Singh Bahadur had established it as the capital of the Sikh state. A trust named after Baba Banda Singh Bahadur had been constituted to preserve the historical, religious and cultural heritage of Lohgarh. The CM said the teachings of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji transcend the boundaries of religion, society and time and remain a source of inspiration for the entire humanity.The CM also announced financial assistance of Rs 2 crore to the Shrine Board for development works at 32 dharamshalas located within the Sri Kapal Mochan-Adi Badri Mela complex. A drone, light and sound show was organised during the celebrations, showcasing Haryana’s heritage, Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji’s 52-day stay at Kapal Mochan and the valour of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur.Saini said Kapal Mochan was a symbol of shared faith and cultural heritage. “The sacred site finds mention in the traditions of the Mahabharata and the Puranas. Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji had also visited the place, while Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji’s 52-day stay following the Battle of Bhangani reflected its association with Sikh history,” the CM said.The chief minister said the Haryana govt had taken several steps to preserve the legacy of the Sikh Gurus. “Eight Sikh Gurus had visited the holy land of Dharmakshetra-Kurukshetra at different times, while Lakhnaur Sahib in Ambala district was the maternal home of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji,” Saini said.Saini said the establishment of the Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee in December 2022 had fulfilled a long-standing demand of the Sikh community and granted it autonomy in the state.

headline: 1,394 of 2,831 teaching posts vacant in Haryana: Hooda
content: Rohtak: Former chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Tuesday alleged that the BJP govt in Haryana had been caught manipulating votes and would no longer be able to get away with it, claiming that public resentment against the regime was growing. Addressing a news conference here on Tuesday, Hooda backed the ongoing sugarcane farmers’ agitation, calling the state govt’s Rs 15 per quintal hike in procurement price a “cruel joke”. He said the 3% increase was inadequate amid rising input costs and record-high sugar prices, and urged govt to accept farmers’ demand for a reasonable hike.Hooda also accused BJP govt of pushing Haryana’s education system into crisis, citing large-scale vacancies in govt-aided colleges. He said 1,394 of 2,831 teaching posts and 785 of 1,668 non-teaching posts were vacant, while 56 of 97 aided colleges had no principal. Highlighting the shortage of schoolteachers, he said 723 primary schools were being run by a single teacher each, including 19 Model Sanskriti Schools. He further claimed that drinking water in 398 schools was unfit for consumption, based on samples from 6,000 schools, while 7,800 schools were yet to be assessed. Hooda also alleged that delays in fund allocation forced schools to buy mid-day meal supplies on credit, with teachers often paying out of pocket.

headline: Mohali: Haryana govt employee duped of ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad | Hindustan Times
content: A 53-year-old Haryana health department employee was allegedly duped of nearly ₹5 lakh by cyber fraudsters who lured her with a Facebook advertisement offering financial assistance.The complainant, who resides in Nayagaon, told police that she was in urgent need of money. So when she came across a Facebook advertisement offering assistance, she clicked on it and shared her phone number on the link.About a week later, a man identifying himself as Jagdish Singh called her and sought copies of her Aadhaar and PAN cards. According to the complainant, the caller later claimed that an inspector general of police had withheld the funds meant for her. Later, another person contacted her, alleging that her GST documents were incomplete and that a court had imposed a fine. She was asked to pay the amount to receive the promised financial assistance. Believing their claims, the woman transferred the money through multiple transactions. The accused later demanded another ₹4 lakh. She stopped responding to their calls after realised that she had been cheated.Based on her complaint, a case under Sections 318(4) and 319(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act has been registered against unidentified persons.Man cheated of ₹4 cr on pretext of goods supplyA Gujarat-based man allegedly cheated a city resident of ₹4 crore on the pretext of supplying goods ordered online.The accused, identified as Yash Panchal, has been booked under Section 318(4) (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Mauli Jagran police station.According to the complaint filed by Roha Partap Singh, a resident of Raipur Kalan, the accused received ₹4 crore through online transactions between November 26 and December 25, 2024, against an order for certain goods. However, he neither supplied the goods nor refunded the money.

headline: Farmers’ organisations call for protest on December 2 seeking better crop price
content: GURUGRAM Amid growing resentment among farmers in Haryana over “inadequate” prices for bajra and sugarcane, a joint front of farmer organisations has called for a demonstration in Kurukshetra on December 2, demanding remunerative prices for crops. While bajra growers are demanding procurement at the announced minimum support price (MSP) of ₹2,900 per quintal, sugarcane farmers have rejected the ₹15 per quintal hike announced by the State government this year, taking the price to ₹430 per quintal. Extending support to bajra farmers, the Haryana Kisan Congress organised a day-long dharna at the new grain market in Charkhi Dadri, demanding procurement at MSP. A large number of farmers, agricultural labourers and commission agents participated in the protest. Addressing the gathering, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala alleged that despite Haryana producing 1.3 million metric tonnes of bajra in 2025-26 and an estimated 1.5 million metric tonnes in 2026-27, government procurement at MSP had been limited to just 420 quintals. He said the BJP government had promised compensation of ₹600 per quintal under the “Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana”, assuring farmers that they would effectively receive ₹2,300 per quintal for their produce. However, farmers had been forced to sell bajra at ₹1,800-₹2,200 per quintal and had not received any compensation under the scheme, he alleged. Mr. Surjewala demanded that the e-Kharid portal be reopened until December 15, the Food Corporation of India and HAFED procure bajra at ₹2,900 per quintal, and the price difference be transferred to farmers within seven days. He also sought a 2.5% commission for commission agents. Meanwhile, sugarcane growers have also stepped up their agitation. A panchayat organised by the Samyukt Kisan Morcha on the premises of a sugar mill in Rohtak on Tuesday rejected the hike, citing rising input costs and inadequate returns from sugar and other by-products. All India Kisan Sabha national vice-president Inderjit Singh criticised Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini for what he termed his double standards, alleging that the Chief Minister was seeking votes in Punjab while ignoring the interests of Haryana’s farmers. Following the panchayat, protesters demonstrated outside the office of the sugar mill’s managing director and submitted a memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister. They demanded a sugarcane price of ₹600 per quintal in line with the Swaminathan Commission’s recommendations and warned of shutting down sugar mills if their demand was not met. At a separate meeting in Kaithal, representatives of various farmer organisations decided to intensify the ongoing agitation under the leadership of Bharatiya Kisan Union (Haryana) president Rattan Mann. Mr. Mann said the prices of diesel, fertilisers, labour and electricity had risen, while crop prices had failed to keep pace.

headline: Teen walking with earphones on railway track killed after being hit by train in Gurugram
content: Gurugram: A 17-year-old boy died after being hit by the Ranikhet Express on the Delhi-Rewari railway track on Tuesday morning. The boy was walking on the railway track wearing earphones, an official of the Government Railway Police (GRP) said. .After getting information, the GRP reached the spot and took possession of the body and kept it in the mortuary. .According to the GRP, the deceased was identified as Desraj Rajput (17), a resident of Chhapra village in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. .Gurugram woman runs over domestic worker, takes her to hospital; then returns body to accident spot.He worked as a gardener with his maternal uncle in Sector-80 of Gurugram and was living on rent in Garhi Harsaru village. .According to the police, Desraj was walking along the railway track at around 8:00 am, wearing earphones, when he was hit by the train going from Delhi to Rewari. He died on the spot in the accident. The loco pilot of the train informed about the accident at Gurgaon railway station. .The police found the teenager's body in a mutilated condition on the track.

headline: Jharkhand minister writes to PM over steep rise in airfare; seeks cap on ticket prices
content: Ranchi, Nov 25 (PTI) Jharkhand Health Minister Irfan Ansari wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging a steep rise in airfares and urging the Centre to cap ticket prices and curb “arbitrary” fare hikes by airlines. In his letter to the prime minister, Ansari recounted the plight of a Jharkhand woman who was unable to shell out an exorbitant amount on airfare to visit her ailing husband, who was undergoing treatment in Chandigarh for a kidney ailment. “I was travelling to Delhi from Ranchi to attend an event organised by the Jharkhand Cabinet at the Bharat Mandapam. I was shocked to see that the fare from Ranchi to Delhi was around Rs 31,000. The Jharkhand government will cover my travel expenses, but what about that middle-class family for whom even raising such a large sum is difficult?” he wrote in the letter. The minister said a sight at the airport left him deeply pained. “A woman was crying, seeing the steep fare. Upon inquiry, it was learnt that her husband is battling a serious kidney ailment in Chandigarh. His condition is extremely critical. He had expressed a final wish: to see his wife one last time,” Ansari mentioned in the letter. The minister said he arranged for her ticket so that she could reach her husband.

headline: Chandigarh: 2 booked for duping man of ₹2 crore on promise of PGI job | Hindustan Times
content: Two Kharar residents have been booked for allegedly duping a 49-year-old Mauli Jagran resident of ₹2 crore on the pretext of securing him a job at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.According to the complainant, the accused, identified as Kamlesh Jha and Ravi Jha, both residents of Sunny Enclave, Kharar, allegedly took ₹2 crore and documents from him on the promise of arranging the job. However, they neither secured him the promised job nor returned the money.Based on his complaint, a case under Sections 316(2) (criminal breach of trust) and 318(4) (cheating and dishonest inducement of property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered against the two.

headline: 3 lakh residents, 12 wards: Colony vote at centre of Chandigarh MC battle
content: Chandigarh: The battle for Chandigarh’s civic polls could hinge on 12 wards dominated by rehabilitation colonies, home to an estimated 3 lakh residents. With a predominantly Purvanchali electorate, these constituencies have become a key political battleground ahead of the Dec 23 municipal elections.The stakes rose after the Chandigarh administration announced ownership rights for rehabilitation colony allottees on Nov 17, days before the Model Code of Conduct came into force. The BJP has projected the move as the fulfilment of a decades-old promise, while the Congress and AAP have questioned its timing and eligibility conditions.The Chandigarh Rehabilitation Colonies Freehold Rights Rules, 2026, cover around 49,000 residential units — 36,000 under the Chandigarh Housing Board and 13,000 under the Estate Office. With 18 seats needed for a majority in the 35-member House, the 12 wards account for more than a third of the electoral contest. Colony areas also record voter turnout of 75% to 80%, considerably higher than in several sectoral areas.BJP councillor Maheshinder Singh Sidhu said, “Purvanchal and rehabilitation colony voters are crucial in deciding the fate of the city’s elections, particularly because of their high concentration. The voter turnout, generally ranging from 75% to 80%, is also much higher than in sector areas.” He believes the ownership announcement will help the BJP consolidate support.However, the political payoff is not guaranteed. The rules allow original allottees and their legal heirs to convert properties into freehold after seven years of occupancy by paying 5% of the collector rate. Subsequent buyers holding General Power of Attorney (GPA) documents or sale agreements are excluded.Congress MP Manish Tewari has questioned the provision, arguing that an estimated 80% to 90% of occupants in older colonies such as Bapu Dham, Dadumajra and Ram Darbar could be left out.Senior Congress leader Rajiv Sharma said, “These areas have been neglected in terms of development. The announcement of ownership rights may initially have attracted people’s interest, but after the conditions were announced, residents are realising the limitations of the scheme. There is strong anti-incumbency over the lack of development in these areas.”The immediate beneficiaries are expected to be concentrated in newer 2006 Small Flats complexes in Dhanas, Maloya and Mauli Jagran, where more original allottees remain. In older colonies, extending the benefit to GPA holders could become a key campaign issue.

headline: Grieving family donates organs of 53-year-old, saves three lives
content: Chandigarh: In a gesture of generosity amid profound personal loss, the family of 53-year-old Parshotam Singh, a resident of Khanpur village in Fatehgarh Sahib district, consented to donate his organs after he was declared brain-stem dead at PGI on Nov 21. His liver, pancreas and both kidneys were retrieved and transplanted, giving three critically ill patients a new chance at life.His wife Raj Kaur and son Davinder Singh, decided to donate his organs despite their grief. The organs benefited three patients, including a 20-year-old woman and two young men.Parshotam was reportedly riding his bicycle on Nov 18 when a car hit him from behind. He was initially taken to Rajindra Hospital, Patiala, before being shifted to a private hospital. He was referred to PGI on Nov 19 for specialised treatment. Despite sustained medical efforts, his condition remained critical and he was declared brain-stem dead on Nov 21.A daily-wage labourer, Parshotam was the family’s principal earning member. His wife is a homemaker. Despite the loss of their primary source of income, the family chose to help others by donating his organs.Raj Kaur said, “I have lost my husband, the pain of which is beyond words. But when we were told that his organs could help others live, we felt this was something meaningful we could do for humanity. We may be a simple family with limited means, but if his organs can give someone another chance at life, we consider it a blessing. We hope the recipients recover well and live long, healthy lives. This would be the greatest tribute to him.”Prof L Kaman, head of the department of general surgery, PGI, said liver transplantation was often the only definitive treatment for patients with advanced liver disease. “The successful liver transplantation in this case has given a 20-year-old female patient a valuable second chance at life. We are deeply grateful to the donor family for taking this decision amid immense grief. Their generosity has made this life-saving intervention possible,” he said.Prof Ashish Sharma, head of the department of renal transplant surgery, PGI, said the transplantation of both kidneys, including one as part of a simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplant, highlighted the potential of deceased organ donation.“These procedures offer renewed hope to patients suffering from advanced kidney and pancreatic disorders, who otherwise face significant challenges in their daily lives. The family’s generosity has made these life-transforming procedures possible,” he said.

headline: AIIMS Delhi urges schools to support students with diabetes, suggests 5 ways to help
content: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Delhi has called on schools to provide better support to children living with Type 1 diabetes, including allowing them to monitor their blood glucose levels, administer insulin, and participate in sports and other school activities without discrimination. The recommendations were discussed at a national engagement organised by the Health Related Information Dissemination Amongst Youth (HRIDAY) in collaboration with AIIMS Delhi on November 23, focusing on the everyday challenges faced by children with Type 1 diabetes at home, in schools and in their communities. AIIMS Delhi Director Dr Nikhil Tandon said children with Type 1 diabetes need support beyond diagnosis and should be equipped to manage their condition confidently. He said insulin management, regular blood glucose monitoring, healthy nutrition and physical activity were essential to everyday care. The discussions also highlighted the need for families, teachers and healthcare professionals to understand the condition and help children manage it without stigma. Type 1 diabetes: 5 ways schools can support students The recommendations emerging from the AIIMS-HRIDAY engagement focus on making routine diabetes management possible during school hours, rather than treating the condition as something that can be managed only at home or in hospitals: -Allow regular blood glucose monitoring: students should be allowed to check their blood glucose levels during school hours whenever required. Schools should also permit the use of glucose monitoring devices, including continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGMS). -Provide access to insulin: children should be allowed to administer insulin during school hours. Schools should make arrangements for the safe storage of insulin, including access to refrigeration where required, so that students do not have to interrupt their treatment routine. -Allow timely meals and snacks: students with Type 1 diabetes may need to eat at specific intervals to manage their blood glucose levels. Schools should accommodate their meal schedules and allow them to consume food or glucose when required. -Ensure participation in sports and physical activities: those with Type 1 diabetes should not be excluded from physical education, sports or other school activities because of their condition. Schools should provide the necessary support to help them participate safely. -Build awareness among teachers and classmates: teachers and school staff should understand the condition, recognise warning signs and know how to respond if a student experiences a sudden change in blood glucose levels. Children should also be supported without stigma or discrimination. Keralam's measures for students with Type 1 diabetes Keralam has also announced additional examination-related concessions for students with Type 1 diabetes. For the Kerala Engineering Architecture Medical (KEAM) 2027 entrance examination, the state government has approved 20 minutes of additional time for every hour of the examination. Candidates will have to submit a medical certificate issued by a doctor to avail themselves of the concession. The state has also allowed candidates to carry insulin pens, insulin pumps, glucose tablets, water, continuous glucose monitoring systems, snacks and fruits into the examination hall after security checks. Higher Education Minister Roji M John announced the decision on November 13 following a representation from the Type-One Diabetes Foundation and a report from the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations. The proposal also received approval from the Finance Department and the Chief Minister. The additional time provision had earlier been extended to examinations conducted by higher education institutions and professional colleges in the state. It will now also apply to KEAM 2027. The measure recognises that fluctuations in blood glucose levels, including hypoglycaemia and hyperglycaemia, may require candidates to pause and manage their condition during an examination. The AIIMS-HRIDAY engagement also highlighted the importance of extending such support beyond examinations, so that children with Type 1 diabetes can manage their condition during regular school activities and continue their education without avoidable restrictions.

headline: CJP's Saurav Das moves Delhi High Court over being stopped from flying to UK; hearing on November 26
content: New Delhi: Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an Oxford University event, where he was slated to speak on the "cockroach movement." .The plea was mentioned for urgent hearing on Wednesday. .A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said the matter would be listed on Thursday. .Das has alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London. .CJP's Saurav Das claims govt stopped him from flying to London; passport office flags discrepancies in documents."I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are," Das's counsel submitted. .He said the flight is on Thursday. "Let it be (heard) tomorrow," the bench responded. .On Monday, in a series of posts on X, Das criticised the central government after being prevented from boarding his 1 am flight to London. ."I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford. This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London, where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement," Das said. ."Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" he added. Das said he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion. ."And that's why I was going to London. But as soon as I went to the immigration check, I came to know that my passport has been flagged," he said. ."Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion? I wish I was Nirav Modi. I wish I was Vijay Mallya. I wish I had looted thousands of crores from the banks..." he said.

headline: Delhi nursery admissions 2027-28: Schools announce admission criteria, neighbourhood distance and sibling
content: Entry-level admissions for the next academic session in Delhi's private schools are set to begin, with some schools announcing their admission criteria, giving weightage to neighbourhood proximity, siblings of existing students, and alumni parents, among other categories.Schools are expected to publish their admission criteria on Monday. The application process will cover nursery, kindergarten, and Class 1 in private unaided recognised schools, with parents required to check the points allotted to different categories before applying.Sudha Acharya, principal of ITL International School in Dwarka, said the school has to consider distance from the school, siblings of existing students, alumni, parents, and children of staff members under its admission criteria.Mallika Preman of Tagore International School in East of Kailash said the school has given distance, siblings of existing students, alumni parents, and first-born children weightage under its admission criteria.Similarly, Vasant Valley School has allotted points to applicants living within a 10 to 15 km radius of the school, and to applicants whose father or mother is an alumnus. Siblings of existing students will also be considered under its admission criteria.Delhi Public School, RK Puram, has allotted 50 points to applicants residing within 6 km of the school, 40 points to those living beyond 6 km and up to 8 km, 30 points to those residing beyond 8 km and up to 15 km, and 20 points to applicants living beyond 15 km.The distance will be calculated on the basis of an aerial map and not road distance, according to the school's criteria.The school has allotted 26 points to applicants whose brother or sister is currently studying at DPS RK Puram, DPS Vasant Vihar or DPS East of Kailash. It has also allotted 12 points each to fathers and mothers who are alumni of DPS RK Puram, with Class 10 or 12 certificates required as proof.Shalimar Public School in Mahipalpur has allotted points to applicants residing within 1-3 km. The school has also included single-girl-child applicants in its admission criteria.The Directorate of Education, in its 59-page circular, has listed around 62 prohibited admission criteria, including parents' educational qualifications, interview-based assessments, management quota, gender, and Delhi domicile by birth. Schools have been directed to upload their admission criteria and detailed point-wise break-up on their respective websites.The department has also prescribed age limits in accordance with the National Education Policy 2020. Children applying for nursery must be aged 3-4 years, kindergarten applicants four to five years, and Class 1 applicants five to six years as on March 31, 2027.Registration for admission to nursery, lower KG, upper KG and class 1 in private schools in Delhi for the next academic session will begin on December 1, with December 28 set as the last date for submitting applications, according to a Directorate of Education circular.The first list of selected children, including the waiting list, will be published on January 20, followed by a second list on February 5. The admission process will conclude on March 12, the circular said.Schools have been directed to upload their admission criteria and the corresponding points on the Directorate's portal by November 26. They will also have to display the criteria and points on their respective websites.DPS RK Puram admission criteria: Distance carries up to 50 pointsDelhi Public School (DPS), RK Puram, has outlined a detailed point-based system, with the maximum weightage allocated to applicants living closer to the institution.According to the school's admission criteria, the distribution of points based on residential distance is as follows:Distance from schoolPoints allottedWithin 6 km50Above 6 km and up to 8 km40Above 8 km and up to 15 km30Beyond 15 km20The school has clarified that distance will be calculated using an aerial map rather than the actual road distance. This distinction is important for parents assessing their child's eligibility under the neighbourhood category.Apart from distance, DPS RK Puram has allotted 26 points to applicants whose brother or sister is currently studying at DPS RK Puram, DPS Vasant Vihar or DPS East of Kailash.The school has also included alumni parents in its criteria. Fathers and mothers who studied at DPS RK Puram will receive 12 points each. Applicants will have to submit their parents' Class 10 or Class 12 certificates as supporting documents.Shalimar Public School includes single-girl-child categoryShalimar Public School in Mahipalpur has included residential proximity and the single-girl-child category in its admission criteria.The school has allocated points to applicants residing within a distance of 1-3 km. The inclusion of the single-girl-child category provides another consideration in its point-based admission framework.These criteria indicate that schools are following different combinations of neighbourhood, family association and other permitted categories while preparing their admission lists.DoE circular prohibits 62 admission criteriaWhile schools have been allowed to frame their admission criteria within the prescribed framework, the Directorate of Education has specified categories that cannot be used to determine admissions.In its 59-page circular, the department has listed around 62 prohibited admission criteria. These include parents' educational qualifications, interview-based assessments, management quota, gender and Delhi domicile by birth.Schools have been instructed to ensure that their admission policies comply with the prescribed guidelines. They must also upload their criteria along with a detailed point-wise break-up on their respective websites and the Directorate's portal.The restrictions are intended to ensure transparency in the admission process and prevent schools from introducing arbitrary conditions while evaluating applications.Delhi nursery admission 2027-28: Age limit prescribed under NEP 2020The Directorate has also specified age requirements for children applying to entry-level classes in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.The prescribed age limits, calculated as on March 31, 2027, are:ClassPrescribed ageNursery3 to 4 yearsLower KG4 to 5 yearsUpper KG4 to 5 yearsClass 15 to 6 yearsParents should check the age requirements carefully before applying, as the eligibility conditions will determine whether a child can be considered for the respective entry-level class.Delhi private school admission 2027-28: Important datesThe Directorate of Education has issued the admission schedule for entry-level classes in private unaided recognised schools for the 2027-28 academic session.The important dates are as follows:Admission eventDateSchools to upload admission criteria on DoE portalNovember 26, 2026Registration beginsDecember 1, 2026Last date to submit applicationsDecember 28, 2026First selection list and waiting listJanuary 20, 2027Second admission listFebruary 5, 2027Admission process concludesMarch 12, 2027Schools will have to display their admission criteria and point-wise allocation on their respective websites in addition to uploading the details to the Directorate's portal.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. headline: Delhi riots case: SC refuses interim bail to Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam; seeks police response
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused, as of now, interim bail to activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, who had challenged a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in a UAPA case related to the alleged “larger conspiracy” behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response. During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail in the meantime. Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Imam, also sought similar relief on grounds of long incarceration. It said it will hear the police before considering the prayer for interim bail. The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration.

headline: Over 6,500 lung cancer cases reported in prominent Delhi hospitals in six years; one death every three days
content: New Delhi Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days. This information was provided in response to an RTI query to AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute. Fear, stigma, financial concerns keep cancer patients from seeking timely care, says expert Fear, stigma, financial concerns keep cancer patients from seeking timely care, says expert Fear, stigma, financial concerns keep cancer patients from seeking timely care, says expert storyline 1 Under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, data regarding lung cancer cases and associated deaths between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, were requested from the hospitals. Safdarjung Hospital only provided the number of lung cancer deaths but did not disclose the total number of cases. A request was also made for data on patients who had never smoked. However, none of the institutes provided any data on it. According to information provided in response to separate RTI applications filed by PTI Bhasha, 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded across three of the four hospitals (excluding Safdarjung), averaging 83 cases per month. Across all four hospitals, 913 deaths were reported, which translates to one patient dying every three days. The national capital is currently grappling with a severe air pollution crisis, an annual affair now in November, which is observed as the Lung Cancer Awareness Month. Although health experts state that long-term exposure to air pollution increases the risk of lung cancer, it is not the sole cause. Smoking and genetic mutations are two of the other contributing factors. The highest number of cases was recorded at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). This central government hospital provided data for the period from January 2020 to March 2026, during which 4,860 cases of lung cancer were registered and 158 deaths occurred. This averages to approximately 65 cases per month, with two patient deaths occurring monthly. Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity — and crop burning is not the culprit Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity — and crop burning is not the culprit This counter-intuitive phenomenon is driven by the high use of wood, dung and other household fuels for cooking and heating, a study finds. Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity — and crop burning is not the culprit storyline 1 According to data from the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), 1,613 cases of lung cancer were reported between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, resulting in 354 deaths. This translates to an average of 20 cases per month, with four patient deaths occurring monthly during this period. The institute noted that in 2021, the disease was also diagnosed in two children, and over a span of about six and a half years, 351 women were found to be suffering from lung cancer. However, it did not provide a gender-segregated breakdown of the deaths. Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital reported 108 cases of lung cancer during this period, including 47 women, with eight deaths recorded. Safdarjung Hospital reported 393 deaths among patients suffering from lung cancer during the same timeframe. A senior doctor at the DSCI, speaking to PTI on the condition of anonymity, mentioned that the institute receives patients not only from Delhi but also from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, and even Nepal. Regarding the role of air pollution in Delhi on lung cancer cases, the doctor said the primary cause is smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke, though genetic mutations also play a role. According to doctors, lung cancer has also been detected in non-smoking women; this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution. Doctors also said that the disease is often diagnosed only in its final stages, making treatment extremely challenging. Dr Geeta Kadayaprath, a senior specialist at the Apollo Athenaa Women’s Cancer Centre, said that long-term exposure to polluted air—common in cities like Delhi—can increase the risk of lung cancer. She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), under the World Health Organization, has classified outdoor air pollution and the particulate matter it contains as carcinogenic to humans. She explained that PM 2.5 particles are so minute that they can penetrate deep into the lungs and, over time, cause damage to cells. When asked about symptoms, Dr Vikas Maurya, a senior specialist at Fortis Hospital in Shalimar Bagh, explained that there are often no clear symptoms in the early stages. However, potential warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, changes in one’s voice, unexplained weight loss, and recurring chest infections. He further noted that the condition cannot be detected through a standard X-ray; instead, a CT scan is required for diagnosis.

headline: Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama allotted bungalow in Lutyens’ Delhi
content: New Delhi: The central government has allotted a bungalow to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama in Lutyens’ Delhi, sources said. Although there is no official word from the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, sources said on Tuesday that the Dalai Lama has been allotted the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane. They said the allotment to Gaden Phodrang Trust — the office of the Dalai Lama — has been made following a request from the Ministry of External Affairs. Such accommodation is generally transferred for three years, with provision for extension. According to the website of Gaden Phodrang, the Trust is dedicated to preserving and upholding the institution of the Dalai Lama and his spiritual work, while advancing his humanitarian vision. The website states that the Trust also supports His Holiness’s core commitments: promoting human values, fostering interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment, and encouraging a deeper appreciation of ancient Indian wisdom.

headline: 2 Indians injured in Riyadh attack; New Delhi condemns strike
content: Two Indians were among those injured in an attack on a financial district in Riyadh that triggered strong condemnation from New Delhi.India also denounced continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia."Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.The attack was carried out on Tuesday. Local authorities said the injured included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese and four Egyptian nationals.The MEA said that India strongly condemns the attack in Riyadh as well as the continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia."These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks," it said in a statement.India also reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed its unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity."We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.There has been a sudden escalation in tensions in West Asia, especially after the Houthis carried out several strikes on Saudi Arabia.The West Asia conflict began in February following attacks on Iran by the US and Israel. New Delhi has consistently called for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.India has been specifically voicing serious concern over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's civilian infrastructure and economic assets, cautioning that such strikes undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

headline: Delhi High Court refuses additional DU PG seats for four-year UGCF students, directs UGC to examine griev
content: The Delhi High Court has declined to direct Delhi University (DU) to create additional seats in its one-year postgraduate programmes for students who completed the four-year undergraduate programme under the Undergraduate Curriculum Framework (UGCF-2022). However, providing relief to the first batch of students affected by the admission criteria, the court has directed the University Grants Commission (UGC) to examine their grievances and explore admission opportunities at other universities and colleges within three weeks.In an order dated November 20, Justice Jasmeet Singh disposed of a batch of writ petitions filed by students enrolled in DU's four-year undergraduate programme during the 2022-26 academic session. The petitions challenged the university's admission criteria for its one-year postgraduate programmes for the 2026-27 academic session.The students had approached the court after DU introduced preferential consideration for candidates holding a four-year Bachelor's Honours degree, including Honours with Research or Entrepreneurship, over those who completed a four-year multidisciplinary undergraduate programme with a Major subject.Why did DU students challenge the one-year PG admission criteria?The petitioners argued that DU and its constituent colleges had encouraged students to continue into the fourth year by indicating that completing the programme would facilitate their progression to a one-year master's degree, in line with the academic pathways envisaged under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.However, the university's Bulletin of Information for Admission to One-Year Post-Graduate Programmes, issued on July 4, 2026, introduced preferential consideration for students with a four-year Bachelor's Honours degree.According to the petitioners, this placed graduates of the multidisciplinary programme with a Major subject at a disadvantage, even when they had studied the same discipline and fulfilled the prescribed subject-specific credit requirements.They contended that the distinction was based primarily on the structure and nomenclature of their undergraduate degrees rather than their subject-specific academic preparation.The students also submitted that had the preferential admission criteria been disclosed earlier, they might have opted for a three-year undergraduate degree and subsequently pursued postgraduate admission through the entrance-based route.What did the Delhi High Court observe about DU's admission policy?While considering the petitions, the Delhi High Court acknowledged the students' grievance and observed that they had continued into the fourth year in the bona fide belief that completing the programme would facilitate admission to a one-year master's course.The court noted that their legitimate expectation regarding progression to postgraduate studies under the academic framework envisaged by DU deserved consideration, particularly in view of the subsequent introduction and application of preferential admission criteria without adequate prior disclosure.DU, however, defended its admission policy before the court. Its counsel argued that the four-year Honours programme was academically distinct and more extensive than the multidisciplinary undergraduate programme with a Major subject.The university submitted that Honours students undertook 132 credits and that the preferential admission criteria had been prescribed after considering the academic requirements of postgraduate programmes.The court declined to enter into an assessment of the comparative curricula, academic rigour and credit requirements of the two undergraduate pathways. It observed that these matters fell within the domain of academic and regulatory authorities.It also refused to direct DU to create additional postgraduate seats, noting that such a decision would involve several academic and administrative considerations, including sanctioned intake, faculty availability, infrastructure and institutional resources.UGC directed to examine students' grievances within three weeksAlthough the court declined to order the creation of additional seats at DU, it observed that the circumstances involving the first batch of students admitted under UGCF-2022 warranted consideration by the UGC.The commission, as the parent regulatory body, has been directed to treat the writ petitions as representations and examine the possibilities of securing admission opportunities for the affected students.The UGC has specifically been asked to assess whether seats are available in one-year master's programmes at other universities and colleges. Wherever feasible, it should endeavour to accommodate the petitioners under the existing guidelines.The court has also directed the commission to take into account the notification dated August 12, 2026, which was annexed to one of the petitions.The UGC has been given three weeks from November 20 to complete the exercise and examine the students' representations.Will DU students get admission to one-year master's programmes?The Delhi High Court's order does not guarantee admission to the petitioners in DU or any other university. It also does not direct Delhi University to revise its existing admission criteria or increase the sanctioned intake for its one-year postgraduate programmes.Instead, the responsibility now rests with the UGC to examine the students' grievances and identify possible admission opportunities at other institutions, subject to the availability of seats and applicable academic guidelines.The matter brings attention to the challenges faced by the first batch of students transitioning through the four-year undergraduate structure introduced under UGCF-2022. Their admission concerns have also raised questions about the communication of eligibility conditions and the alignment of undergraduate pathways with postgraduate admission policies under the NEP 2020 framework.For the affected students, the next three weeks will be crucial as they await the UGC's assessment and the possibilities of securing admission to one-year master's programmes at other universities and colleges.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Delhi: Youth and women to get a state-of-the-art skill development centre with employment training facilities | Education
content: Under the leadership of Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, a state-of-the-art Skill Development Centre will be developed in Shalimar Bagh, where youth will be trained in accordance with modern technology and industry requirements.According to the Chief Minister Office, the government is set to give shape to an ambitious project aimed at connecting youth and women with skills, employment, and self-reliance. India and Cyprus discuss operationalising MoU on higher education and researchAlong with this, women will be prepared for employment, self-employment, and entrepreneurship. Specifically, employment-orientated technical courses on the lines of ITIs will be launched for 12th-pass youth, and short-term courses related to bakery, beauty, fashion, tailoring, and other practical skills will be introduced for women.The objective of this initiative is not to limit training merely to a certificate but to make it a medium of employment and economic self-reliance.RRB Station Master Recruitment 2026: Last date to apply today for 1265 posts at rrbapply.gov.in, link hereThe Chief Minister stated that providing better employment opportunities to the youth of Delhi and economically empowering women are among her government's top priorities."This centre to be built in Shalimar Bagh is an important part of this vision. Here, youth will be prepared for the modern workplace by aligning training with market demand and industry needs. Women will get opportunities to learn skills suited to their interests, capabilities, and family circumstances and to start their own businesses. Flexible timings, weekend batches, and online-offline training facilities are also proposed at the centre, enabling women who miss out on training due to domestic responsibilities to hone their skills as well. This centre will not only become a major hub for skill development for youth but will also prove to be a milestone in bringing women into the mainstream by making them financially self-reliant," the CM said. Maharashtra govt to introduce tougher law against exam malpractices during winter session: FadnavisThe modern building of this centre will be constructed by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC) over an area of approximately eight acres.The CM said, "To be built near DESU Colony, this centre will feature smart classrooms, 14 state-of-the-art labs and training centres, a library and learning resource centre, a multipurpose auditorium with a capacity of 250 people, and facilities related to conferences and placements. Modern equipment related to digital and IT labs, fashion and textile labs, tailoring and handicrafts, beauty and wellness, bakery and food processing, healthcare, etc., will be available for training."A horticulture training field will also be developed in an area of about two acres adjacent to the campus, where practical training in plant care, plant health, and landscaping can be imparted. Keeping in view the convenience of students coming from far-flung areas of Delhi and from outside, there is also a plan to develop hostels and modern sports facilities there so that youth receiving training can get a complete and accessible educational environment, the release said. Courses such as fashion design, tailoring, embroidery, beautician, hair styling, bakery, food processing, and handicrafts will be particularly useful for women at the centre. After training, apart from taking up jobs, women will be able to start their own boutique, beauty salon, bakery, tiffin service, or other businesses. Through the Women Entrepreneurship and Incubation facility, arrangements are proposed to connect them with guidance, mentorship, market linkages, and financial assistance opportunities to start a business. For the convenience of working mothers, two crèche units with a capacity of 25 children each and a medical sick-bay for first aid will also be built on the campus. This will relieve women from worries about childcare during training, the release said. The academic and technical operations of this centre will be carried out through the Skill Development Centre of Dr B R Ambedkar University, which comes under the government's Directorate of Higher Education. The training programmes will focus on industry-based practical skills in line with the standards of the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). Youth will receive training in sectors such as digital services, IT support, artificial intelligence, retail, and hospitality, the release said.After completing the course, guidance will be provided for employment, apprenticeship, or starting one's own enterprise. Linking this centre with priorities like Skill India, Mission Shakti, National Education Policy-2020, and 'Viksit Bharat-2047', there is also a plan to open further avenues of higher education for the trainees. A special feature is that the youth and women trained here will also be awarded certificates by the government, making it easier for them to find employment elsewhere as well, the release said. (ANI)

headline: Delhi wakes up to coldest morning of season; Air quality ‘poor’
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) Delhi recorded its coldest morning of the season on Wednesday, with the minimum temperature settling at 10 degrees Celsius. The minimum temperature at Safdarjung, the city’s base weather station, was 1.3 degrees below the season’s normal, while it dropped by 1.2 degrees compared to the previous day. Air quality in Delhi remained in the poor category, with four monitoring stations recording ‘very poor’ readings, even as the city’s average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 224. The total number of weather stations active at 9.05 am was 56 out of the total 59 in the city. Other parts of the city also recorded relatively low temperatures. Lodhi Road recorded a minimum of 10.1 degrees Celsius, followed by Ayanagar at 10.4 degrees, Palam at 11 degrees and the Ridge at 11.7 degrees. The minimum temperature at Palam remained unchanged from Tuesday, while Lodhi Road recorded a drop of 0.6 degrees. The Ridge saw a fall of 0.3 degrees, while Ayanagar recorded a marginal rise of 0.2 degrees.

headline: Dr Atul Mohan Kochhara named DGHS chief | Latest News Delhi
content: Dr Atul Mohan Kochhara, a senior dermatologist, was appointed the new director general of health services (DGHS), according to an order by the Delhi government’s health and family welfare department.Previously, Dr Vinod Kumar, medical director of the GTB Hospital, had been holding the additional charge of the post.The order, dated November 21, said, “Pursuance to the approval of Lieutenant Governor, Delhi, Dr Atul Mohan Kochhar, NTS (Dermatology), SAG (senior administrative grade), is hereby posted as Director (DGHS), Government of NCT of Delhi, with immediate effect.”HT has seen a copy of the order.Kochhar served as chief executive officer of the National Accreditation Board for hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) from December 2019 to March 2026. Before that, he worked as a professor and consultant in dermatology at Maulana Azad Medical College and Lok Nayak Hospital.This is the fifth appointment to the post in two years. In May 2025, Dr Rati Makkar was appointed to the post but opted for voluntary retirement in August. Dr Vatsala Aggarwal succeeded her the same month. She was arrested by the anti-corruption branch and subsequently suspended over alleged irregularities in the procurement of medicines and medical equipment for Delhi government health services.Dr Sushma Jain, then medical superintendent of Jag Pravesh Chandra Hospital, was assigned the additional charge of DGHS director in June this year.Kumar was subsequently entrusted with the additional charge in July 30.

headline: No end in sight for tin-roof classrooms in Delhi schools
content: NEW DELHI: As the city government approaches completion of two years in office, a basic question of school infrastructure remains unanswered: when will children studying under ‘tin sheds’ get proper classrooms?Despite repeated complaints, judicial interventions and the issue being flagged before multiple authorities, thousands of children remain deprived of the basic classroom facilities.From Ashok Nagar and Baprola to Government Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya at Bulbuli Khana, near Turkman Gate, and Zeenat Mahal School at Hamdard Chowk, Kamla Market, students continue to attend classes in structures with rusted tin roofs, inadequate walls and little protection from extreme weather. The list also includes Qaumi Senior Secondary School in Sadar Bazar, Government Senior Secondary Boys School in Kewal Park, Azadpur, and Government Boys’ Secondary School, Dev Nagar, 22-B Block, Karol Bagh.The condition of Qaumi Senior Secondary School is particularly telling. One of the oldest schools in the area, its four-storey building was demolished during the Emergency in 1976. The CBSE-affiliated institution was subsequently shifted to a DDA colony but was never provided land or a permanent building. .Nearly five decades later, it continues to operate from 13 makeshift classrooms, arranged in an L-shape on a corner of the Eidgah premises. With tin-sheet roofs and walls, each classroom has little more than a ceiling fan, a blackboard placed on a stand and rusted iron benches. One of the teachers said that it is unfortunate that even the principal’s office and teachers’ room have also been squeezed into the same makeshift arrangement.Rahim Uddin, an RWA member from Old Delhi, said it was shameful that successive authorities had failed to address something as fundamental as school education. Despite the school being repeatedly highlighted, he said, its condition had barely changed.In Karol Bagh’s Dev Nagar, Government Boys’ Secondary School continues to run entirely from tin-shed classrooms on MCD land, where construction is prohibited is another example of sheer neglect.The issue resurfaced before the high court last week, with concerns raised over nearly 1,000 children studying under tin sheds at the Ashok Nagar government school..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Delhi plans 2 new biomedical waste plants at ₹41 cr amid pollution violation concerns | India News
content: Delhi is planning a major overhaul of its biomedical waste management system, with two new common biomedical waste treatment and disposal facilities proposed across the national Capital at an estimated cost of ₹41 crore.The move comes amid concerns over environmental violations at the two existing facilities, one of which continued to emit thick black smoke and failed to properly segregate biomedical waste despite repeated inspections by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC).Project detailsThe two proposed facilities will cater to different geographical zones of the city. The first, estimated to cost ₹20 crore, will cover East, North-East, Old Delhi and Central districts, while the second, with an estimated cost of ₹21 crore, will serve West, South-West and Outer North districts.The DPCC has already initiated the process of setting up the two facilities by inviting bids for the project. According to the project report, the facility will be developed on a Built, Own and Operate (BOO) basis.Also Read: Pollution crackdown: DPCC inspects 3K sites, sends closure notice to 103The company deployed for the project will execute collection, transportation, reception, storage, treatment and final disposal of biomedical waste generated in the designated districts.The proposed expansion assumes significance as Delhi currently relies on two operational common biomedical waste treatment facilities, with a combined installed capacity of 62.8 tonnes per day. These facilities process biomedical waste generated by hospitals, nursing homes, clinics and other healthcare establishments that do not have their own treatment infrastructure.Environmental Compliance Under ScrutinyHowever, their environmental compliance has come under scrutiny. In a status report submitted to the National Green Tribunal (NGT), the DPCC flagged several violations at Biotic Waste Solutions (BWS) in Jahangirpuri and SMS Water Grace at the Delhi Jal Board’s Nilothi sewage treatment plant.Also Read: DPCC asks seven agencies to submit daily pollution action reports by 5pmWhile Biotic Waste Solutions rectified some deficiencies identified during the initial inspection, SMS Water Grace continued to violate three significant parameters during a follow-up inspection in July. These included emissions of thick black smoke from its incinerator, mixing of different categories of biomedical waste at the unloading area and inadequate effluent treatment. The facility was subsequently issued another show-cause notice in September, proposing closure and withdrawal of its authorisation.

headline: Missing machinery in Delhi’s fight for clean air
content: Containing Delhi’s unyielding air pollution requires a multi-pronged approach. Regulating emissions from the transport, industrial, and agricultural sectors involves strategies that have economic consequences. Dust, in contrast, can be removed with far less disruptive measures — keeping roads clean and in good repair. However, in May, an investigation by this newspaper revealed that Delhi had a shortfall of more than 80 per cent in mechanised road-sweeping machines (MRSM). Now, as the capital confronts peak pollution, a follow-up investigation shows that the gap continues to be yawning. The MCD commissioned 70 MRSMs in October. Only 11 are expected to be on the road by next month, while the remaining 59 are scheduled to arrive by the end of December, or later. The MRSMs are being imported from Italy and Switzerland. Shipping route disruptions caused by the West Asia crisis may explain some of the delivery delays. But precious time was lost in the procurement process. Despite flagging the need for 88 MRSMs at a high-level crisis meeting last year, the MCD took over eight months to issue purchase orders. Since last year, the Centre and the Delhi government have projected a commitment to tackling the crisis on a priority basis. However, the municipality’s protracted procedures tell a different story. With a “triple-engine” government at the helm in the Capital, bureaucratic hurdles should have been cleared months ago. The procurement exercise has a larger lesson. The decision to import MRSMs points to a gap in domestic manufacturing. Indian companies make road-sweeping machines by mounting additional vacuum engines on cargo trucks. These devices operate at just 2-3 km/h and tend to break down within a year or two. The imported machines, more efficient, require modifications to adapt to Indian conditions. The need, therefore, is to develop equipment suited to the country's roads and climate. Like Delhi, several Indian cities face the challenge of road dust, and the demand for mechanised cleaning will only grow. There is little reason for the country to depend on imported equipment for a task with implications for public health. Building domestic capacity in air-cleansing infrastructure must become a part of the broader anti-pollution project — that combines public health science, sound policy, administrative intent and capacity.
