Restraint and moderation, rather than agitational language, are the hallmarks of the paper.The Tribune has two sister publications, Punjabi Tribune (in Punjabi) and Dainik Tribune (in Hindi).

headline: Delhi to make annual registration compulsory for free power subsidy
content: Delhi’s free electricity benefit is set to become an annual opt-in exercise, meaning consumers who have so far received subsidies will also have to register afresh every year to keep their power bills down. The Delhi Government plans to launch a dedicated portal in the first week of December, giving domestic electricity consumers a month to enrol and select the subsidy option.Under the proposed arrangement, consumers will have to submit the required documents and authenticate their details through their electricity consumer numbers and Aadhaar. Distribution companies (DISCOMs) will verify the applications. Those who fail to complete registration within the stipulated period will not be eligible for the subsidy.The change makes an important distinction between being an electricity connection holder and a registered subsidy beneficiary. Even households already receiving free or subsidised electricity will have to take action rather than assume the benefit will continue automatically.The existing subsidy structure is expected to remain the basis of the benefit. Domestic consumers using up to 200 units a month receive free electricity, while those consuming between 201 and 400 units get a 50 per cent subsidy, capped at Rs 800. The proposed registration requirement changes how consumers access the benefit, not the stated consumption slabs.The annual renewal requirement could, however, create fresh administrative hurdles, particularly for elderly consumers, tenants and households with discrepancies in Aadhaar or electricity account details. Consumers will also need to keep track of the renewal cycle to avoid losing the benefit because of missed registration or verification delays.The scale of the exercise is significant. Delhi has more than 73 lakh electricity consumers, around 40 per cent more than a decade ago. Domestic households account for 84.1 per cent of the total.The financial stakes are equally considerable. The government's power subsidy allocation stood at Rs 3,500 crore for 2026-27, while expenditure had reached Rs 4,037.63 crore as of February. The subsidy bill has more than doubled over the past decade.The move also comes against the backdrop of a Comptroller and Auditor General report questioning whether the existing policy adequately benefits needy and underprivileged households, noting that a large share of beneficiaries had relatively high electricity consumption.

headline: Punjabi Academy plans digital push to revive language among youngsters
content: Almost two years after coming to power in Delhi, the BJP Government has reconstituted the governing bodies of five language academies, including the Punjabi Academy. The newly appointed council plans to strengthen Punjabi language education, revive literary activities and expand cultural programmes, with a special focus on connecting the younger generation with the language through digital platforms.Newly appointed vice-chairman Impreet Singh Bakshi, who took charge on Monday, said the academy would focus on strengthening Punjabi education in schools, improving its libraries, supporting writers and artists and organising cultural programmes across Delhi.Established in September 1981 by the erstwhile Delhi Administration as an autonomous organisation, the academy works towards promoting Punjabi language, literature and culture. Its activities include publishing books, supporting writers, conducting research and organising literary and cultural programmes.Talking to The Tribune, Bakshi said one of the priorities of the newly constituted governing council would be to strengthen Punjabi language education and encourage people to read and write the language. He pointed out that the number of Punjabi teachers in schools had declined considerably over the years, affecting the language's presence in the education system.“We will work towards addressing the bottlenecks related to teachers and libraries. Strengthening the existing infrastructure and bringing Punjabi back into people's everyday lives will be among our priorities,” he said.The academy plans to launch a YouTube channel and use Instagram to make Punjabi learning accessible to youngsters, particularly those who speak the language but cannot read or write its script.Bakshi said the academy would collaborate with young people and researchers to produce short videos explaining the Punjabi script, pronunciation and basic language skills. Bilingual learning material would also be explored to help beginners.“We want to make Punjabi easy to reach, read and learn. The younger generation spends considerable time on digital platforms, and we want to use these platforms to teach them through short videos," he said.The academy also plans to revive literary awards, cash prizes, book releases, poetry gatherings and Kirtan Darbars. A Punjabi Literature Festival, on the lines of Hindi and English literary festivals, is among the proposed initiatives.Bakshi said the academy would also promote Punjabi theatre, folk art, music, calligraphy and traditional sculpture, while providing emerging artists a platform to showcase their work.The newly reconstituted governing council has members from different professional backgrounds and districts, including academia and the arts.Bakshi said their expertise would be utilised to develop programmes and address community-specific concerns. The council is expected to meet regularly, with the academy aiming to introduce new activities approximately every fortnight.The academy is also planning a major Kirtan Darbar on December 12, 13 and 14, with the dates tentative. Bakshi said the Prime Minister was expected to attend. An event marking Veer Bal Diwas is also on the agenda.Felicitation ceremony marks new governing body's appointmentThe Punjabi Academy organised a felicitation ceremony on Monday to welcome newly appointed vice-chairman Impreet Singh Bakshi and members of its reconstituted governing body. The ceremony began with an Ardas seeking blessings for the new leadership's successful tenure. Bakshi thanked the BJP's central leadership and the Delhi Government for entrusting him with the responsibility, assuring that he would work with dedication to promote Punjabi language, literature and culture.

headline: Parents to protest as 12 students face expulsion despite DoE show-cause notice
content: A fee dispute at Salwan Public School in Mayur Vihar has escalated into a confrontation that could keep 12 children, aged between eight and 14, out of classrooms from November 25, with their parents planning a protest outside the Directorate of Education (DoE) office at Civil Lines on Wednesday, seeking intervention to reverse the school's decision.The school has issued notices to parents informing them that their children's names are being struck off its rolls under Rule 35 of the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973, with effect from November 25. The notices, dated November 23, also explicitly advise parents not to send their wards to the school from that date.The notices cite outstanding fee dues despite repeated reminders and show-cause notices issued on October 23. Several notices examined by The Tribune show the school claiming arrears ranging from Rs 34,956 to Rs 77,863, with the periods of outstanding dues varying between students. In one case, the dues are calculated from February 2025 to November 2026, while another covers April 2026 to November 2026.However, parents maintain that the dispute is not over a refusal to pay school fees altogether, but over the amount being demanded following successive fee revisions, over which DoE has already issued warnings to this school in past.Pradeep Soni, a parent and one of the organisers of Wednesday's protest, alleged that the school had increased fees by 32 per cent in one year and 19 per cent in another over the past two years, taking the cumulative impact to 57 per cent. He said the affected parents had continued paying the fees approved by the DoE but were refusing to pay the disputed increase."We are not against the school or our children's education. We are questioning why we should pay the fee demanded by the school when the Directorate of Education is the authority that should decide the approved fee," Soni told The Tribune.The dispute is also before the Delhi High Court, according to Soni, who said the parents' petition was pending and cited an earlier judicial direction against coercive action over non-payment of increased fees during an ongoing academic session. He further claimed that parents had offered in writing to pay the revised fee prospectively from April 1, 2026, while leaving the disputed past dues to be settled through the court proceedings. The school, he alleged, rejected the proposal.Soni also claimed that the DoE had issued directions against striking off students' names and served the school a show-cause notice on April 1, warning of possible de-recognition over such practices. These orders and the parents' interpretation of the court proceedings could not be independently verified from the documents made available.At Wednesday's protest, parents plan to seek two immediate interventions: restoration of the children's names on the school rolls and protection of their studies from disruption. They also want the department to conduct an audit and settle the permissible fee instead of allowing the dispute to continue.The parents plan to take the children to meet DoE Director Ankita Anand and explain how exclusion from school could affect their education.The immediate concern is that the dispute, which began over fee revisions, is now threatening classroom attendance and continuity of studies for children in the middle of the academic session. The school's response to the allegations was not available at the time of filing.

headline: PLI Auto disbursements surge to  ₹4,385 crore in FY27
content: New Delhi: The Centre has disbursed ₹4,385 crore under its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto parts in the current fiscal as of 25 November, signalling a sharp acceleration in payouts under a scheme that has faced concerns over slow fund utilization.The disbursement takes the cumulative incentives paid under the ₹25,938 crore PLI Auto scheme to ₹6,771 crore since payouts began in fiscal year 2025 (FY25), or about 26% of its total outlay as of November 2026, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.The scheme, which has the largest outlay among those run by the ministry, will continue to provide incentives until FY29. As of November, nine automakers and 10 auto component manufacturers were eligible to receive incentives under it.The latest addition to the list is the Indian arm of South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor, which received government approval in September this year to claim incentives under the scheme for two models of its electric Creta car.The PLI Auto scheme provides incentives to manufacturers on sales of zero-emission vehicles, including electric vehicles and some hydrogen-based vehicles. The objective is to lower manufacturing costs and improve manufacturers' margins.Disbursements accelerateThe ministry has previously faced questions over low budget utilization from the Rajya Sabha's department-related standing committee on industry. In March this year, the parliamentary panel, headed by MP Tiruchi Siva, flagged the under-utilization of budget estimates. It noted that the PLI Auto scheme, the ₹18,100 crore PLI scheme for batteries and the ₹11,900 crore PM E-Drive electric vehicle subsidy scheme had all seen reductions of more than 30% between budget estimates (BE) and revised estimates (RE) in multiple years.In its response to the committee, the ministry said the initial under-utilization of funds under PLI Auto was because investments by automakers in cleaner vehicle manufacturing took time to fructify, delaying the sales-based incentives that could be disbursed.Under the scheme's original disbursement plan, payouts were targeted at ₹604 crore in the first year, ₹3,150 crore in the second, ₹5,925 crore in the third, ₹7,199 crore in the fourth and ₹9,060 crore in the fifth year.Against these targets, the government's budget estimates stood at ₹3,500 crore in FY25, ₹2,818 crore in FY26 and ₹5,939 crore in FY27.EV adoption gathers paceThe acceleration in incentive disbursements comes as electric vehicle adoption in India gains momentum. EV registrations rose to 2.55 million in FY26, from 2.04 million in the previous fiscal year, according to the government's VAHAN registry of new vehicles.Based on its analysis of 2025 data, the International Energy Agency (IEA) ranks India as the world's second-largest electric two-wheeler market, the largest electric three-wheeler market and the third-largest electric bus market.India aims to become a net-zero carbon emitter by 2070. Transport accounts for 12% of the country's carbon emissions, according to the IEA. A shift towards electric vehicles could also help reduce India's dependence on imported oil, with the country currently meeting about 90% of its oil requirements through imports.

headline: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Holds High-Level Meeting with Madhya Pradesh CM Dr. Mohan Yadav on Agricultural and Rural Development Proposals Centre Approves ₹643.14 Crore for Construction of 223 Bridges in Madhya Pradesh
content: Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held a comprehensive and productive meeting today with the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav, along with State Ministers Shri Prahlad Singh Patel and Shri Aidal Singh Kansana, and senior officials, to review key proposals aimed at accelerating agricultural growth and rural infrastructure development in Madhya Pradesh. Congratulating Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav and his entire team for their proactive approach toward the state's development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that the delegation presented several vital proposals pertaining to roads, bridges, housing, irrigation, and various central missions. Approval of Bridges and Road Infrastructure: In a major boost to rural connectivity, the Centre has approved ₹643.14 crore for the construction of 223 bridges in Madhya Pradesh. Additionally, road construction proposals worth approximately ₹600 crore were also presented and discussed during the meeting. Scientific Agricultural Roadmap: Shri Chouhan announced that a dedicated Scientific Agricultural Roadmap will be formulated for Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with agricultural scientists to enhance productivity and sustainability. Agriculture Clusters and Centres of Excellence: Madhya Pradesh will be allotted two Agriculture Clusters and two Centres of Excellence to promote modern farming practices and value addition. Clean Plant Programme: Work will be undertaken to develop specialized nurseries in Madhya Pradesh under the Clean Plant Programme to ensure the availability of disease-free, high-quality planting material for farmers.

headline: Section 301 probe: India rejects US claim of structural excess capacity
content: India rejected the United States’ (US) claim of structural ‘excess capacity’ in any sector, the commerce department said on Wednesday, emphasising that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of trade deal negotiations between the two countries. The US administration on Wednesday proposed imposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, alleging structural excess capacity, but offered to lower the rate to 17 per cent if New Delhi and Washington conclude a trade deal. “Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation concerning Acts, Policies, and Practices of 14 economies, including India, relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors. The Notice is currently under examination. “India engaged constructively throughout this investigation. In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector,” the department said in a statement. “India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations,” it said, adding that India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US bilateral trade agreement.

headline: Navi Mumbai Airport Crosses 4 Million Passengers Milestone Ahead Of First Anniversary
content: The Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) hit a major milestone as it crossed the landmark 4 million passenger milestone in less than 11 months since commencing its commercial operations on December 25, 2025. Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA), developed and managed by Navi Mumbai International Airport Limited (NMIAL), a public-private partnership between Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) and City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited (CIDCO), is poised to become a world-class aviation gateway for the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and western India. As the second international airport in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, NMIA plays a transformative role in decongesting existing aviation capacity while catalysing economic growth and urban development across Navi Mumbai. "This exceptional operational achievement highlights NMIA's rapid integration into the aviation ecosystem of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) and sets a robust foundation as the airport approaches its first anniversary next month," a statement from the airport said. With a cumulative passenger volume of 4,101,409, the airport has witnessed a well-balanced distribution of traffic, comprising 4,088,840 domestic and 12,569 international travellers; arriving passengers stood at 2,023,241, while departing passengers reached 2,078,168, reflecting the growing preference for NMIA as a premier gateway, the statement added. The airport's operational footprint continues to grow exponentially, recording 31,043 passenger aircraft movements (30,940 domestic and 103 international). Regional and national carrier partnerships have been central to this growth. IndiGo led the movement share with 24,777 flights, followed by Akasa Air (3,125), Air India Express (2,955), Fly91 (132), and Star Air (54). In addition, NMIA successfully managed 1,092 general aviation movements, demonstrating its versatile operational handling capacity.

headline: US proposes up to 25% tariff on India, offers 17% upon trade deal
content: The Donald Trump administration in the United States (US) on Wednesday proposed imposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, alleging structural excess capacity, but offered to lower the rate to 17 per cent if New Delhi and Washington conclude a trade deal. The preliminary findings of the latest Section 301 investigation into excess industrial capacity put fresh pressure on India to conclude the first tranche of its bilateral trade agreement with the US. A 25 per cent tariff would leave India facing the second-highest proposed rate among the countries/blocs covered by the investigation, behind only Vietnam at 35 per cent. A reduced rate of 17 per cent, however, could give Indian exporters a modest competitive edge over regional rivals such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and Thailand, which face proposed rates of 18 per cent, as well as Vietnam and China at 20 per cent. The US currently imposes a 10 per cent tariff on Indian goods, in addition to regular Customs duties. However, the proposed levy is not intended to be added on top of this existing tariff. The office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed calculating the rate “net of existing Section 301 duties” and said Washington would consider adjustments to account for other Section 301 and Section 232 tariffs. Several Indian exports, including steel, aluminium, automobiles, patented pharmaceutical articles and semiconductors, are already subject to Section 232 duties. India is among the 14 trading partners covered by the eight-month investigation launched under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act of 1974. The provision authorises the Office of the USTR to investigate and respond to foreign governments’ acts, policies or practices that burden or restrict US commerce. The other economies covered by the investigation include China, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia, as well as the European Union. The USTR has not proposed tariffs on Mexico and Norway for now. Following the announcement, USTR Jamieson Greer told CNBC that the proposed tariff ceilings were consistent with trade agreements reached over the past year, which had also lowered barriers to US exports. “We’re sticking to that in terms of our proposals because we think a lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” he said. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we're proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.” The office of the USTR said India’s “unreasonable” acts, policies and practices included industrial plans to expand manufacturing, inadequate labour protections, financial repression, persistent market-access barriers and a failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies. These practices, it argued, restricted US commercial opportunities in India and third-country markets, contributed to lost production, exports, jobs and investment in American manufacturing, and heightened economic security risks through reliance on inputs from non-market economies. “This is especially true in sectors like health (pharmaceuticals and medical devices), steel, solar, and information and communications technology (ICT),” it added. Delhi-based Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), however, described the proposed rates as a deliberate attempt to extract one-sided concessions. It argued that Washington was reviving the reciprocal tariff regime under a different name, using steep baseline duties -- of up to 40 per cent -- to pressure trading partners into signing trade agreements that disproportionately benefit the US. With the threat of tariffs of up to 100 per cent under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act also hanging over India, New Delhi should reject the trade deal and instead respond to Washington’s allegations sector by sector, the think-tank said. India and the US have been negotiating the first tranche of their bilateral trade agreement since March last year. In February, the two countries issued a joint statement outlining the contours of an interim trade agreement and agreeing to reduce the tariff on Indian goods to 18 per cent. The rate had been negotiated and finalised as part of the interim arrangement. Weeks later, however, the US Supreme Court struck down the tariffs, revoking President Donald Trump’s authority to impose country-specific reciprocal duties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). The Trump administration has since been working to establish a new tariff architecture while pursuing investigations under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act. Last week, India’s Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations on the first tranche of the trade deal were nearing conclusion, but that its signing would depend on Washington finalising the new tariff framework and providing clarity on the ongoing Section 301 investigations.

headline: Economy resilient; passthrough of oil price shock limited, says RBI
content: India’s economy continued to show resilience in October, supported by strong credit demand, robust exports and foreign portfolio inflows, despite the global headwinds from elevated energy prices, geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in financial markets, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its November bulletin on Wednesday. The bulletin also noted that the West Asia conflict generated a sharper crude oil price shock than the Russia-Ukraine conflict. However, the pass-through to retail fuel prices in the current episode has been relatively lower, limiting the pressures on imported inflation, the bulletin noted. Higher precious metals prices emerged as another source of imported inflation since 2024, it said. The views are expressed in the articles in the bulletin are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India. India’s domestic growth drivers and overall macroeconomic fundamentals remain useful buffers, the bulletin said in an article on the ‘State of the Economy.’ “The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators”, the article said, adding that strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Additionally, the central bank highlighted that sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion. As of end October, banking credit grew by 19.5 per cent year - on - year (YoY), while deposits have grown by nearly 17 per cent YoY during the same period. RBI also highlighted in the bulletin that India’s equity markets displayed buoyancy amidst robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows. India’s equity markets have seen a sharp rebound as investors went for markets with lower exposure to the artificial intelligence (AI) trade amid mounting valuation concerns. Overseas investors poured nearly $14 billion into Indian equities so far in November, following substantial outflows earlier this year. India’s Nifty index is up over 12 per cent since foreign flows started pouring in. The RBI flagged rising food prices and a broader spread of price pressures across commodities, with headline CPI inflation rising to 6.09 per cent in October from 5.54 per cent in September. October’s inflation print has breached the monetary policy committee’s inflation tolerance band. “Pullback in AI-related stocks and elevated sovereign bond yields, despite some softening from multi-decade highs, remain a source of volatility in financial markets. Amidst uneven economic performance globally, the Indian economy stood out”, the bulletin said. It also highlighted signs of robust domestic demand, with gross goods and services tax (GST) collections in October rising sharply to the second-highest monthly level since the rollout of the tax in July 2017, driven by higher revenues from imports and domestic activity, and reflecting strong retail consumption during the festive season. Toll collections also maintained steady growth, pointing to sustained momentum in transport and logistics activity, it said. The bulletin also noted that balance sheets of listed private non-financial companies remained resilient despite global uncertainties, with aggregate sales growth strengthening in the September quarter of FY27, led by manufacturing firms in the automobile, petroleum and chemical sectors. Sales growth among IT and non-IT services companies remained strong, although it moderated during the quarter, while year-on-year operating profit growth among manufacturing companies accelerated on the back of higher sales. System liquidity normalised in October amidst expansion in currency in circulation. Liquidity surplus rose from end-October with the drawdown in government cash balances before moderating again around mid-November, the bulletin said. headline: 25 IPS, 6 PPS officers shifted in Punjab
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (PTI) In a major reshuffle ahead of the state assembly polls, the Punjab government on Wednesday transferred 25 IPS and six PPS officers with immediate effect. The transfers included changes at important positions in Amritsar, Ludhiana and other districts. Senior IPS officer Satinder Singh has been posted as Ludhiana Police Commissioner, replacing Swapan Sharma who has been given the charge of DIG (Ropar Range), according to an order. Gurpreet Singh Bhullar has been posted as Jalandhar Police Commissioner, replacing Satinder Singh, while Harmanbir Singh has been appointed as DIG (Border Range). Jagadale Nilambari Vijay has been posted as IG (Jalandhar Range), replacing Naveen Singla, who has been given the charge of DIG (Jalandhar Range). Kuldeep Singh has been posted as Amritsar Police Commissioner, while Harjeet Singh has been posted as DIG (Bathinda Range).

headline: HC questions Punjab’s legal authority to divert buses for Moga rally, seeks proof of permits
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Wednesday questioned Punjab Government’s legal authority to divert its buses from their designated routes to transport people to “Moga Maha Rally”. Among other things, the bench observed that no provision had been shown under which buses operating under statutory permits could be requisitioned, utilised or diverted for another purpose.“It will have to be examined whether the authorities have passed any orders consistent with the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, under which such buses could be diverted for any other purpose,” the bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor asserted.The bench added one of the issues also requiring determination was whether the state would be justified in departing from the statutory scheme for plying of road transport services by a State Transport Undertaking “merely because the smart ration cards are to be distributed at a particular rally”.At the same time, the bench made it clear that it was not questioning the welfare initiative itself. “The laudable state action of issuing smart ration cards and ensuring the distribution of food is neither questioned, nor does this court intend to interfere with it in any manner. The question for consideration is whether the diversion of state buses for carrying persons from different districts to Moga is an inseparable part of the distribution of smart ration cards and whether such action has the sanction of law?” the bench observed.It also took note of the commuters’ inconvenience by observing: “The ancillary question would be whether the inconvenience caused to common commuters who travel by these buses would be justified and also whether the state would be justified in requisitioning buses plying on different routes solely to facilitate the transportation of such persons to the venue itself.”In a subsequent order passed later in the evening, the bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor recorded that the state had produced an order dated November 24 issued by the Moga District Magistrate, “vide which, the impugned action has been taken”. As the petitioner sought time to verify the document and respond, the matter was adjourned to November 26 at 10 am.The matter has its genesis in a public interest litigation filed by Arshdeep Singh Sra seeking directions to restrain the state from transporting supporters and workers of the ruling AAP to an event at Matwani village in Moga, on November 26. The petitioner alleged that the programme was a political event and sought directions to ensure that government buses were not diverted from regular public transport services at the cost of ordinary commuters.The petitioner relied on a statement allegedly published on AAP’s official website, which stated that the Moga rally would mark the commencement of the party's 2027 election campaign, besides newspaper reports highlighting the inconvenience that could be caused to commuters.The state, on the other hand, contested the petition, maintaining that the programme was a state-level function for the distribution of smart ration cards to beneficiaries. It produced an office order dated November 12 declaring the Chief Minister’s programme at Moga a state-level function.The state informed the court that nearly six lakh citizens were to receive smart ration cards. It also relied on Section 87 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which empowered transport authorities to grant temporary permits for specified purposes, and referred to Sections 99(2) and 66 of the Act in support of its position.The bench, however, noted that the state was seeking to justify the diversion under Section 87 of the Act, but it had not produced any temporary permit to substantiate its stand. The court observed: “We may note at the outset that, though the state action is sought to be justified with reference to Section 87 of the Act of 1988, no temporary permit has been placed before the court to justify such action.”Examining the structure governing State Transport Undertakings, the bench explained that the statutory framework envisaged publication of a transport scheme, inviting objections and subsequently issuing permits to State Transport Undertakings. The court observed that the statutory scheme indicated that once such permits were issued, the buses were required to operate strictly in accordance with the scheme.“The statutory scheme is, therefore, clearly indicative of the fact that once permits are issued to the State Transport Undertakings, the buses are to be plied strictly in accordance with such scheme. No provision has been shown to the court under which buses issued permits under Section 103 of the Act of 1988 could be requisitioned, utilised or diverted for any other purpose.”

headline: Connecting Amritsar’s 450-year journey with the direction of future development is essential: Governor Gulab Chand Kataria
content: AMRITSAR: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria said that preserving Punjab’s rich historical, religious and cultural heritage while preparing the younger generation to meet future challenges is the need of the hour. Addressing the inaugural session of international conclave ‘Amritsar 450’, organised by Guru Nanak Dev University to commemorate the 450th Foundation Year of Sri Amritsar Sahib, he said that the teachings of the Sikh Gurus had established a great tradition of humanity, equality, service and sacrifice, giving Punjab a distinct identity at the global level. Referring to the tradition of Langar and the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas, he said that the history of Punjab is an inspiring example of courage, conviction and social responsibility. Expressing concern over the growing trend of drug abuse among youth, he called upon the government, educational institutions and society to make collective efforts to address this problem. The two-day international conclave ‘Amritsar 450’ is based on the theme ‘Remembering the Past, Understanding the Present and Envisioning the Future’. Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Karamjeet Singh, special guest S. Taranjit Singh Sandhu and eminent scholar Prof. (Dr.) Gurinder Singh Mann, along with other distinguished personalities, participated in the conclave. Dean Academic Affairs Prof. Harvinder Singh Saini proposed the vote of thanks, while Director, Sikh Studies Chair, Prof. Amarjit Singh elaborated on the conclave. Registrar Prof. K.S. Chahal was also present on the occasion. On this occasion, Punjab Governor Shri Gulab Chand Kataria released a book on Sikhism authored by Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Karamjeet Singh in Punjabi, Hindi and English. The Vice-Chancellor also honoured the distinguished guests with mementoes. A panel discussion was organised at the Convention Centre, in which Dr. Avtar Singh, Prof. R.S. Ghuman, Bibi (Dr.) Inderjit Kaur, S. Jagjit Singh Dardi, S. Gunbir Singh and Mrs. Himani Arora participated. The discussion was moderated by Dr. Nirmal Singh Joura. A meeting of college principals was also held, attended by Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Karamjeet Singh, Prof. S.S. Behl, Prof. Saroj Bala and Prof. Vasudha Sambyal. Besides, a discussion on ‘The Spiritual and Sacred Heritage of Amritsar’ was organised, in which Dr. Rajwant Singh, S. Amarjit Singh Grewal, Dr. Inderjit Singh Gogoani, Prof. S.S. Sohal, Dr. Sulakhan Singh and Dr. Gurmeet Singh Sidhu shared their views. The day's programmes concluded with the light and sound show ‘Dastaan-e-Amritsar’ at Dashmesh Auditorium. In his address, Shri Kataria said that Punjab needs to undertake new initiatives in education, research, agriculture and industrial development in accordance with future requirements. He emphasised the need to promote agricultural diversification, food processing, water conservation, alternative energy sources, environmental protection and technological innovation. He said that India's achievements in medical science, space research, defence technology and vaccine manufacturing are opening up new opportunities for the youth. He added that the 450th Foundation Year of Sri Amritsar Sahib is not merely an occasion to remember the past, but also a valuable opportunity to understand present challenges and develop a clear and forward-looking vision for the future of Punjab and Amritsar. In his welcome address, Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Karamjeet Singh said that the 450th anniversary of Sri Amritsar Sahib is not merely an occasion to remember the past, but also an important opportunity to prepare a roadmap for a better future of the city for coming generations. He said that Guru Nanak Dev University has initiated three major initiatives in this direction. These include preparing a vision document for the development of Amritsar over the next 25 years, creating a digital repository of oral history through 450 videos to preserve the city's heritage and the memories of its elderly residents, and connecting education with skills and employment. Taranjit Singh Sandhu, in his address, shared his views on the 450-year historical journey and the spiritual and cultural heritage of Sri Amritsar Sahib. He said that founded by Sri Guru Ramdas Ji in 1577, the city has remained an important centre of spirituality, education and culture for centuries. He emphasised the need to preserve heritage buildings, old neighbourhoods and cultural traditions, improve urban infrastructure and connect tourism potential with economic development for the city's future growth. Prof. (Dr.) Gurinder Singh Mann, while speaking on historiography, observed that imitating Western approaches and methodologies has not benefited the understanding of Sikh history to a great extent, as the West itself changes by the time its approaches are adopted. He emphasised the need to develop an original approach to Sikh historiography based on Gurbani, Sikh philosophy and historical sources.

headline: AAP to launch Punjab poll campaign on Nov 26, present Mann govt's 5-year report card
content: The AAP will present a five-year report card of the Bhagwant Mann-led Punjab government and formally launch its campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections at its Punjab Kushhaal Rally in Moga on November 26, news agency PTI reported.AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, the entire Punjab Cabinet and senior party leaders will attend the rally, which will also mark the party's 15th foundation day.AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu said the rally would be held on the Moga-Ludhiana Road. Extensive arrangements had been made to ensure that people arriving from different parts of Punjab did not face any inconvenience, he added.Pannu appealed to people across the state to attend the rally in large numbers and join the Foundation Day celebrations. He said fulfilling promises made to the people had remained the government's priority since it took office in 2022.“We introduced 600 units of free electricity per billing cycle for every household in July 2022. Today, nearly 90 per cent of households in Punjab are receiving zero electricity bills. This reflects our commitment to providing direct relief to ordinary families,” Pannu said, according to PTI.He said the AAP government had prioritised employment from its first Cabinet meeting and had provided more than 78,000 government jobs to young people on merit, without recommendations, favouritism or bribery.Describing the revival of canal irrigation as one of the government's most significant achievements, Pannu said, “When AAP came to power, only 22-23 per cent of canal water was reaching agricultural fields.”“Through sustained efforts, this figure has now increased to nearly 88 per cent. We began working on this from our very first day because Punjab's groundwater depletion was a matter of serious concern,” he said.In a statement cited by PTI, Pannu said the improved use of canal water had strengthened water management during the flood season and helped Punjab avoid major flood-related difficulties this time. Better availability of canal water had also improved crop yields during the paddy season, providing relief to farmers, he added.Highlighting the work of the Sadak Surakhya Force, Pannu said Punjab was the only state to have created such a specialised road safety force. Citing parliamentary data, he said deaths at accident sites in Punjab had fallen by 48 per cent.“The Sadak Surakhya Force is not only saving precious lives but also safeguarding valuables worth crores of rupees belonging to accident victims, which could otherwise have been lost or stolen,” he said.Pannu also said the Mann government had strengthened public hospitals and established Mohalla Clinics across Punjab, improving access to healthcare and providing relief to ordinary people.- EndsMust Watch

headline: Govt clears six brownfield urea projects worth ₹54,000 crore to boost domestic production
content: New Delhi: The Centre has approved six brownfield urea manufacturing projects involving an estimated investment of ₹54,000 crore under the National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026 as it looks to expand domestic production capacity, reduce import dependence and strengthen fertiliser security.The projects, spread across Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Rajasthan, will add a combined annual production capacity of 7.62 million tonnes, with each plant designed to produce 1.27 million tonnes annually.The proposed investments involve public sector undertakings, cooperative institutions and private companies. The six projects include Madras Fertilizers Ltd's (MFL) unit in Chennai, National Fertilizers Ltd's (NFL) Nangal plant in Punjab, KRIBHCO's Shahjahanpur project in Uttar Pradesh, Matix Fertilizers' Panagarh unit in West Bengal, Chambal Fertilizers' Gadepan complex in Rajasthan and Indian Potash Ltd's (IIPL) proposed unit at Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh.With each brownfield project estimated at a capital cost norm of around ₹9,000 crore, the 6 urea plants are poised to attract nearly ₹54,000 crore in fresh investment, advancing India toward self-reliance (Atmanirbharta) in urea production while generating employment.Policy incentives, import gapTo strengthen investor confidence and project bankability, the NIPU-2026 framework pairs a balanced 12–16% Return on Equity (RoE) band—anchored by a 12% floor and a 16% ceiling—with a foreign exchange rate mitigation mechanism that normalizes exchange rates and converts into INR after four years based on prevailing rates. Coupled with brownfield advantages that deliver an estimated ₹225 crore in annual savings—or roughly ₹1,800 crore over eight years—these provisions enhance financial viability and drive sustained capital inflows into domestic fertilizer manufacturing.The policy also seeks to encourage investment by allowing companies to leverage existing land, utilities, logistics infrastructure and technical manpower at operating fertilizer complexes. This is expected to lower project costs and accelerate execution compared with setting up entirely new facilities.India consumes around 40 million tonnes of urea annually, while domestic production stood at 29.33 million tonnes in 2025-26. Production had increased from 22.5 million tonnes in 2014-15 to a record 31.40 million tonnes in 2023-24. With fresh capacity additions and expansion plans measured against an annual consumption of around 40 million tonnes, reliance on imported urea is set to decrease substantially, saving foreign exchange and strengthening domestic availability.Two of the proposed projects will replace ageing manufacturing facilities. MFL's Chennai unit, which is more than 60 years old, and NFL's Nangal plant, around 50-55 years old, face higher production costs and energy consumption, apart from operational and safety concerns. The modernization of these units is expected to improve energy efficiency and operational reliability.Building on NIP 2012The latest initiative builds on the New Investment Policy (NIP) 2012, which facilitated the commissioning of six urea plants with a combined capacity of 7.62 million tonnes annually. These comprises four units through joint venture companies of nominated PSUs (Ramagundam unit of RFCL in Telangana; and Gorakhpur, Sindri, and Barauni units of HURL in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar, respectively) and two by private companies (Panagarh unit of Matix Fertilizers in West Bengal and Gadepan-III unit of Chambal Fertilizers in Rajasthan).Each unit has an annual production capacity of 1.27 million tonnes, adding 7.62 million tonnes in total. Two more 1.27-million-tonne projects are under execution: the coal-gasification-based Talcher Fertilizer Project (TFL) in Odisha, expected to be completed by December 2027, and Assam Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Company Ltd (AVFCCL) at Namrup, Assam, announced on 19 March 2025.

headline: AAP defends use of govt buses for Punjab maha rally, calls it state function
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Wednesday adjourned a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) challenging the use of government buses to ferry supporters to the Aam Aadmi Party's (AAP) rally in Punjab's Moga, with the matter scheduled to be heard on November 26 at 10 am.The petition seeks to stop government buses from being used to transport supporters to the party's Khushhaal Punjab maha rally at Matwani village in Moga and has sought details of the buses deployed, along with the statutory approvals and financial sanctions for their use.The order was passed by a bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor. During the hearing, Punjab's counsel produced an order issued by the Moga District Magistrate on November 24, 2026, permitting the diversion of buses. The bench noted that the order had not been placed before it during the first hearing.Petitioner Arshdeep Singh Sra sought time to verify the order and respond to it, following which the court adjourned the matter to Thursday morning. The petition has been filed against the Punjab Chief Secretary, the Transport Department and the Managing Director of PRTC.AAP RALLY OR STATE-LEVEL FUNCTION?The controversy centres on the nature of the event, with the petitioner relying on AAP's website announcement describing the maha rally as the launch of the party's 2027 Punjab Assembly election campaign. The petition also cited reports of commuter hardship due to the alleged deployment of government buses for the event.Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for Punjab through video conferencing, argued that the event was a state function for the distribution of smart ration cards to nearly six lakh citizens, rather than a political rally.A government order issued on November 12, 2026, by the General Administration Department's Protocol Branch declared the event a State-Level Function. It designated the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department as the nodal department and said it would bear the expenses.The state also cited Section 87 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arguing that it empowers authorities to issue temporary permits for such purposes. It maintained that the legal questions raised need not be examined unless the petitioner amends the plea to include them. The state further argued that the distribution of smart ration cards itself had not been challenged.AAP'S MAHA RALLY MARKS CAMPAIGN LAUNCHAAP is holding its Khushhaal Punjab maha rally in Moga on Thursday, November 26, to mark the party's Foundation Day and formally launch its campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann are scheduled to address the gathering, alongside senior state leaders and 71 declared candidates.The rally has triggered a political row over the alleged use of public transport for a party event, with opposition leaders accusing the ruling party of putting taxpayers' money to political use and potentially inconveniencing commuters.OPPOSITION SLAMS BUS DEPLOYMENT, AAP REJECTS CHARGESLeader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa called the controversy unfortunate, alleging that while the rally belonged to AAP, its expenses would be borne by the state government using taxpayers' money.AAP general secretary Baltej Pannu rejected the opposition's allegations, calling them a "pack of lies" and accusing the opposition of targeting the party without having anything better to do.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh had earlier alleged that more than 2,500 buses belonging to PRTC and Punjab Roadways were being deployed for the rally. He claimed the move would leave commuters short of buses and amount to misuse of public funds.KEJRIWAL, MANN MEET SANJEEV ARORA'S FAMILYMeanwhile, AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann visited Sanjeev Arora's residence in Ludhiana, where they met his family and team.The two leaders are also scheduled to hold an important meeting with Arora's family and team to discuss election strategy.- EndsMust Watch

headline: Punjab polls: SAD-BJP reunion pushes Congress towards Left parties for alliance talks
content: NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh on Wednesday said the party is in talks with CPI and CPM for an alliance ahead of the 2027 assembly elections in the state."Comrades are part of the INDIA bloc," Singh told reporters in Chandigarh.Asked about seat-sharing arrangements, Singh said Congress had formed a team to hold discussions with the two parties.Meanwhile, leader of opposition in the Punjab assembly Pratap Singh Bajwa said that all parties were exploring possibilities of alliances."Leaders of INDIA bloc members - CPI, CPM and other parties - are sitting in Delhi. The thing is that we should be seen together. Seats can be given only where they have a presence," Bajwa said in response to another question.The Congress leaders' remarks come a day after Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and BJP announced an alliance for the upcoming assembly elections, marking a reunion after six years.Announcing the alliance, Union home minister Amit Shah said the chief minister's post would go to SAD, which would be the "big brother" in the alliance.Taking aim at the SAD-BJP reunion, Singh compared the two parties to the East India Company and alleged that they were conspiring to take control of Punjab's resources and rights.He also took a dig at SAD leader Sukhbir Singh Badal, asking whether the Akali leader, who had earlier questioned the DNA of those joining BJP, would now agree to undergo a DNA test himself.Singh claimed that both parties had already been reduced to single-digit political strength and alleged that their position would weaken further in the 2027 assembly elections.He expressed confidence that the people of Punjab would reject these "self-serving" political forces.Singh said Congress would remain united in raising its voice for Punjab's rights and the interests of farmers, labourers, youth and ordinary citizens.He also asserted that Congress would form the next government in Punjab with a full majority in the 2027 assembly elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Mann, Kejriwal visit jailed minister Sanjeev Arora’s family in Ludhiana ahead of Moga rally
content: Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal visited the family of jailed AAP minister Sanjeev Arora at their residence in Ludhiana on Wednesday evening.Arora has been declared the AAP candidate for the Ludhiana West constituency. A family member said the two leaders had come to support the family while the minister remains in jail.“The leaders motivated the entire family to work hard in Arora’s absence and assured us of full support. We are thankful to both leaders for keeping our spirits high,” said Sandhya Arora, his wife.The leaders spent about 15 minutes with the family.Mann and Kejriwal will stay overnight in Ludhiana before leaving for AAP’s “Khushhal rally” in Moga on Thursday. The district administration and police are on their toes for the rally.A well-placed source in the administration said Thursday’s rally will be the formal kickstart of AAP’s election campaign in Punjab.“We cannot take it lightly. Chief Secretary KAP Sinha and DGP Gaurav Yadav visited Moga on November 23 to review the arrangements. Village Aitiana near the Halwara airport will serve as the helipad for the Chief Minister’s chopper,” the source said.Mann received Kejriwal and other VIPs at the Halwara airport after Kejriwal arrived on the evening Air India flight from Delhi. The VVIPs then reached Ludhiana.Heavy police deployment was seen at the Halwara airport since morning, and by evening, security was also tightened near Hyatt on Ferozepur Road, where the CM is staying.

headline: Ahead of Punjab polls, Cong keeps options open for alliance with Left parties
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (PTI) With SAD and the BJP re-stitching alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Wednesday said his party is in talks with two Left parties, the CPI and the CPI-M, for an electoral tie-up in the state. Leader of Opposition in Punjab Assembly, Partap Singh Bajwa, also indicated that the proposed tie-up with the Left parties has support in the state Congress leadership. “All of us have a thinking that the CPI, CPM and other Communist parties be taken together,” he said. Asked if the Congress will enter into an alliance for the upcoming assembly polls, Punjab Congress chief Singh said his party is in talks with the CPI and CPI-M. “Comrades are part of the INDIA bloc,” he told reporters here. Asked about the seat allocation, Singh said the Congress has formed a team which is in discussion with them.

headline: Tankeshwar Kumar assumes charge as Panjab University Vice-Chancellor
content: Prof Tankeshwar Kumar on Wednesday assumed charge as the Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University (PU), succeeding Prof Meenakshi Goyal, Dean of University Instruction, who was holding the additional charge.The charge was formally handed over in the presence of University Registrar Prof YP Verma, Director of the Research and Development Cell Prof Savita Gupta, Controller of Examinations Prof Jagat Bhushan, Secretary to the Vice-Chancellor Prof Krishan Kumar, Dean Students Welfare Prof YK Rawal, Dean, College Development Council, Prof Ravi Inder Singh and other senior university officials. Former Vice-Chancellor Prof KN Pathak and several faculty members were also present.Prof Kumar brings with him over three decades of experience in teaching and research, along with around 11 years of experience as Vice-Chancellor at various universities. He previously served as Vice-Chancellor of Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology (GJUST), Hisar, and the Central University of Haryana.A PU alumnus, Prof Kumar has a long association with the university, having served in its Department of Physics for over two decades. During his tenure, he was a UGC Professor of Physics under the Faculty Recharge Programme and headed the Abdul Kalam Computer Centre from 2005 to 2014. He was also a member of the university’s Senate and Syndicate.He played a key role in strengthening the university’s IT infrastructure, including campus networking, Wi-Fi connectivity and the introduction of online admission and entrance examination systems.Prof Kumar completed his postgraduate and doctoral studies in Physics at PU. He undertook postdoctoral research in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), Trieste, Italy, in 1991. He subsequently served as an Associate of ICTP from 1997 to 2004 and worked as a Research Leader at the centre.A specialist in theoretical and computational condensed matter physics, his research interests include nanoscience and nanotechnology, liquid-state dynamics, computer simulations, modelling and electron correlations. He has published extensively in national and international research journals.His recognitions include the Vice-Chancellor of the Year Award, Shiksha Ratna Award 2022, Elite Academician Award and International Higher Education Excellence Award, among others.In November 2026, he received the Legendary Teachers’ Award at the Padma Vibhushan Dr Murli Manohar Joshi Awards. He is also a member of the National Academy of Sciences, India, and was the first UGC Professor in the country under the Faculty Recharge Programme.

headline: Major Reshuffle in Punjab Police: 31 Officers Transferred, Three Major Cities Get New Commissioners
content: Chandigarh, November 25: In a major reshuffle ahead of the Assembly elections, the Punjab Government on Wednesday ordered the transfer of 31 police officers, including several IPS officers. Ludhiana: Commissioner of Police Swapan Sharma has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range. He will be replaced by Jalandhar CP Satinder Singh, who will now take charge as the new Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana. Jalandhar: IGP, Border Range, Gurpreet Bhullar has been appointed as the new Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar. Amritsar: DIG, Technical Services, Kuldeep Singh has been appointed as the new Commissioner of Police, Amritsar. Outgoing CP Harmanbir Singh has been posted as DIG, Border Range. Changes have also been made at the Range level. ANTF chief Nilambari Vijay Jagadale has been appointed as IGP, Jalandhar Range. Naveen Singla has been given the additional charge of Director, Vigilance Bureau, along with DIG, Faridkot Range. – Harkamalpreet Khakh (SSP Malerkotla) -> SSP Jalandhar Rural

headline: ED raids Punjab SAD leader's premises in money laundering case
content: Chandigarh The Enforcement Directorate on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) searched the premises of a Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader based in Punjab's Mohali as part of a money laundering investigation, officials said. Also Read | NDA-SAD reunion: Why the Akali Dal severed ties with BJP 6 years ago https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/nda-sad-reunion-why-did-akali-dal-broke-alliance-with-bjp-6-years-ago/article71741205.ece The politician, Ravinder Singh Khera, is SAD's constituency in-charge for the Mohali-Kharar Assembly seat. Recent news reports suggest that he is a contender for the party ticket for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning Had they contested separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals; united, they have become serious contenders Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning storyline 1 The Enforcement Directorate's action comes a day after the SAD and BJP announced a pre-poll alliance for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year. Mr. Khera did not immediately comment on the ED raids. Officials said action was taken against Mr. Khera, a rice miller and proprietor of Guru Kripa Rice and Agro Industries in Kharar village of SAS Nagar, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The raids against the SAD leader stem from a January 2023 FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation on charges of criminal conspiracy with officials of the Food Corporation of India to obtain undue favours for procurement, storage and quality inspection of foodgrains, they said. The CBI later charge-sheeted Mr. Khera and other accused individuals.

headline: Railway officials avert major accident after cement pillars found on track in Fatehgarh Sahib
content: Timely detection by a railway crew helped avert a major train accident here after unidentified miscreants placed heavy cement pillars on a railway track, officials said on Wednesday.The incident occurred around 12.15 am when a train travelling from Delhi to Jammu was passing near the Sirhind railway station, they said.The train’s guard noticed heavy cement pillars lying on an adjacent railway track and immediately informed the Sirhind station superintendent.Responding to the alert, teams from Government Railway Police (GRP) and Railway Protection Force (RPF) rushed to the spot, accompanied by a large police contingent and railway staff, the officials said.The teams removed the cement pillars from the track, ensuring safe movement of trains passing through the route, they said.Senior GRP officials visited the spot on Wednesday, accompanied by technical officials from the Railways, and conducted a detailed inspection of the track.

headline: From 'Sikhya Kranti' to School Crisis: Dewan Slams AAP Over Education Failures
content: Ludhiana, November 25, 2026: Former District Congress Committee, Ludhiana (Urban) president and former Chairman of Punjab Large Industrial Development Board Pawan Dewan has said the AAP government's much-publicised claims of an educational transformation stand exposed by the grim reality prevailing in Ludhiana's government schools. In a statement issued here today, Dewan said behind the glossy advertisements, ribbon-cutting ceremonies and carefully curated photo opportunities lies a deepening crisis of neglect. “Schools are struggling without principals, classrooms are grappling with an alarming shortage of teachers and flagship projects touted as game changers continue to languish in delays,” he rued. Dewan said that according to several media reports, nearly half of Ludhiana’s government schools continue to function without regular principals, exposing the widening gap between the Punjab government’s tall claims and the ground reality in public education. “Despite repeated announcements and flagship initiatives such as Sikhya Kranti, the leadership crisis in schools remains unresolved, which raises serious questions about the government’s priorities,” he argued. Dewan also said that more than two years after the launch of the much-publicised ‘Schools of Happiness’ initiative, the project's progress in Ludhiana paints a disappointing picture. “Conceived to transform government primary schools into vibrant and child-friendly learning centres with modern infrastructure, the scheme has largely remained confined to promises. Of the 35 schools identified under the project in Ludhiana district, just a school have been completed so far, while the remaining continue to be at different stages of execution, with staggered release of funds slowing the pace of work,” he added. Dewan said that at a time when the government is projecting an education revolution, the reality is that hundreds of teaching posts remain vacant in the district. “With hundreds of master cadre positions lying unfilled, serious concerns persist over how quality education can be ensured when schools continue to face an acute shortage of teaching staff,” he said. Asserting that what is unfolding in Ludhiana is a classic case of optics triumphing over outcomes, Dewan said, “Grand buildings and ambitious slogans cannot substitute for qualified teachers, accountable principals and a functional academic ecosystem. While the government remains busy celebrating milestones on paper, thousands of students are paying the price for administrative apathy and misplaced priorities.” He further said that education cannot be transformed through publicity campaigns; it requires sustained investment in human resources, effective governance and genuine commitment to learning. headline: Punjab hikes sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal, highest in country
content: In a major bonanza for sugarcane cultivators, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday announced an increase in the sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, making it the highest in the country.Chairing a high-level meeting here, the Chief Minister said the decision reflected the state government’s unwavering commitment to the welfare and economic prosperity of the farming community.Taking to X, Mann said, “Big news for sugarcane farmers in Punjab. Our government has increased the sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, the highest in the entire country. To ensure convenience for farmers, sugar mills across the state will commence operations from November 25, 2026. Our government remains firmly committed to the prosperity of our food providers and ensuring that farmers receive the rightful price for their crops.”Addressing the meeting, Mann said, “This is a major initiative for the hardworking sugarcane farmers of Punjab. Our government has increased the sugarcane price to Rs 431 per quintal for the 2026-27 season, which is the highest in the country. This increase will provide much-needed financial relief to thousands of sugarcane cultivators across the state.”The Chief Minister said farmers worked tirelessly day and night to feed the nation and strengthen its economy, adding that it was the government’s responsibility to ensure that their hard work received its rightful value.“Farmers are the backbone of our economy, and their prosperity is essential for the overall progress and economic well-being of Punjab. Our government is fully committed to safeguarding their interests, strengthening their financial position and ensuring that they receive remunerative prices for their produce,” he added.Mann further said the commencement of operations at sugar mills from November 25 would facilitate the timely and convenient supply of sugarcane by farmers.“Our government is consistently taking farmer-friendly decisions to strengthen the rural economy and secure a dignified and prosperous future for the farming community,” he said.Reiterating his government’s commitment to the farming sector, the Chief Minister said providing remunerative prices for agricultural produce and extending every possible support to farmers remained among the foremost priorities of the Punjab Government.ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਗੰਨਾ ਕਾਸ਼ਤਕਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਵੱਡੀ ਖੁਸ਼ਖਬਰੀ.. ਸਾਡੀ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਨੇ ਸਾਲ 2026-27 ਲਈ ਗੰਨੇ ਦਾ ਰੇਟ ਵਧਾ ਕੇ ₹431 ਪ੍ਰਤੀ ਕੁਇੰਟਲ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਕਿ ਪੂਰੇ ਦੇਸ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਹੈ..ਕਿਸਾਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਲਈ ਸੂਬੇ ਦੀਆਂ ਖੰਡ ਮਿੱਲਾਂ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ, 2026 ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋ ਜਾਣਗੀਆਂ.. ਸਾਡੀ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਅੰਨਦਾਤੇ ਦੀ ਖੁਸ਼ਹਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਸਲਾਂ ਦਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ ਦੇਣ ਲਈ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਵਚਨਬੱਧ ਹੈ..ਇਨਕਲਾਬ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਾਬਾਦ!— Bhagwant Mann (@BhagwantMann) November 25, 2026

headline: Punjab: AAP to present five-year report card at Moga rally
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (IANS) The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)’s 15th foundation day celebrations and the Punjab Kushhaal Rally on November 26 in Moga would mark a new chapter in the state’s politics, with the party presenting its five-year report card before the people ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, said media in-charge Baltej Pannu. He said party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, the entire Cabinet and senior party leadership will be present at the rally. “This mega gathering will mark the beginning of our campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections, and people from across Punjab are expected to participate in large numbers,” he told the media here. He said fulfilling the promises made to the people had remained the government’s priority since it assumed office in 2022. “We introduced 600 units of free electricity per bill cycle for every household in July 2022. Today, nearly 90 per cent of households in Punjab are receiving zero electricity bills. This reflects our commitment to providing direct relief to ordinary families,” he said. Highlighting the government’s employment initiatives, Pannu said CM Mann prioritised employment from the very first Cabinet meeting.

headline: AAP to launch 2027 poll campaign at Moga rally on 26, present five-year report card : Baltej Pannu
content: Kejriwal, Mann and senior party leadership to attend Punjab Kushhaal Rally; AAP highlights 78,000 government jobs, free electricity and development initiatives Ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) 15th Foundation Day celebrations and the Punjab Kushhaal Rally scheduled for November 26 in Moga, AAP Punjab Media In-charge Baltej Pannu on Wednesday said the mega event would mark the formal launch of the party’s campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Addressing a press conference, Pannu said AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, the entire Punjab Cabinet and senior party leaders would attend the rally. He added that the party would present its five-year report card to the people, highlighting the achievements of the Mann-led government since it came to power in 2022. Highlighting the government's achievements, Pannu said providing 600 units of free electricity per billing cycle to every household was among its key initiatives. He claimed that nearly 90 per cent of households in Punjab were now receiving zero electricity bills. On employment, he said the government had provided more than 78,000 government jobs to youth purely on merit, without recommendations, favouritism or bribery. Pannu also highlighted the revival of canal irrigation, stating that the availability of canal water for agricultural fields had increased from 22-23 per cent when AAP assumed power to nearly 88 per cent. He said the initiative had helped address groundwater depletion, improve water management during the flood season and support better crop yields during the paddy season.

headline: Punjab declares Nov 28 public holiday in Patiala, Bagha Purana and Dharamkot for Municipal Polls
content: Chandigarh, November 25, 2026: The Punjab Government has declared November 28 (Saturday) a public holiday in the areas under the Municipal Corporation, Patiala, and Municipal Councils of Bagha Purana and Dharamkot, where municipal general and bye-elections will be held. The elections will cover 30 wards in Patiala, 15 wards in Bagha Purana and seven wards in Dharamkot. The holiday will also apply under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The government has also allowed eligible voters employed in Punjab government offices, boards, corporations and educational institutions to avail themselves of special leave to cast their votes. Employees will have to present their voter cards to the competent authority to avail of the leave, which will not be deducted from their regular leave account.

headline: Punjab government transfers 31 police officers ahead of 2027 Assembly elections
content: AHMEDABAD: Ahead of the 2027 assembly election, the AAP-led Punjab Government ordered the transfer of 31 police officers, including several IPS officers, with immediate effect. The Additional DGP of Punjab Armed Police (PAP) has been changed; police commissioners of Amritsar, Ludhiana and Jalandhar have been shifted, and many IGPs, all DIGs (Ranges) and nine SSPs have also been transferred. As per the orders issued by the state home department, Naunihal Singh will continue as Additional DGP of Internal Vigilance Cell. He has also been given additional charge as ADGP of Punjab Armed Police at Jalandhar. The reshuffle has brought significant changes in the police set-up in key districts and ranges. While Gurpreet Singh Bhullar is the new Police Commissioner of Jalandhar, Nilambari Vijay Jagadale has been posted as IGP of Jalandhar Range; Naveen Singla is DIG of Faridkot Range; Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range; while Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh will replace him as Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana. While Kuldeep Singh, DIG, Patiala Range, goes as Amritsar Police Commissioner, Harmanbir Singh Gill, who was Amritsar Police Commissioner, has been posted as DIG, Border Range. Nanak Singh has been transferred as DIG (Technical Services), Gurmeet Singh Chauhan as DIG (Provisioning), Snehdeep Sharma as DIG, Ferozepur Range, and Amneet Kondal will take over as DIG, Patiala Range.Vivek Sheel Soni has been appointed AIG, Internal Vigilance Cell. At the district level, Surendra Lamba will be SSP Sangrur, Charanjit Singh SSP of Ludhiana (Rural), Rajvot Grewal has been posted as SSP Vigilance Bureau, Punjab, SAS Nagar, Ankur Gupta is new SSP of Faridkot, Ashwini Gotyal is posted as SSP of Ferozepur, Vatsala Gupta is SSP of SBS Nagar, Dr Pragya Jain as new SSP of Amritsar (Rural), Tushar Gupta as SSP of Gurdaspur, Ajay Gandhi SSP of Taran Taran and Harkamal Singh as SSP of Malerkotla.
