headline: Sukhbir Badal promises textile hub in Talwandi Sabo-Bhucho Belt, food park for Bathinda
content: Bathinda (Punjab), November 25, 2026: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal has promised to develop the Talwandi Sabo-Bhucho Mandi belt as a textile and spinning hub and establish a food park in Bathinda if the SAD-BJP alliance forms the next government in Punjab. During meetings with traders and representatives of industry in Bathinda, Bhucho Mandi and Talwandi Sabo, Badal also announced a proposed industrial incentive package, including electricity at Rs 5 per unit for businesses and permission for new industrial units to retain 50 per cent of the State GST collected from them. He said industrial parks would also be developed in the region, taking advantage of its connectivity with the Jamnagar highway. The proposed food park in Bathinda, he added, would be made tax-free for entrepreneurs. Addressing concerns raised by property dealers, Badal said a future SAD-BJP government would remove the requirement of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for property transactions and introduce a faceless registry system. He also promised to regularise all irregular colonies on an “as is where is” basis. Under the proposed system, property registration and transfer of ownership (inteqal) would be completed simultaneously, without requiring buyers to deal directly with Tehsildars, he said. The announcements followed demands raised by representatives of the Property Dealers Association, including Ravi Kumar, who highlighted difficulties faced by people during property transactions.

headline: Centre approves new 12.7 lakh MT urea plant at NFL Nangal
content: The Centre has approved the proposal of National Fertilizers Limited (NFL) to set up a new urea manufacturing plant with an annual installed capacity of 12.7 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) at its Nangal unit in Punjab. This will increase the production capacity of the Nangal-based NFL unit from the existing 4.8 LMT to 12.7 LMT.The approval has been conveyed by the Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, through an official communication dated November 25, addressed to the Chairman and Managing Director of NFL. The proposal has been approved under the National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026, which was notified by the Central Government on July 30, 2026, as part of its initiative to promote Atmanirbhar Bharat in the fertiliser sector.The letter was released to the media here today by BJP state vice-president Subhash Sharma. He claimed that the expansion would create around 3,000 new jobs in the Nangal area and help address the shortage of urea in Punjab. The approval comes in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly elections in the state, with Sharma reportedly seeking to contest from the Anandpur Sahib Assembly constituency.The approval, however, comes with a significant condition: the proposed new manufacturing facility will replace the existing old urea manufacturing plant at Nangal. The project has been cleared under the brownfield category, indicating the modernisation and replacement of existing industrial infrastructure rather than the establishment of an entirely new facility at a separate location.The communication, issued by Amar Kushwaha, Director (UPP), Department of Fertilisers, states that the proposal was examined under the provisions of the new investment policy and subsequently approved with the consent of the Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers.The decision is being viewed as an important development for Nangal, which has been home to one of India's oldest fertiliser manufacturing facilities. Established in the post-independence period in the Bhakra-Nangal region, the NFL unit has played a significant role in meeting the fertiliser requirements of farmers in Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.Over the years, the ageing infrastructure of the plant and the need to improve energy efficiency and production capacity have brought its modernisation into focus. The proposed replacement is expected to equip the Nangal complex with modern manufacturing technology and strengthen its contribution to the country's domestic urea production.The approval also marks a significant step forward in addressing the long-pending demand for the expansion and modernisation of the NFL Nangal unit. The issue had been raised at various levels, with political representatives from Punjab and neighbouring Himachal Pradesh highlighting the importance of the project for industrial development and employment generation in the region.Earlier, BJP leaders from Punjab and Himachal Pradesh, led by Subhash Sharma, had taken up the matter with Union leaders, including Union Minister JP Nadda.For the Nangal region, the approval has raised hopes of a fresh phase of industrial development after years of demands for the modernisation of the ageing fertiliser complex.However, the approval communication does not specify the actual implementation timeline, project investment or expected commencement of construction. Nevertheless, the Centre's decision marks a major breakthrough for the proposed modernisation of the NFL Nangal unit and has raised expectations of a renewed industrial push in Punjab's border region.

headline: Akal Takht panel invites Punjab govt committee for Nov 30 meeting over Guru Granth Sahib Act
content: AMRITSAR: The expert committee constituted by Akal Takht with regard to ‘The Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026’, passed by the Punjab government, has invited the Punjab government’s coordination committee for discussions at Sri Anandpur Sahib on November 30, informed a release issued by Akal Takht secretariat here on Wednesday.Expert committee coordinator Lakhvir Singh said on Wednesdat that he has written to the nodal officer of the government’s coordination committee.“The expert committee has asked the Punjab government’s coordination committee not to mislead the Sikh Sangat regarding the directives of Akal Takht Sahib”, he alleged.The meeting of the expert committee was attended by justice (retd) Rupinder Singh Sodhi, justice (retd) Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, Dr Kehar Singh, Prof Jagmohan Singh and coordinator Lakhvir Singh.The letter stated that the press conference held following the November 23 meeting of the Punjab government’s coordination committee in Amritsar, along with the statements issued thereafter, were discussed seriously at the expert committee’s meeting.The committee expressed grave concern over misleading statements made during the press conference by two individuals who were not even members of the government-constituted committee, as well as the disregard shown towards objections outlined in the letters sent by the expert committee.In the interest of Panthic unity and to prevent the general public from being misled on the issue, the expert committee has invited the Punjab government’s coordination committee to attend a meeting at 11am at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, Anandpur Sahib, for deliberations on the matter in the light of Akal Takht directives, said he.The headline: Punjab: ED raids SAD leader’s premises in money laundering case
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (PTI) The Enforcement Directorate on Wednesday searched the premises of a Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader based in Punjab’s Mohali as part of a money laundering investigation, officials said. The politician, Ravinder Singh Khera, is SAD’s constituency in-charge for the Mohali-Kharar Assembly seat. Recent news reports suggest that he is a contender for the party ticket for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The Enforcement Directorate’s action comes a day after the SAD and BJP announced a pre-poll alliance for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year. Officials said action was taken against Khera, a rice miller and proprietor of Guru Kripa Rice and Agro Industries in Kharar village of SAS Nagar, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The raids against the SAD leader stem from a January 2023 FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation on charges of criminal conspiracy with officials of the Food Corporation of India to obtain undue favours for procurement, storage and quality inspection of foodgrains, they said. The CBI later charge-sheeted Khera and other accused individuals. PTI NES RUK

headline: ‘Balwant Rajoana does not believe in Constitution, courts’, Centre tells SC in Beant Singh assassination case
content: The Centre on Wednesday opposed in the Supreme Court a plea filed by Balwant Rajoana seeking commutation of his death sentence to a life term in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, saying he does not have faith in the Constitution or the courts.Rajoana, who has been incarcerated for around 30 years, including on death row for over 15 years, has sought commutation of his death sentence to a life term due to the delay in deciding his mercy petition.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh reserved its decision on the plea of Rajoana and asked the parties to file their written submissions within three weeks.Appearing for the Centre, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) KM Nataraj opposed the plea saying Rajoana has stated that he does not believe in the Constitution and does not have faith in the courts, and his statements are recorded in the trial court judgment.He submitted that Rajoana never filed any appeal against his death sentence awarded by the trial court before the high court and never filed any mercy petition or reference against the capital punishment.The ASG also relied on the 2025 Constitution bench opinion in the presidential reference concerning the powers of governors and the president over state bills and argued that the relief could not be granted by invoking Article 142, as Article 142 cannot substitute the constitutional powers of remission under Articles 72 and 161.Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Rajoana, said that the man, who was "misguided" at some point of time due to the prevailing circumstances then in Punjab, has spent around 30 years in jail and cannot be allowed to continue under the sword of death sentence.He said that his death sentence be commuted to life term and benefit of remission be granted to him.Rohatgi accepted that Rajoana has never filed any mercy petition nor has he filed any appeal against the death sentence before the high court but the co-accused in the case have been granted bail by the top court. Another accused, Jagtar Hawara, who was awarded death sentence, had his sentence commuted to life by the high court, he added."Yes, he has not filed any representation nor has he filed any mercy petition. He has also not filed any appeal against the death sentence."A mercy plea was filed by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) on behalf of Rajoana in March 2012. The SGPC is part of my community," Rohatgi submitted.He argued that the Supreme Court's May 2023 judgment, which declined to commute his death sentence at that stage, left the competent authority free to consider the mercy petition in due course.Rohatgi submitted that nearly three-and-a-half years have since passed without a decision.The bench said if the facts are not disputed, then it is reserving its decision and parties may file their written submissions within three weeks.On October 28, the Centre had opposed Rajoana's plea for commutation of death sentence, saying such a relief cannot be granted.In September 2024, the top court sought responses from the Centre, the Punjab government and the administration of the Union Territory of Chandigarh on Rajoana's plea.Beant Singh and 16 others were killed in a blast at the entrance of the civil secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. A special court sentenced Rajoana to death in July 2007.

headline: Nepal national gets life term for beating fellow labourer to death over ration dispute in Ludhiana
content: The court of Sessions Judge Harpreet Kaur Randhawa in Ludhiana has sentenced a 27-year-old Nepal national, Inerjit Mukhia, to life imprisonment in a murder case.He was facing charges of murdering a fellow migrant labourer by repeatedly hitting him with a wooden stick following a dispute over sharing of ration at a tubewell in village Dhilwan in August 2023.Giving details, Additional Public Prosecutor Monika Gupta said the prosecution examined 12 witnesses to prove the guilt of the accused. A fine of Rs 20,000 was also imposed on the convict.According to the prosecution, the incident took place on the night of July 31, 2023. The deceased, Shiv Nath Mukhia, was working for a labour contractor, Lal Babu Paswan, and was residing at the tubewell motor room of a farmer, Harlabh Singh.Paswan told the court that he had visited the tubewell around 10 pm to inform Shiv Nath about the next day’s work when he saw the accused assaulting Shiv Nath with a wooden stick and hitting him on the head. Fearing that the accused might attack him too, he left the place. The following morning, he found Shiv Nath’s body lying in a pool of blood inside the motor room.The prosecution established that the murder followed a dispute over the distribution of ration between the accused and the deceased. The victim had reportedly complained that the accused had consumed a major portion of the ration brought by the victim.The court relied on the testimony of Paswan, the sole eyewitness, which was corroborated by Harlabh Singh, who stated that the complainant had informed him about the incident the following morning. The court also considered an extra-judicial confession allegedly made by the accused to another villager, Hardeep Singh.During investigation, the accused led to the recovery of a blood-stained wooden stick and a yellow T-shirt concealed in the tubewell room. The Forensic Science Laboratory report confirmed the presence of human blood on both items.The postmortem examination revealed six injuries, including serious head injuries, multiple rib fractures and damage to vital organs. The doctors opined that the injuries to the brain, liver and lungs were sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature.Rejecting the defence arguments regarding discrepancies in the eyewitness account, delay in reporting and alleged irregularities in recovery, the court held that the prosecution had proved the charge of murder beyond reasonable doubt.

headline: PNB partners with Deutsche Bank to explore acquisition financing in India
content: After State Bank of India (SBI) and Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank (PNB) has joined hands with a foreign lender for acquisition financing in India. The Delhi-based state-owned lender said on Wednesday it had signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Deutsche Bank AG to establish a framework for cooperation in financing share acquisitions by clients in the country. Under the proposed arrangement, the two banks will explore opportunities to collaborate on acquisition financing through various modes, including underwriting, arrangement, participation, syndication, referral and facilitation, depending on client requirements. The partnership aims to leverage the strengths of both institutions to provide financing solutions for clients undertaking share acquisition transactions, the bank said in a statement. “This collaboration with Deutsche Bank marks an important step towards exploring new opportunities in acquisition financing. By leveraging our respective strengths and capabilities, we aim to facilitate tailored financing solutions for clients while strengthening our presence in the corporate banking ecosystem,” said Ashok Chandra, managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO), PNB. “India is a strategically important market for Deutsche Bank. As a Global Hausbank, we see considerable opportunity to support Indian companies as they grow in scale, pursue their strategic ambitions and deepen their connections to global markets,” said Kaushik Shaparia, CEO, Deutsche Bank Group, India & Emerging Asia. Previously, SBI and Bank of Baroda tied up with Japanese banks to tap opportunities in acquisition financing. SBI had entered into a strategic partnership with Japan's MUFG Bank to collaborate on structuring and financing transactions across mergers and acquisitions (M&A), aviation and real estate. SBI has a lending capacity of around ₹94,000 crore under the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI's) new acquisition financing norms. Separately, Bank of Baroda has partnered with Mizuho Bank to jointly pursue acquisition financing, M&A advisory, structured lending and cross-border financing opportunities. The acquisition financing norms, which allowed domestic banks to enter the space, came into effect on July 1. The RBI framework allows banks to finance up to 75 per cent of the acquisition value, with the acquirer funding the remaining 25 per cent. Both listed and unlisted non-financial companies, as well as their subsidiaries and special purpose vehicles (SPVs), are eligible to raise acquisition finance, subject to eligibility conditions. The framework caps a bank's acquisition finance exposure at 20 per cent of its eligible capital base, within the overall capital market exposure limit.

headline: Back in NDA, Akalis put up wish list before BJP
content: Chandigarh: Having returned to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s December 8 rally in Moga on Parkash Singh Badal’s birth anniversary, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) is pressing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for concrete concessions in the run-up to the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.To rebuild traction against the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), the Congress and rival Panthic challengers, the SAD wants Union home minister Amit Shah’s pledge of issue resolution to translate into action on Bandhi Singhs (Sikh prisoners), farmer demands and seat-sharing.Panth, peasants priorityMovement on Sikhs held in different jails even after completing their sentences is at the top of the SAD’s wish list. Party insiders argue that visible steps on this front are needed to counter rival Panthic groups, particularly Amritpal Singh’s Waris Punjab De, which threaten to pull away core Akali votes.Citing the Union government’s 2019 remission notification, a SAD leader speaking on condition of anonymity said nine detainees were named on the list, three are out of jail, and others clear of pending cases who have finished their terms could safely be freed.Not everyone sees Panthic concessions as an easy win for the partnership. “The Bandhi Singh issue is important yet divisive, and it can alienate other sections of the electorate. It has to be dealt with very carefully,” said Amanpreet Gill, a political science professor at Khalsa College, New Delhi.Easing agrarian hostility toward the BJP—a fallout of the three farm laws that prompted the SAD to exit the NDA in 2020 before their repeal in November 2021 on Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s Parkash Purab—is the second pillar of the SAD’s push. “We have announced support to the SAD, and it will electorally benefit both alliance partners—the SAD and the BJP—only when the BJP shows a resolve to take up farmers’ issues. We have demanded a debt waiver and minimum support price on all crops,” said Harinder Singh, general secretary of farm union Bhartiya Kisan Union (Lakhowal).‘Big brother’ testSeat-sharing is the third test on the Akalis’ agenda. Though the BJP has cast the SAD as the “elder brother” along with the chief ministerial slot, ground negotiations over constituencies remain unfinished. SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal has already announced candidates for nearly 60 assembly seats—including Barnala, Sangrur, Sanour, Dera Bassi and Ropar—where BJP leaders are also staking claims.Whether Sukhbir can turn the “elder brother” billing into practical leadership after the six-year split since 2020—following a 24-year partnership that began when Parkash Singh Badal backed the BJP in 1996 and yielded state governments in 1997, 2007 and 2012 along with Union ministries and Rajya Sabha seats—will depend on whether talks move past general assurances into settled policy and seat agreements.BJP leaders, meanwhile, insist the leadership will iron out differences. “The Union home minister had very explicitly announced resolving all the issues. I am sure it will be done with the same finesse with which the alliance was announced,” said former BJP state unit president Sunil Jakhar.

headline: Punjab Kushhaal Rally’ On Nov 26 To Showcase 5 Years Of Bhagwant Mann Govt's Work, Reflect People’s Support & Set Direction For 2027 Polls: Baltej Pannu
content: Ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)’s 15th Foundation Day celebrations and the Punjab Kushhaal Rally scheduled for November 26 in Moga, AAP Punjab Media In-charge Baltej Pannu on Wednesday said the mega rally would mark a new chapter in Punjab’s politics, with the party presenting its five-year report card before the people, highlighting the achievements of the CM Bhagwant Singh Mann-led government and formally launching its campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections. Addressing a press conference, AAP Punjab Media In-charge Baltej Pannu said, “AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, the entire Cabinet and senior party leadership will be present at the rally. This mega gathering will mark the beginning of our campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections, and people from across Punjab are expected to participate in large numbers.” The AAP Punjab Media In-charge said fulfilling the promises made to the people had remained the government’s priority since it assumed office in 2022. “We introduced 600 units of free electricity per bill cycle for every household in July 2022. Today, nearly 90 per cent of households in Punjab are receiving zero electricity bills. This reflects our commitment to providing direct relief to ordinary families,” he said. Highlighting the Bhagwant Mann government’s employment initiatives, Baltej Pannu said, “CM Bhagwant Singh Mann prioritised employment from the very first Cabinet meeting. Today, more than 78,000 government jobs have been provided to young people purely on merit, without recommendations, favouritism or bribery.” Describing the revival of canal irrigation as one of the most significant achievements of the government, Baltej Pannu said, “When AAP came to power, only 22-23 per cent of canal water was reaching agricultural fields. Through sustained efforts, this figure has now increased to nearly 88%. We began working on this from our very first day because Punjab’s groundwater depletion was a matter of serious concern.” He added that improved utilisation of canal water had strengthened water management during the flood season, helping Punjab avoid major flood-related difficulties this time. Better canal water availability had also contributed to improved crop yields during the paddy season, providing further relief to farmers.

headline: BJP eyes 42-45 Punjab assembly seats, moves to finalise CMP with SAD
content: Chandigarh: A day after the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) revived their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, the BJP is looking to contest around 42 to 45 of the state’s 117 seats, leaving roughly 72 to 75 to the SAD.The figures, nearly finalised, would mark a near doubling of the BJP’s share from its earlier 24-year partnership, under which the saffron party contested 23 seats and the SAD 94.Party insiders said the BJP had pressed for a bigger share on the back of its expanded urban and semi-urban footprint, while the SAD insisted on retaining its senior partner status.The BJP is set to retain all 23 seats it contested under the previous arrangement dating back to the 1997 assembly polls.Sources added that the constituency-wise list is still being worked out, with mutual adjustments possible on a few seats where both sides claim strong candidates.On policy, the two parties plan to form a joint committee within a couple of days to flesh out the common minimum programme (CMP). Comprising leaders from both sides, the panel will translate the broad understanding already reached into a detailed, actionable document for the joint manifesto.BJP Punjab affairs in-charge Satish Poonia is expected to play a key role on the panel, while former Rajya Sabha member Avinash Rai Khanna has already been tasked with preparing the party’s manifesto input.Former Punjab BJP president Sunil Jakhar said a common minimum programme addressing Panthic issues and curbing militancy is already in place, adding that the Bandi Singhs (Sikh prisoners) issue will also be resolved.The reunion was formalised on Gurpurb on November 24—six years after the split over the three farm laws—at a joint press conference in New Delhi attended by Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal.Leaders from both sides said the CMP will focus on a drug-free Punjab, restoring law and order, cracking down on gangsters, farmer welfare, and Hindu-Sikh unity. Jakhar said the tie-up would strengthen the principal Panthic party, counter militancy and radicalism in the border state, and reflect the BJP’s acceptance of the SAD as the senior partner signalling a united Punjab.

headline: Amritsar 450 Conclave begins at GNDU; View Pics
content: Governor Kataria Calls for Vision to Preserve Heritage and Shape City’s Future Amritsar (Punjab), November 25, 2026: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Wednesday called for linking Amritsar’s 450-year historical and cultural legacy with a forward-looking development strategy, as Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU) hosted the inaugural session of the two-day international conclave, ‘Amritsar 450’. Held on the theme ‘Remembering the Past, Understanding the Present and Envisioning the Future’, the conclave brought together academics, historians, public representatives and other prominent personalities to discuss the city’s spiritual heritage, historical journey and future development. Addressing the gathering, Kataria said preserving Punjab’s historical, religious and cultural heritage while preparing younger generations for future challenges was essential. He highlighted the teachings of the Sikh Gurus, saying their emphasis on humanity, equality, service and sacrifice had given Punjab a distinct identity across the world. Referring to traditions such as Langar and the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas, the Governor described Punjab’s history as an example of courage, conviction and social responsibility. He also expressed concern over growing drug abuse among young people and called for collective efforts by the government, educational institutions and society to tackle the problem. Kataria said Punjab needed fresh initiatives in education, research, agriculture and industrial development. He emphasised agricultural diversification, food processing, water conservation, renewable energy, environmental protection and technological innovation as important areas for future growth.

headline: Govt clears 6 brownfield gas-based urea projects worth ₹54,000 crore
content: The government has cleared six brownfield gas-based urea projects worth ₹54,000 crore under its new investment policy approved in July, a senior Fertiliser Ministry official said on Wednesday, as the country seeks to cut fertiliser imports and improve self-sufficiency. The 2026 National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU), notified on July 30, aims to attract fresh capacity, particularly greenfield and brownfield or expansion projects. "Out of 18 proposals received under NIPU-2026, six key brownfield urea projects have been taken forward across public sector, private sector and cooperative enterprises," the official told PTI. The Projects Cleared Are: MFL-Madras in Chennai, NFL Nangal in Punjab, KFL-Shahjahanpur in Uttar Pradesh, Matix-Panagarh in West Bengal, CFCL Gadepan in Kota, Rajasthan, and IIPL-Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh. MFL-Madras is a public sector project to replace a unit over 60 years old, which has higher production costs, high energy consumption and safety hazards. NFL Nangal is a public sector project to replace a plant set up in 1978, with a present capacity of 4.73 lakh tonnes per annum, by a modern 12.7 lakh tonnes unit. KFL-Shahjahanpur is a cooperative project by KRIBHCO to expand a unit commissioned in 1995. Matix-Panagarh is a private project building on a plant commissioned in 2017. West Bengal has only one urea plant at present, and the new unit will support the state's requirement. CFCL Gadepan is a private project to expand a complex operational since 1994, while IIPL-Jagdishpur is a private project proposing a 12.7 lakh tonnes per annum capacity addition at a plant established in 1988. Brownfield projects benefit from existing land, utilities, infrastructure, logistics and technical manpower, which supports faster execution and cost efficiency, the official said, adding that more projects are in the pipeline. Aging Plants Legacy units face higher production costs, elevated energy consumption and process-safety risks, the official said.Nangal operates at 6.498 Gcal per tonne, against the weighted industry average of 5.95 Gcal and the new energy norm of 5 Gcal. India's annual urea consumption is around 400 lakh tonnes. Domestic production rose from 225 lakh tonnes in 2014-15 to a record 314.07 lakh tonnes in 2023-24 and stood at 293.30 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Total indigenous reassessed capacity rose from 207.54 lakh tonnes per annum in 2014-15 to 269.42 lakh tonnes in 2026-27.With new capacity and expansion plans, reliance on imports is set to decline substantially, saving foreign exchange, the official said. Investment With each brownfield project estimated at a capital cost of around ₹9,000 crore, the six plants are poised to attract nearly ₹54,000 crore in fresh investment, he said. To improve bankability, the framework offers a return on equity of 12-16 per cent, along with a foreign exchange rate mitigation mechanism that converts to rupees after four years at prevailing rates. Brownfield advantages are estimated to yield annual savings of ₹225 crore, or about ₹1,800 crore over eight years. Policy Background The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved NIPU-2026 on July 15. The policy separates fixed cost and variable or energy cost, keeps the energy cost component unchanged and reduces fixed cost by around 8 per cent, lowering concession prices by about 14 per cent for both greenfield and brownfield projects. Its predecessor, the New Investment Policy-2012, announced on January 2, 2013 and amended on October 7, 2014, led to six new urea units of 12.7 lakh tonnes per annum each, adding 76.2 lakh tonnes of capacity. Four were joint ventures of public sector units -- Ramagundam in Telangana, and Gorakhpur, Sindri and Barauni in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar, respectively,-- and two were private: Matix Fertilizers' Panagarh unit and Chambal Fertilizers' Gadepan-III. The New Urea Policy-2015, notified on May 25, 2015, for the existing 25 gas-based units, generated an additional 20-25 lakh tonnes of urea annually compared with 2014-15. Two more 12.7 lakh tonne projects are under execution: the Talcher Fertilizer Project in Odisha via the coal gasification route, expected by December 2027, and Assam Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Company Ltd's plant at Namrup, announced on March 19, 2025

headline: Punjab IPS Reshuffle: 25 IPS, 6 PPS Officers Transferred; Bhullar Gets Jalandhar, Kuldeep Singh Amritsar
content: Chandigarh: The Punjab government has ordered a major reshuffle in the state police department, transferring 31 officers, including 25 Indian Police Service (IPS) officers and six Punjab Police Service (PPS) officers, with immediate effect. According to an order issued by the Department of Home Affairs on November 25, the transfers and new postings have been made on administrative grounds with the approval of the competent authority. The reshuffle involves several senior-level appointments, including changes in the offices of Additional Directors General of Police (ADGPs), Inspectors General of Police (IGPs), Deputy Inspectors General of Police (DIGs), Commissioners of Police and Senior Superintendents of Police (SSPs). Among the major changes, 1997-batch IPS officer Naunihal Singh has been given additional charge of ADGP, State Armed Police, Jalandhar Cantt. Gurpreet Singh Bhullar (2004, SPS) has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar, while Kuldeep Singh (2009-batch IPS officer) will take charge as Commissioner of Police, Amritsar. Satinder Singh (2010, SPS) has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana, replacing Swapan Sharma (2009-batch IPS officer), who has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range. Jagadale Nilambari Vijay (2008-batch IPS officer) has been appointed IGP, Jalandhar Range, while Naveen Singla (2009-batch IPS officer) will take charge as DIG, Faridkot Range. At the district level, several officers from the 2013 to 2019 IPS batches have received new responsibilities. These include Surendra Lamba (2013-batch), Ravjot Grewal (2015-batch), Ankur Gupta (2016-batch), Dr. Pragya Jain (2017-batch), Tushar Gupta (2018-batch) and Maninder Singh (2019-batch). Major Changes in Commissioner of Police and Range-Level Postings The reshuffle brings changes in the leadership of three major police commissionerates in Punjab – Jalandhar, Amritsar and Ludhiana. Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, who was serving as IGP, Border Range, Amritsar, has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar. He replaces Satinder Singh, who has been transferred as Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana. Kuldeep Singh, who was serving as DIG, Technical Services, Punjab, with additional charge of DIG, Patiala Range, has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Amritsar. He replaces Harmanbir Singh, who has been transferred as DIG, Border Range, Amritsar. Meanwhile, Swapan Sharma, who was serving as Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana, has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range. At the range level, Jagadale Nilambari Vijay has been appointed IGP, Jalandhar Range, while Naveen Singla has been transferred as DIG, Faridkot Range. Harjeet Singh has been posted as DIG, Bathinda Range, and Snehdeep Sharma will take charge as DIG, Ferozepur Range. Amneet Kondal has been appointed DIG, Patiala Range. Read also: Punjab Police Transfers 273 DSPs and One IPS Officer in Major Reshuffle Ahead of Assembly Elections Naunihal Singh Gets Additional Charge of ADGP, State Armed Police Naunihal Singh, a 1997-batch IPS officer, will continue as ADGP, Internal Vigilance Cell (IVC), Punjab, Chandigarh, and has additionally been assigned the charge of ADGP, State Armed Police, Jalandhar Cantt. Other important appointments include Dr. Nanak Singh (2011-batch IPS officer) as DIG, Technical Services, Punjab, Chandigarh, and Gurmeet Singh Chauhan (2011, SPS) as DIG, Provisioning, Punjab, Chandigarh. Vivek Sheel Soni (2011-batch IPS officer), who was awaiting posting, has been appointed AIG, Internal Vigilance Cell, Punjab, Chandigarh. Several SSPs Transferred Across Punjab The reshuffle also brings changes in several district-level police appointments. Surendra Lamba (2013-batch IPS officer), who was serving as SSP, Tarn Taran, has been transferred as SSP, Sangrur. Ravjot Grewal (2015-batch IPS officer), who was SSP, Sangrur, has been appointed SSP, Vigilance Bureau, Punjab, SAS Nagar. Ankur Gupta (2016-batch IPS officer), previously SSP, Ludhiana Rural, has been posted as SSP, Faridkot. Ashwini Goyal (2016-batch IPS officer) has been appointed SSP, Ferozepur, while Vatsala Gupta (2016-batch IPS officer) will take charge as SSP, SBS Nagar. Dr. Pragya Jain (2017-batch IPS officer) has been appointed SSP, Amritsar Rural, while Tushar Gupta (2018-batch IPS officer) has been transferred as SSP, Gurdaspur. Ajay Gandhi (2018-batch IPS officer) will take charge as SSP, Tarn Taran, while Aditya (2018-batch IPS officer) has been appointed AIG, Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), Punjab, SAS Nagar. Maninder Singh (2019-batch IPS officer), who was serving as AIG, Welfare, Punjab, with additional charge of SSP, Ropar, has been posted as SSP, Ropar. Full List of 25 IPS Officers Transferred in Punjab The following 25 IPS officers have been assigned new responsibilities under the November 25 order. Their previous postings, service/batch identifiers and new assignments are as follows: Naunihal Singh (1997, RR) – ADGP, Internal Vigilance Cell, Punjab, Chandigarh – ADGP, Internal Vigilance Cell, with additional charge of ADGP, State Armed Police, Jalandhar Cantt. Gurpreet Singh Bhullar (2004, SPS) – IGP, Border Range, Amritsar – Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar. Jagadale Nilambari Vijay (2008, RR) – IGP, ANTF, Punjab, SAS Nagar, with additional charge of IGP, Faridkot Range – IGP, Jalandhar Range. Naveen Singla (2009, RR) – DIG, Jalandhar Range, with additional charge of Director, Vigilance Bureau, Punjab – DIG, Faridkot Range. Swapan Sharma (2009, RR) – Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana – DIG, Ropar Range. Kuldeep Singh (2009, RR) – DIG, Technical Services, Punjab, with additional charge of DIG, Patiala Range – Commissioner of Police, Amritsar. Harjeet Singh (2010, RR) – DIG, Training, Punjab, with additional charge of DIG, Bathinda Range – DIG, Bathinda Range. Satinder Singh (2010, SPS) – Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar – Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana. Harmanbir Singh (2010, SPS) – Commissioner of Police, Amritsar – DIG, Border Range, Amritsar. Dr. Nanak Singh (2011, RR) – DIG, Internal Vigilance Cell, Punjab, with additional charge of DIG, Ropar Range – DIG, Technical Services, Punjab. Gurmeet Singh Chauhan (2011, SPS) – Awaiting posting – DIG, Provisioning, Punjab, Chandigarh. Snehdeep Sharma (2011, SPS) – DIG, AGTF, Ludhiana, with additional charge of DIG, Ferozepur Range – DIG, Ferozepur Range. Amneet Kondal (2012, RR) – DIG, Personnel, Punjab, Chandigarh – DIG, Patiala Range. Vivek Sheel Soni (2011, RR) – Awaiting posting – AIG, Internal Vigilance Cell, Punjab, Chandigarh. Surendra Lamba (2013, RR) – SSP, Tarn Taran – SSP, Sangrur. Charanjit Singh (2013, RR) – AIG, Special Branch-I, Intelligence, Punjab – SSP, Ludhiana Rural. Ravjot Grewal (2015, RR) – SSP, Sangrur – SSP, Vigilance Bureau, Punjab, SAS Nagar. Ankur Gupta (2016, RR) – SSP, Ludhiana Rural – SSP, Faridkot. Ashwini Goyal (2016, RR) – AIG, ANTF, Punjab, SAS Nagar – SSP, Ferozepur. Vatsala Gupta (2016, RR) – AIG, Personnel-II, Punjab, Chandigarh – SSP, SBS Nagar. Dr. Pragya Jain (2017, RR) – AIG, ANTF, Ludhiana, with additional charge of AIG, Internal Security, Punjab, Ludhiana – SSP, Amritsar Rural. Tushar Gupta (2018, RR) – SSP, SBS Nagar – SSP, Gurdaspur. Ajay Gandhi (2018, RR) – AIG, Provisioning, Punjab, Chandigarh – SSP, Tarn Taran. Aditya (2018, RR) – SSP, Gurdaspur – AIG, ANTF, Punjab, SAS Nagar. Maninder Singh (2019, RR) – AIG, Welfare, Punjab, with additional charge of SSP, Ropar – SSP, Ropar. Six PPS Officers Also Get New Postings Along with the 25 IPS officers, the Punjab government has also transferred six Punjab Police Service (PPS) officers. The changes include district-level appointments and the placement of three officers at the disposal of the Vigilance Bureau, Punjab. Bhupinder Singh (PPS, TP/88) – SSP, Ferozepur – SSP, Malerkotla. Harkamalpreet Singh Khakh (PPS, TP/100) – SSP, Malerkotla – SSP, Jalandhar Rural. Harvinder Singh Virk (PPS, TP/108) – SSP, Jalandhar Rural – AIG, Special Branch-I, Intelligence, Punjab. Kanwalpreet Singh (PPS, 1366/PAP) – SP Headquarters, Amritsar Rural, with additional charge of SSP, Amritsar Rural – Services placed at the disposal of Vigilance Bureau, Punjab. Gurbans Singh Bains (PPS, 22/PR, 198/J) – SP, PBI, Faridkot, with additional charge of SSP, Faridkot – Services placed at the disposal of Vigilance Bureau, Punjab. Karamvir Singh (PPS, 43/BR, 41/JR) – SP Operations, Barnala – Services placed at the disposal of Vigilance Bureau, Punjab. Order Issued by Punjab Home Department The transfer order was issued by the Department of Home Affairs, Punjab, on November 25, 2026, and signed by Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Alok Shekhar. The order states that the transfers and postings have been made on administrative grounds with the approval of the competent authority. All officers concerned have been directed to join their new places of posting immediately. The reshuffle covers senior police leadership, commissionerates, police ranges, district-level appointments, intelligence, vigilance and specialised units, marking a major administrative restructuring of the Punjab Police establishment. headline: One devotee killed, 14 injured as bus collides with truck in Fatehgarh Sahib
content: A devotee was killed and 14 others were injured when a bus collided with a truck near Sirhind here on Wednesday, officials said.The accident occurred when the bus was returning from a gurdwara in Karnal to Amritsar. The impact was so severe that the front portion of the bus was badly damaged, leaving passengers screaming for help.Locals and police personnel rushed to the spot and launched rescue efforts.The injured passengers were shifted to a nearby hospital.SSP Shubham Aggarwal reached the spot and said an investigation is under way.

headline: PB BJP PRINT MEDIA AT CHANDIGARH
content: BROAD DAYLIGHT FIRING ON SARPANCH'S HUSBAND FOR RAISING VOICE AGAINST DRUGS EVIDENCE OF LAWLESSNESS UNDER AAP: KEWAL SINGH DHILLON WHEN RULING PARTY LEADERS THEMSELVES ARE NOT SAFE, WHAT FATE AWAITS COMMON CITIZENS: BJP Chandigarh, 25 November 2026:Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Punjab State President Kewal Singh Dhillon took the Punjab government to task while expressing grave concern over the incident in which Sukhbir Singh, husband of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch Manjit Kaur of Nawan Pind Daleke village in Tarn Taran district, was shot at and critically injured by alleged drug peddlers in broad daylight. Dhillon stated that law and order in Punjab has deteriorated to such an extent that even panchayat representatives belonging to the ruling party are no longer safe from the drug mafia. If the family of a sarpanch who opposed drug trafficking can be cornered on the road and shot at, the security of common citizens in the state is left entirely to god's mercy. Brazen Attack to Avenge Opposition to Drug Peddling; Smugglers Have No Fear of LawSharing details, the State President noted that Sukhbir Singh had opposed illegal drug trafficking activities in the village and informed the police. Nursing a grudge over this, drug peddlers intercepted Sukhbir Singh and his wife while they were travelling on a motorcycle and opened direct fire. He emphasized that the brazen use of illegal firearms by drug smugglers in the border district of Tarn Taran proves that all claims made by the Punjab government regarding action against drugs are completely hollow. The drug mafia is carrying out retaliatory attacks with utter disregard for the police and the law. Culprits Must Be Arrested Immediately; Political Patronage to Drug Mafia Must EndKewal Singh Dhillon demanded that the culprits who carried out the murderous attack on Sukhbir Singh be arrested without delay and strict legal punishment be ensured. He urged the Punjab government to provide robust security to vigilant panchayat members, sarpanches, and ordinary citizens who raise their voice against drugs, so that anti-social elements are deterred. The State President asserted that political patronage extended to drug peddlers and criminals must be terminated immediately and Punjab Police given a free hand to uproot the drug-gangster nexus, in order to protect Punjab's youth and uphold the rule of law Departments of Three AAP Ministers Handed Over 150 Acres of Panchayat Land to Favoured Mining Mafia: Sunil Jakhar

headline: Satinder Singh replaces Swapan Sharma as Ludhiana Police Commissioner
content: The Punjab Government on Wednesday transferred 2009-batch IPS officer and Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma. He has been replaced by 2010-batch IPS officer Satinder Singh, who was serving as the Police Commissioner of Jalandhar.Sharma has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range. He had taken charge as Ludhiana CP on March 29, 2025, and served in the position for 20 months.Related News: Punjab transfers 31 police officers ahead of Assembly election; Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar get new commissionersDuring his tenure, Sharma busted several major networks of gangsters and international syndicates, arrested terrorists and gangsters, and oversaw encounters in which several gangsters and aides of terrorists were killed.Sharma has previously served in several important positions in the Punjab Police. He also served as DIG, Jalandhar Range. As AIG, Counter Intelligence, he dealt a major blow to the networks of gangsters and illegal weapon suppliers.He also served as SSP in several police districts, including Fazilka, Bathinda, Ropar, Sangrur, Jalandhar and Amritsar, where he busted major drug networks and arrested smugglers.The new CP, Satinder Singh, has previously served as DIG, Ludhiana Range. He has also served as DIG, Border Range, and SSP, Amritsar Rural.Satinder’s father, Swaran Singh, was also in the police force and served as SSP, Jagraon, in the 1990s. Satinder is closely associated with Dera Baba Murad Shah in Nakodar.The government also transferred Ludhiana SSP Dr Ankur Gupta, who has been posted as SSP, Faridkot. AIG, Special Branch Intelligence-I, Charanjit Singh, has been posted as SSP, Ludhiana Rural.

headline: BJP steps aside from Punjab CM race? Amit Shah's 'bada bhai' remark puts Shiromani Akali Dal in driver's seat
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appears to have stepped back from the race for Punjab's chief ministerial post, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah making it clear that the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will lead the two parties' alliance in the 2027 Assembly elections. Shah's announcement also puts SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal in the spotlight as a potential contender for the top job. Announcing the revival of the BJP-SAD partnership in New Delhi on Tuesday, Shah said the Akali Dal would be the "big brother" in the alliance and that the chief minister would come from the senior partner. "Akalis will be the big brother," Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal. Making the arrangement clear, Shah added that the party playing the big brother's role would get the chief minister's post. Amit Shah's 'bada bhai' remark: Is Sukhbir Badal the likely Punjab CM face? While Amit Shah did not announce a specific chief ministerial candidate, his remarks indicate that the BJP is willing to let the Akali Dal lead the government if the alliance wins the 2027 Punjab elections. This is a significant shift in the political arrangement between the two parties, which had shared power in Punjab in the past but parted ways in 2020 over the Centre's three farm laws. Shah described the Akali Dal as the NDA's oldest ally and welcomed its return to the coalition, saying the partnership had been renewed after discussions between senior leaders of both parties. He also revealed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had spoken to Badal on Monday and expressed happiness over the Akali Dal's return. Shah said Modi believed the NDA was complete with the return of the Badal family's party to the alliance. BJP and Akali Dal to contest Punjab's 117 Assembly seats together The two parties have agreed to contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, formally bringing the Akali Dal back into the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance after six years. Shah described the partnership as more than an electoral arrangement, calling it a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood. Recalling the parties' long association under former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, he said they had fought several elections together, experiencing both victories and defeats. The two parties split in September 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA in protest against the three farm laws. The legislation was subsequently repealed following widespread farmers' protests. Drug-free Punjab by December 2029: What Amit Shah promised Amit Shah said tackling drug addiction would be the alliance's biggest priority if it came to power in Punjab. He set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to make the state completely drug-free. He also identified corruption, farmers' concerns and employment opportunities for young people as key areas of focus. Shah said the BJP and SAD had spent the past three months discussing Punjab's economic development, farmers' issues and job opportunities. Talks between Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal had resulted in a roadmap for the government the alliance hopes to form after the 2027 elections, he added. Shah expressed confidence that the BJP-SAD partnership would win a majority and form the next government in Punjab.

headline: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy: Playing for Punjab might give him an edge, says Kartik Chadha
content: INDORE Despite attending trials with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), Chennai Super Kings (CSK), Mumbai Indians (MI), Rajasthan Royals (RR), and Punjab Kings (PBKS), leg-spinner Kartik Chadha went unsold at the IPL 2026 auction. He had gone unsold in the previous auction too, but had a net-bowling stint with CSK during IPL 2025. Reflecting on why he went unsold, the 22-year-old had felt that playing for his state Punjab might give him an edge. Now, in his maiden T20 season for the side, he has featured in three matches and made an impression against Tamil Nadu in the ongoing Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT). He picked up three for 30, including two wickets in three balls when Tamil Nadu needed 39 off 39 with seven wickets in hand, triggering a collapse. Punjab eventually prevailed by five runs. “I kept attacking the stumps, leaving no room for the batters,” he said after the match. Seven of his 14 wickets in the 2026 Sher-e-Punjab T20 League came through bowled or LBW dismissals, underlining his effectiveness in targeting the stumps. Representing Ludhiana Lions, he finished as the competition’s second-highest wicket-taker with an economy of 6.46 from 10 matches, helping his side reach the final. His accuracy stood out in a tournament dominated by big scores. He recalled a conversation with former India captain M.S. Dhoni during IPL 2025, which changed his perspective on bowling. “His point was that the number of variations you have doesn’t really matter. What matters is where the ball lands. So, even if you only have one variation, it needs to land in the right spot. I learned a great deal from that,” Chadha said. He had also dismissed Dhoni in a CSK practice match. “I had never even imagined something like that. Since childhood, I had only ever seen him on TV. But to actually bowl a ball and get him out! I mean, it was just a practice game, but for me, it was still a huge deal,” he said. He has also added Shubman Gill, Naman Dhir, and Prabhsimran Singh to his list of prized scalps in the Punjab T20 League. Kartik has also found a mentor in former India leg-spinner Rahul Sharma, who, like him, is from Jalandhar. “He has helped me a lot. He is my mentor and continues to guide me. He is here commentating on the matches and gives me feedback along the way. We speak before and after every match. Before the Punjab T20 League, it was really helpful that I had some sessions with him. He provides a lot of mental motivation, which I feel is even more beneficial,” he said. A batter until 2019, Kartik continues to work on his batting. “But the bowling is getting the upper hand,” he said.

headline: Punjab Transfers 31 Police Officers, Appoints 3 New CPs
content: Chandigarh: The Punjab government has appointed new Commissioners of Police for Jalandhar, Amritsar and Ludhiana as part of a reshuffle involving 25 IPS and six PPS officers. headline: Punjab transfers 31 police officers ahead of Assembly election; Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar get new commissioners
content: In a major administrative reshuffle ahead of the Assembly election next year, the Punjab Government on Wednesday ordered the transfer of 31 police officers, including several IPS officers, with immediate effect.The reshuffle has brought significant changes in the police leadership of key districts and ranges. Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range, while Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh will replace him as Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana.Gurpreet Bhullar, who was serving as IGP, Border Range, Amritsar, has been posted as Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar, replacing Satinder Singh. Harmanbir Singh, the outgoing Commissioner of Police, Amritsar, has been posted as DIG, Border Range.IGP Nilambari Vijay Jagadale, who was heading the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), Punjab, and also holding the additional charge of IGP, Faridkot Range, has been posted as IGP, Jalandhar Range. Naveen Singla, who was heading Jalandhar Range, has been posted as DIG, Faridkot Range, and will also hold the additional charge of Director, Vigilance Bureau.At the district level, Surendra Lamba, SSP, Tarn Taran, has been posted as SSP, Sangrur, replacing Ravjot Grewal, who has been posted as SSP, Vigilance Bureau. Lamba will be replaced at Tarn Taran by Ajay Gandhi, who was serving as AIG, Provisioning.Ankur Gupta, SSP, Ludhiana Rural, has been posted as SSP, Faridkot, while Charanjit Singh, who was serving in Special Branch-I of Intelligence, has been appointed SSP, Ludhiana Rural.The reshuffle also includes changes in the leadership of several other districts. Ashwini Gotyal, AIG, ANTF, has been posted as SSP, Ferozepur, replacing Bhupinder Singh, who will take over as SSP, Malerkotla.Harkamalpreet Khakh, currently SSP, Malerkotla, has been posted as SSP, Jalandhar Rural, replacing Harvinder Virk.Virk has been posted as AIG, Special Branch-I, Intelligence. Aditya, SSP, Gurdaspur, has been posted as AIG, ANTF, while Tushar Gupta, SSP, SBS Nagar, will replace him at Gurdaspur. Vatsala Gupta has been posted as SSP, SBS Nagar.At the range level, Harjeet Singh has been posted as DIG, Bathinda Range, while Snehdeep Sharma has been appointed DIG, Ferozepur Range. Amneet Kondal will take over as DIG, Patiala Range.Kuldeep Singh, DIG, Technical Services, has been posted as Commissioner of Police, Amritsar, replacing Harmanbir Singh. Nanak Singh will take over as DIG, Technical Services, Punjab.The order also assigns additional responsibilities to several officers. Naunihal Singh will continue as ADGP, Internal Vigilance Cell, while taking additional charge as ADGP, State Armed Police, Jalandhar Cantt.Gurmeet Chauhan has been posted as DIG, Provisioning, on a vacant post, while Vivek Sheel Soni has been appointed AIG, Internal Vigilance Cell.Kanwalpreet Singh, Gurbans Bains and Karamvir Singh have been placed at the disposal of the Vigilance Bureau.The transfer order, issued by Department of Home Affairs on November 25, directs all officers concerned to join their new postings immediately.

headline: Senu Duggal appointed observer for Patiala MC re-elections on November 28
content: The State Election Commission, Punjab, has appointed IAS officer Senu Duggal as the Observer to ensure that the re-elections in 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation, Patiala, in Patiala district, scheduled for November 28, are conducted in a free, fair and peaceful manner.The Observer, Senu Duggal, on Wednesday held a meeting with Additional Deputy Commissioner Kuldeep Bawa in Patiala to review the arrangements for the elections.During the meeting, the Observer shared the mobile number 96460-06027 and email ID patialazp@gmail.com of the Nodal Officer (Complaints) for the convenience of voters and candidates contesting in the 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation.She said that voters and candidates could contact the Nodal Officer at any time through the given mobile number or email address regarding the Municipal Corporation Re-elections 2026.ADC Kuldeep Bawa informed that Dr. Senu Duggal would remain stationed in Patiala as the Observer until November 28.Polling will take place on November 28 from 8 am to 4 pm. Besides Patiala, elections will also be held in seven wards in Dharamkot and 15 wards in Baghapurana.The re-elections are being held following a Supreme Court decision directing fresh polls in wards where alleged irregularities were reported during the previous municipal elections.In compliance with the directions of the apex court, the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has constituted a judicial monitoring committee to supervise the election process being conducted by the State Election Commission and ensure compliance with the safeguards laid down by the Supreme Court.

headline: Breaking: Amritsar, Ludhiana and Jalandhar get new Commissioners of Police
content: Breaking: Amritsar, Ludhiana and Jalandhar get new Commissioners of Police Chandigarh, November 25, 2026: Chandigarh, November 25, 2026: The Punjab Government on Wednesday appointed new Commissioners of Police in Amritsar, Ludhiana and Jalandhar as part of a major police reshuffle involving 31 senior Indian Police Service (IPS) and Punjab Police Service (PPS) officers across the state. Click the link to read order copy:https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MzzM_cDPGkuRPQBeHw4ruCU09aTMbo6i/view?usp=sharing According to the transfer orders issued by the Department of Home Affairs, Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, IPS (2004 batch), has been appointed as the new Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar. He was earlier serving as Inspector General of Police (IGP), Border Range, Amritsar, and replaces Satinder Singh. Satinder Singh, IPS (2010 batch), who was serving as Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar, has been transferred as the new Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana. He replaces Swapan Sharma, IPS (2009 batch), who has been posted as Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Ropar Range. Meanwhile, Kuldeep Singh, IPS (2009 batch), has been appointed as Commissioner of Police, Amritsar. He was earlier serving as DIG, Technical Services, Punjab, and also held the additional charge of DIG, Patiala Range.

headline: Beant Singh assassination: SC reserves verdict on Balwant Rajoana’s plea for commutation of death sentence
content: The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved its verdict on former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh assassination case convict Balwant Singh Rajoana’s petition seeking commutation of his death sentence to life imprisonment on the ground of inordinate delay in deciding his mercy petition pending before the President since 2012.A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Aparesh Singh reserved the judgment after senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi submitted on behalf of Rajoana that the Supreme Court's May 2023 judgment refusing to commute his death sentence at that stage, left it to the competent authority to consider it in due course.However, even after the expiry of three-and-a-half-years, no decision has been taken, he said, adding the convict’s continued incarceration for almost three decades violated his rights under Article 21 of the Constitution.On behalf of the Centre, Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj sought to emphasise that there was no substantial change in the circumstances in Punjab, which the top court took into account in its May 2023 judgment.Nataraj pointed out that Rajoana himself did not file the mercy petition and that Article 21 could not be invoked on the basis of a mercy petition/representation made by someone else. The ASG also drew the court’s attention to Rajoana’s statements expressing lack of faith in the Constitution and the judicial system during the trial and said now he could not invoke the Constitution to claim reliefs.However, Rohatgi countered the ASG, saying the Article 21 remained available to a person irrespective of his opinion about the constitutional system and that Rajoana's earlier refusal to pursue the matter could not permanently deprive him of constitutional rights and remedies.Rajoana (59) — a former Punjab Police constable — has been in jail for more than 29 years, awaiting his execution. Former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh and 16 others were killed in an explosion outside the Civil Secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. Rajoana was sentenced to death in 2007 by a special court. A mercy petition filed by the SGPC on his behalf has been hanging fire for more than 13 years.On May 3, 2023, the top court had refused to commute his death sentence to life imprisonment and asked the Centre to take decision on his mercy plea “as and when it is deemed necessary”.More than 16 months after refusing to commute the death penalty of Rajoana, the Supreme Court had on September 25, 2024 agreed to re-examine the issue afresh. It had asked the Centre and the Punjab Government to respond to his fresh petition for commutation of his death penalty on the ground the Centre has failed to take a decision on his March 25, 2012, mercy petition till date.In his fresh petition, Rajoana submitted that “About 01 year and 04 months have now elapsed since disposal of the petitioner’s first writ petition, and a decision on his fate still hangs under a cloud of uncertainty, causing deep mental trauma and anxiety to the petitioner every single living day, which by itself is a sufficient ground for exercise of this court’s Article 32 powers to allow the reliefs sought.”Citing Devender Pal Singh Bhullar’s case, the petitioner had claimed that the “Delay caused by circumstances beyond the prisoners’ control mandates commutation of death sentence” as the inordinate delay caused agony and adversely affected his physical and mental health.The MHA had earlier contended that Rajaona’s mercy petition can’t be considered as it was filed by SGPC and not by Rajoana himself and that it can’t be decided until the appeals of other convicts were decided by the top court. Considering the prevailing situation, a decision has been taken by the MHA that it would be appropriate to defer any decision on the mercy petition as it could potentially compromise national security and create a law-and-order situation, it had said.

headline: PM Modi to address first NDA rally in Punjab's Moga after BJP-SAD tie-up
content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the first NDA rally in poll-bound Punjab on December 8 after the renewal of the BJP-SAD alliance, Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said on Wednesday..He said the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP will organise the mega rally in Moga to mark the birth anniversary of Akali Dal patriarch Parkash Singh Badal.."The prime minister will arrive in Moga on December 8 on the occasion Parkash Singh Badal’s birth anniversary," Sirsa said..“This will be the first rally of the NDA which Prime Minister Modi will address (after the alliance was announced). Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal will also address the rally,” the BJP leader told reporters at the party headquarters here..BJP, SAD to fight Punjab polls as 'true partners': Kewal Singh Dhillon.Sirsa said the rally will be historic because it is the first such event the SAD and the BJP are organising together after the passing of Parkash Singh Badal..Parkash Singh Badal died in April 2023 at the age of 95..“In my belief, if any historic rally or historic programme is going to take place for Punjab after 1996, it will be the one in Moga to be organised on December 8,” Sirsa added..The BJP and the SAD on Tuesday announced their alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years, with Home Minister Amit Shah making it clear that the Akali Dal will take the role of "elder brother" and also get the CM post if they are voted to power.

headline: Punjab Congress keeps door open for alliances ahead of 2027 polls, Pargat says ‘nothing ruled out’
content: Keeping its options open ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the Congress on Wednesday signalled that it was not averse to an electoral alliance, including with INDIA bloc partners, with state party president Pargat Singh saying “nothing could be ruled out”.Addressing a press conference at Punjab Congress Bhawan, Pargat said the final call on alliances would rest with the party high command. He indicated that the Congress could explore an understanding with the CPI and the CPM in Punjab, even as he asserted that the party was prepared to contest all seats with full strength and form the next government.The statement comes amid renewed political realignments in Punjab following the revival of the BJP-SAD alliance, which the Congress leaders today sought to portray as a coming together driven by electoral compulsions rather than political conviction.Pargat, former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Dr Amar Singh launched a joint attack on the BJP-SAD reunion, claiming that adverse feedback in the two parties’ internal surveys had prompted them to abandon their separate political paths.Questioning the rationale behind the reunion, Channi asked whether the issues that had led to the BJP and SAD parting ways six years ago, particularly over the farm laws and the farmers’ agitation, had been resolved.He also questioned the Akali Dal’s apparent shift on the issue of the Chief Minister’s post amid discussions about Sukhbir Singh Badal being projected as the alliance’s CM face.Describing the BJP-SAD alliance as “dangerous” for Punjab, Channi alleged that the BJP wanted to weaken minorities in the state. He also targeted the BJP over the farmers’ agitation, claiming that more than 750 farmers had lost their lives during the protest.The Congress leaders further questioned the BJP and SAD over allegations of corruption during their previous tenures in power and accused the BJP of using central investigative agencies to target Opposition leaders.On the Congress’s candidate selection strategy, Pargat said the party would give opportunities to young leaders, particularly those with a clean image and the ability to win elections.Responding to former PPCC chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring’s suggestion that 60-70 young candidates be fielded, Pargat said the party would encourage younger faces but would not distribute tickets merely to meet a numerical target.Channi also claimed that the SAD was facing internal turmoil, with several leaders leaving the party, and said the revived BJP-SAD alliance had failed to generate enthusiasm among people in Punjab.He added that the Congress would continue the existing public welfare schemes if voted to power.

He also questioned the Akali Dal’s apparent change of position on the chief ministerial face amid discussions about projecting Sukhbir Singh Badal for the post.Describing the alliance as “dangerous” for Punjab, Channi alleged that the BJP wanted to weaken minorities in the state.He also targeted the BJP over the farmers’ agitation, claiming that more than 750 farmers had died during the protest.
