headline: Kartarpur Corridor reopening hinges on security review as Delhi HC refuses to intervene, leaves decision with Centre
content: The reopening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor remains uncertain, with the Delhi High Court on Wednesday declining to intervene in the Centre’s decision to keep the pilgrimage route closed, even as Union Home Minister Amit Shah reiterated a day earlier that it would be restored once national security concerns were resolved.The court’s decision effectively leaves the question of reopening with the Union Government, offering no immediate relief to Sikh devotees who have been unable to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan through the corridor since May 7, 2025. The Centre had suspended operations following the Pahalgam terror attack, amid the subsequent security situation.A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma refused to entertain a petition filed by Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation, which sought directions to the government to reconsider the prolonged closure.The petitioner argued that the shutdown had caused considerable inconvenience to Sikh pilgrims for whom the shrine, associated with Guru Nanak Dev, holds immense religious significance. It urged the government to explore a controlled or phased reopening, subject to national security requirements.The court observed that the closure was a policy decision taken in the interest of citizens and did not warrant judicial interference under its extraordinary writ jurisdiction. However, it noted that the petitioner's representation was still pending before the authorities and expressed hope that it would be considered.The development comes a day after Shah, addressing a press conference announcing the BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, said the corridor would reopen as soon as national security concerns were completely resolved.Shah maintained that the closure followed security concerns after Operation Sindoor and asserted that national security should not be politicised. He also credited the Modi government with building the corridor and facilitating the pilgrimage.However, his assurance came without a reopening date or any indication of a phased restoration. This leaves devotees dependent on the outcome of the government's security assessment rather than any judicially mandated timeline.For now, the court's order does not change the existing restrictions. The pending representation offers a channel for reconsideration, but neither the court nor the Home Minister has indicated when the corridor will become operational again.

headline: AAP sarpanch, husband escape firing in Tarn Taran; BJP targets Mann government
content: An Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch and her husband escaped unhurt after unidentified assailants opened fire at them near a road junction in Daleke village of Tarn Taran district, police said on Wednesday.The incident took place on Tuesday when Sukhbir Singh, husband of AAP sarpanch Manjit Kaur, was intercepted by the assailants. Kaur, who was riding pillion on his motorcycle, said the attackers fired four shots at them.Tarn Taran Senior Superintendent of Police Surendra Lamba said none of the bullets hit Singh and the assailants fled the spot. The accused had been identified and had criminal records, he said, adding that they were also involved in a personal dispute with the victim’s family.Several police teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. CCTV footage from the area is being examined to establish the sequence of events. A case has been registered, the SSP said.Kaur alleged that the attack was linked to her husband’s opposition to the illegal sale of narcotics in the area. She claimed drug smugglers were targeting him to silence his campaign against the drug menace.The incident triggered a political reaction, with Punjab BJP leader Vineet Joshi accusing the AAP government of failing to maintain law and order. He alleged that people raising their voices against drugs were increasingly becoming targets of the drug mafia.“Today, Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal, Harpal Cheema, Aman Arora, Baltej Pannu and Kuldeep Dhaliwal must hold a press conference and answer AAP Sarpanch Manjit Kaur: What was her husband’s crime?” Joshi said.He also questioned whether speaking against drugs in Punjab was becoming a life-threatening act and referred to the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa.The latest firing incident comes amid a series of attacks on elected village representatives and people associated with anti-drug campaigns in Punjab.On October 27, Tirath Singh, son of AAP sarpanch Paramjit Kaur, was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Chite Kalan village of Amritsar district. Police attributed the murder to an old enmity.Jhota was shot dead inside a medical store in a busy Mansa marketplace on October 13. He was known for raising his voice against drug abuse and the illegal sale of addictive substances.Earlier, on October 6, AAP sarpanch Ashwani Devgan of Toot village in Tarn Taran was shot dead by unidentified assailants.In another incident, former sarpanch Navjeet Singh Neetu was shot dead near Mannewal village in Ludhiana district last month. In July, Hoshiarpur sarpanch Satpal alias Mintu was allegedly attacked with sharp-edged weapons and run over by a car.

headline: Two Shooters Arrested After Woman's Killing In Punjab's Amritsar
content: Amritsar: Two shooters, who shot dead a woman during an attack on a man in Punjab s Amritsar were arrested after being shot at in an encounter with the police on Wednesday.Divulging further details about the operation, Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill stated that the armed assailants shot at one Simranjit in the Guru Ki Wadali area of Amritsar. Simranjit was hit in the chest by a bullet, which ricocheted and hit a woman named Dalbir Kaur nearby. Both injured individuals were immediately rushed to the hospital; however, Kaur succumbed to her injuries.Gill said that given the gravity of the incident, teams led by ACP (West) and SHO of Chheharta police station, Sardar Balwinder Singh under the overall supervision of DCP (City) Jaskaran Teja were immediately put on high alert.Various police teams began searching for the suspects, he said adding based on human intelligence and technical investigation, the police received a lead indicating that the suspects were hiding in the Kot Khalsa area."When the police parties cornered the suspects and signaled them to stop, the miscreants launched a life-threatening attack on the police team, firing three rounds. In self-defense, the police returned fire, discharging five rounds. During the ensuing crossfire, both shooters were struck in the legs and fell to the ground, sustaining injuries," Gill said.The injured shooters have been identified as Harmanpreet and Jagroop, both residents of Amritsar. The police have taken them into custody and admitted them to a hospital for medical treatment. According to the doctors, both are currently out of danger, though the next 48 hours remain critical for observation.Police recovered a 9mm pistol, three spent cartridge casings, and a motorcycle used in the crime from the possession of the accused. Gill said that the motorcycle bears no registration number, and no documentation. This aspect is currently under investigation. Additionally, the police have seized Rs 7,000 rupees in cash, part of a Rs 20,000 contract payment as well as the mobile phones belonging to the accused.According to Gill, interrogation of the arrested duo has revealed that both shooters are associates of Ankush Baman, a notorious criminal based abroad. Baman and Keshav Shivala had hired these two shooters offering a contract (supari) of 20,000 rupees to kill a Sarpanch from Batala or his personal security personnel.However, the incident that took place in Guru Ki Wadali was the result of an old enmity according to police. The shooter, Harmanpreet, had a prior dispute with Simranjit involving the removal of a turban. While Harmanpreet and Jagroop were on their way for another task, Simranjit suddenly appeared before them.Due to an old enmity, they opened fire on Simranjit. The bullet struck Simranjit in the chest which ricocheted, and hit a neighbor, Dalbir Kaur.The Police Commissioner stated that the timely apprehension of these shooters has averted a major murder in Batala. The police are now conducting a forensic examination of the seized mobile phones. Additionally, a list of the local associates and relatives of the foreign-based gangster, Ankush Baman, is being prepared, and they will also be questioned.Read More:Amritsar Man Dies By Suicide After Shooting Pet Dogs and MotherHazaribag: Two Members Of Rahul Dubey Gang Injured In Police Encounter

headline: Akalis dumped BJP over farm laws, now revive alliance for Harsimrat’s Union Cabinet berth: Raja Warring
content: Former Punjab Congress president and sitting Ludhiana MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Wednesday alleged that the SAD-BJP alliance had been revived only to secure a Union Cabinet berth for Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal.Warring was in Goniana, falling in the Bhucho Assembly segment in Bathinda district, where he took out an 'Insaaf March' along with the party's district leadership to highlight the alleged deteriorating law and order situation in Punjab.He said the SAD-BJP alliance had failed to resolve key issues, including the release of 'Bandi Singhs', the farmers' concerns over the three farm laws and the Chandigarh issue."These were the very issues on which the alliance was broken, but none of them has been resolved. Actually, the alliance was broken after farmers protestsd outside their (Badal family's) residence," he said.Targeting AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal ahead of his scheduled visit to Punjab, Warring said people had lost faith in him because of the situation prevailing in the state. He claimed the AAP would face defeat in the coming Assembly elections.Warring further said that Kejriwal's photographs were missing from posters, because the people of Punjab no longer trusted him.Explaining the purpose of the 'Insaaf March', Warring said he had launched it from Ludhiana to question the state government over the growing influence of gangsters, the atmosphere of fear and insecurity among the business community.Holding Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann responsible for the situation, he alleged that several incidents had taken place right under the Chief Minister's nose. "Through this march and with the help of the media, we want to convey our message to this deaf and mute government," he said.

headline: Anti-sacrilege Act row: Akal Takht panel invites Punjab government committee for talks on November 30
content: In a bid to break the deadlock over the Jagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026, the Akal Takht-appointed expert committee has invited members of the Punjab Government’s officially constituted coordination committee for talks at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, Anandpur Sahib, on November 30.The meeting has been proposed in the light of directives issued by Akal Takht amid the continuing disagreement over the amendment legislation, which was passed by the Punjab Government allegedly without taking Akal Takht and Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) officials into confidence.The controversy centres on objections raised by the highest Sikh religious authorities to certain provisions of the amended law, which they contend affect Sikh principles and traditions.Akal Takht had issued directives on May 11 and June 29, 2026, asking the government to keep the Act in abeyance until a consensus was reached with Sikh stakeholders.In a letter to the nodal officer of the government’s coordination committee, Akal Takht expert committee coordinator Lakhvir Singh said the panel was willing to engage in dialogue. However, it expressed serious concern over statements made to the media in Amritsar on November 23 by certain individuals who were not even members of the government’s coordination committee.The expert committee described the statements as misleading and said they failed to accurately explain the directives issued by Akal Takht.It also accused the government panel of repeatedly ignoring its objections and concerns, which had been conveyed through letters dated November 7, 14, 17 and 21.The issue was discussed at a meeting of the expert committee attended by former judges Justice Rupinder Singh Sodhi and Justice Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, Dr Kehar Singh, Prof Jagmohan Singh and coordinator Lakhvir Singh.The committee expressed concern over the lack of clarity on whether the Amendment Act remained in force or had been kept in abeyance in compliance with Akal Takht's directives.Maintaining that it had always been willing to engage with the government, the expert committee said the proposed meeting was intended to ensure transparency, prevent confusion within the Sikh community and preserve Panthic unity.It has also sought formal clarification from the Punjab Government on whether any order or notification has been issued to suspend the implementation of the Act until amendments are made in accordance with Akal Takht's directives.The committee members maintained that despite being given a month's ultimatum on June 29 to address objections concerning the custodian clause and other religious provisions, the government had taken no concrete steps either to amend the law or suspend its implementation.

headline: Punjab begins process to bring 1,719 outsourced PRTC employees under contract
content: The Punjab Government has begun the process of bringing 1,719 outsourced employees of the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) under contract.Finance and Transport Minister Harpal Singh Cheema on Tuesday handed over appointment letters to 104 employees from various depots at a function held at the PRTC's Sangrur depot.Congratulating the employees, Cheema said the government, led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, was committed to providing them with job security, dignity and better service conditions.Addressing mediapersons, the minister said the government had enacted legislation to fulfil the long-pending demand of outsourced employees.With the stipulated 90-day process under the law completed, the exercise to bring eligible employees under contract had commenced.He said appointment letters were being prepared after completing departmental formalities, including verification of service records, medical examinations and police verification.The entire exercise would be carried out transparently and in accordance with rules, he added.Cheema said previous governments had ignored the demands of outsourced employees, forcing them to stage repeated protests and strikes. The present government, he said, had taken legal measures to safeguard their interests.He urged the employees to perform their duties with dedication, honesty and responsibility.Earlier, the minister conducted surprise inspections of offices of the GST and Excise Department in Sangrur. Several employees were found absent, following which attendance registers were taken into custody for verification.Cheema said strict action would be taken against those found absent without authorisation after an inquiry. He added that negligence and dereliction of duty in government offices would not be tolerated.PRTC Managing Director Jashanpreet Kaur Gill, Sangrur General Manager Maninderpal Singh Sidhu, OSD to the Finance Minister Tapinder Singh Sohi, departmental officials and employees were present at the function.Alternative headline: 104 PRTC employees get appointment letters as Punjab starts regularisation processSubhead: State government begins exercise to bring 1,719 outsourced workers under contract; Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema launches drive at Sangrur depot.

headline: 1+1=11 — BJP-Akali Dal reunion is powered by old chemistry, new energy
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal have formally revived their political alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Rival parties swiftly criticised the tie-up, with the Aam Aadmi Party calling it a power-driven pact. ThePrint asks: Is the Akali Dal-BJP tie-up good for Punjab or cynical, unprincipled politics? In the political arena, ‘1+1=11’ is considered one of the most formidable mathematical equations. This equation aptly explains the BJP-SAD reunion after six years. The tie-up is powered by old chemistry and renewed energy. It is a ‘3S’ alliance—stable, solid, and solution-oriented—with a common mission to restore Punjab’s glory. From the standpoint of political chemistry, the BJP and the Akali Dal have a long history of serving Punjab together, strengthening communal harmony and delivering development. From the standpoint of electoral arithmetic, their combined vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in Punjab stood at approximately 32 per cent, translating into nearly 43 lakh votes—almost six percentage points ahead of the AAP. In today’s political scenario, amid growing anger over the AAP’s unfulfilled promises and Congress resembling a pack of tired horses pulling in different directions, the NDA’s promise is to provide Punjab with a stable vehicle of governance, firmly steered toward its destination of peace, progress, and prosperity. Today, Punjab needs a decisive government that tackles the menace of drugs, gangsterism, and deteriorating law and order with an iron fist, rather than the butterfingers approach adopted by the AAP.

headline: Punjab’s Solar & Storage Industry Gathers in Ludhiana Tomorrow for the Solar & Storage Show 2026
content: Ludhiana, Punjab, 25 November 2026 — Punjab’s solar and power industry will gather tomorrow, 26 November, at Regenta Central Klassik for the Solar & Storage Show 2026 – Ludhiana. Organised by FirstVIEW, the one-day event will bring policymakers, utility representatives, developers, manufacturers and industrial energy buyers together to discuss how Punjab can expand solar adoption and where storage can help meet demand for reliable power. Shri Tarunpreet Singh Sondh, Cabinet Minister, Government of Punjab, will join the event as Chief Guest. The show will also welcome two esteemed Guests of Honour — Shri Supinder Singh, Director, Punjab Energy Development Agency (PEDA), and Shri Jagdev Singh Hans, Chief Engineer – Electrical, Punjab State Power Corporation Ltd. (PSPCL). Their participation brings the state’s renewable energy agency and power utility into the same forum as the businesses developing and delivering projects across Punjab. The conference will feature two insightful panel discussions under the theme “Shaping Ludhiana’s Energy Future: Progressive Policies, Innovation-Driven Growth & Sustainable Economic Prosperity.” The programme will feature 20+ speakers, with discussions spanning rooftop solar, open access, hybrid power, commercial and industrial energy solutions, agrivoltaics and energy storage. For Punjab’s manufacturers, the discussions will address a practical question — how can industrial facilities use solar and storage to meet their power needs? For developers, EPC companies and installers, the panels will offer perspectives on how policy and technology choices influence projects, from factory rooftops to agricultural sites. The exhibition showcase will feature 25+ exhibitors presenting solar and energy storage products, technologies and services. Industrial buyers and project teams will be able to compare offerings and discuss site requirements directly with the companies supplying the equipment. For manufacturers and technology providers, the exhibition offers an opportunity to hear what buyers need for upcoming installations and identify potential EPC and distribution partners. With 300+ industry attendees expected, top-tier networking will be a central part of the Ludhiana gathering. Developers, EPC companies, manufacturers, installers and project consultants will have opportunities to meet policymakers, utility representatives and commercial buyers. Conversations can continue beyond the panels and onto the exhibition floor, where participants can discuss specific projects, sourcing requirements and partnerships in Punjab.

headline: Akali Dal needs BJP’s money and resources to fight Punjab polls
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal have formally revived their age-old political alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, six years after splitting over farm laws. ThePrint asks: Is the Akali Dal-BJP tie-up good for Punjab or cynical, unprincipled politics? Any party has the right to enter into an alliance with other parties. If two parties feel that they cannot come to power on their own, they have every right to enter into an alliance to transfer each other’s votes and do better in elections. This is not unprincipled. The Akali Dal and the BJP have an age-old alliance. They came together in 1967, soon after Punjab was created in 1966, and have been together at different points since then. This alliance has suited both parties because the Akali Dal basically has a rural base. It is supposed to be a farmers’ party, a Sikh party, while the BJP is traditionally an urban-based party—a Hindu party. In that way, they complement each other. It is a natural alliance, though they have different agendas. The BJP believes in a centralising agenda, whereas the Akali Dal has always stood for autonomy and demanded greater powers for the states. The Akali Dal was more desperate for this alliance. It has lost four elections—in 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024—and has been out of power for more than ten years. You need resources and money to fight elections. Having a big brother like the BJP, which is resourceful in every sense, is always helpful. But how long this alliance will continue is uncertain. If the BJP feels it is not gaining much from the Akali Dal’s vote transfer, the alliance may break. The alliance was good for Punjab in 1997 because the state had just come out of militancy. There was a need to bring communal harmony and bring Hindus and Sikhs together. Right now, there are concerns about separatist and ethnic agendas in Punjab. Two people who won the 2024 elections, including Amritpal Singh, have an agenda which is quite separatist. In that sense, the alliance could be good for Punjab because both parties would be constrained from taking up ethnic or regional agendas. That is the coalition dharma.

headline: Punjab: AAP sarpanch, husband unhurt in Tarn Taran firing incident; BJP attacks AAP govt
content: Tarn Taran, Nov 25 (PTI) An AAP sarpanch and her husband had a narrow escape after some assailants opened fire at them near a road junction in Daleke village here, police said on Wednesday. The sarpanch said the attack was due to her husband’s anti-drug activism, which prompted the BJP to corner the ruling AAP over the issue. The incident took place on Tuesday when Sukhbir Singh, the husband of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Sarpanch Manjit Kaur, was intercepted by the assailants, according to police. Kaur said she was riding pillion on Singh’s motorcycle when the assailants allegedly fired four gunshots. Tarn Taran Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Surendra Lamba said none of the bullets hit Singh. The assailants fled the scene after the attack. The SSP said the accused have been identified and they have criminal records. They were also involved in a personal dispute with the victim and his family, he said, adding that they will be arrested soon.

headline: NDA-SAD reunion: Why the Akali Dal severed ties with BJP 6 years ago
content: Six years after parting ways over differences on the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), have reunited ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections in 2027. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the development as an effort to place Punjab and the welfare of its people above all else. After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election storyline 1 Why did the SAD walk out of the NDA? The SAD and the BJP had been allies since the late 1990s. However, amid widespread protests against the Centre’s farm laws, the SAD severed ties with the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 2020. Subsequently, on November 19, 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the three farm laws. The SAD exited the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal also resigning from the Union Council of Ministers in protest against the legislation, which sought to overhaul agricultural marketing and triggered months-long demonstrations at Delhi’s borders. Responding to questions about the party’s current stand on the farm laws, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) there was little relevance in revisiting the issue since the legislation had already been withdrawn. The laws under contention were the Farmers’ Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020; the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020; and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020. Together, they sought to remove restrictions on the stocking, contracting and purchase of agricultural commodities. Amid protests from Opposition parties and farmers, particularly in Punjab, both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha passed the Farm Laws Repeal Bill without discussion on the opening day of the Winter Session in December 2021. Subsequently, the Law Ministry notified the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021, nullifying the three farm laws enacted by Parliament in 2020. The move came after President Ram Nath Kovind gave his assent to the Bill, completing the process of repealing the contentious legislation. Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning Had they contested separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals; united, they have become serious contenders Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning storyline 1 Opposition attacks renewed alliance The Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have criticised the renewed alliance, alleging that the two parties have put political convenience above Punjab’s interests. Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement storyline 1 Former Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and former Union Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal of presenting a misleading picture by publicly distancing themselves from the BJP while backing it on important issues in Parliament. Mr. Warring contended that, despite their formal split in 2020 over the farm laws, the two parties had remained politically aligned and had now come together again after losing electoral ground in Punjab. Describing the alliance as a “thaggjod” (an alliance of deceivers), Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann urged voters not to place their trust in the two parties again. He alleged that the previous SAD-BJP government, which was in office from 2007 to 2017, failed to curb the drug menace and did not act decisively on incidents of sacrilege reported in 2015. Watch: Punjab elections 2027: Can the Akali Dal regain lost ground with the BJP? | Above the Fold | Nov 24, 2026 Watch: Punjab elections 2027: Can the Akali Dal regain lost ground with the BJP? | Above the Fold | Nov 24, 2026 The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal will contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, marking the SAD’s return to the NDA after six years. What does the alliance mean for Punjab’s electoral politics? Watch: Punjab elections 2027: Can the Akali Dal regain lost ground with the BJP? | Above the Fold | Nov 24, 2026 video 1 A chance for SAD revival? In Punjab, where Panthic politics, rooted in the collective identity of the Sikh community, continues to play a pivotal role, the revival of the alliance could benefit the SAD, which has struggled to regain its political footing in recent years. Political observers believe that if the party’s core support base sees a realistic path to power in 2027 through its renewed partnership with the BJP, that perception itself could help draw voters back to the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led SAD. Over the past decade, the SAD has witnessed a marked decline in Punjab politics, where issues linked to Sikh identity remain central to public discourse. At the same time, various Akali factions have competed to occupy the Panthic space. In 2025, the SAD effectively split after a rebel faction launched a separate outfit, Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). Separately, Waris Punjab De, led by independent Lok Sabha MP Amritpal Singh, who is currently lodged in Dibrugarh jail in Assam under the National Security Act, has steadily expanded its support base within the Panthic constituency. Observers attribute part of this rise to the weakening influence of the SAD.

headline: BJP, Akali Dal join hands for Punjab elections six years after split | India News
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced they would contest the 2027 Punjab assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after six years when the Akali Dal broke away from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 2020.The two parties didn’t share details of a seat-sharing agreement but people aware of developments said the BJP may contest 40-45 seats. If this holds, it’ll be the largest share of seats contested by the BJP in alliance in the state. The two parties aim to dislodge the Aam Aadmi Party from power in a contest where the Congress is also hoping to win power.Union home minister Amit Shah, who along with SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, announced the alliance at the BJP headquarters, also ended speculation about the chief ministerial candidate.“Akali Dal will remain in the role of elder brother. Akali Dal and BJP will fight together. Both the parties will contest together on all 117 seats. But Akali Dal will take the role of elder brother,” Shah said.“The elder brother is the one who becomes the chief minister,” he added.He said that after Prime Minister Narendra Modi was apprised about the “NDA’s expansion”, he called Badal with great joy. The PM also called Nabin and expressed his sentiments, saying the NDA was “now complete with Badal saheb’s party,” the home minister added. After the formal announcement, Modi said he was confident that the coalition will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab.“Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji,” Modi said on X.“Nurtured by Atal Ji, Advani Ji and Sardar Parkash Singh Badal Ji, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. I am confident that our alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab,” he added. The SAD is one of the BJP’s oldest allies. The two parties joined hands in 1996 when the party patriarch Parkash Singh Badal announced support for the BJP after the 1996 general elections, and a formal alliance was announced ahead of the 1997 Punjab assembly polls.The two parties, which contested the 2022 assembly elections separately, ended with the SAD winning just three seats and the BJP two, in the 117-member assembly. The alliance fell apart in September 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA. Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal also resigned from the Union cabinet in opposition to the Centre’s three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.The AAP, Congress and farm unions criticised the alliance.Shah, credited with working out the contours of the reunion, referred to the alliance as a favourable partnership and said it would be a “symbol of Hindu-Sikh bhaichara” (amity). He also asserted that unlike the Congress and the AAP, the NDA will crack down on drugs and corruption in the state.“Our priority will be eradicating drugs, ending corruption and improving security in this border state… Kejriwal had promised drug abuse would be eradicated in three months, nothing happened. Rahul Gandhi also made a similar promise but did not do anything. We have a roadmap for jobs and employment of the youth. The AAP government has not fulfilled any promise. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free,” he said.Shah said a detailed manifesto – which will pave the way for the development of every section including farmers, businessmen and young people – will be finalised soon. Responding to a question about apprehensions regarding Hindu-Sikh amity in the state, Shah said there was no problem and a strong NDA will ensure no scope for “any party to create a rift”.BJP chief Nitin Nabin said the two parties were “natural allies” and reiterated Shah’s statement that the alliance will “promote Hindu Sikh Ekta (unity)...”Badal – whose meeting with Modi during the monsoon session of Parliament had sparked speculation about the merger – said the “relationship that was forged” by his father Parkash Singh Badal and Vajpayee and Advani was revived.“First the Congress and then the AAP destroyed the state. Gangsters are ruling, I have never seen such chaos anywhere else. We need to save the farmers, the businesses and all this can be done by a double engine government,” he said.According to party leaders, the reunion was preceded by discussions within the BJP about the merit of joining hands with the SAD.“We conducted extensive surveys to assess the mood on the ground… Initially our cadre was not in favour of SAD being back in the NDA, there were some voices against the BJP assuming the role of the junior partner, but eventually it was decided that for the benefit of the state and its people, the BJP will let the SAD play big brother,” said a senior party leader.The leader said issues of national security prevailed to a large extent in deciding the contours of the alliance. “The home minister was emphatic that we cannot allow politics to overshadow national concerns. Punjab is a border state, grappling with corruption, drug mafia, lawlessness and joblessness. In the best interest of the people it was necessary that the state get a stable government and parties that put the nation first come together,” the leader said.Asked whether the BJP found it difficult to gain a foothold in the state after the prolonged protest over the farm laws, the leader said, “In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls the BJP’s vote percentage grew from 9.63% (in 2019) to 18.5%. It is true we did not convert the votes into seats, but it will be wrong to assume that there is no acceptance [for the BJP].”In 2019, the BJP won two of the 13 Lok Sabha seats but zero in 2024. The SAD won two in 2019 and one in 2024.The two parties had also explored the possibility of joining hands before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, but talks fell through due to disagreements over the proposed alliance terms. Discussions about a reunion gathered pace again in recent months, particularly after Shah repeatedly said the NDA would form the next government in Punjab. The partnership, which saw the two parties govern Punjab for 15 years across three five-year terms, came apart in September 2020 when the Akalis walked out of the NDA.The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Congress leaders hit out at the move, calling it an “opportunistic” bid for power.“This alliance...is not for Punjab, but a ‘thug pact’ to save their own families and seats,” CM Bhagwant Mann said.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal said, “They come together for the sake of power, then they part ways, and then they come together again.”Punjab Congress President Pargat Singh said the “biggest lie” told on Gurpurab concerned the alliance. Congress’s Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot called it a prime example of “opportunism.”“It existed all along, but has only been announced today,” he said, adding that the BJP and SAD had now “joined AAP in the same category of politics of deception.”He also called it a “compromise alliance, an alliance born of necessity, because neither party has explained why they split six years ago.”

headline: Punjab Roadways, PRTC workers defer three-day strike after govt assurance
content: Contractual employees of Punjab Roadways and Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) have postponed their three-day statewide strike scheduled to begin on November 25 following fresh assurances from the state transport department.The decision was taken by the Punjab Roadways, Punbus and PRTC Contract Workers Union after telephonic discussions between its representatives and senior transport department officials on Tuesday evening.Shamsher Singh Dhillon, general secretary of the union said, "We have decided to wait until Wednesday afternoon for the government to fulfil its commitments before deciding its next course of action.He said the Secretary, State Transport and the Director, State Transport, had assured that contract numbers will be allotted to outsourced employees of Punbus and PRTC on Wednesday and their agreements will be issued immediately." The union also said a meeting with the Transport Minister had been scheduled for November 27 to discuss and resolve its remaining demands.The strike had been announced over the delay in implementing assurances given by the state government during previous meetings. The employees had been demanding regularisation with appointment letters distributed only to employees at the Chandigarh depot while those posted at other depots were still awaiting completion of the process.In an earlier video statement, Resham Singh Gill, state president of the union, had said employees had met Transport Minister Harpal Singh Cheema in Chandigarh on Monday, following which appointment letters were issued to Punbus and PRTC employees at the Chandigarh depot. However, the department had yet to complete the process for employees at other depots.The employees are seeking regularisation of thousands of contractual and outsourced workers employed as drivers, conductors and workshop staff, many of whom have been working for more than a decade. Their other demands include an end to recruitment through third party contractors and withdrawal of FIRs registered against employees during previous protests.

headline: Tankeshwar Kumar assumes charge as Panjab University vice chancellor
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (PTI) Professor Tankeshwar Kumar on Wednesday assumed charge as vice chancellor of Panjab University (PU), Chandigarh. Professor Meenakshi Goyal, Dean of University Instruction (DUI), who had been holding the additional charge of vice chancellor, handed over the charge to Kumar, according to an official statement. Kumar was appointed vice chancellor of the university on November 9 by the office of the vice president, who is the chancellor of PU. He will serve a three-year term from the date of assuming charge. Goyal had been discharging the duties of vice chancellor after the tenure of former vice chancellor Professor Renu Vig ended on July 28. Kumar has over three decades of experience in teaching and research, besides extensive experience in university administration. He has served as vice chancellor of Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology in Hisar, Haryana, and Central University of Haryana. He also has a long association with Panjab University, where he served in the Department of Physics for more than two decades.

headline: BJP govt working tirelessly to translate Guru Ravidas’ vision of ‘Begumpura’ into reality: Saini
content: Kurukshetra, Nov 25 (PTI) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Wednesday said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the ‘double-engine’ government of the BJP is working tirelessly and with unwavering commitment to translate Guru Ravidas’ vision of ‘Begumpura’ into reality. Saini was addressing a ceremony organised at Umri in Kurukshetra to welcome the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra being undertaken to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas. Earlier, the Chief Minister welcomed the Yatra upon its arrival at Umri. “The prime minister’s guiding mantra of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas’ is, in essence, a modern and practical manifestation of Guru Ravidas’ philosophy of social harmony and equality,” he said. Saini said the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra aims to take Guru Ravidas’ message of equality, social harmony, service, social justice and humanity to the last person in society and unite different sections of society in the spirit of social unity. He said the yatra, which commenced from Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Jalandhar on November 18, will cover approximately 2,402 kilometres over 16 days.

headline: Transport minister Nitin Gadkari urges states to adopt bike taxi guidelines for youth employment
content: New Delhi: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari on Wednesday said app-based aggregators and delivery services can create employment opportunities for Indian youth and urged states to implement the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines (MVAG) 2025, which permit private motorcycles to offer passenger rides through aggregator platforms.Addressing the 13th National Conference on Disability, Gadkari noted that after the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways issued the guidelines in July, only Rajasthan has implemented them fully, while Haryana and Uttar Pradesh have done so partially. “Only three states have allowed all non-transport (private) motorcycles for passenger rides through aggregator platforms. I am trying to convince all states to allow this,” he said..Bike taxi drivers, ride aggregators push for clear regulations after SC verdict.The MVAG 2025 provides regulatory clarity for India’s shared mobility sector, officially enabling states to permit non-transport motorcycles for passenger services. The move offers relief to bike-taxi operators such as Rapido and Uber, who had operated in a legal grey area, particularly in states like Karnataka where bans had sparked protests.Gadkari recently wrote to states seeking wider adoption. The guidelines aim to reduce traffic congestion and pollution while providing affordable mobility, hyperlocal delivery and livelihood opportunities under a light-touch regulatory framework focused on safety and driver welfare. They revise the 2020 guidelines to keep pace with the rapid growth of bike-sharing, electric vehicles and other flexible mobility options.

headline: Turned down over one inch in 1998, he fought for ASI’s post for 28 years. HC has now fined him Rs 1 lakh
content: Chandigarh: Sub Inspector Prem Dutt died on 4 February 1995 while posted at the Ambala Range of the Haryana Police. His family wanted a job for his eldest son, Rohtash Kumar. It has taken 31 years, at least five court cases and one Supreme Court appeal to reach the end of that file. Rohtash’s mother applied under the state’s ex-gratia scheme. The son was a graduate, so the family sought the post one step below his father’s, that of Assistant Sub Inspector (ASI). The department returned the first application in August 1996, saying he did not meet the physical standards. A second representation followed in 1997. In March 1998, Haryana offered him an ASI’s post in the Haryana Armed Police. He refused. He wrote that he wanted the district police cadre in Ambala instead. In August that year, he was called for a physical test. In September, he wrote back asking for more time, citing family responsibilities as the eldest son. In February 1999, the department said he would be offered a clerk’s job, as his measurements were below the prescribed standards. He challenged that order in the High Court. In March 2002, the court directed that he be sent to a medical board and a recruiting board and appointed if found fit. A civil surgeon in Rohtak certified him medically fit for the ASI post. The Director General of Police still rejected him on 1 July 2002. The rules specify a minimum height of 5 feet 7 inches and a chest of 33 inches, expanding to 34½. Rohtash was 5 feet 6 inches, with a chest of 31 inches, expanding to 32½. He went back to the High Court. In May 2003, a Division Bench dismissed his petition. It recorded that no relaxation in physical standards was permissible for the post of ASI. The Supreme Court dismissed his special leave petition in December 2003 without issuing notice.

headline: 805 CM announcements still pending, 339 declared unfeasible in Haryana
content: Manvir.saini@timesofindia.comChandigarh, November 25: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini’s directive to officials to expedite implementation of development announcements has once again brought the state government’s mounting backlog of unfulfilled political promises into focus, with 805 announcements still pending and another 339 declared unfeasible despite claims that departmental feasibility is obtained before such commitments are made.Of the 7,988 announcements made by successive governments during visits to Assembly constituencies, 5,743 have been completed, while work on 1,101 is stated to be progressing. However, the remaining 1,144 announcements either continue to hang fire or have been abandoned as unfeasible. The backlog also includes announcements dating back to the tenure of former chief minister and now Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar, indicating that the problem predates the present government.The figures raise questions over the process through which political announcements are made, their financial viability and the accountability of departments that give feasibility clearances but subsequently cite hurdles in execution.At a review meeting at Sant Kabir Kutir on Wednesday, Saini directed officers to accord priority to announcements made during rallies and public programmes and complete them within stipulated timelines. He warned that laxity in implementation would not be tolerated and asked MLAs to coordinate with departments to resolve bottlenecks.Interestingly, the Chief Minister himself acknowledged that announcements cleared as feasible by departments sometimes subsequently become unviable because of non-availability of land or other reasons. This admission puts the spotlight on the adequacy of preliminary scrutiny before political commitments are made.Officials, while acknowledging delays and announcements that cannot be implemented, have largely attributed the situation to technical constraints, financial implications, land-related issues and the need for timely amendments to the original proposals. However, the explanations leave unanswered why such considerations were not adequately examined before the announcements were made and feasibility was certified.The 339 announcements declared unfeasible also represent commitments that will not translate into development works, raising questions about whether affected constituencies and legislators have been formally informed about their abandonment and what alternatives, if any, have been proposed.The review was followed by department-wise discussions across 17 roundtables, where MLAs and senior officers examined the status of constituency-specific announcements and identified hurdles. The decisions and action points are to be compiled for follow-up and regular monitoring.The government has also reviewed departmental budget allocations and expenditure to ensure optimum utilisation of resources. However, the immediate challenge remains translating announcements into completed projects rather than allowing political commitments to remain on official files across successive governments.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
