headline: Haryana Assembly session set for stormy debate as Congress plans Panchkula showdown
content: Manvir.Saini@timesofindia.comChandigarh: Haryana’s special Assembly session on Thursday is set to witness a political contest over the Constitution, electoral rights and the state’s development, with the Opposition preparing to use the occasion to corner the BJP government even as Speaker Harvinder Kalyan has urged legislators to rise above party politics and make the discussion meaningful.The Congress is gearing up for an aggressive show of strength, with Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda, AICC in-charge Sanjay Dutt and HPCC president Rao Narender Singh scheduled to chair the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) meeting ahead of the session. The meeting is expected to finalise the party’s legislative strategy and coordinate its campaign on alleged electoral irregularities, unemployment, farmers’ problems and other public issues.The Congress has already announced a massive Samvidhan Raksha March in Panchkula on November 26 as part of its ongoing Vote Bachao–Desh Bachao campaign. The party intends to link the alleged deletion of voters’ names and concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls with what it describes as the larger battle to protect constitutional institutions and democratic rights. Its parallel Vote Rakshak Abhiyan is aimed at identifying and verifying cases of alleged wrongful deletion of names.The INLD, which has two members in the House, is also expected to raise farmers’ concerns and unemployment, seeking to bring agrarian distress and the lack of job opportunities into the debate. Its intervention could add another dimension to the Opposition’s attempt to make the session politically consequential.On the other hand, Kalyan has consistently advocated a constructive discussion on Haryana’s 60-year journey since its formation, highlighting the contribution of prominent political leaders, public representatives and institutions to the state’s development. He has appealed to members across party lines to participate actively and rise above political differences.The Speaker has emphasised that the session should reinforce constitutional values, parliamentary traditions and public faith in democratic institutions. He has also stressed the responsibility of elected representatives to create awareness about citizens’ constitutional rights and duties.The Business Advisory Committee (BAC), which deliberates on the conduct and scheduling of Assembly proceedings, has been involved in settling the programme for the special sitting. The announced schedule provides for obituary references at 11 am, followed by a 75-minute adjournment for a special Constitution Day programme. The House will reconvene at 12.30 pm. No separate item-wise political debate schedule has been publicly detailed.The special programme will include tributes to Dr BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, screening of a documentary on the making of the Constitution and presentation of Hindi and English copies of the Constitution to legislators.With the Congress planning a parallel show of strength in Panchkula and the INLD preparing to flag agrarian and employment concerns, the challenge before the Speaker will be to maintain the commemorative character of the sitting while ensuring that the House reflects the democratic spirit and public issues it is meant to represent.

headline: Saini to lead Haryana investment mission to UK, Germany from Nov 28
content: Chandigarh: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini will lead a high-level delegation to the UK and Germany from Nov 28 to Dec 5 to attract global investments, explore industrial partnerships and strengthen cooperation in emerging technologies, education and skill development.The eight-day visit will include meetings with leading global companies, investors, industrialists, universities and research institutions. Industries and commerce minister Rao Narbir Singh and senior departmental officials will accompany the CM.A key highlight of the CM’s visit will be a Haryana investment roadshow in Germany on Dec 2, aimed at showcasing the state’s industrial infrastructure, investor-friendly policies, connectivity and skilled workforce to European investors.The delegation will also explore opportunities for long-term business partnerships and setting up industrial units in Haryana.The commissioner and secretary, industries and commerce, Amit Kumar Agrawal, said the visit was part of govt’s sustained efforts to position Haryana as a global investment destination. Previous delegations led by Saini to Japan, Singapore and Sweden had secured MoUs and investment proposals worth over Rs 10,000 crore, he added.During the UK leg, Saini will hold one-to-one meetings with leading companies, investors and educational institutions on Nov 30 and Dec 1. Discussions with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) delegation will focus on investment opportunities and industrial cooperation.The delegation will also explore trade and investment opportunities under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), besides cooperation in education, vocational training and skill development. The CM will invite UK MPs and other prominent representatives to Haryana’s proposed Global Investors Summit in April 2027.The CM’s engagements will include meetings with representatives of the Centre for Science and Policy at the University of Cambridge, interaction with Indian students at Oxford University and a visit to Queen Elizabeth’s School, Barnet, to explore educational cooperation, including the possibility of setting up an educational campus in Haryana.Saini will also participate in a special International Gita Jayanti Mahotsav celebration in London to showcase Haryana’s cultural and spiritual heritage.In Germany, the focus will be on research, innovation and advanced technology. On Dec 3, Saini will meet representatives of Fraunhofer, a leading German research institution, to discuss setting up a centre of excellence in Haryana. An MoU is also proposed to be signed for the initiative, which will focus on microelectronics and energy storage.The CM will hold further meetings with German companies and potential investors on Dec 4 and 5 to explore investment prospects and industrial collaboration.

headline: Bihar, Haryana and UP lead India's company boom as active firms grow 12%
content: India is witnessing a fresh wave of entrepreneurship, with new company registrations rising 37% in FY26 and the number of active businesses increasing 12% year-on-year, according to an Axis Capital report. The investment bank's report, *India's enterprise wave – Everything, everywhere, all at once*, estimates that India had 2.1 million active companies in FY26, with 248,000 new companies added during the year. The total paid-up capital of active companies stood at ₹68.6 trillion. The expansion is being driven by lower borrowing costs, improved access to equity and debt funding, infrastructure development and policy support, the report said. It also points to a geographical shift, with states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Haryana recording some of the strongest growth in company formation. But the report also highlights a critical distinction: a rising number of companies does not automatically translate into higher productivity, stronger investment or wealth creation. India continues to have significantly fewer companies relative to its economic size and population than several major economies. Meanwhile, investment by existing companies remains below historical levels, and weak net foreign direct investment (FDI) could constrain the next phase of expansion. Key highlights: Surge in entrepreneurship: Active companies in India grew 12% YoY in FY26, while new company registrations increased 37% YoY, reaching approximately 248,000 new companies. Improved access to capital: Lower borrowing costs, stronger PSU bank balance sheets, increased NBFC lending to MSMEs and greater availability of public and private risk capital have supported business expansion and new company formation. Emerging business hubs: Previously untapped states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Haryana are witnessing strong entrepreneurial growth. Improvements in infrastructure, electricity, connectivity, and credit availability are supporting this expansion. Sectoral growth opportunities: Growth is broadening across services and manufacturing, with sectors such as electronics, automobiles, EVs, textiles, defence, industrials, utilities, NBFCs and real estate expected to benefit. Company registrations rise 37%, active businesses grow 12% The pace of company formation has accelerated sharply after nearly two decades of relatively subdued growth. India added approximately 248,000 companies in FY26, taking the number of active companies to 2.1 million. New company registrations rose 37% year-on-year, while active companies grew 12% as closures moderated. The report describes the current expansion as a break from the slower growth seen during the 2000s and 2010s. Company formation was particularly strong in the 1980s and 1990s, when active companies grew at a compound annual growth rate of around 14% and 10%, respectively. Growth slowed in subsequent decades, partly because of company closures and weaker new registrations. The current decade has seen a revival, with company formation supported by lower capital costs, improved infrastructure and policy reforms. However, the figures also show that India remains under-represented in terms of its corporate base. The country has around 2.1 million active companies, compared with 33.2 million in the US and 55.5 million in China, according to the report's country comparison. India has approximately 537 companies per $1 billion of GDP, compared with 1,138 in the US, 2,962 in China and 1,959 in Vietnam. The report also estimates that India has 1,457 companies per million people, among the lowest levels in its comparison of major economies. This suggests that the expansion of the corporate sector could remain a long-term growth driver, provided new companies become productive, scale up and generate sustainable employment. Smaller states emerge as new entrepreneurial hubs One of the most interesting findings is the geographical broadening of company formation. Maharashtra continues to have the largest number of active companies, with 397,713 as of June 2026. Delhi had 272,924, while Uttar Pradesh had 187,447. But the fastest growth is increasingly coming from states that historically had a smaller corporate base. Bihar recorded a 15% compound annual growth rate in active companies between 2015 and 2026, followed by Haryana and Uttar Pradesh at 13% each. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recorded growth of 11% and 10%, respectively, while Kerala's active company stock grew at 10%. The report's state-level data also shows that Uttar Pradesh added 27,934 new firms in the 12 months to June 2026, while Haryana added 13,012 and Bihar 8,909. Maharashtra remained the largest contributor in absolute terms, with 41,433 new firms added during the period. The growth is being supported by the emergence of new industrial and commercial hubs, better road connectivity, electricity access, water infrastructure and improved access to credit. Axis Capital's analysis of satellite night-light data between 2012 and 2024 found a broadening of economic activity across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi-NCR and southern India. Bihar recorded a 21% compound annual growth rate in night-time light intensity over the period, while Kerala recorded 16%. The report also found that credit demand, power consumption and e-way bill activity had improved across several of these states over the past decade. Services account for two-thirds of active companies The corporate expansion is not limited to manufacturing. Services account for around 67% of India's active companies and contributed 71% of the year-on-year increase in active companies in FY26. Within services, business services account for 38% of active companies, followed by trading at 21% and community and personal services at 22%. Community and personal services include businesses such as schools, hospitals and salons. The report found that the fastest growth in services was in community and personal services, trading and transport. The number of active service companies grew at a compound annual rate of 10% between 2020 and 2026, compared with 5% between 2015 and 2020. Personal and social services accounted for 28% of the incremental increase in active companies in FY26. The shift is significant because it points to a broader entrepreneurial base, with businesses emerging beyond large technology companies and established corporate groups. However, the report notes that services companies generally have lower paid-up capital per company than manufacturing and mining businesses. Manufacturing growth accelerates, led by metals, chemicals and machinery Manufacturing is also showing signs of a revival. The number of active manufacturing companies grew at a compound annual rate of 8% between 2020 and 2026, compared with 2% in the previous five-year period. The growth was broad-based across food processing, metals and chemicals, machinery and equipment. Metals and chemicals account for 34% of active manufacturing companies, followed by machinery and equipment at 24%, food processing at 16% and textiles at 12%. But the distribution of capital is much more concentrated. Metals and chemicals, along with machinery and equipment, account for more than 84% of total paid-up capital in manufacturing. The report also highlights the relatively high economic contribution of manufacturing companies. Manufacturing generated ₹288 million in gross value added per company in FY24, compared with ₹67 million across all companies. Gross value added is a measure of the economic value created by a business and is an important indicator of its contribution to GDP. This difference suggests that the economic impact of company formation will depend not only on how many firms are created, but also on the sectors in which they operate. Private companies dominate, but public firms hold most of the capital India's corporate base is overwhelmingly private. Private companies account for 96% of active firms, while public companies make up just 4%. Between 2011 and 2026, private companies grew at a compound annual rate of 8%, compared with 2% for public companies. The report attributes the faster growth of private firms partly to lower initial capital requirements and a lighter compliance burden. However, the distribution of paid-up capital tells a very different story. Public companies account for 61% of total paid-up capital, while private companies account for 39%. The average paid-up capital of a public company was ₹550 million, compared with ₹13 million for a private company. This highlights the difference between the number of businesses and the amount of capital deployed in the corporate sector. The report also found that paid-up capital grew at a compound annual rate of 10% for private companies and 8% for public companies between FY22 and FY26. For private companies, the growth was largely driven by the addition of new firms. For public companies, it was more strongly linked to an increase in capital per company. Lower borrowing costs and record equity fundraising support the boom The report identifies improved access to capital as one of the key drivers of company formation. The weighted average lending rate on corporate loans declined by around two percentage points over the past decade, while the cost of equity also fell as market valuations increased. Only around 3% of outstanding credit to industry was priced at interest rates above 12%, according to the report. Equity capital market fundraising has also increased sharply. Annual equity capital market transactions averaged around ₹2 trillion between 2020 and 2024, compared with ₹700 billion between 2012 and 2019. Fundraising reached a record ₹3.5 trillion in 2024. The report said the bulk of the transactions were through initial public offerings and qualified institutional placements, although some included offers for sale by promoters and private equity investors, which do not add fresh equity capital to the company. The expansion of funding has been supported by stronger public sector bank balance sheets, greater NBFC lending to MSMEs, government schemes and a larger pool of private and public risk capital. Corporate cash flows rise, but investment remains subdued A particularly important wealth-investment angle is the divergence between corporate cash generation and capital expenditure. Operating cash flow for BSE 200 companies, excluding financials, rose 25% year-on-year to ₹6 trillion in the first half of FY26. Profit before tax increased 23%, while revenue grew only 7%, indicating that stronger cash generation was partly supported by improved margins. However, capital expenditure was only 62% of operating cash flow, below the post-Covid range and well below levels seen between 2012 and 2016. Aggregate capital expenditure grew just 5% year-on-year. Excluding telecom and Reliance, capital expenditure growth was healthier at 15%, suggesting that the overall slowdown was largely driven by the completion of major 5G investments. The report said companies were increasingly using excess cash for acquisitions, with acquisition activity picking up over the past three years. For investors, this is an important distinction: companies are generating cash, but not all of it is being channelled into fresh productive capacity. Conglomerates diversify into new industries The report also highlights the growing role of large corporate groups in creating new businesses. Tata Group, Reliance Industries, Aditya Birla Group, Adani Group, JSW Group and Larsen & Toubro are expanding into newer sectors, including batteries, semiconductors, renewable energy, electric vehicles, technology and green hydrogen. The diversification is being supported by stronger operating cash flows and cleaner balance sheets, which allow companies to invest in new sectors without necessarily relying entirely on external funding. The report expects new company formation and higher paid-up capital to benefit sectors such as NBFCs, industrials, utilities and real estate. It also points to the potential for indirect gains in consumption as new businesses create employment and economic activity. FDI remains a major risk Despite the improvement in domestic capital availability, the report flags external capital flows as a significant near-term risk. Net FDI fell to $6.7 billion in FY26, compared with an average of around $30 billion between FY20 and FY24. Net capital inflows fell to just $235 million in the second quarter of FY26 as portfolio outflows surged and net FDI remained weak. The report said rising FDI repatriation had offset much of the fresh investment entering the country. The rupee also depreciated by around 8% in FY26, while higher global interest rates could put further pressure on India's cost of capital. There are signs of a recovery in gross FDI, with trailing 12-month flows reaching $14 billion as of August 2026. But the report cautions that higher borrowing costs in developed markets could continue to affect capital flows. The wealth creation challenge: more companies, but higher productivity The report's central message is that India needs to move beyond simply increasing the number of companies. The corporate sector has expanded, capital access has improved and economic activity is spreading across more states. But the long-term wealth impact will depend on whether these businesses can scale, invest, generate higher productivity and create sustainable employment. India's company count remains low relative to its GDP and population, while manufacturing and services companies differ significantly in capital intensity and economic contribution. The report also identifies persistent challenges, including bureaucracy, shortages of skilled labour and delays in government support, based on its field visits to Kanpur and Lucknow.

headline: The IFS officer who flagged illegal felling in Faridabad now finds himself facing the axe
content: Chandigarh: Early in the morning of 11 November, Jhalkar Uyake, the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF), Faridabad, visited the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserve Forest in the Bhopani forest block of Haryana. In a letter dated 12 November to the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF), Haryana, he wrote that he visited the reserve forest over apprehensions about the ongoing CAMPA-funded plantation work, and that he saw large-scale felling of mature green Kikar trees. CAMPA is an acronym for Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority, and it manages the money that companies and government agencies pay when forest land is given up for mines, roads or industry, and it is meant to be spent on raising new forests. But in an ironic turn of events, the very officer who raised the alarm over the felling of thousands of trees is now facing the axe himself. Uyake, a 2022-batch IFS officer, who sought action against three field officials, has now been recommended for dismissal by the very department he alerted. The three officials he named have since been dismissed, but the forest department has now accused him of conniving in the felling 2,585 trees in the reserve forest. The department alleges that nearly 25 acres of forest land were cleared and around 3,000 quintals of timber recovered. A senior forest department officer confirmed to ThePrint that the recommendation for Uyake’s dismissal has been sent to the state government. It will need the chief minister’s approval before it goes to the Centre. “Since the decision in case of an All India Services officer is to be taken by the Centre, the state government will send its recommendations to the Centre, in case the state government goes with the recommendations of the state forest department,” the officer said.

headline: CRSU Jind Teaching Recruitment 2026 Out - Apply Online for 68 Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professor Posts
content: Chaudhary Ranbir Singh University (CRSU), Jind, has released the CRSU Teaching Recruitment 2026 notification for 68 regular faculty vacancies across various academic departments. The recruitment includes Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor posts under Advertisement Nos. 01/2026 to 38/2026. Interested and eligible candidates can apply online through the official university website, crsu.ac.in, from 25 November 2026. The last date for online application submission is 16 December 2026 at 11:59 PM. According to the official Recruitment Bulletins 2026 (I) and (II), candidates must fulfil the relevant educational qualifications, teaching or research experience and other eligibility conditions. Applicants are also required to submit a printed copy of their completed online application with supporting documents to the university by 21 December 2026 at 5:00 PM. The recruitment covers multiple subjects, including Chemistry, Commerce, Computer Science, Economics, Education, English, History, Management, Mathematics, Psychology and other disciplines. CRSU published the teaching recruitment advertisements on 19 November 2026. The university has notified separate deadlines for online applications and submission of printed application forms. Important: Completing the online application alone is not sufficient. Candidates must also ensure that the printed application and supporting documents reach the university before the prescribed hard-copy submission deadline. Chaudhary Ranbir Singh University has advertised 68 faculty vacancies through two recruitment bulletins. Bulletin I covers Advertisement Nos. 01/2026 to 28/2026, while Bulletin II covers Advertisement Nos. 29/2026 to 38/2026. The university has provided subject-wise and category-wise reservation details separately for each advertisement. Applicants should check the relevant post code and reservation category before submitting the online form.

headline: How Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor could reshape NCR property market
content: The proposed Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor is drawing attention not only for its potential to shorten journeys across North India’s busiest economic belt, but also for the way it could influence the next phase of urban and real estate growth in the National Capital Region (NCR). Planned along the National Highway 44 axis, the 136.3-km corridor is intended to connect Delhi with Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. The project is estimated to cost about Rs 33,051 crore, with a target of completion by 2030, according to media reports. The proposed service is expected to bring the Delhi-Panipat journey (~90 km) closer to an hour and the Delhi-Karnal trip (~123 km) to around 90 minutes. The corridor should also be viewed as part of a wider regional network. Interchanges at Sarai Kale Khan and Kashmere Gate are intended to connect passengers with rail, bus and Metro services. In Haryana, links with industrial areas and road infrastructure could improve access to jobs and markets. The quality of these connections will determine how widely the benefits are distributed locally. How the corridor could reshape NCR's property market For the property market, the corridor could make locations farther from Delhi more attractive to people working in the capital and other NCR centres. Faster public transport can change the trade-off between workplace proximity, housing costs and living space, while making corridor locations more relevant to employers and service businesses. Growth is unlikely to be uniform. Areas close to stations, employment clusters and supporting roads may be better placed to attract demand. Schools, healthcare, retail, public spaces and last-mile transport will determine whether new catchments become liveable neighbourhoods or speculative propositions.Also read: India’s real estate market heads into 2027 with strong demand for premium housingRobin Mangla, President of M3M India, said the corridor could help integrate economic centres across the NCR and Haryana, gradually expanding the residential catchment for premium and luxury housing. He said improved access to employment and commercial hubs would give homebuyers greater commuting flexibility and convenience, while creating opportunities for developers to plan destinations around changing preferences. In the premium segment, he added, accessibility would need to be matched by quality and lifestyle offerings. TOD policy could guide development around stations In September 2026, Haryana brought the route within its Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) policy, which encourages a mix of housing, workplaces and services around mass-transit nodes. With clear land-use rules and civic infrastructure, the framework could channel growth towards station areas. Santosh Agarwal, Executive Director and CFO of Alpha Corp Development Limited, said the corridor, alongside expressways and other infrastructure, was improving the region’s accessibility and expanding its economic catchment. He said better links to emerging industrial and logistics hubs could support residential development beyond established urban pockets, with demand from both end-users and investors potentially strengthening as employment opportunities deepen. He expects the infrastructure pipeline to reshape the residential landscape across the Panipat-Karnal belt and open up new growth and investment opportunities. Project execution remains key That outlook will depend on execution. The National Capital Region Transport Corporation’s 2025-26 annual report said the revised detailed project report, incorporating the extension to Karnal and updated technical parameters, was awaiting approval from the Union government. It also noted that consultancy and enabling works had been awarded and were under way. However, preparatory work and inclusion under the TOD policy should not be mistaken for the commencement of full-scale construction or the start of commercial operations.Also read: India's realty investment hits Rs 57,917 crore, but affordable housing lagsFor developers, the corridor could broaden the geography for viable projects; for buyers, it may offer more choice between established NCR markets and emerging Haryana locations. But property appreciation is not guaranteed: Delivery timelines, station access, planning, utilities and the surrounding urban environment will shape outcomes. The larger test for the Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor, therefore, is whether faster regional mobility can be converted into balanced economic growth. If transport investment is supported by disciplined urban planning and job creation, the corridor could become more than a commuter link; it could help establish a connected network of residential and commercial centres across northern NCR.

headline: Haryana Recommends Termination of IFS Officer Jhalkar Uyake Over Felling of 2,585 Trees in Faridabad
content: Chandigarh: The Haryana Forest Department has recommended the termination of Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer Jhalkar Uyake over alleged negligence and involvement in the illegal felling of 2,585 trees in the Alipur-Sikargarh Reserved Forest in Faridabad. The recommendation has been forwarded to Sudhir Rajpal, Additional Chief Secretary, Environment, Forests and Wildlife, and is currently under consideration by the state government. If approved by the Chief Minister, the proposal will be sent to the Centre for a final decision on the officer's termination, according to a report by The Indian Express. Uyake, a 2022-batch IFS officer, was serving as Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF), Faridabad, when the alleged tree felling took place. He was suspended on November 18 under Rule 3(1) of the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969. 2,585 Trees Found Felled Across Nearly 25 Acres The investigation into the incident has revealed large-scale felling in the reserved forest area. Read Also: Haryana Forest Probe Uncovers 2,724 Quintals of Timber; IFS Officer Jhalkar Uyake Suspended According to officials, nearly 25 acres of forest land were allegedly cleared, with the number of felled trees initially estimated at around 2,000. A subsequent count established that 2,585 trees had been cut. A senior Forest Department officer also told The Indian Express that approximately 3,000 quintals of wood had been recovered. The alleged operation involved the felling of mature green kikar trees. Officials suspect that contractors engaged for plantation-related work may have carried out the activity in connivance with forest personnel responsible for protecting the reserved area. The plantation work was being undertaken under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) programme. Jhalkar Uyake Had Flagged Illegal Felling Before Suspension An important aspect of the case is that Uyake had reportedly raised concerns about the illegal tree felling before the government suspended him. In a communication dated November 12 addressed to Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) and Head of Forest Force K.C. Meena, Uyake flagged the large-scale cutting of mature trees in the reserved forest. He stated that during an inspection on the morning of November 11, he had noticed extensive felling at a site where CAMPA-funded plantation work was being undertaken across approximately 19 hectares. The project involved the proposed planting of around 64,000 saplings. Uyake reportedly suspected that the plantation activity was being used as a cover for commercial timber extraction. He also raised concerns that the illegal activity could have been continuing for nearly two months or may have started even before the contractor was awarded the work. In his communication, he alleged negligence and possible connivance involving Range Officer Afzal Khan and Foresters Ankit Kumar and Sandeep Kumar. He also pointed to discrepancies between the plantation progress reported by field staff and the actual condition of the site, raising concerns about possible manipulation of official records. Three Forest Officials Dismissed in the Case The investigation has also led to action against three other forest personnel. On November 20, the Haryana government dismissed Range Officer Afzal Khan, Forester Ankit Kumar and Forester Sandeep Kumar in connection with the alleged illegal felling. Their services were terminated by invoking Article 311(2)(b) of the Constitution, which permits dismissal without a regular departmental inquiry under specified circumstances. The government cited alleged connivance with contractors and the impracticability of conducting a regular inquiry. Earlier, Uyake had reportedly sought action against these officials, including their suspension pending investigation. FIR Registered as Forest Department Continues Investigation The Forest Department has also initiated criminal proceedings in the matter. Police have registered an FIR based on a complaint lodged by the department regarding the illegal felling. A team of senior Forest Department officers visited the Alipur Reserved Forest on Tuesday to assess the damage. The investigation has brought attention to alleged lapses in the protection of reserved forest land and the role of contractors and departmental personnel involved in plantation-related work. Final Decision on IFS Officer's Termination Awaited While the Forest Department has recommended termination of Uyake's services, the proposal has not yet received final approval. It is currently under consideration by the state government. If cleared by the Chief Minister, it will be referred to the Centre for a final decision. Uyake was not available for comment on the latest recommendation, according to sources. The case has therefore reached a new administrative stage, with the proposed termination of the IFS officer awaiting the prescribed state and central government decisions. headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM HARYANA STATE UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF C.M.SH.NAYAB SINGH SAINI AND OTHER NEWS
content: *Haryana's Global Investment Push to Gain Fresh Momentum- CM Nayab Singh Saini to Lead High-Level Delegation to UK and Germany* *Key Meetings with Leading Industrialists, Global Investors, Prestigious Universities and Research Institutions from November 28 to December 5* *Focus on Cooperation in Trade, Investment, Education, Skill Development and AI Technology; Haryana State Roadshow to Be Held in Germany* Chandigarh, November 25 – Taking Haryana’s investment outreach to key European markets, Chief Minister Sh. Nayab Singh Saini will lead a high-level delegation to the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany from November 28 to December 5, 2026. The visit marks a significant step in the state’s efforts to attract global capital, forge strategic industrial partnerships and strengthen its footprint in the international investment landscape. During the visit, the delegation will hold extensive deliberations with leading global companies, investors, prestigious universities, research and technology institutions and representatives from various sectors. Industries and Commerce Minister Rao Narbir Singh, along with senior officers of the department, will also be part of the delegation. Divulging more details, Commissioner and Secretary, Industries and Commerce Department, Dr. Amit Kumar Agrawal said the Haryana Government has been consistently working to establish the state as a major global investment destination. As part of these efforts, high-level delegations led by Chief Minister Sh. Nayab Singh Saini have previously visited Japan, Singapore and Sweden.

headline: Power drain : Jind exposes Haryana’s distribution failures
content: JIND’s staggering 36.68% aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) power losses expose the glaring inefficiencies in Haryana's electricity distribution system. The figure is particularly indefensible when compared with Gurugram-1, where losses are a mere 0.83%. Both circles fall under the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN), making the contrast a telling commentary on the disparity in distribution management. Jind’s line losses of 31.31% are equally alarming. This is not a problem that has surfaced overnight. The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC), in its March 2026 review, had identified Jind as the worst-performing circle, with distribution losses of 33.06% in 2024-25. Its recommendations included faster smart-meter installation, better energy accounting, replacement of defective meters and strengthening of distribution infrastructure. The persistence of such high losses suggests that regulatory warnings have not translated into effective corrective action.

headline: Jai Ram targets Sukhu government over closure of institutions | Hindustan Times
content: Leader of the Opposition and former chief minister Jai Ram Thakur, on Wednesday slammed the Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu-led government over the closure of institutions, decisions regarding old-age pensions, the Old Pension Scheme, and unfulfilled election guarantees.Terming Sukhu the “Taale wala Mukhyamantri”, Thakur, speaking at a felicitation ceremony for panchayati raj and urban local body representatives in Arki’s Kotli, said that, for the first time in the history of independent India and since Himachal Pradesh’s inception, people were referring to Sukhu as a chief minister associated with locks.Thakur alleged that upon assuming power, instead of advancing development initiatives, the current government began locking institutions that had been established by the previous BJP administration. “Approximately 2,500 such institutions, which the former government had launched in the public interest, have been shut down across the state. If a government, elected to serve the public and carry out development, begins its tenure by shutting down institutions, it can only be described as a taale wali Sarkar,” he said.BJP focused only on criticising the govt: ChauhanChief minister’s principal media adviser Naresh Chauhan on Wednesday hit back at the BJP, saying that the opposition was largely focused on criticising the government instead of offering constructive suggestions or taking up Himachal Pradesh’s concerns with the Centre.He said the opposition should raise issues such as the state’s financial rights, pending commitments and development concerns instead of concentrating on political controversies.Referring to the BJP’s demand concerning the promised financial assistance of ₹1,500 crore, Chauhan said the opposition should pursue the matter with the Centre and work towards securing the funds for Himachal Pradesh.Taking a swipe at Thakur, Chauhan said, “An opposition leader has a much bigger responsibility. There should be meaningful discussions inside the Assembly, constructive suggestions and business that serves the interests of the state. Merely using the media to create publicity does not serve Himachal Pradesh.”

headline: 11 Dubai flats, Rs 129-crore trail: PMLA court rejects bail in Rs 1,600-crore QFX ponzi scam
content: A Special Court under the PMLA, Panchkula, on Wednesday rejected the bail application of a Delhi resident, accused of procuring multiple bank accounts of various entities into which Rs 129 crore, the proceeds of the crime, were deposited.Thirty-five-year-old Subin Cherian was operating the crypto wallet through which proceeds of crime were processed.While rejecting the bail, the court said, “The prosecution case pertains to a large-scale investment fraud wherein numerous innocent investors were duped of their hard-earned money running into several hundred crores of rupees. The specific role attributed to the applicant is for arranging the accounts wherein said money was received and subsequently the applicant has facilitated conversion of the aforesaid amount into cryptocurrency.”Scam that began with a Rs 12-lakh complaintThe case has its genesis in an FIR registered at Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, in 2023. The complainant, Rajesh Saini, alleged that he was being lured into forex trading by accused Ramesh Chauhan, Rohit, Rajinder Sood, Santosh Kumar, and Vineet Kumar in the guise of QFX Group of Companies, whereby he was assured a 5 per cent monthly payout on the investment. Believing the same, the complainant had invested Rs 12.60 lakh, for which he had been given post-dated cheques, which were subsequently found to be blocked.Later, it came out that seven other FIRs against QFX Trade Limited had been registered in various parts of India wherein investors were defrauded by same modus operandi.ED found that QFX Trade Limited and its group companies, through its directors, namely Rajender Kumar Sood, Vineet Kumar, Santosh Kumar, and the beneficial owner, Navab Ali alias Lavish Chaudhary, had orchestrated a ponzi-style investment fraud under the guise of QFX Trading. In order to avoid detection, the accused repeatedly shifted the investors across identical-looking platforms viz a viz Yorker Capital Markets Limited (YORKERFX), BOTBRO, etc. Initially, in the ponzi scam, the bank accounts of QFX Group of Companies were used to accept investments, through which Rs 200 crore were received. However, upon expansion of the investment scheme, the accused started using the services of payment aggregators to accept amounts from the public and to make payouts.During the search of payment aggregators, proceeds of crime amounting to Rs 390 crore were frozen.It came out that the QFX Company had collected Rs 210 crore as investment, out of which a payout of Rs 115 crore only was made.The funds were being collected in cash or in benami accounts and the return was also paid either in cash or in the form of a crypto coin, namely “TLC 2.0 coin”, which is yet to be launched. Investors were being lured to become agents.As per the ED, as on date, the total identified proceeds of crime are approximately Rs 1,600 crore, and the value of attached and frozen assets is about Rs 410 crore.Cherian’s alleged roleED alleges that Cherian arranged bank accounts for multiple firms, including Zenith Enterprises, Bhavya Enterprises, and Iconic Traders, through intermediaries on commission. About Rs 129 crore in scam proceeds allegedly passed through these accounts. He allegedly admitted to earning around Rs 5 lakh in commission, and ED cites WhatsApp chats recovered from other accused in which he shared bank details.The agency further claims that in June and July 2025 he moved about 2.56 lakh USDT (roughly Rs 2.35 crore) from his crypto wallet to addresses linked to a new investment platform. It also alleges that documents on his seized device show payments of about Rs 6.64 crore toward 11 apartments in Dubai, and that another Dubai property in his name was later sold for about Rs 3.53 crore.

headline: Preserving Himachal’s Dev Sanskriti vital to cultural unity: Governor
content: Shimla, Nov 25 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh Governor Kavinder Gupta on Wednesday stressed the need to preserve the state’s Dev Sanskriti and Sanatan traditions and pass them on to younger and future generations. Gupta made the remarks during his visit to the temple of Shri Chhatrdhari Chalda Mahasu Maharaj at Pashmi village in Sirmour district, falling under the Shillai Assembly constituency. Addressing the gathering, the governor said India’s centuries-old Dev Sanskriti and rich Sanatan traditions form the foundation of its spiritual strength, consciousness, social harmony and cultural unity. He said Shri Chhatrdhari Chalda Mahasu Maharaj, worshipped as a form of Lord Shiva, symbolises truth, justice, dharma and public welfare. The unique tradition of the deity visiting different villages reflects social harmony, mutual respect and collective faith among people, he added. Gupta said the shared Dev Sanskriti of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand exemplifies India’s spiritual and cultural unity, strengthening brotherhood and social harmony beyond geographical boundaries.

headline: Himachal Congress removes 2 vice-presidents over ‘indiscipline’
content: In a move to send a strong message against indiscipline, the Himachal Pradesh Congress has removed two of its state vice-presidents, Rajneesh Kimta and Mohinder Chauhan, from their posts for allegedly remaining absent from party meetings and organisational programmes.State Congress president Vinay Kumar issued orders relieving the two leaders of their responsibilities with immediate effect.Kumar said their prolonged absence from important party meetings, organisational events and other official activities had been taken seriously.“Office-bearers holding key positions are expected to participate actively in party activities and discharge their responsibilities with commitment,” he said.The decision was taken after discussions with the chairman and members of the State Congress Disciplinary Committee. “The decision has also been approved by state party in-charge Rajni Patil,” the party president said.He further said the state Congress was committed to making the organisation active, accountable and strong.“Holding a position in the party is not merely a matter of honour, but it also entails organisational responsibilities,” he added.He said indiscipline and negligence in discharging organisational duties would not be ignored and that accountability applied equally to all party office-bearers and workers.

headline: HP to Get 50% Free Power Royalty from Central PSUs
content: Key PointsHimachal Pradesh approved an amendment to its Swaran Jayanti Energy Policy-2021.Central PSUs will provide 50% free power royalty for 10 years after 40 years of project commissioning.After 50 years of commissioning, these hydroelectric projects will revert to the state government free of cost.The amendment aims to ensure HP receives a fairer share from its natural resources and strengthens its financial position.Major projects like Baira Siul, Nathpa Jhakri, and Kol Dam are covered by this new provision.Shimla, Nov 25 (PTI) The Himachal Pradesh government has approved an amendment to Swaran Jayanti Energy Policy-2021 to enhance free power royalty from hydroelectric projects operated by Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs), including NHPC, SJVN and NTPC, upon completion of 40 years of commissioning. As per the amended provisions, these projects will be required to provide free power royalty to the state at the enhanced rate of 50 per cent for the first 10 years following completion of 40 years of commissioning, a statement issued here on Wednesday said. Thereafter, upon completion of 50 years of commissioning, the projects will revert to the state government free of cost and free from all encumbrances and liabilities. Separate agreements will be executed with the concerned CPSUs to give effect to these provisions. At present, the state receives free power royalty under the existing policy at the rate of 12 per cent for the first 12 years, 18 per cent for the subsequent 18 years and 30 per cent for the remaining 10 years of the agreement period. However, the provisions notified on September 30, 2024, primarily covered projects allotted or proposed to be allotted to Central and State PSUs and joint-sector entities, leaving the issue of enhancing royalty from already commissioned projects of NHPC, SJVN and NTPC inadequately addressed. The amendment will cover several major hydroelectric projects in the state, including Baira Siul, Chamera-I, Chamera-II, Chamera-III, Parbati Stage-II and Parbati Stage-III of NHPC, Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur projects of SJVN and Kol Dam of NTPC. Notably, Baira Siul Hydroelectric Project, commissioned in 1982, has already completed more than 40 years of commercial operation. The state government maintains that water is among the most valuable natural resources of Himachal Pradesh, particularly in view of its unique geographical and economic circumstances as a hill state. The amendment seeks to ensure that the state receives a fairer and enhanced share of the benefits generated through the utilisation of its water resources, especially from hydroelectric projects that have completed 40 years of operation. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that the state government was firmly committed to protecting the interests of Himachal Pradesh and ensuring that its natural resources were utilised in a manner that maximises benefits for its people. He said that hydropower was one of the major sources of revenue for the state and it was essential to ensure that Himachal Pradesh received its rightful share from projects harnessing its water resources. The chief minister said that the enhanced free power royalty would strengthen the states financial position and generate additional resources for developmental and welfare activities.

headline: Himachal to Get 50% Free Power Royalty from Central PSUs After 40 Years of Hydropower Projects
content: Shimla: In a significant move to strengthen its financial resources, the Himachal Pradesh government has approved an amendment to the Swaran Jayanti Energy Policy-2021, providing for an increase in free power royalty from hydroelectric projects operated by Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) to 50 per cent after completion of 40 years of commissioning. Under the amended provisions, hydropower projects operated by central public sector companies, including NHPC, SJVN and NTPC, will have to provide 50 per cent of their generated power to the state as free power royalty for the first 10 years after completing 40 years of commissioning. Furthermore, upon completion of 50 years of commissioning, these projects will be transferred to the Himachal Pradesh government free of cost and without any encumbrances or liabilities. Separate agreements will be executed with the concerned central public sector undertakings to implement the revised provisions. At present, Himachal Pradesh receives free power royalty under the existing policy at the rate of 12 per cent for the first 12 years, 18 per cent for the subsequent 18 years and 30 per cent for the remaining 10 years of the agreement period. However, the provisions notified on September 30, 2024, primarily covered projects allotted or proposed to be allotted to central and state public sector undertakings and joint-sector entities. The issue of enhancing royalty from already commissioned projects operated by NHPC, SJVN and NTPC remained inadequately addressed. The amendment will bring major hydropower projects under the revised royalty framework. These include Baira Siul, Chamera-I, Chamera-II, Chamera-III, Parbati Stage-II and Parbati Stage-III operated by NHPC; Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur projects of SJVN; and the Kol Dam project operated by NTPC.

headline: BJP Sees Backdoor Privatisation in HRTC’s E-Bus Policy, Questions Costly Maintenance Deals
content: Shimla: BJP state spokesperson Sanjay Sharma has accused the Himachal Pradesh government of paving the way for the gradual privatisation of the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) under the pretext of environmental protection, raising serious questions over its proposed procurement of 1,000 electric buses and the decision to outsource their maintenance to private companies. Sharma alleged that the government’s approach could weaken HRTC’s existing technical infrastructure and gradually eliminate the posts of mechanics and other technical employees. He questioned the rationale behind purchasing expensive electric buses when the cost of a single e-bus could reportedly be sufficient to procure four to five durable diesel buses, which he said were better suited to the challenging geographical conditions and steep terrain of Himachal Pradesh. Raising concerns over the financial implications, the BJP spokesperson questioned the 12-year maintenance contract awarded to a private company for the 297 electric buses already operating in the state. He demanded that the government make the complete agreement public before proceeding with a similar arrangement for the proposed fleet of 1,000 new electric buses. According to Sharma, the private company is initially being paid ₹5.31 per kilometre for maintenance, with the rate scheduled to increase to ₹18 per kilometre over the contract period. He questioned the justification for such a costly long-term arrangement, particularly when newly purchased buses generally require less maintenance during their initial years. He demanded disclosure of the total financial burden the contract would place on the public exchequer over 12 years, the formula governing the escalation in maintenance charges and whether the government had compared the arrangement with the cost of maintenance carried out by HRTC itself. Sharma pointed out that HRTC has decades of experience, a trained technical workforce and an established network of workshops across the state. Instead of upgrading these facilities and training existing employees in modern electric vehicle technology, the government appeared to be increasingly relying on private companies, he alleged.

headline: November heat breaks 31-year record in Shimla; Tabo shivers at -5.9°C
content: Shimla: Unusual weather conditions have brought contrasting temperatures across Himachal Pradesh, with Shimla recording its highest November maximum temperature in 31 years while the mercury in the tribal belt of Lahaul-Spiti has plunged below freezing. Shimla recorded a maximum temperature of 24°C on Tuesday, breaking the previous November record of 23.5°C set on November 15, 1995. The unusually warm daytime conditions have highlighted the sharp contrast between rising temperatures in the state capital and the intensifying cold in higher-altitude areas. Meanwhile, Tabo in Lahaul-Spiti emerged as the coldest location in the state, recording a minimum temperature of -5.9°C. Kukumseri also witnessed severe cold, with the minimum temperature dropping to -4°C. These are the lowest nighttime temperatures recorded at both locations so far this winter season. The relatively warm conditions were not confined to Shimla. Several other parts of the state also recorded maximum temperatures considerably higher than typical winter conditions. Una recorded the highest maximum temperature at 27.2°C, followed by Bilaspur at 26.5°C, Kangra at 24.9°C, Mandi at 24.6°C, Solan at 24.5°C and Dharamshala at 24°C. Nahan recorded a maximum temperature of 22.1°C, while Manali settled at 19.8°C. Keylong recorded a comparatively lower maximum temperature of 13°C. According to the Meteorological Centre, dry weather is expected to prevail across Himachal Pradesh until November 29, with clear skies and sunshine likely in most areas. However, falling nighttime temperatures, particularly in high-altitude regions, are expected to intensify the cold during the coming days.

headline: Cong to protest in support of sugarcane farmers in front of Shahabad sugar mill on Dec 1
content: Chandigarh, Nov 25 (PTI) The Congress will hold a sit-in protest and strike in support of sugarcane farmers in front of the Shahabad Sugar Mill in Kurukshetra district on December 1, party senior leader Bhupinder Singh Hooda said here on Wednesday. The Leader of Opposition in Haryana urged the government to increase the sugarcane price in accordance with the farmers’ demands. Hooda said that farmers’ demand is that the sugarcane price be increased to Rs 600 per quintal. Last month, the government had increased the state advised price (SAP) from Rs 415 per quintal in 2025-26 to Rs 430 for the current season and announced a further increase of Rs 20 per quintal for 2027-28, taking it to Rs 450 per quintal. He described the increase in the sugarcane price from Rs 415 to Rs 430 per quintal, a hike of only Rs 15 per quintal, or just 3 per cent, as a cruel joke on the farmers. Hooda said sugarcane farmers in Haryana are being forced to take to the streets to press for their demand for a price of Rs 600 per quintal.

headline: Missing name in Army records no bar to family pension: How 68-year-old disabled son won case in AFT
content: A 68-year-old physically disabled man has won the right to receive a lifelong family pension more than five decades after his soldier father’s death, after the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT), Chandigarh, ruled that the benefit cannot be denied merely because his name was missing from his father's service records. According to a Times of India report, the tribunal directed the Centre to grant family pension to Anil Kumar with effect from January 17, 2016, the day after his mother's death. It also reportedly ordered the authorities to issue a Pension Payment Order (PPO) within three months and release the arrears with 6% annual interest. AFT rejects Centre's argument over missing service records Allowing Kumar's application, a bench comprising Justice Umesh Chandra Sharma (member-judicial) and Air Marshal Manavendra Singh (member-administrative) rejected the government's contention that the absence of his name in his father's service documents disqualified him from receiving family pension, as per TOI. The tribunal observed that a physically disabled son who is unable to earn a livelihood because of his disability remains eligible for ordinary family pension throughout his life, even after crossing the age of 25, provided the prescribed conditions are fulfilled.13-year battle for mother's family pensionKumar's father served in the Indian Army from 1940 to 1957 and died in 1975.His mother, Guffi Devi, subsequently fought a 13-year bureaucratic battle before her family pension was sanctioned in 1988.She continued receiving the pension until her death in 2016, Kumar told TOI.Kumar, who has a congenital disability affecting his right leg, said he had been pursuing the transfer of the family pension in his name since 2017, as per the report.However, the Army's Record Office rejected his applications in 2017 and 2019, citing the absence of his name in his father's service documents, as per the TOI report.The authorities also argued that the relevant records had been destroyed after the mandatory 50-year retention period and that his claim was time-barred.Medical records established lifelong disabilityTo establish his eligibility, Kumar submitted medical certificates issued by the senior medical officer at Civil Hospital, Palampur, and the chairperson of the Medical Disability Board at Zonal Hospital, Dharamshala.The medical board assessed his congenital deformity at 45% disability for life.He approached the Armed Forces Tribunal in 2021 through his counsel, Abhimanyu Sharma, seeking the quashing of the rejection orders dated April 15, 2017, and January 16, 2019. He also sought lifelong family pension as a disabled son, along with the outstanding arrears.The Centre, represented by counsel Shalini Atri, maintained that Kumar's name was not recorded in his father's service documents and that neither his father nor his mother had informed the Army about his birth. It also sought dismissal of his application on the grounds of limitation.AFT cites Army instructions on pension for disabled dependantsRejecting the government's objections, the tribunal reportedly relied on Army Instruction No. 51 of 1980, which provides for lifelong family pension to disabled children who are unable to sustain themselves after attaining the age of 25.It also emphasised that the absence of his name in his father's service records could not, by itself, override his substantive entitlement to the benefit.‘Tribunal's order has brought great relief’Kumar, who lives in Palampur with his homemaker wife, told TOI he had spent years trying to secure the family pension that his mother had received."I have been running from pillar to post since 2017 to get the pension that my mother was receiving," he said, as quoted by the Times of India.
