headline: IIT Delhi alumnus reveals how he repaid over  ₹1 cr family debt before 25, quit Google to built own startup
content: An IIT Delhi graduate shared his extraordinary turnaround story on the internet as he went from a debt of more than ₹1 lakh to securing a job at Google and eventually building his app business. This is the story of Yash Garg, who shared his streak of struggles in life while trying to clear off his family debt. Meet Yash Garg Garg took to X and penned a long note on overcoming his family's financial troubles. He discovered his family was in more than ₹1 crore in debt while he was in the second year. "My father ran a real estate business, and he had invested in under-construction flats from builders like Jaypee and Wave, paying most of the price up front through home loans. Years went by without the flats being delivered, but the banks still wanted their EMIs on time. So my parents borrowed from friends and relatives, and when that was not enough, from credit cards," he shared. As collection agents began visiting his home, Garg made his parents sit down and listed every outstanding payment. He shared that the principal amount alone crossed the ₹1 crore mark. Garg realised that his only way out was to secure a high-paying job and clear the debt before pursuing his dream of building a startup. First job after failed placement Despite being ranked second in his department with a CGPA of 9.7, Garg's campus placement plans did not go as expected. While he failed to clear the final round at Tower Research, he said he eventually accepted a job at Cohesity for ₹18 lakh a year. He moved to Bengaluru in July 2019 and lived in a paying guest setup under tight monthly expenses below ₹20,000. "My friends would talk about investing and going on trips, but I did none of that," he added. Garg said that although he sent most of his earnings home, it didn't improve the financial worries. He decided to look for vacancies at Google and upgraded himself accordingly. However, hirings were stopped due to COVID-19. “One of the lowest points of my life” Yash Garg, around the same time, joined Spotnana, hoping to earn more from the role and its equity. However, nothing much changed for him. He added, "About a year after I had started sending money home, I sat down to see where it had gone. Almost my entire salary had been spent on interest for our credit card loans. We had not reduced the principal and had not saved anything either. After a full year of hard work and sacrifice, the list was exactly as long as the day I had written it." Garg called it the lowest point of his life. Joining Google and launching side business A referral from a college senior eventually helped him land a job at Google. When he joined the company, he still had ₹80 lakh of debt left. To accelerate repayments, Garg began a side hustle. He launched a mobile apps business with his father. He worked nights and weekends alongside his full-time job. After initially struggling to generate money from Android apps, he said that he shifted his focus to iOS games. "I bought a MacBook Pro for a hefty ₹2.1 lakh, picked our most downloaded game on Android, built its Swift version in six days, and launched it on iOS. Installs were high from day one, and within a couple of days we turned on monetization," he shared. Finally, the business generated ₹6 lakh in its first month, which climbed to ₹24 lakh by the fourth month. Over the next 18 months, Garg's games crossed 2,00,000 downloads, mainly from users in the US, and generated more than ₹2 crore in revenue. Along with his Google salary and the earnings from the app business, Yash Garg was able to repay the outstanding loans. In June 2023, he cleared the debt.Life after quittingWhile Garg was no longer in debt, it was just the beginning of his dream startup. Soon after, he resigned from Google just before turning 25. He turned to entrepreneurship full-time.After several failed attempts, Garg built Super Workday, a business creating apps for users of the project management platform monday. Now, it has more than 300 paying customers, mostly US-based, and is close to $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR).In January 2025, Yash Garg secured a $400,000 investment from Silicon Valley venture capital firm South Park Commons at a valuation of $5.7 million to build an AI executive assistant, as per his post. "I am ready for whatever comes next," he concluded his post.

headline: Delhi parks get new rate card:  ₹1 for school picnics,  ₹5,000 pre-wedding shoots,  ₹1 lakh film shoots
content: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has introduced a new booking policy for designated spaces across 17 parks in the national capital, allowing them to host educational, cultural, recreational and commercial activities at prescribed rates.Under the revised policy, schools can organise approved picnics and other non-commercial activities for ₹1 plus GST, while pre-wedding and post-wedding photography will attract a charge of ₹5,000 per day plus GST. Commercial film shoots, advertisements and documentaries will cost ₹1 lakh per day, excluding taxes.However, weddings, marriage receptions and political functions will not be permitted in the designated park spaces.The policy, introduced following directions from Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, also provides for a single-window online booking system to streamline applications and reservations.According to NDTV, the initiative aims to make designated spaces in Delhi's parks available for a wider range of activities while protecting their ecological character.Delhi parks booking charges: What is allowed and how much will it cost?The DDA has prescribed different charges depending on the nature of the activity and the category of the applicant.School picnics for ₹1: Schools can book designated park spaces for ₹1 plus GST for approved educational and recreational activities, including picnics, painting competitions, photography and debates.The concession applies to non-commercial events that do not involve ticket sales.Recognised higher educational institutions, government departments, public sector undertakings (PSUs) and autonomous bodies will receive a 50% discount on booking charges. Schools will also receive the concession for activities that do not fall under the ₹1 booking provision.Pre-wedding shoots for ₹5,000: While marriage ceremonies, wedding receptions and political functions are prohibited, pre-wedding and post-wedding photography will be permitted at designated locations for ₹5,000 per day plus GST.Commercial film shoots for ₹1 lakh: Commercial films, advertisements and documentaries will attract a booking fee of ₹1 lakh per day plus GST. Organisers will also have to deposit ₹50,000 as refundable security.Charbagh bookings for ₹5 lakh: The commercial booking rate for the Charbagh area near Quli Khan's Tomb in Mehrauli Archaeological Park has been fixed at ₹5 lakh per day, excluding taxes and other applicable charges.Which 17 Delhi parks can be booked for events?The DDA has identified 17 park locations under the new policy. These include Sanjay Lake, Hauz Khas Park, Baansera, Indraprastha Park, Swarna Jayanti Park, Asita Yamuna River Front and Mehrauli Archaeological Park.Designated areas within these parks can also host ticketed concerts, theatre performances, literary festivals, book fairs, exhibitions, yoga sessions and community gatherings, subject to approval.The policy provides for a single-window online portal where applicants can access information about available parks, facilities, booking charges and capacities.Applications must ordinarily be submitted at least five working days before the proposed event. Bookings will be confirmed only after the required approval.What penalties will apply for failing to clean up Delhi parks?The DDA has also specified penalties to ensure that organisers maintain the allotted spaces and restore them after events.Organisers who fail to clean or restore the designated area will face a penalty of ₹5,000. They will also have to pay additional cleaning charges of ₹2.85 per square metre of the affected area.The refundable security deposit applicable to commercial film shoots is separate from these penalties.Will public access to Delhi parks be restricted?Booking a designated area will not give organisers control over the entire park. Other sections must remain accessible to the public, while special restrictions will apply at ecologically sensitive locations.The DDA's policy aims to expand the use of public green spaces for educational, cultural, recreational and commercial activities without compromising their ecological character.The new framework also establishes a prescribed booking and approval process for organisers seeking to use designated park spaces.

headline: Centre's decision to shut Kartarpur Sahib Corridor taken in interest of citizens: Delhi High Court
content: New Delhi: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to interfere with the Centre's decision to close the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor following the Pahalgam terror attack, saying it was done in the interest of citizens..The high court observed this while refusing to entertain a petition challenging the government's decision to shut the corridor, which links Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan, the final resting place of Sikhism founder Guru Nanak Dev, to the Dera Baba Nanak shrine in Punjab's Gurdaspur district..The Kartarpur Sahib Corridor has been shut since May 7, 2025..A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said it cannot interfere with the government's policy decision..Sikh pilgrims leave for Pakistan via Attari border to attend Guru Nanak's birth anniversary celebrations."It appears that the corridor was made operational to secure and promote the religious sentiments of Sikh pilgrims. However, the record reveals that after the Pahalgam terror attack, a policy decision was taken by the Government of India to suspend the services of Kartarpur Sahib Corridor from May 7, 2025. Such a decision is taken by the Government of India in the interest of its citizens," the bench noted.."In view of the aforesaid policy decision, we see no reason to cause any interference in the same in extraordinary writ jurisdiction," it said, however, expressing hope that the government will look into the petition pending before it.."With the above liberty, the petition is disposed of," it said..The court passed the order on a public interest litigation filed by the NGO Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation, which sought the opening of Kartarpur Sahib Corridor for Sikh pilgrims to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan..Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba carried out an attack at Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025, killing 26 innocent people, mostly tourists from across India..In retaliation, India carried out Operation Sindoor, a military offensive against the neighbouring country, in which Indian armed forces destroyed military and terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

headline: Delhi: Drones identify garbage dumps ahead of MCD clean-up drive
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi conducted a drone survey to identify garbage-filled vacant plots and open spaces in its West Zone, ahead of a special sanitation drive to clear the accumulated waste, officials said on Wednesday. The survey aimed at locating sites where garbage has been indiscriminately dumped, including areas difficult to identify through conventional ground-level inspections, according to an official statement. The corporation will use the findings to map garbage accumulation sites and deploy sanitation workers and machinery for targeted clearance, officials said. The upcoming drive will focus on clearing waste from vacant plots and open spaces, which can become sources of environmental pollution and pose public health risks. The MCD said the initiative would also help prevent open burning of garbage and eliminate potential breeding grounds for disease-carrying vectors. The drone survey is part of the preparatory exercise for the special sanitation drive, which will be launched shortly, the corporation said.

headline: CJP’s Saurav Das claims his passport leaked, blames ‘BJP-aligned’ social media handles
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das on Wednesday alleged that his passport has been leaked by social media handles aligned with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), raising concerns over the safety and privacy of citizens’ personal documents. In a post on X, Das questioned the ministry of external affairs over the alleged circulation of his passport details and asked whether doxxing had been legalised in what he called “New India”.Das had moved the Delhi high court on Monday, alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at Oxford University. He accused the BJP-led central government of sending a show-cause notice over alleged discrepancies in his passport just five hours before his trip. “Certain BJP-aligned social media handles have now leaked my passport. This is a matter of serious concern. Will the Ministry of External Affairs clarify whether such leaks of citizens’ passports are a routine affair? Has doxxing been legalised in New India?” Das posted on X.Alleging targeted harassment, Das claimed that his Delhi residential address was leaked earlier, followed by YouTubers allegedly barging into his house in his absence. “First, a BJP-aligned lowlife leaked my Delhi residential address. Then sent propagandist YouTubers who barged into my house while I was out of town. This was followed by fabricated stories about my family life and even a morphed picture of me. Now, my passport is being circulated to peddle yet another stupid, ridiculous narrative,” he said.ALSO READ: Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being allegedly stopped from flying to UK Citing concerns over his personal safety and privacy, Das said he had specifically urged the SEM court to ensure that his rent agreement was not leaked.“It is precisely because of this pattern of targeted harassment that I specifically asked the SEM Court to ensure that my rent agreement is not leaked," he further said.Das also said he would file a criminal complaint with the relevant authorities against every social media handle allegedly involved.“I shall be filing a criminal complaint with the relevant authorities against EVERY social media handle involved in circulating my passport," he said.“And to those who mistake the prevailing climate of impunity for permanent immunity: I am documenting every instance and every handle involved. Governments come and go. When the time comes, they will face the full wrath of law. Fleeing the country will be the only option left for them," Das added.Passport leaked from within the system: DipkeDrawing a contrast, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned how a citizen's passport could be leaked so openly while information about the prime minister's degree remained inaccessible.“Saurav’s passport has been leaked from within the system and is now being circulated by several BJP supporters. What kind of world are we living in where nobody can access the Prime Minister’s degree, but a citizen’s passport can be leaked and circulated so openly?” Dipke posted on X.ALSO READ: CJP's Saurav Das claims he was stopped at Delhi airport, barred from flying to London for Oxford lectureDas was asked for clarification on place of birth, advised not to use passport for 7 days: MEAThe external affairs ministry on Wednesday said that a show-cause notice had been issued Das, asking him to explain discrepancies in his place of birth in his passport and advising him not to use the travel document until he submits his response."The passport application process requires the applicant to provide accurate information. If, at any stage, a discrepancy is noted or reported by the authorities, amounting to a suppression of facts, we issue a show-cause notice to the applicant, allowing them to present their side of the matter," Jaiswal said at a media briefing."Based on reports that we received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Saurav Das on November 23, requesting a clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth. He was also advised not to use the passport until he had submitted his response," Jaiswal added.

headline: Delhi HC says senior citizens can evict children from own property without proving harassment, ill treatment
content: The Delhi High Court has ruled in favour of senior citizens who may not want to cohabit with their kids for various reasons. Anyone 60 and above seeking to evict their children from self-acquired properties does not necessarily have to prove harassment or ill-treatment in order to do so, the court said.Justice Amit Mahajan held that establishing the need to protect the property and live a peaceful and dignified life can be sufficient reasons for eviction as per the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007.Subhash Chander Malhotra vs Raman Malhotra and othersThe statement was made by the court while allowing an 85-year-old man's plea against orders passed by the District Magistrate and the Divisional Commissioner. The senior citizen moved court seeking eviction of his eldest son and daughter-in-law from his house in South Delhi's Masjid Moth, reported news agency PTI.The court directed the couple to vacate the property within four weeks. It also asked the Station House Officer (SHO) concerned to provide the senior citizen with necessary police assistance to ensure compliance, the news agency added.The court noted that the petitioner was the absolute owner of the property, and the son and daughter-in-law had no ownership claims. However, they reportedly resided in the house solely because of their relationship with the 85-year-old.According to Live Law, the judgment was passed on November 20, 2026, in the case.Why senior parents can evict their children from homeJustice Mahajan held that the authorities had wrongly insisted that the senior citizen establish allegations of harassment through clear and cogent evidence before ordering the eviction. The court said that neither the 2007 Act nor the Delhi Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules, 2009, mention such a requirement.It observed that mistreatment cases involving elderly parents often take place within the confined walls of homes, which may make it difficult to report with evidence.The Delhi High Court also raised questions regarding two enquiry reports submitted by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). The first report, filed on February 25, 2023, reportedly only stated that the harassment claims could not be verified. The second report, filed on September 17, 2025, also mentioned that harassment had not been established. However, the evidence or findings behind the conclusion are missing from the reports.The court said a conclusion without supporting evidence cannot be treated as a finding. It also rejected the authorities' reliance on a business dispute between the petitioner's sons as grounds for dismissing his grievance.Similar rulingsThe court relied on the Supreme Court's August 2026 ruling in Ravi Kant Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh, which recognised the power of Maintenance Tribunals to order eviction where necessary to protect senior citizens. It also referred to Pritam Singh v. Government of NCT of Delhi, which clarified that proof of ill-treatment is not always required for eviction.Case historyThe petitioner had acquired the property from the Delhi Development Authority in 1980, which was later converted into freehold in 2000.According to PTI, the dispute arose years ago when the senior citizen approached the authorities in 2022. He had alleged that his son and daughter-in-law had refused to vacate despite being asked to.The District Magistrate rejected his plea in August 2023 and again in October 2025, which was also upheld by the Divisional Commissioner in April 2026. The senior citizen subsequently approached the Delhi High Court.

headline: Delhi-Gurugram traffic relief: NHAI may finalise 2.7-km Shiv Murti-Ambience Mall flyover plan soon
content: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is expected to finalise the detailed project report (DPR) for a proposed 2.7-km elevated corridor connecting Shiv Murti in Delhi with Ambience Mall in Gurugram within a month.The proposed three-lane flyover aims to ease congestion on NH-8 by providing vehicles arriving from the Dwarka Expressway with a dedicated route into Gurugram, instead of requiring them to merge with traffic already travelling from Delhi towards the city, The Times of India reported. At present, vehicles emerging from the three-lane right-turn underpass at the Dwarka Expressway interchange near Shiv Murti have to join the same carriageway as other motorists heading towards Gurugram. During peak hours, this merging of traffic slows down movement and creates long queues, affecting commuters using the highway.The proposed elevated corridor is designed to address this bottleneck by separating the two traffic streams.Vehicles exiting the existing underpass will be channelled onto the elevated road, while traffic already travelling on NH-8 will continue along the main carriageway below. The two routes will remain separate, reducing the need for vehicles to cross paths at the interchange, The Times of India reported. NHAI identifies severe congestion at Shiv Murti interchangeNHAI's traffic assessment rated the stretch, including its service road, at "Service F" during peak hours. This is the lowest grade in the level-of-service classification and indicates severe congestion.Traffic at the interchange has increased following the opening of the Dwarka Expressway, adding pressure to an already heavily loaded section of NH-8.The proposed three-lane elevated corridor will begin immediately after the exit ramp of the existing underpass. It is planned along the space currently occupied by the surface drain between the main carriageway and the service road.The flyover will cross into Gurugram and terminate opposite Ambience Mall, TOI reported. How will the proposed Shiv Murti-Ambience Mall flyover work?The proposed corridor will include an exit ramp near the approach to the existing Rajokri flyover. This will allow motorists to access the service road leading towards Ambience Mall, Cyber City and Udyog Vihar.Commuters travelling farther into Gurugram will continue along the elevated stretch before rejoining the main carriageway.The arrangement is intended to provide a separate route for vehicles entering Gurugram from the Dwarka Expressway, while allowing traffic already on NH-8 to continue without being affected by the merging movement."The DPR is at an advanced stage, and we expect to finalise it within a month. The design has been prepared and is being examined by a committee.Once the DPR is finalised, the proposal will be submitted to the ministry for approval," an NHAI official said.The project's estimated cost is yet to be worked out.NHAI plans to coordinate flyover work with DLF projectNHAI is also looking to coordinate the proposed corridor with a separate infrastructure project being undertaken by DLF near Ambience Mall.In October, the authority granted in-principle approval for a flyover along the service road and a right-turn underpass beneath the expressway.DLF has finalised an agency for the project, with construction expected to begin after the traffic police approve the traffic management plan."We have already given DLF an NOC for the flyover near Ambience Mall. We intend to expedite this project as well so that work on both projects can be completed simultaneously and the two structures complement each other in easing the bottleneck," the official said.Coordinating the two projects is expected to help address traffic congestion around the Ambience Mall interchange and improve connectivity between Delhi and Gurugram.

headline: DUAC approves Delhi Police women’s training centre in Narela
content: New Delhi: The Delhi Urban Art Commission (DUAC) has approved the building plan proposal for a women’s training centre for Delhi Police at Narela, subject to a series of observations and recommendations concerning the complex’s layout, architectural design, parking, landscaping and sustainability features.The proposal, forwarded by Central Public Works Department (CPWD), was scrutinised by the commission after it received the building plans, drawings, documentation and photographs.A detailed online discussion was also held with the architect, during which clarifications were provided in response to the commission’s queries.The proposed building will have a basement, a stilt floor and three upper floors.Among its key observations, DUAC suggested that the width of the internal road network within the complex be rationalised by reducing the proposed road widths. It also asked that the location and design of the complex’s entrance be reviewed, considering its proximity to the entrance of an existing adjoining college.The commission flagged the proposed surface parking arrangement, which is fragmented and distributed across two locations on the site. It suggested consolidating all parking spaces at a single location to free up the remaining areas for landscaping and green spaces.On the architectural front, DUAC directed that all plumbing pipes, rainwater pipes, service equipment, diesel generator (DG) sets, DG exhaust pipes, water tanks, outdoor air-conditioning units, solar panels, clothes-drying areas and other service installations be appropriately screened or camouflaged and integrated with the building’s architectural design.The commission also suggested installing solar panels on a well-designed structural frame, integrated with the building’s architecture. The proposal envisages placing the panels on a clear-storey arrangement, subject to feasibility under the applicable building bye-laws, to ensure effective utilisation of the space beneath them.It clarified that any deviation from the approved artwork must be submitted to the commission for approval before construction starts. .

headline: DUAC rejects ‘Mini-Secretariat’ proposal at Dwarka, directs changes
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) The Delhi Urban Arts Commission (DUAC) has rejected the Delhi government’s proposal for the first ‘Mini Secretariat’ at Dwarka and asked it to resubmit with suggested changes. Last year, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta had announced that the Delhi government would establish 13 mini-secretariats across its revenue districts, starting with South-West district in Dwarka, to decentralise governance. One of the main observations of the DUAC was related to traffic movement after the building’s construction. “The commission observed that the proposed site is located in close proximity to the existing Dwarka Sector 10 Metro Station, which is expected to serve as a significant mode of access for visitors to the complex. Accordingly, a well-defined access and circulation plan for Intermediate Public Transport, supported by a clearly delineated pedestrian network, shall be incorporated,” DUAC said in the October 30 meeting, whose minutes were released recently. Estimated to cost Rs 213 crore, the ‘Mini-Secretariat’ will have several departments of government, zonal offices of the Public Works Department, Delhi Jal Board, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, etc. The DUAC also observed that the proposed facade, comprising glazing, aluminium fins, louvres (walls), sandstone cladding and GRC jaali “appears visually cluttered” due to the combination of multiple materials and architectural elements.

headline: Delhi healthcare boost: 2 hospitals with 1,815 beds, 40 Arogya Mandirs in pipeline
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) Two hospitals with a combined capacity of 1,815 beds in Siraspur and Hastal will become operational next year, while 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are set to open next month, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Wednesday. Reviewing various healthcare infrastructure projects at the Delhi Secretariat, Gupta directed officials to ensure their timely completion and said negligence would not be tolerated. The 1,164-bed hospital in Siraspur is ready, with procurement of medical equipment underway and targeted for completion by the end of January. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal is also nearing completion, according to a statement issued by the Chief Minister’s Office. The two hospitals are expected to improve access to healthcare in their surrounding areas and reduce the patient load on existing facilities. Gupta informed that 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are being developed across Delhi, of which 415 are currently operational. The government aims to open another 40 centres next month, on the occasion of the 102nd birth anniversary of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

headline: India’s bio-economy to touch USD 300 billion by 2030, biotech startups cross 11,000: Jitendra Singh
content: India’s bio-economy is projected to reach $300 billion by 2030, with biotechnology emerging as a key driver of the next Industrial Revolution, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Wednesday. He highlighted the growth of the country’s biotech startup ecosystem from just 50-60 ventures in 2014 to over 11,000 at present.Addressing the CII Global Genomics Summit 2026 in New Delhi, Singh said India’s bio-economy had expanded from approximately $10 billion in 2014 to nearly $195 billion, reflecting the growing contribution of biotechnology to the country’s economy.Drawing a parallel with the role of information technology in the previous industrial revolution, he said biotechnology was now emerging as a strategic technology platform that would shape the future of healthcare, agriculture and global economic competitiveness.He urged industry leaders, startups and investors to increase their participation and investment in genomics, multi-omics and advanced biotechnology, warning that businesses failing to adapt to emerging technologies risked becoming irrelevant.Singh said the convergence of DNA sequencing, computational biology, artificial intelligence and technologies such as metabolomics, transcriptomics and proteomics would transform the understanding of complex diseases and enable personalised healthcare.Highlighting India’s advantage in genomic research, he said the country’s genetic diversity offered an extensive knowledge base for research and development. Referring to the Genome India Project, he said whole-genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals representing 80 different population groups had been undertaken, providing a foundation for future research and commercial applications.Singh said biotechnology offered significant opportunities beyond healthcare, particularly in agriculture and livestock, where genomic applications could help improve crop productivity, nutritional quality, resistance to pests and diseases, and climate resilience. In livestock, these technologies could strengthen breeding practices and disease surveillance.He also referred to the government’s BioE3 Policy (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment), which aims to accelerate biotechnology-led growth through research, startups and industrial participation. The establishment of bio-foundries and other infrastructure was intended to help translate scientific discoveries into commercially viable products.Citing India’s growing capabilities in advanced biotechnology, the Minister referred to the country’s DNA vaccine for Covid-19, which was supplied to 30 countries, developments in HPV vaccines, research on haemophilia treatment and cost-effective CAR-T cell therapy for cancer at Tata Memorial Centre.Calling for greater private-sector investment in research and development, Singh highlighted the Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme as an opportunity to accelerate investment in high-impact technologies. He also urged companies to support scientific research through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding, particularly in areas such as cancer and diabetes.On concerns over regulatory procedures for biotechnology products and advanced therapies, he said the government was working with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to simplify processes and address overlapping regulatory requirements.

headline: After Patna FIR, Delhi BJP moves police against comedian Yash Maheshwari over Chhath Puja sindoor remarks
content: NEW DELHI: Troubles are mounting for stand-up comedian and YouTuber Yash Maheshwari, with the controversy over his alleged objectionable remarks about married women's sindoor during Chhath Puja spreading beyond Bihar.Hours after the Patna Cyber Police registered an FIR against him, Delhi BJP leaders on Wednesday approached the police with a complaint, demanding strict action against the comedian.Delhi BJP Purvanchal Morcha chief Santosh Ojha met Central Delhi deputy commissioner of police Rohit Rajbir Singh and submitted a written complaint, alleging that Maheshwari had made derogatory and obscene remarks about Chhath devotees in a stand-up comedy video, news agency PTI reported.'We have received a complaint. Teams will investigate the entire matter and go through the content first,' a senior police officer told PTI.The BJP delegation demanded that an FIR be registered against Maheshwari, accusing him of disrespecting the dignity of women and hurting the religious sentiments of people who observe Chhath. Ojha said those who insult Chhath and the women who perform the Puja would not be spared.Strongly condemning the comedian's alleged remarks about the sacred vermilion associated with the festival, Ojha said entertainment and freedom of expression could not be used as an excuse to insult the religious sentiments, social dignity and cultural traditions of millions of women.He urged the Delhi Police to conduct an impartial investigation, register an FIR, preserve all digital evidence and take strict legal action if Maheshwari was found guilty.LJP seeks FIR, writes to Delhi CMAdding to the pressure on the comedian, the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) also approached the Delhi government, urging CM Rekha Gupta to direct the police to register an FIR against Maheshwari over his alleged obscene and derogatory remarks about the sindoor worn by married women during Chhath Puja, PTI reported.In a letter to the CM, LJP youth wing national president and Delhi in-charge Pranab Kumar alleged that the comedian's remarks had insulted the dignity of women observing the Chhath fast and the religious and cultural traditions of the Purvanchali community.Kumar said Chhath Mahaparv had become an integral part of Delhi's identity, with lakhs of people from Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh celebrating the festival with devotion every year.Explaining the religious significance of the sindoor ritual, he said women observe a 36-hour 'nirjala' fast and worship the setting and rising Sun while standing in water. During the fast, they apply sindoor from the tip of their nose to their forehead.'This is not merely a ritual but a sacred symbol of good fortune, family welfare and penance,' he wrote in the letter.Kumar also referred to the arrangements made by the Delhi government for Chhath celebrations at more than 1,400 ghats this year, including an 11-km-long ghat along the Munak Canal. He also mentioned the chief minister's participation in Chhath prayers on the banks of the Yamuna.Expressing anguish over the controversy, Kumar said it was particularly painful that the incident had occurred in the national capital just five days after the conclusion of the festival.In his letter, he alleged that Maheshwari had uploaded a video of a stand-up performance organised in Delhi on November 21, in which he made extremely obscene and insulting remarks about the sindoor traditionally worn by married women observing the Chhath fast.'This was not merely an attempt at humour but a direct attack on the dignity of mothers and sisters from the Purvanchali community in Delhi and their folk faith and traditions,' he wrote.Kumar also said that an apology alone was not sufficient to address the issue.'We respect freedom of expression and the independence of humour. However, freedom of expression cannot be allowed to become a licence to insult women's dignity and religious faith,' he said.He urged the chief minister to ensure that the Delhi Police registered an FIR against the comedian under appropriate provisions of law and initiated necessary action.FIR filed in PatnaThe action in Delhi followed the registration of an FIR by Patna Cyber Police on Wednesday against Maheshwari over his alleged objectionable and abusive remarks about women in Bihar on social media.Police said such content could potentially disrupt social harmony, trigger law-and-order issues and hurt public sentiments on a wider scale.The row began after a clip from Maheshwari’s stand-up act, Morally Questionable | Standup Comedy, which was uploaded to his YouTube channel on November 21, started circulating widely on social media.In the clip, Maheshwari allegedly made a vulgar comparison involving the long streak of sindoor traditionally worn by married women in Bihar during Chhath Puja. The remarks drew sharp criticism, with several social media users calling for action against the comedian.As the backlash intensified, Maheshwari posted an apology video on November 24, acknowledging that his comments about Bihar’s cultural traditions were inappropriate and should not have been made. He took responsibility for his remarks, apologised to those whose sentiments had been hurt and assured viewers that he would be more careful with his content in the future.Despite the apology, the issue has continued to gather momentum, with political leaders in Delhi joining the calls for police action against him.

headline: 'No reason to interfere with govt decision': Delhi HC refuses to reopen Kartarpur Corridor | India News
content: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to direct the Centre to reopen the Kartarpur Corridor, holding that its closure following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack was a policy decision taken in the interest of citizens.A bench of acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said there was “no reason to interfere with the government’s decision”, while leaving it to the authorities to consider a representation seeking the corridor’s reopening.The court was hearing a petition filed by the Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation, which sought the reopening of the corridor to allow Sikh pilgrims to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan. The plea said the shrine holds deep religious significance for the Sikh community and sought the restoration of the pilgrimage route.The bench noted that the Centre had decided to suspend the corridor from May 7, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed. It held that the decision was taken “keeping the interests of citizens in mind and was a matter of government policy”.The court also noted that the petitioner’s representation seeking the corridor’s reopening was pending before the authorities and expressed hope that they would consider it.“With the aforesaid liberty, the petition stands disposed of,” the bench said.The Kartarpur Corridor was inaugurated on November 9, 2019, to mark the 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev. It provides visa-free access to Indian pilgrims visiting Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, where the founder of Sikhism spent the last 18 years of his life.The corridor connects Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab’s Gurdaspur district with Kartarpur in Pakistan’s Narowal district. It was suspended on May 7, 2025, amid heightened tensions between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam attack and the subsequent military action under Operation Sindoor. The suspension remains in place.The Centre reiterated its position on July 31, 2026, in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha, saying it had received representations from Sikh religious groups and organisations seeking the corridor’s reopening. However, minister of state for external affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said the prevailing security situation compelled the government to keep the corridor suspended.

headline: Supreme Court directs Centre to file comprehensive response on pleas against detention of political leaders during Delhi protests
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response to petitions alleging detentions, particularly of political leaders, during the October 10 anti-CEC protests in New Delhi. Anti-CEC protest in Delhi top developments: detentions, curbs, crackdown storyline 1 A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed the order after Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted that affidavits had been filed in only some of the petitions relating to the detentions. Justice Surya Kant: Striking a balance in a divided nation storyline 1 The top court directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file the response within 10 days and asked the petitioners to file their rejoinders, if any, within a week thereafter. CEC protest: Political leaders, students and social activists detained across India CEC protest: Political leaders, students and social activists detained across India Thousands of protesters, including leaders, activists, and lawyers, were detained nationwide demanding the CEC’s resignation and the rollback of electoral roll revisions. CEC protest: Political leaders, students and social activists detained across India video 1 Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court that a habeas corpus petition filed by TMC MP and lawyer Menaka Guruswamy over the alleged removal of former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee from the protest site has become infructuous as no one was arrested or detained during the October 10 protests. Habeas corpus is a fundamental constitutional remedy and legal prerogative writ used to protect individual liberty against unlawful detention or restraint. The apex court in a special sitting on October 11 had said people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained and also asked the Centre to ensure that the Delhi Metro functions normally and that there is no disruption to internet services, subject to law-and-order conditions. Dhruv Rathee, CJP leaders released after detention amid Delhi protest crackdown Dhruv Rathee, CJP leaders released after detention amid Delhi protest crackdown Dhruv Rathee, CJP leaders released after detention amid Delhi protest crackdown video 1 The protest call was given by the CJP and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission (EC). The government thwarted the planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on October 11 after an unprecedented security clampdown and the detention of more than 7,000 protesters, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

headline: Mahadev betting app scam: Why ED arrested Delhi lawyer over alleged  ₹15 crore payment from kingpin Saurabh Chandrakar
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested a Delhi-based lawyer for allegedly receiving more than ₹15 crore from Saurabh Chandrakar, the alleged mastermind of the Mahadev online betting app scam, on the promise of influencing judges, advocates and government officials connected with the case, according to a PTI report.The accused, Himanshu Shekhar, was reportedly remanded to the ED's custody until November 28 by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Raipur late Monday night.The remand came hours after the Bombay High Court set aside a Mumbai court order that had rejected the agency's request for his transit remand.ED counsel Sourabh Kumar Pande told PTI that Chandrakar had named Shekhar during his custodial interrogation and alleged that the lawyer had promised to manage people in the government and judicial system, including judges and advocates.According to the agency cited by PTI, Chandrakar told investigators that he had paid Shekhar ₹15 crore, followed by additional amounts in smaller instalments. The ED subsequently issued a lookout circular (LOC) against the lawyer to prevent him from leaving the country. Lawyer detained at Mumbai airport while attempting to fly to Dubai Shekhar was reportedly detained by immigration officials at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport around 3 pm on November 20, when he was scheduled to board a flight to Dubai. He was subsequently handed over to the Customs Department, which informed the ED about the lookout circular, Pande said. An ED team from Raipur reached Mumbai and took Shekhar into custody at around 1.10 am on November 21. After questioning him, the agency produced him before a special court in Mumbai at approximately 2.45 pm the same day and sought transit remand to take him to Raipur for further investigation. However, the Mumbai court rejected the application, citing procedural grounds. According to the ED's counsel, the court observed that Shekhar should have been produced during the first session of working hours rather than towards the end of the 24-hour period. The dispute also involved the calculation of the period of detention. The ED maintained that the clock began ticking at 1.10 am on November 21, when its officials formally took Shekhar into custody. The Mumbai court, however, considered his detention to have started at 3.03 pm on November 20, when immigration officials first detained him under the LOC. The court subsequently directed Shekhar to appear before the ED's Raipur office on November 23. Bombay High Court overturns Mumbai court order The ED challenged the Mumbai special court's decision before the Bombay High Court, which quashed the order on Monday, clearing the way for the agency to proceed with the arrest in Raipur. Shekhar's lawyer, Faizal Rizvi, disputed the ED's account of the subsequent events. Rizvi claimed that the agency had told the Bombay High Court that his client failed to appear before its Raipur office, whereas Shekhar had actually reached the office at 4.25 pm on Monday. He further said that Shekhar was arrested after reaching the office. The defence has also approached the special court in Raipur seeking directions to preserve CCTV footage and entry registers of the ED office. According to Rizvi, these records could be produced before the Supreme Court in any future legal proceedings. Chandrakar extradited from Oman, lodged in Raipur jail The alleged payment to Shekhar is linked to the wider investigation into the Mahadev online betting app network. Chandrakar, who was extradited from Oman earlier this month following an operation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), is currently lodged in Raipur Central Jail in judicial custody. The ED has alleged that illegal betting operations through the Mahadev app and associated money-laundering activities continued, with the total proceeds of crime estimated to have exceeded ₹92,000 crore. Investigative agencies have alleged that Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal, both natives of Bhilai in Chhattisgarh's Durg district, promoted the Mahadev Book App and ran an online betting network through a system of panel and branch operators. The alleged network involved payments described as protection money to police personnel, administrative officials and influential political figures to facilitate its operations. How the Mahadev betting network allegedly operated According to investigative agencies, Chandrakar and other promoters operated from Dubai, which they allegedly treated as the network's headquarters. The promoters are accused of recruiting several youths from Chhattisgarh to work as managers, supervisors and other staff members to run the betting operations. The alleged network functioned through multiple panels and branches, allowing betting activities to be conducted across locations. The ED's investigation has reportedly focused on the alleged generation and laundering of proceeds from these operations, as well as the suspected involvement of officials and influential individuals who may have helped the network function. With inputs from PTI report.

headline: Bengaluru’s success as deep-tech hub depends on Delhi, but the road is fraught, writes global media
content: New Delhi: A rural thali in India is costlier at the moment than an urban platter, with food inflation hitting India’s villages harder than its cities. Also, India is looking beyond its immediate realities, and dreaming of satellites, space technology and a global deep-tech future. Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das being stopped from travelling abroad ahead of scheduled speaking engagements at leading universities in the UK has reignited debate over freedom of speech under the Modi government. This week, international media looks at a country caught between the pressures of the present and how it’s fuelling the rocket of its ambitious future. [/dropcap]B[/dropcap]engaluru has reinvented itself with every phase of India’s technology boom. It first became the country’s IT and outsourcing hub, home to giants like Infosys and Wipro. The 2010s brought a wave of consumer-facing start-ups, such as Flipkart and Ola. Now, the city is betting big on “deep tech”, from satellites and defence systems, to semiconductors and artificial intelligence.

headline: Delhi protests: Supreme Court seeks Centre's reply on leader detentions
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response to petitions alleging detentions, particularly of political leaders, during the October 10 anti-CEC protests here..A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order after Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted that affidavits had been filed in only some of the petitions relating to the detentions..The top court directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file the response within 10 days and asked the petitioners to file their rejoinders, if any, within a week thereafter..Delhi court seeks police report on woman's complaint alleging sexual assault during protest.Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court that a habeas corpus petition filed by TMC MP and lawyer Menaka Guruswamy over alleged removal of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee from the protest site has become infructuous as no one was arrested or detained during the October 10 protests here..Habeas corpus is a fundamental constitutional remedy and legal prerogative writ used to protect individual liberty against unlawful detention or restraint..The apex court in a special sitting on October 11 had said people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained and also asked the Centre to ensure that the Delhi Metro functions normally and that there is no disruption to internet services, subject to law-and-order conditions..The protest call was given by the CJP and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission (EC)..The government thwarted the planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on October 11 after an unprecedented security clampdown and the detention of more than 7,000 protesters, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

headline: Delhi govt to set up 540 public EV chargers across 180 locations in city
content: New Delhi, The Delhi government will expand the public charging infrastructure in the national capital, setting up 540 chargers at 180 locations across the city to boost its mission of accelerating EV adoption, officials said on Wednesday.The project will be developed with the charger configuration approved by the Ministry of Heavy Industries. The Delhi government's nodal agency Transco has started the process to appoint operators to set up and operationalise the chargers under the PM e-drive scheme, they said.The charging infra will include one 12 kW charger with two charging guns for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers, one 60 kW charger with two charging guns for N1 goods carriers, electric four-wheelers and private four-wheelers, and one 120 kW fast charger with two charging guns at each location, according to an official document.The 180 sites are grouped into 90 Sites each broadly by geographic location, with Package 1 primarily covering western and northern Delhi and Package 2 primarily covering southern, New Delhi and eastern Delhi.The project is estimated to cost around ₹62 crore, officials said.The shortlisted Central Delhi sites occur in two distinct geographic clusters six sites around Inderlok, Pratap Nagar, Shahi Idgah and Kamla Market/ Lok Nayak Jai Prakash hospital, and two co-located sites at Rajghat.Under the phased electrification mandate of the Delhi EV Policy 2026, only electric three-wheelers and electric N1 goods carriers will be eligible for new registration in Delhi from January 1, 2027, and only electric two-wheelers from April 1, 2028.These mandates will substantially increase the demand for public charging in the city, particularly fast charging for commercial and high-use vehicles. The Commission for Air Quality Management has also prescribed a target of establishing 32,062 EV charging points in Delhi, in a phased manner, by December 2029.The Delhi EV Policy 2026 designates Delhi Transco Limited as the nodal agency for planning, coordination, and implementation of public electric vehicle charging and battery swapping infrastructure in Delhi.Delhi faces a persistent challenge of poor air quality, to which road transport is a significant contributor.The electrification of vehicles, particularly in high-use segments such as two-wheelers, three-wheelers, goods carriers and fleets, is therefore central to the efforts of the Delhi government to improve air quality in the city, the document stated.The policy seeks to accelerate the adoption of EVs across major vehicle segments, and to improve air quality, through purchase and scrapping incentives, exemption from road tax and registration fees, phased electrification mandates, and the expansion of charging and battery swapping infrastructure.Achieving these objectives will require Delhi's public charging network to expand in line with EV adoption and provide reliable, safe and accessible services, officials said.Also, user confidence depends on being able to locate a suitable charger, find it operational and complete charging and payment with ease. Provision for additional charging capacity, subject to site and power availability, will enable the network to respond to growing demand, they said.The availability of adequate charging infrastructure has been one of the key impediments to accelerating the adoption of EVs in India, and the Ministry of Power has issued the guidelines for installation and operation of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure – 2024.The key provisions include setting up public charging stations as a de-licensed activity, and any individual or entity is free to set it up provided that the station meets the technical and performance standards and protocols set by the ministry and the Central Electricity Authority or the State Authority from time to time.Capital subsidy is provided by the government for setting up EV charging stations in select cities, which can reduce the initial investment cost and improve the financial viability of projects.Under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, it is proposed to set up an additional 22,100 fast public chargers , in cities and on highways , to support the public charging requirements of the various e-4W vehicle segments, the document said.In order to address the public charging requirements of the e-2W and e-3W segments, PM E-DRIVE will support the setting up of public fast chargers in cities. The scheme will also support the setting up of 1,800 fast chargers for e-buses and e-trucks. Approximately 1,600 of these chargers will be installed on identified highways, and about 200 in cities, it said.Delhi EV Policy 2026 specifies Delhi Transco Limited as the nodal agency for planning, coordination, and implementation of public EV charging and battery swapping infrastructure in the NCT of Delhi under PM E-DRIVE.Support for charging infrastructure under PM E-DRIVE: The Government of India has approved the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement Scheme, with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crore over a period of two years. The primary objective of the scheme is to expedite the adoption of EVs by providing upfront incentives for their purchase and by facilitating the establishment of essential charging infrastructure for EVsTo cater to the need for fast chargers, the PM E-DRIVE scheme has an outlay of ₹2,000 crore for setting up public fast charging stations. Under the scheme, the Ministry of Heavy Industries intends to support the development of charging infrastructure by extending an 80 per cent capital subsidy on the upstream infrastructure required for setting up public fast charging stations.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Why Delhi court has revived Israel embassy car bomb case with ‘Iran link’ after 14 years in limbo
content: New Delhi: A Delhi Court has revived a 2012 case proceeding of an Israeli embassy car blast in the city, calling it an act of terrorism carried out in furtherance of a conspiracy. The latest order takes cognisance of the Delhi Police Special Cell’s chargesheet, following a submission that four Iranian nationals had hatched a conspiracy with the city-based freelance journalist Sayed Mohammed Ahmad Kazmi to carry out the explosion. While the Delhi Police arrested and charged Kazmi, the four Iranian nationals remain at large, with Interpol Red Corner Notices issued against them. The entire proceeding stems from an explosion that took place on 13 February 2012, in a car that belonged to Tal Yehoshua Koren, the wife of an Israeli diplomat. She and three others were injured in the blast. The explosion was triggered by a magnetic explosive device affixed to the rear end of the car at around 3:15 pm at Aurangzeb Road – Safdarjung Road crossing in Central Delhi. Weeks later, the Delhi Police Special Cell arrested Kazmi and charged him under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) for allegedly conspiring with the Iranian nationals, namely Houshang Afsar Irani, Mohammad Reza Abolghasemi, Seyed Ali Mahdiansadr and Sedaghatzadeh Masoud. The initial probe suggested the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) role in the blast.

headline: E-rickshaw driver with wife, mother rob passenger in east Delhi; four of family held
content: New Delhi, An e-rickshaw driver and his family members, including his wife and mother, have been arrested for allegedly robbing a passenger at knife-point in east Delhi, police said on Wednesday.The incident took place on November 14 when the complainant, Rajesh Kumar, boarded an e-rickshaw from Noida T-Point for Anand Vihar Bus Terminal around 10.30 pm.Two women and two children were already travelling in the vehicle. During the journey, the driver allegedly diverted the vehicle towards a hospital, claiming that he had to drop his wife and children home, an official said.Then he took the e-rickshaw towards an isolated stretch near Dharamshila Bridge and threatened the passenger with a knife and robbed him of his documents and some money and the accompanying women were also allegedly intimidating the victim, they added.A PCR call regarding the robbery was received at New Ashok Nagar police station, following which an FIR was registered and further investigation was launched.The accused have been identified as Jubair , Najre Alam , Muskan and Ishrat .Alam was allegedly driving the e-rickshaw, while Muskan, his wife and Ishrat, Jubair's mother, were sitting behind. Jubair is the son of the vehicle's registered owner, police said.Jubair was apprehended from Turkman Gate on November 20, while Alam was arrested near Lajpat Nagar underpass the following day. The two women were also apprehended from the Lajpat Nagar area. Police said CCTV footage helped identify and trace the accused."The investigation also revealed that Jubair and Najre Alam were previously involved in another robbery case registered at Sunlight Colony police station. A knife used in the crime, the victim's documents and some money were recovered at Jubair's instance," the officer said.Further investigation is underway.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Delhi HC refuses to interfere with govt’s decision to shut Kartarpur Sahib Corridor for pilgrims
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to entertain a petition challenging the Centre’s decision to close the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor following the Pahalgam terror attack. The corridor links Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan, the final resting place of Sikhism founder Guru Nanak Dev, to the Dera Baba Nanak shrine in Gurdaspur district in Punjab. It has been shut since May 7, 2025. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said it cannot interfere with the government’s policy decision. “It appears that the corridor was operational to secure and promote the religious sentiments of sikh pilgrims. However, the record reveals that after the Pahalgam terror attack, a policy decision was taken by the government of India to suspend the services of Shri Kartarpur Sahib corridor from May 7, 2025. Such decision is taken by the government of India in the interest of its citizens,” the bench noted. It added, “In view of the aforesaid policy decision, we see no reason for us to cause any interference in the same in extraordinary writ jurisdiction.” However, the bench expressed hope that the government will look into the petition pending before it.

headline: Delhi: Skill development centre to come up in Shalimar Bagh
content: The Delhi Government will set up a state-of-the-art skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh to provide industry-oriented technical training to Class XII pass-outs and job-oriented courses to women, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said on Tuesday.Spread over 8 acres near Desu Colony, the proposed centre will have 14 advanced laboratories, smart classrooms, an entrepreneurship and incubation facility, a library, an auditorium with a seating capacity of 250 and a two-acre horticulture training field.The centre will offer courses in digital services, information technology, artificial intelligence, retail, hospitality and other technical fields. Women will be able to enrol in short-term courses in fashion design, tailoring, embroidery, beauty and wellness, baking, food processing and handicrafts to help them secure jobs or start their own businesses.According to the government, the initiative aims to link skill development with employment and entrepreneurship, with training programmes designed in line with industry requirements and the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).The facility will offer flexible schedules, weekend batches and online and offline training options to make courses accessible to women who may be unable to attend regular classes due to domestic responsibilities.Two crèche units, each with a capacity of 25 children, are also proposed on the premises to facilitate the participation of working mothers. A medical sick bay will provide first-aid facilities. The centre’s building will be constructed by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC).

headline: Why Indians are flocking to hold watch parties of a Pakistani TV show in Delhi and Bengaluru
content: New Delhi: A cafe in Central Delhi became an unlikely gathering place over the weekend for fans of a Pakistani television drama. People gathered not just to watch an episode of Dar-e-Nijaat but also to take part in what might seem improbable: a communal screening of a Pakistani serial in India. Hundreds of miles away, cafés in Dhaka have been organising similar gatherings. Some screenings draw dozens of people; others have become elaborate affairs featuring food carnivals, shopping and cardboard cutouts of the show’s characters. Dar-e-Nijaat, an ARY Digital production, has become a phenomenon well beyond Pakistan. In India, apart from Delhi, watch parties have been organised in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, with viewers turning a television experience into a social event. With more than 1.7 billion social media views, Dar-e-Nijaat is now the most-watched show in Pakistani history. It premiered on 1 August, with episodes airing on Fridays and Saturdays at 8 pm. Its reach has extended well beyond its television schedule, with clips, character discussions and fan edits circulating across social media. The first Delhi screening was hosted by Tales of City Official. Organiser Abu Sufiyan said the response was so overwhelming that they had to stop accepting entries, with the team eventually forced to close its DMs. Sufiyan said they had initially planned the screening for 10-15 people, but around 45 turned up, despite the absence of any large-scale promotional campaign. Influencer Aanchal Malhotra told ThePrint that the most enjoyable part of the gathering was the quizzes and discussions around the show.

headline: November Deadline Missed; Ludhiana Residents Deprived of Modern Commute Due to AAP Government’s Incompetence: BJP
content: Ludhiana, November 25, 2026: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Punjab State General Secretary Anil Sarin today launched a sharp attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and the Municipal Corporation over their failure to ready bus depots for 100 electric buses allotted to Ludhiana city under the Central Government's ‘PM-eBus Sewa’ scheme even after three years. Sarin stated that the Central Government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi had approved the budget three years ago to put the city's public transport system back on track and reduce pollution, yet due to the sheer lethargy of the Aam Aadmi Party government and the incompetence of the engineering branch, not a single depot has been completed even after the set November 2026 deadline has passed. Work on ₹12.33 Crore Ghora Colony Depot Halted for Months; Only 20% Completed Sharing facts, Anil Sarin said that under this project, two depots were to be constructed for the 100 e-buses: a 70-bus capacity depot at Ghora Road Colony (costing ₹12.33 crore) and a 30-bus capacity depot at Hambran Road (costing ₹5.82 crore). Sheds, charging stations, workshops, and administrative infrastructure at both sites were supposed to be ready by November. "Surprisingly, barely 20 per cent of the work on the Ghora Colony depot has been completed, and construction has been lying completely stalled for the past several months. On the other hand, after missing the deadline for the Hambran Road depot, officials are now making hollow promises to complete the work by the end of December," Sarin stated. Buses Running in Chandigarh, While Even Routes and Stoppages Are Not Finalised in Ludhiana Drawing a comparison, the State General Secretary said that under the very same central scheme, electric buses are running successfully on the roads of the capital Chandigarh, whereas Punjab's largest industrial city, Ludhiana, has been left at the mercy of pollution and traffic jams due to the AAP government's incompetent governance. No blueprint has been prepared so far regarding bus operations, stoppages, timetables, and coordination with e-rickshaws across the seven proposed routes spanning 152 kilometres. headline: Who is Jalandhar’s new Police Commissioner? A look at his first term and policing career
content: The Punjab Government has appointed Gurpreet Singh Bhullar as Jalandhar’s Commissioner of Police. Bhullar, who led the city police from September 2018 to September 2021, moves to Jalandhar from his posting as Inspector General of Police, Border Range, Amritsar. The Punjab Home Affairs Department issued the transfer with immediate effect and directed him to join his new posting immediately. Punjab Government transfer order⁠..What did Bhullar prioritise during his first term?When Bhullar took charge in 2018, he set out three immediate priorities for the city police: preventing crime, pursuing unsolved cases and making it easier for residents to approach the police. He called for a review of CCTV cameras that were out of service and said the Police Control Room needed to respond more quickly to emergencies.Among the cases he flagged at the time were the Maqsudan police station blast, the killing of the mother of an assistant inspector general of police, and a robbery targeting employees of liquor traders..Jalandhar, Ludhiana and Amritsar get new police commissioners as 31 officers transferred.What experience does he bring back to Jalandhar?Bhullar served as SSP of Jalandhar Rural before taking charge of the city commissionerate in 2018. He has also served as Amritsar Police Commissioner, held DIG-level posts with Punjab’s Anti-Gangster Task Force and Ropar Range, and completed two stints as SSP of Mohali. A third-generation police officer, he has held district postings in Bathinda, Moga and Muktsar.

headline: Punjab Government transfers 31 IPS, PPS officers in major police reshuffle
content: In a major administrative reshuffle, the Punjab Government has issued transfer and posting orders of 31 police officers, including several senior IPS and PPS officers. The orders will come into immediate effect. Punjab Government has ordered a major reshuffle in the state police department, transferring and assigning new postings to 31 Indian Police Service (IPS) and Punjab Police Service (PPS) officers. According to an order issued by the Department of Home Affairs on November 25, the transfers have been made on administrative grounds and will take immediate effect. The order has been issued with the approval of the competent authority. Among the key changes, Naunihal Singh, IPS, has been posted as Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), Internal Vigilance Cell, Punjab, Chandigarh, while Gurpreet Singh Bhullar has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar, replacing Swapan Sharma, who has been posted as DIG, Ropar Range. Jagadale Nilambari Vijay has been posted as Inspector General of Police (IGP), Jalandhar Range, while Naveen Singla has been appointed DIG, Faridkot Range. Swapan Sharma will take charge as DIG, Ropar Range. Kuldeep Singh has been posted as Commissioner of Police, Amritsar, replacing Harjot Singh, who has been transferred as DIG, Bathinda Range. Satinder Singh will take charge as Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana, replacing S. Bhupinder Singh, who has been posted as DIG, Border Range, Amritsar.

headline: PM Modi to address first NDA rally in Punjab on December 8 after BJP-SAD tie-up
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (PTI) Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the first NDA rally in poll-bound Punjab on December 8 after the renewal of the BJP-SAD alliance, Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said on Wednesday. He said the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP will organise the mega rally in Moga to mark the birth anniversary of Akali Dal patriarch Parkash Singh Badal. “The prime minister will arrive in Moga on December 8 on the occasion Parkash Singh Badal’s birth anniversary,” Sirsa said. “This will be the first rally of the NDA which Prime Minister Modi will address (after the alliance was announced). Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal will also address the rally,” the BJP leader told reporters at the party headquarters here. Sirsa said the rally will be historic because it is the first such event the SAD and the BJP are organising together after the passing of Parkash Singh Badal. “In my belief, if any historic rally or historic programme is going to take place for Punjab after 1996, it will be the one in Moga to be organised on December 8,” Sirsa added.

headline: Harpal Cheema conducts surprise inspection at Sangrur GST office, checks staff attendance
content: Cheema reviews attendance registers and questions employees over late arrival; says negligence in government offices directly affects public services. Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema has stepped up efforts to ensure punctuality and discipline among employees in government offices. As part of this initiative, Cheema conducted a surprise inspection at the GST and Excise Department office in Sangrur. Soon after reaching the office, the Finance Minister sought the attendance records of employees and inspected the attendance register to check whether staff members were reporting for duty on time. He also reviewed the attendance system and sought details about the functioning of the office. Expressing displeasure over employees reporting late for duty, Cheema said that punctuality in government offices cannot be ignored. He stressed that government employees must adhere to official working hours and discharge their responsibilities sincerely. He pointed out that negligence by government employees directly affects the work of the general public. The government's objective, he said, is to ensure that people visiting government offices do not have to wait unnecessarily and that their files and official work are processed within the stipulated time. Notably, this is not the first time that attendance-related issues have come to light at the Sangrur GST and Excise Department office. On August 7, 2025, Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema had also conducted a surprise inspection at the same office.

headline: CPRI team visits Nauni varsity for talks on Himachal Krishi roadmap
content: Home » National » CPRI team visits Nauni varsity for talks on Himachal Krishi roadmap Shimla, Nov 23 (SocialNews.XYZ) In line with the government of India's vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) has been entrusted with the preparation of the ‘Himachal Pradesh Krishi Roadmap Vision 2047’ in coordination with YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry (UHF) in Nauni, CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya in Palampur, state government departments and regional stations of ICAR institutes in the state.
