headline: Chandigarh’s 2027-28 school admission calendar out, December 9 marks first day
content: Education Department releases admission schedule for entry-level classes in 85 unaided recognised private schools; eligible candidates’ list to be published by January 18, 2027. The admission process for entry-level classes in Chandigarh’s unaided recognised private schools for the academic session 2027-28 will begin on December 9, with parents able to submit applications until December 22. The Chandigarh Administration’s Education Department has released the admission schedule for the upcoming academic session. The process will apply to categories other than Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Disadvantaged Groups (DG). Before the admission process begins, all 85 private schools in the city have been directed to publish detailed admission-related information on their notice boards and official websites by December 7. Schools will have to disclose details such as the number of available seats, age criteria, fee structure, admission criteria, required documents and the date of the draw of lots. The move is aimed at ensuring transparency and helping parents understand the admission requirements before applying. Application forms for admission will be made available free of cost on the respective school websites. Parents can submit the duly filled forms between December 9 and December 22, following the prescribed procedure.

headline: 331k Form 6 applications filed as Delhi SIR claims phase ends
content: Delhi has received over 331,000 applications seeking inclusion in the electoral roll since the publication of the draft voters’ list on August 31, which deleted nearly 4.7 million voters’ names, as the extended deadline for filing claims and objections under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) ended on Wednesday.The latest data released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Delhi, showed that 331,540 Form 6 applications were received between August 31 and November 24.The claims and objections window, which was originally scheduled to close on September 30, has been extended at least five times, with the Election Commission of India (ECI) granting voters additional time to seek inclusion or raise objections. The latest extension moved the deadline from October 30 to November 25.The latest bulletin showed that 35,592 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names were received during the claims period. Form 8 applications, used for corrections and other modifications, stood at 124,554 during the period.Also Read | Delhi SIR: Of 326k Form 6 applications, 280k disposed so farDistrict-wise ApplicationsAmong the districts, West Delhi recorded the highest number of Form 6 applications during the claims period at 40,029, followed by North East Delhi at 32,673 and East Delhi at 31,619. South East Delhi received 31,771 applications.For deletion of names, South West Delhi topped the list with 4,816 Form 7 applications, followed by South Delhi with 4,729 and North East Delhi with 4,325. North East Delhi recorded the highest number of Form 8 applications at 16,918, followed by West Delhi with 13,116 and East Delhi with 12,838.The bulletin also recorded 618 Form 6A applications, filed by overseas electors, during the claims period.Also Read | Supreme Court seeks Delhi SIR progress data to decide on deadline extensionApplication Disposal and SIR NoticesThe draft electoral roll was published on August 31 following the SIR exercise. As of November 23, election authorities had disposed of 281,360 Form 6 applications, 34,204 Form 7 applications and 264,688 Form 8 applications during the claims and objections period.The disposal of applications is taking place alongside the notice phase under the SIR, during which voters flagged for no-mapping or logical discrepancies are being scrutinised. Of the 3,314,032 electors issued notices under these categories, 3,295,950 have been parked for inclusion in the final electoral roll.ASDD Electors and Final Roll TimelineThe election office has also launched a special drive to enrol electors whose names were left out of the draft roll after being marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate (ASDD). Such electors, who were issued enumeration forms during the enumeration phase between June 30 and August 17, have been given another opportunity to get their names included in the final electoral roll.Also Read | Election Commission extends SIR timelines for Delhi and 5 statesBooth-level officers are visiting their registered addresses and distributing enumeration forms, while also coordinating with resident welfare associations and booth-level agents of recognised political parties to trace them.The last date for ASDD electors to submit enumeration forms is November 30. The disposal of enumeration forms is scheduled to be completed by December 10, while claims and objections are to be disposed of by December 15.The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on December 22.

headline: MCD begins restoration of Chandni Chowk Town Hall
content: More than three weeks after a large section of the 160-year-old Town Hall in Chandni Chowk collapsed, teams of experts have been deployed to map the area around the building and restore it to its original state over the next three months using original construction material and cross-referencing archival material, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) said Wednesday.MCD also issued a detailed standard operating procedure for protecting notified heritage sites, their annual inspections, and safeguards.HT had reported on November 4 that a large section of Town Hall, a Grade-I protected heritage building owned by MCD, collapsed following rains, damaging its facade, first floor, roof, walls of the main entrance porch, and the clock mounted above it. The complex, largely unused since MCD shifted its headquarters in 2011-12, has crumbling corridors, damaged windows, peeling plaster, and blocked passageways.Also read: Delhi govt kicks off technical review of duct setup for Chandni Chowk Experts to map damaged section and begin restoration workA senior civic official said two entrance sections have been marked as dangerous and barricaded. “Typically, heritage restoration work requires permission from bodies like the heritage conservation committee, but the structure is in such a critical state that it can prove hazardous. We have decided to take up work on the damaged section on priority in the first phase, citing the dangerous structure,” the official, who asked not to be identified, said.The damage came even as the Delhi government announced plans to redevelop the building as a “Global Heritage Centre,” showcasing the Capital’s art, culture, and cuisine. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta made the announcement in her budget speech in April.A second official said the remaining Town Hall, including the meeting halls, will be taken up for conservation and adaptive reuse in the second phase.“We are hiring ASI-empanelled experts to execute restoration of the damaged section. The main portico had three massive iron beams which are still in good shape even after so many years. They will be reused in laying the missing roof of the main portico. The damaged clock has been sent to storage. We have checked that the internal components are not very old; they were replaced a few years back. The facade and clock will be restored to original state,” the official added.The Town Hall stands on the site of a caravan sarai built by Begum Jahanara, daughter of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. After the British took control of Delhi in 1857, the sarai was demolished. Construction of the new building finished in 1863, housing the Delhi Institute, also known as Lawrence Institute. During the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Town Hall served as the city’s municipal office while also housing a European Club and library.Also read: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta calls for authorities to step up Chandni Chowk redevelopmentSOP for heritage protectionThe heritage cell of MCD, in an order dated November 25, 2026, issued the SOP for conservation and protection of all notified heritage buildings in Delhi. Earlier this year, the MCD was slammed by the Supreme Court over the poor status of several Grade-1 heritage buildings, including Lodhi-era tombs in Zamrudpur, as reported by HT.The SOP mandates inspections of every notified heritage property at least once a year. Every MCD maintenance/building division has been directed to inspect at least two notified heritage properties every month. The annual inspection cycle will be reviewed in December.A senior MCD official said inspections will cover cracks, seepage, vegetation, unsafe portions, encroachments, ownership, heritage grade, and changes in building use. “At least three dated, labelled, and location-referenced photographs must be taken during inspections, with findings recorded in a Preliminary Inspection Report,” the order states.Also read: MCD, police intensify anti-encroachment drive across Old DelhiThe heritage cell will maintain a central database and coordinate heritage-related approvals, while zonal deputy commissioners will be responsible for handling serious violations and escalating unresolved issues. More than 1,300 notified heritage sites will be covered under the plan. The immediate repairs at Town Hall are aimed at addressing the damage caused by the collapse and preventing further deterioration of the historic structure before the detailed restoration project begins in the second phase.

headline: Residential EV charging in Delhi: A ready opportunity
content: The Delhi Electric Vehicle (EV) Policy 2.0 sets out an ambitious 4-year vision to accelerate EV adoption across Delhi, backed by an allocation of ₹7,000 crore. Among other measures, it introduces clear phaseout mandates for internal combustion engine (ICE) two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and N1 goods carriers and provides incentives for pure electric vehicles. The policy also places strong emphasis on public charging infrastructure, designating Delhi Transco Ltd (DTL) as the nodal agency for the planning and implementation of public EV charging stations and battery swapping infrastructure, with a mandate spanning demand aggregation, technical standards, and service-level benchmarks. Importantly, the new policy also covers residential charging. Under Section 5.10, it encourages Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), group housing societies, residential communities, and private entities to facilitate the deployment of community and private EV charging infrastructure within residential premises and other private spaces. This is a meaningful enabling provision: it formally recognizes residential charging as an integral part of the ecosystem, alongside a single window clearance system for charge point operators (CPOs). In Delhi, residential consumers constitute the largest electricity consumption category (56%) and are the most heavily subsidized segment—making them a substantial target group for EV charging policies. This is reinforced by the city’s vehicle mix and EV penetration: two-wheelers make up roughly two-thirds of vehicles in Delhi, while the EV penetration rate for passenger cars reached 7.5% in 2025 and continues to rise. Both of these vehicle segments primarily charge at home, which means residential charging readiness will directly shape how smoothly the policy’s adoption targets are met. As with any large-scale mandate, translating this enabling provision into consistent, ground-level practice will take coordinated effort. RWAs routinely delay or deny permissions to deploy private chargers, citing such reasons as the need for electrical infrastructure upgrades, structural infeasibility, fire safety concerns, and load thresholds. Residential consumers relying on street parking face additional constraints, particularly in older colonies lacking designated parking bays. This is especially relevant for two- and three-wheeler drivers who live in informal settlements, where vehicles are parked in congested or shared spaces. These are precisely the kinds of operational issues that can be resolved through institutional coordination, driven by a structured implementation approach. While Section 5.10 provides the enabling mandate for residential charging, the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD) and key stakeholders could consider various measures to translate this mandate into consistent, scalable action on the ground: Drawing on the enabling provisions that the policy already offers, coordinated ground-level action on residential charging can help translate the ambitious targets into reality. Delhi’s approach could well set the template for other states.

headline: Delhi plans special resting zones for gig workers across city; centres to offer toilets, drinking water,
content: 5 key highlights1. Delhi govt plans to set up resting zones for gig workers and delivery personnel across the capital, identifying areas with high concentrations of such workers.2. The centres will provide seating, toilets, drinking water and phone-charging points, allowing workers to take breaks between deliveries.3. The existing Shalimar Bagh centre sees around 50 gig workers daily, with footfall increasing to nearly 70 during summer.4. The govt will provide land and involve e-commerce companies in developing the facilities. Heaters will be installed for winter, while coolers will be provided during summer.5. The centres may also help workers apply for govt welfare schemes and spread awareness about workplace safety, social security and other benefits.NEW DELHI: Delhi govt has planned to set up resting zones for gig workers, delivery personnel and other workers across the city by replicating a model facility already in Shalimar Bagh where every day nearly 50 gig workers and others get some rest during their work hours.The proposed centres will provide basic amenities, including seating arrangements, toilets, phone charging points and drinking water, offering relief to delivery partners who spend long hours on the streets without shelter. Govt is scouting for suitable locations, particularly in areas where the concentration of gig workers is high.An official said that govt wants to make resting zones across the city but their numbers will be increased from time to time according to the needs of the gig workers so that they get maximum benefits of the space.Labour and employment minister Kapil Mishra said govt will involve e-commerce companies in developing the restrooms, and the land for the purpose will be provided by govt. “The gig economy has become an important part of the country’s employment landscape where a large number of delivery partners, warehouse employees and other ground-level workers play a key role. The safety, health, rest and mental well-being of workers operating in extreme heat, rain and cold is important to govt and Delhi govt is working on it,” Mishra said.The Shalimar Bagh centre has been developed on govt land as a resting facility. It has seating arrangements, a toilet block, phone charging points and drinking water. It is next to an Atal Canteen, where meals are available for Rs 5 and the workers use it. Heaters are to be installed during winter and coolers are used in the summer.Suresh Kumar, who is the caretaker of the Shalimar Bagh centre, said around 50 people visit the centre every day. “The number was high in summer months because of the heat and sometimes the maximum number went up to 70,” Kumar said.An official said meetings involving gig workers, employers and employee representatives have been held under the chairmanship of chief minister Rekha Gupta to discuss issues concerning them, and the Shalimar Bagh facility was developed on her directions.An official said govt may use a corner of these restrooms to provide facilitation services to help gig workers fill out forms and apply for various govt welfare schemes. “These centres may also be used to create awareness about workers’ safety, social security benefits and other welfare initiatives of govt,” said the official.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: IMSACON XIV and Silver Jubilee Celebrations of Indian Meat Science Association Inaugurated in New Delhi
content: The 14th Conference of the Indian Meat Science Association (IMSACON XIV), along with the Silver Jubilee celebrations of the Indian Meat Science Association (IMSA), was inaugurated today, at the A. P. Shinde Symposium Hall, NASC, New Delhi. The three-day scientific conference is being organised by ICAR–National Research Centre on Mithun, Medziphema, Nagaland, under the aegis of IMSA, Hyderabad, on the theme “Technological and Policy Interventions to Future-Proof the Meat Value Chain: Pathway towards a Developed India@2047”. The event brings together scientists, academicians, researchers, industry representatives, policymakers and other stakeholders to deliberate on emerging developments and opportunities in the meat sector. Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, graced the inaugural ceremony as the Chief Guest. Dr Raghavendra Bhatta, Deputy Director General (Animal Science), ICAR, and Dr K. M. Bujarbaruah, former Deputy Director General (Animal Science), ICAR and former Vice-Chancellor, Assam Agricultural University, attended as Special Guests. Dr Yashpal Singh Malik, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Education), ICAR, and Dr Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, were the Guests of Honour. Dr Girish Patil S., Chairman and Organising Secretary, IMSACON XIV, and Director, ICAR-NRC on Mithun, welcomed the dignitaries and participants. Dr Prabhat Kumar Mandal, President, IMSA and Convenor of the conference, presented an overview of the Association, highlighting its 25-year journey and contributions to the advancement of meat science and technology.

headline: How Tanjot Singh aims to make Delhi's air cleaner: Meet the mind behind India's first bio-based air filtration platform
content: Tanjot Singh, a student of Delhi Public School (DPS), RK Puram, developed an alternative to conventional HEPA (high efficiency particulate filtration) air-purification filter media using compressed wool felt and electrostatic cotton. His project has earned him a place among the top 60 national winners at the 12th National Level Exhibition and Project Competition (NLEPC) under the INSPIRE-MANAK programme, an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, implemented in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation (NIF)-India. Here's all you need to know about Tanjot Singh and his award-winning innovation. Who is Tanjot Singh? Singh is a founder of PraaNavya, an initiative focused on developing climate hardware and deep-tech engineering solutions for cleaner air. According to his blog, PraaNavya is backed by Emergent Ventures US , Antler India and Masters' Union. He had previously co-founded SES Clean Air, his blog stated. He is currently a Class 11 student at Delhi Public School, RK Puram. He completed Grade 9 (2025) and 10 (2025) at Lilawati Vidya Mandir. Singh dropped out of school after Grade 10 in 2025-2026 to work full-time on his hardware startup PraaNavya. He self-studied Grade 11–12 Physics and Mathematics, wrote in his blog, built three prototype generations, filed a patent, raised grants, pitched to 30+ stakeholders and deployed school pilots. He rejoined school as an 11th grader in 2026. Tanjot Singh's achievements According to his blog, Tanjot Singh built his "first serious engineering project" — a 10-foot industrial scrubber — at age 14 with a team of five under CEEW mentorship. That project became the second-largest engineering build in his school's history and laid the foundation for everything that followed, he claimed. "Today, I'm building PraaNavya — India's first bio-based air filtration platform — with a published patent, school pilots protecting 300+ students, and a clear mission: to build globally scalable climate technologies through engineering research and entrepreneurship," he wrote. About Singh's award-winning innovation Singh positioned his PraaNavya Climate Tech as "India's first bio-based air filtration platform — sustainable alternatives to disposable HEPA filters." His innovation explores the possibility of using bio-based materials for air filtration while addressing concerns about the disposal of synthetic filter materials. The problem he aims to solve is Delhi's air pollution crisis. His blog says current solutions (Dyson, Philips, etc.) are expensive, generate massive plastic waste, and are inaccessible to many people. HEPA filters are single-use, petroleum-based, and environmentally costly. Notably, Conventional air purifiers commonly use HEPA filters, ideal for capturing airborne particles as air passes through a dense network of filter fibres. Although these filters play an important role in improving air quality, their synthetic fibre filters eventually need replacement. How PraaNavya is different Developed through his initiative, PraaNavya, the prototype uses compressed wool felt and electrostatic cotton as bio-based alternatives to conventional synthetic HEPA filter media, the Times of India reported. Singh claims that a five-stage bio-based filtration stack — triboelectric wool, electrostatic cotton, activated charcoal, polyester, PLA bio-polymer — achieves 99.7 percent PM2.5/PM10 reduction with ~80 percent less plastic waste than conventional HEPA filters. Some of the key features he highlighted in his blog are: > 5-stage filtration — multi-layer bio-based media > ₹5,000 purifier — with ₹800 biodegradable replacement filters > 5 application domains — consumer, HVAC, industrial, automotive, respiratory > Flutter BLE companion app — with AI-powered purifier placement > Published Indian patent — co-inventor, 2025 Real-world deployment His innovation, he claims, is currently piloting across two schools, five classrooms — serving 300+ students. An analysis measured ~40 percent lower PM levels in-situ, he wrote, adding that school pilots demonstrate tangible impact: cleaner air, healthier students, validated technology. Recognition The project is backed by Antler India, Masters' Union, ThinkStartup. At Shark Tank India S5 Stage 2, he was selected from 120,000+ startup registrations for virtual pitch submission. Other notable recognitions include: Masters' Union Elevator Pitch — youngest finalist & winner; Youth Ideathon — National Winner (2022) & Top 3 (2025); INSEF National Science Fair — Bronze Medal; InnoHEALTH Young Innovator Awards; EMERGE Sustainable Leaders — National Top 10. He has pitched to 30+ stakeholders including VC firms, IITD, Ministry of Environment, Government of Delhi.

headline: Delhi govt approves Rs 17,969-crore project to improve sewerage infrastructure
content: 01/10/26 | 12:55 pm | Delhi govt approves Rs 17969-crore project | improve sewerage infrastructure | Water Minister Parvesh Verma Water Minister Parvesh Verma on Wednesday said the Delhi government has approved the “One Zone, One Operator” project worth Rs 17,969 crore, aiming to improve sewerage infrastructure in the city. At a Delhi Jal Board (DJB) meeting, the government approved the Delhi Water and Sewer (Tariff and Metering) Regulations 2026, which replace the outdated 2012 rules, he said. “Under the new regulations, the government plans to implement fair billing rules for non-functional, locked or inaccessible water meters. The DJB also plans to simplify the process to get new water and sewer connections,” Verma said. The Board also approved a Rs 6,044.05 crore project for comprehensive transformation of South Delhi’s water supply infrastructure, under which smart meters with chlorine sensors will be installed. Under the “One Zone, One Operator” project, the city will be divided into six zones, each with a single operator responsible end-to-end for sewer lines, manholes, pumping stations and complaints, he added.

headline: Dwarka Expressway was sold as NCR’s Dubai. Buyers are flocking, roads & sewers missing
content: Gurugram: Prakhar Sahay fought for almost a decade to get the Dwarka Expressway built. He protested at Jantar Mantar in 2016 and lobbied endlessly so that his distant corner of Gurugram would finally be connected to Delhi. The expressway is here now, but Sahay is still fighting. This time it’s for the basic amenities residents were promised but never got. In premium towers and affordable projects alike, thousands of families who have invested crores in homes along the Dwarka Expressway are grappling with broken approach roads, open drains, incomplete sewage networks and unreliable electricity. They live in apartments with clubhouses and tennis courts beside a Rs 9,000-crore expressway, but some still have to cross open fields to get home. “I would always say that I wanted to see the Dwarka Expressway completed while I was still a father and not a grandfather. Now that it’s finally there, the surrounding infrastructure is nowhere to be seen,” said Sahay, convener of the Dwarka Expressway Gurugram Development Association. Announced in 2006, the 29-kilometre Dwarka Expressway was billed as Delhi-NCR’s answer to Dubai’s Sheikh Zayed Road. Not just India’s first eight-lane elevated expressway, but the centre of a new oasis of urban planning that could give central Gurugram and Noida a run for their money. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Gurugram stretch in March 2024 and the final Delhi section in August last year, though the building and buying boom had started well before that. Of the 42,816 units that were reportedly launched along the expressway between 2010 and 2024, 41,899 were sold in the same period. Today, about 115 housing projects are under construction. Sales of homes priced above Rs 10 crore have increased 22-fold in value to Rs 8,347 crore between 2024 and 2025. Real estate developers are marketing it as the new “power address”. “Dwarka Expressway has been inspired by Dubai. Very soon, you will see towering skyscrapers lining the expressway just like Sheikh Zayed Road. The price rise after the launch of the expressway itself shows that it has become a power address,” said the sales manager of Roots Courtyard, which is selling plots starting at Rs 5 crore in a gated complex with amenities such as guards and EV chargers.

headline: 2,400 km, 16 days, 7 states: How BJP’s Dalit outreach keeps UP, Punjab in focus
content: To reach out to Dalits in north India, the BJP has kicked off a yatra, Samarasta Sankalp Yatra (social harmony march), that also seeks to “strengthen” the bonds of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) with other social groups such as the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and upper castes. While the objective of the 16-day yatra is to connect with a large section of the SCs across seven states, it would especially focus on Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, where Dalits have significant shares in population and play key roles in determining their elections. The yatra would cover 2,402 kms, whose longest stretches would be in UP and Punjab, followed by Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, Chandigarh and poll-bound Uttarakhand. The Assembly elections in UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand are due in February next year. In these states the BJP would also take out smaller “link yatras” from various belts to connect them with the main yatra. An analysis of the yatra's route shows that it passes through 47 cities which encompass 252 Assembly constituencies including 56 SC-reserved seats. The Opposition parties had an upper hand over the BJP in these seats in the previous Assembly elections, of which the BJP-led NDA won 117 as against the Opposition's 135. Of the SC seats, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S) together won 22, while in the rival camp the Congress got 12, SP 3 and the AAP 19. Yatra in UP, Punjab The BJP's yatra, which commemorates Sant Ravidas's 650th birth anniversary year, was flagged off by party national president Nitin Nabin at Raipur Rasulpur village near Dera Ballan in Jalandhar on November 18. In the yatra, a Sant Ravidas idol and his charan-paduka (revered footwear) have been placed in a modified chariot, with about 75 BJP workers in 15 vehicles moving along with it. The yatra would traverse over 820 km through the BJP-ruled UP, covering 99 constituencies or nearly 25% of the state’s 403 Assembly seats. In the 2022 UP polls, when the Yogi Adityanath-led BJP returned to power for a second consecutive term, the BJP and its allies, Apna Dal (S) and Nishad Party, collectively bagged 71 of the 99 seats, with the SP and its then ally RLD together winning 28. These 99 seats include 20 SC seats, of which the NDA won 17 against the SP's 3. In Punjab, the yatra passed through 14 districts in five days, covering nearly 700 km. These 14 districts have 79 seats, of which the AAP won 61 and the Congress 14 in the 2022 elections. Contesting separately then, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) won two seats each. Meanwhile, the BJP and the SAD reunited Tuesday to jointly contest the 2027 Punjab polls. The 79 constituencies include 22 SC-reserved seats, of which the AAP won 18 and the Congress four. In UP, Dalits account for 21% of the state population, with 84 of the state’s 403 Assembly seats reserved for the community. In Punjab, the SCs account for about 32% of its population – the highest among the states in the country. Of the state's 117 seats, 34 are SC-reserved seats. Sant Ravidas’s followers, Ravidassias, belong to the Dalit community. A large section of Ravidassias is based in the Doaba region, which comprises districts like Jalandhar, Kapurthala, Hoshiarpur and Nawanshahr. Arc through other states After making an exit from the AAP-ruled Punjab on November 22, the yatra entered the Congress-ruled Himachal Pradesh where it covered seven Assembly seats. The Congress had won five of these seats, including both two SC seats, whereas the BJP and an Independent won one seat each. The yatra entered the BJP-ruled Uttarakhand Tuesday, passing through Dehradun and Haridwar districts before entering UP's Saharanpur on the same day. These two districts of Uttarakhand have 21 Assembly seats including 4 SC-reserved ones. Of these 21 of the state's 70 seats, the BJP bagged 12 as against the Congress's six and the BSP two in the 2022 elections, with one seat won by an Independent candidate. These seats include four SC seats, of which the Congress won three as against the BJP's one seat. On Wednesday, the yatra entered Haryana, where it would cover eight cities which have 36 Assembly seats, of which the BJP won 24 seats as against the Congress's 11 in the 2024 elections with the remaining one picked by an Independent. These seats include seven SC seats, of which the BJP won four and the Congress three. The yatra is slated to cross Haryana in two legs, as it would weave its way through a few adjoining parts of western UP and Delhi. The yatra's Delhi stretch would cover 10 Assembly seats of which the BJP won seven and the AAP three, including one SC seat, in the 2025 elections. From Haryana, the yatra would enter UP again, for the third time, on November 28 from Mathura. In this politically crucial phase, it would traverse through Mathura, Agra, Firozabad, Etawah, Auraiya, Kanpur, Unnao, Lucknow, Rae Bareli, Prayagraj and Sant Ravidas Nagar before culminating at Seer Govardhanpur in Varanasi on December 3. BJP national vice-president Lal Singh Arya, who is Samarasta Sankalp Yatra's national coordinator, denied any political aim behind taking out this yatra. “Yatra is also passing through Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh where elections are not due next year. BJP flags are not being used in yatra,” Arya told The Indian Express. He said the yatra’s objective is to take Sant Ravidas’s ideas to the people, adding that books and pamphlets on his ideas have been published for distribution. To mark the 15th-century saint-poet's 650th birth anniversary, the BJP has been holding various programmes which, starting from July 29, would continue till February 20, 2027. The party has also taken the soil from Sant Ravidas’s birthplace in Varanasi in 131 kalash (urns) to different parts of the country. The current Samrasta Sankalp Yatra is part of this plan.

headline: Jalandhar gets new Police Commissioner, Rural SSP and Range IGP
content: The Punjab government on Wednesday appointed Gurpreet Singh Bhullar as Commissioner of Police, Jalandhar, Harkamalpreet Singh Khakh as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Jalandhar Rural, and Jagadale Nilambari Vijay as Inspector General of Police (IGP), Jalandhar Range.Bhullar moves to Jalandhar from Amritsar, where he served as IGP, Border Range. He replaces Satinder Singh, who has been appointed Commissioner of Police, Ludhiana.Khakh, who was serving as Malerkotla SSP, will head the Jalandhar Rural police. He succeeds Harvinder Singh Virk, who has been posted as Assistant Inspector General, Special Branch-1, Intelligence, Punjab.Jagadale Nilambari Vijay takes over the Jalandhar Range from Naveen Singla, who moves to Faridkot as Deputy Inspector General. headline: Moga rally: PRTC, Punjab Roadways staff oppose ferrying of AAP supporters
content: Employees of the PRTC and Punjab Roadways have opposed the state government’s directions to ferry Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) supporters to the party’s rally at Moga on November 26, saying they will not perform the “political duty”.Meanwhile, employees’ union has postponed its strike till the afternoon of November 25 following the government’s intervention.According to information, the state government has directed the two corporations to provide about 2,600 buses for transporting AAP supporters from villages to the rally venue. In Faridkot, 90 of the 106 PRTC buses plying on various routes have reportedly been asked to report for the duty, while all 46 Punjab Roadways buses of the Moga depot have also been requisitioned.The PRTC and Punjab Roadways together have about 2,800 buses in Punjab, so nearly entire fleet is set to be diverted for the rally. The move is likely to leave thousands of commuters in the lurch on November 26, as only a small number of buses will remain on the roads. The problem is expected to be more severe for women, who largely depend on PRTC and Punjab Roadways buses for the free travel facility.The employees have objected to the use of public transport for a political event and said they would not ferry people to the rally venue. Following their protest on Tuesday, the state government asked them to postpone their strike and assured them that their long-pending demand for shifting about 5,000 employees in the Transport Department from outsourcing to contractual basis would be taken up.“Keeping in view the assurance of the state government, we have decided to postpone our strike till November 25 afternoon, as the government has assured to meet our demand,” said Simarjit Singh, senior vice-president and state committee member of the PRTC employees’ Union.The employees also alleged that they were being subjected to humiliating treatment during such political duties. Buses have been assigned to particular villages to carry AAP supporters to the rally venue on November 26 morning, but drivers and conductors have been directed to reach their assigned villages on November 25 evening. Upon arrival, they have to share their location, along with a photograph of the bus, in a WhatsApp group with senior officials.Drivers and conductors alleged that at most villages there was no arrangement for food and accommodation. While panchayats in some villages do make arrangements, they added, many villages are neglected by local leaders, forcing the crew to spend the night in their buses.

headline: A day after BJP-Akali reunion, a demand for 12 seats puts BJP in a spot
content: As the BJP reunites with its former ally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (MC) elections will be one of the first major electoral tests for the alliance ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. With the SAD seeking at least 12 of the 35 wards, a difficult seat-sharing negotiations is expected to play out. “We are a family. The BJP and SAD will win all 35 seats. In 2016, when there were 26 wards, we had got four seats. But that was too less. Now, with 35 wards, we want at least 30 per cent of the seats. We want at least 12 seats. We are not asking for much,” Charanjit Singh, president, Chandigarh SAD, said. Emphasising the bonhomie between the two parties, the Chandigarh SAD president said that the party’s leaders had also visited the BJP headquarters at Kamlam in Sector 33, Chandigarh on Tuesday and a gurdwara as part of the outreach following the announcement of the alliance. “Moreover, we are a family. We have also gone to Kamlam in Sector 33 and visited a gurdwara. Very soon our leaders and election incharges will hold a meeting,” he said. For the BJP, the situation is a classic catch-22. While accommodating the SAD could help the two former allies put up a united front, giving away 12 wards would mean turning away several of its own leaders who have been preparing for the elections and staking claims to party tickets. “The problem is particularly acute in wards currently represented by BJP councillors, where multiple contenders are already lobbying for the party nomination. With the SAD now seeking a substantial share, the BJP will have to navigate not just negotiations with its alliance partner but also the possibility of resentment within its own ranks,” a BJP councillor told The Indian Express. Charanjit Singh, however, said the demand was reasonable, pointing to the seat-sharing arrangement between the two parties in the 2016 civic elections. While not elaborating on the seat-sharing mathematics, BJP’s senior leader Sanjay Tandon told The Indian Express that the BJP and SAD are like two brothers, with their bond being “nakhoon aur maas”. “BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal share a bond of ‘nakhoon aur maas’ and are like two brothers. This alliance goes beyond politics and reflects the strong foundation of Hindu-Sikh unity, amity and brotherhood. This time, 1+1 will make 11, as the combined strength and organisational capabilities of both parties will give a major boost to the alliance. Together, we will fight shoulder to shoulder and ensure a thumping victory in the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections,” Tandon said. Meanwhile, the Congress termed it as an alliance of “convenience” and said that the BJP, which is already struggling with factionalism, will now have to make room for the SAD. “The BJP-SAD alliance is an arrangement driven purely by political convenience. The two parties, which parted ways over the farm laws, are now coming together again for electoral gains. The BJP, which is already struggling with factionalism and competing ticket aspirants within its own ranks, will now have to accommodate the demands of its alliance partner. It remains to be seen how the BJP manages its own workers while making room for the SAD,” HS Lucky, president, Chandigarh Congress said. A partnership that goes back to years Last time, the BJP and the SAD contested together for the UT civic body polls in 2016. In the 2016 polls, the SAD was given four seats, out of which the party could win only one, while the BJP swept the elections and won 20 seats. However, the partnership broke down in September 2020 when the SAD walked out of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the Centre’s three farm laws, which were later repealed. The two parties’ separation was reflected in Chandigarh’s subsequent civic electoral arrangements as well. In the 2021 MC elections, the SAD joined hands with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), contesting 19 of the 35 wards, while the BSP contested the remaining 16. However, the SAD again won just one seat. A SAD leader in Chandigarh requesting anonymity said, “In 2021 polls though we may have won one seat but our candidates created a dent at several other seats because of which BJP was reduced to just 12 seats”. The SAD had earlier announced that it would contest all 35 wards independently in the December 2026 elections.

headline: India rejects US' structural excess capacity allegations as Washington links 17% tariff to trade deal, 25% otherwise
content: India has rejected the US' claims of structural excess capacity, which Washigton is citing to impose fresh tariffs on 14 economies. On Wednesday, India said that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector, and that it continues to be committed to conclude the trade deal with the US as early as possible. "Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation...," the Indian government said in a statement, as it added that the notice is "currently under examination." "India engaged constructively throughout this investigation. In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," the statement also said.US to cap India tariff at 17% if trade deal is reachedThe US has said that if a trade deal is reached with India, then it will cap its tariffs imposed on New Delhi to 17%, and that if the deal does not materialise, tariffs will increase to 25%.The announcement was made by US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Wednesday.The Indian government's statement in the wake of this news also stated that the Modi government is committed to getting the trade deal finalised: "Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026, and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026," it said.India, in its negotiations with the US on the trade deal, has been insisting on a competitive advantage over its Asian rivals, a demand that Washington has addressed in the tariff proposals.The GTRI, while commenting on this proposal by the US government, has said that the under Section 301 excess-capacity investigations recreate the reciprocal-tariff regime under a new name, engineered to bait trading partners into signing one-sided, expensive trade deals rather than genuinely addressing structural industrial overproduction, as per a report by PTI.By deploying a dual-rate structure - threatening steep baseline tariffs against countries that refuse a pact while offering lower rates to those that sign - Washington reclaims the bargaining power to impose duties at will and extract unilateral concessions, allowing a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remains unchanged, it said."Under the proposal, Indian imports face a 17 per cent tariff if a trade pact is finalized --offering a calculated 1 per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate) - while rising up to 25 per cent without a deal, alongside the risk that an adverse USTR ruling could bring further duties or import quotas," it added.With Reuters, PTI inputs

headline: US proposes extra tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, 17% after trade deal
content: New Delhi: The US on Wednesday proposed a fresh round of tariffs on India, China and a dozen other countries following an investigation into manufacturing policies and market access barriers in these economies that it said hurt American commerce, complicating efforts to reach an early trade deal with New Delhi.India faces an additional tariff of up to 25%, which can come down to 17% if both sides sign the proposed trade deal, the US Trade Representative said. The US is India’s largest export market, accounting for shipments of goods worth more than $87 billion in the fiscal year through March 2026. This was a fifth of New Delhi’s total merchandise exports in FY26.India has said it’s willing to sign a mutually beneficial trade deal if it gets a comparative advantage over competitors in the US market.The US has alleged that the targeted economies provide financial and policy support to their domestic industries, prompting manufacturers to produce more than their local markets can absorb. This surplus, the US has claimed after concluding the probe under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, is then sold on the cheap in overseas markets, outcompeting American companies. This section empowers the USTR to investigate if unjustifiable acts, policies, or practices followed by foreign governments are burdening or restricting US commerce.In a statement issued late on Wednesday, India reiterated that it doesn’t have any structural overcapacity in any sector, and that it engaged constructively throughout the US investigation.“Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation concerning Acts, Policies, and Practices of 14 economies, including India, relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors. The Notice is currently under examination,” the commerce and industry ministry said in the statement.Under the USTR proposal, Indian imports face a 17% tariff if a trade pact is finalized—offering just a 1% edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18% deal rate) and a 3% edge over Vietnam and China (20% deal rate)—while rising up to 25% without a deal, alongside the risk that an adverse USTR ruling could bring further duties or import quotas, said Ajay Srivastava, founder of think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative.“India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations. Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026,” the commerce ministry said.Srivastava said the proposed duties will be over and above the usual most-favoured nation tariff that currently applies to Indian goods in the US, but includes a 10% punitive tariff imposed earlier this year after a similar Section 301 probe over the alleged use of forced labour in India’s exported products.Indian experts said final negotiations on the trade deal are going to be complicated now.“Countries negotiate deals to lend predictability and transparency to the trade regime. What is the guarantee that the US under Donald Trump won’t raise this additional tariff further once the trade deal is signed?” asked Biswajit Dhar, economist and former professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi.They said the American claim of India’s excess manufacturing capacity putting a burden on the US commerce goes against the fact that the share of manufacturing in the country’s economy has, in fact, fallen in recent years to less than 15%. India has been seeking to raise the share to 25% of its GDP for decades now without success.“Washington’s new Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs are a coercive bait for one-sided trade deals,” said Srivastava. He also highlighted the looming threat of up to 100% Lindsay Graham tariffs on India for Russian oil purchases, although the country has obtained a temporary waiver.“The Trade Representative proposes that appropriate action to obtain the elimination of the acts, policies, and practices would include applying tariffs of up to 25% on all goods of India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods,” the USTR said.“The Trade Representative further proposes to consider whether the additional duties applied should be adjusted to account for, among others, duties applied under other, existing Section 301 actions; duties applied under other, existing Section 232 actions, or were India to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the United States that is responsive to the determinations in this investigation into the acts, policies, and practices of India, a tariff rate of 17%,” the USTR said.The determination does not mean that the proposed additional tariffs have already come into effect. The USTR is seeking public comments on the investigation, which are due by 5 January 2027. Interested parties seeking to appear at the hearings must also submit requests, along with a summary of their testimony, by the same date. Hearings on the proposed actions are scheduled for 25 January 2027, continuing as appropriate.For India, the investigation under section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 flags potential excess capacity or export surpluses across seven sectors, such as solar modules, petrochemicals, steel, textiles, health-related goods, construction materials, and automotive products.Current tariff structureIndian exports to the US currently face an uneven tariff regime. About 55% of shipments, including engineering goods, textiles and garments, and gems and jewellery, attract the usual most-favoured-nation (MFN) duties, along with a punitive tariff of 10% imposed over the alleged use of forced labour in exported goods following another section 301 investigation by the USTR. In textiles and garments, US MFN duties can go up to 32%. For most gems and jewellery, they range between 5.5% and 6%.Another 35-40% of goods, including smartphones, pharmaceuticals and certain farm products, are exempt from the levy. Steel and aluminium exports, however, face a much higher tariff of 50%.The proposed tariffs would be imposed net of existing Section 301 duties, with exemptions for certain goods. The USTR has also proposed considering whether the additional duties should be adjusted to a rate of 17% if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the US that is responsive to the findings of the investigation.Affected economies and tariffsIndia is among 14 economies against which US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has made determinations under Section 301. The other economies are China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh and Japan. The USTR has not made determinations with respect to Mexico and Norway at this time.As per the USTR proposal, China faces up to 40% (or a 20% deal rate stacked on 2018 Section 301 tariffs), Vietnam faces up to 35% (or 20% with a deal) and Bangladesh up to 20% (or an 18% deal rate). Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand face up to 25% (or an 18% deal rate), South Korea and Taiwan up to 25% (or 15% net of the usual most-favoured nation tariffs), the EU, Japan, and Switzerland up to 20% (or 15% net of MFN) and Singapore up to 20% (or a 10% deal rate).In its findings on India, the USTR identified five areas of concern: industrial plans to expand manufacturing, inadequate labour protections, financial repression policies, sustained market access barriers, and failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies.The USTR has claimed that these practices reduce commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in India and third-country markets, contribute to lost production, exports, jobs and investment in the US manufacturing sector, and increase US economic security risks, including through reliance on inputs from non-market economies.

headline: Woman down with TB found escape in PUBG. Her gaming partner killed her
content: When Anjali Shaw left her home at noon, the only reason she gave her family was that she wanted “peace” - to meditate in silence, away from the humdrum of the household that her ailing body so craved. She was not going far, just about a kilometre away from her house in West Bengal’s Baranagar, to an empty flat owned by her elder sister. That wasn’t the truth. What she was really going for, however, was to meet her alleged lover and her death. With an elder brother and two sisters, Anjali was a frail young woman, who had been suffering from tuberculosis since 2021. The illness had given her a tired posture, leaving her resigned to her bed for most of the day. Over the five years since her diagnosis, she had developed an addiction to video games. “She started with PUBG in 2021,” a police officer says. “This (video) game is now banned in India”. PUBG is a mobile game in which players team up with others across the regions to go on military quests. Before that night, the night of November 10, it would have been impossible to predict such a violent end for Anjali. Her father, Rajender Shaw, is a familiar figure in this part of West Bengal. He contested the assembly elections in 1996, and subsequently the municipal elections in 2021, on a BJP ticket. Despite losing both the polls, he ran a profitable motor parts shop in Baranagar. In fact, his standing has grown even further after the BJP’s thumping win in this year’s West Bengal Assembly elections. “She herself was a Vishwa Hindu Parishad member. She was active till about 2024,” another police officer says. The Shaws lived in Shradhanjali Apartments in Baranagar, one of the affluent societies in the Barrackpore district. Located about 25 km from West Bengal’s capital, Kolkata, on the banks of the Hooghly River, Barrackpore was the first British cantonment in India, where the East India Company established its base in the early 18th century. Today, it houses West Bengal’s Police Academy and an operational Air Force base. A secret meeting On November 10, at around noon, Anjali told her mother that she wanted to visit her sister Ananya’s flat, which had been empty since her sister and brother-in-law moved to the nearby town of Sreerampur. “She was very fond of religious chanting. She was a bhakt of Shivanand ji Maharaj. She told her mother that she is going to meditate on his name,” Rajender says. Her mother tried to stop her, saying she had a bad dream the night before. “But Anjali started complaining. She said that we (family) were only preventing her from getting better,’’ Rajender says. “So, her mother backed down and allowed her to go”. Rajender wasn’t home at the time though. He says he was out distributing post-Diwali sweets and once he returned home, Anjali had already left. Once she left home, Anjali walked straight to her sister Ananya’s flat. After an hour, the man she had come to know by his “joystick” name, “Nick Rajput” arrived, a police officer says. Nick had travelled all the way from Delhi, the officer says, and the two were alone in the flat. “She had gone to her sister’s empty flat to meet that man. She wanted to spend time alone with him. That was the purpose”. At about 4:30 pm, Anjali’s mother started worrying. “Anjali was not picking up her phone. That was unusual. Her mother then asked her sister Ananya to call. Anjali didn’t take her call either. But Ananya got a text from her, saying that she is fine,” Rajender recalls. In the message, Anjali had addressed her sister as “Aap”. That was the giveaway. “She has never addressed her sister in that manner. It’s always ‘Tu’. They would regularly snap at each other…typical sibling bickering,” Rajender says. “This time, the tone of her message was unusually formal. It was strange”. Rajender is of medium height and pot-bellied, with a round face, a fairly full head of hair, and a slim moustache. He is a seasoned trader, and seeing Anjali’s message to her sister Ananya made him suspicious. He asked Ananya to call her neighbours and request them to go to her flat and check on Anjali. Rajender, however, couldn’t wait. “I reached around 6 pm, and the door was locked. The neighbours told me that she was not responding,’’ Rajender says. “We finally entered after breaking the door”. What Rajender saw inside still haunts him. His daughter was lying motionless on the floor, her own dupatta wrapped around her neck. She had been strangled to death. There was no one else around. Until then, Rajender had no idea who Nick was. In fact, no one in the family had any clue that Anjali had a man in her life. All that the family knew was that their daughter was obsessed with the game. “I told her many times to quit. But she would say, ‘What am I supposed to do sitting at home?’” Rajender recalls. The family learnt that there was a man with Anjali in the flat only after the police arrived to investigate her murder. The trail to Delhi Nick and Anjali first came into contact in 2021 while playing PUBG. Anjali would often team up with Nick on missions, and soon the duo started talking, a police officer says. They soon exchanged numbers and, within months, were chatting regularly on WhatsApp. He allegedly told her that he owns a gym in Delhi and is a businessman. Sometime between 2024 and 2025, Nick came to meet Anjali for the first time, a police officer says. “He came well-dressed and presentable. Then he came again in 2026, around March. Their chat history reveals that they were constantly chatting and doing video calls with each other. They also used to fight a lot,” the officer says. Simultaneously, the Kolkata police started tracing Nick’s movement around the area. Soon they found CCTV footage showing him entering Kolkata railway station and then boarding a train for Delhi. In the early hours of November 11, the officers at Baranagar police station informed Delhi Police. Within the next 12 hours, officers at the Crime Branch police station, led by SI Anuj Chikkara, Inspector Satish Malik, and ACP Raj Pal Dabbas, identified and tracked Nick. “His real name is Dharamveer. He travelled from West Bengal and reached Delhi on 12th November. He went into hiding in the Sector-5 area of Bawana in Delhi. This is an area close to where he had been living and working,’’ a police officer says. “As police pressure mounted, he tried to flee Delhi through Anand Vihar ISBT to reach Kanpur. He didn’t know that we were keeping a close watch”. A police team soon rushed to ISBT and found Nick, aka Dharamveer, sitting at the food court, eating his last meal before fleeing. Lanky and pale, he wore a shabby pair of distressed jeans and a faded shirt. “Dharamveer didn’t own and run a gym. He had lied to Anjali. He worked as a labourer at a plastic factory in Bawana,’’ a police officer says. “However, he is a graduate and a decently well-read man…. a smooth talker too”. The police found out that Dharamveer is from Hamirpur in UP and was currently living in Holombi Kalan village in Delhi. “He was on his way to his village when we caught him,’’ a police officer says. When questioned by the police, Dharamveer claimed that Anjali was obsessed with him. “He told us that this was his third meeting with Anjali and she wanted him to marry her and take her to Delhi,” a police officer says. “He claimed that when he refused, they got into a fight”. The officer says that Dharamveer didn’t want to bring Anjali to Delhi because he didn’t want her to know his real identity and profession. “He got angry and lunged at her.. and strangled her with her own dupatta”.. “His chats show that Anjali used to be suspicious about him. They would fight if he didn’t take her video calls,’’ a police officer says. “He claimed that even during PUBG, she would get upset if he paired with someone else in the game”. Rajender, however, didn’t believe Dharamveer’s claims. “I have no doubt that this man manipulated my daughter,’’ he says. “He lured my sick daughter with lies and felt threatened once she discovered his real identity”. Dharamveer has been sent to West Bengal and is currently in the custody of Baranagar police station.

headline: ‘I’m going to die’: DU student found dead in Faridabad hotel; rat poison, note recovered
content: A 19-year-old Delhi University student was found dead in a hotel room in Faridabad on Tuesday morning, police said, adding that a bottle of rat poison and an alleged suicide note were recovered from the room. Police said the woman checked in on Monday with her neighbour, identified as Vipin Yadav, who allegedly left the hotel that night. Suspecting that the student's suicide note may have been planted by Yadav, the police have registered a murder case, officers said. Police sources said they also found another note in the room, allegedly written by Yadav, which read: "Mai Marne Jaa Raha hun" (I am going to die). Police sources added that the student spoke to her parents on Monday and allegedly told them she was going to college. "The victim was in touch with her family until Monday afternoon. After this, her calls went unanswered following which her family lodged a missing person's complaint at Dhauj Police Station on Tuesday morning," an officer said. The woman, a second-year BCom student from Kalindi College was found unconscious in a hotel room in Faridabad on Tuesday. A few hours later, the Sarai Khwaja Police Station informed the woman’s family, who rushed there to identify her, officers said. Hotel staff told police that Yadav and the student had checked in on Monday morning, and that Yadav left during the night while the student remained in the room, officers said. The next day, staff kept knocking on the door to ask about checkout but received no response. Soon, the hotel staff alerted the police. According to police, a handwritten note found in the hotel room reads: "Whatever is mine, Ankit will own it after me." Ankit is the name of the DU student's brother. Police are examining the origin and contents of the letter, officers said. Yadav's family runs a transport business, and both his parents died earlier, police said. Meanwhile, the victim’s parents run a grocery shop in their village. "The autopsy is being carried out to ascertain the cause of death. A postmortem examination is also being done. We are also looking for Yadav whose note has been recovered," an officer said.

headline: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
content: NEW DELHI The Supreme Court issued notice on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) on the bail pleas of former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam, accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court, however, declined to take up their pleas for interim relief, saying a three-judge Bench would be set up to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs imposed by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought the Delhi Police’s response to the bail pleas by December 14. It also directed the Registry to place the matter before the CJI on the administrative side for the constitution of a larger Bench in light of the court’s May 22 judgment in Tasleem Ahmed v. State Government of NCT of Delhi. Process as punishment: On the Umar Khalid case Process as punishment: On the Umar Khalid case Repeated bail denial, as in Umar Khalid’s case, enables state overreach Process as punishment: On the Umar Khalid case editorial 1 “Issue notice, returnable on 14.12.2026. The Registry is directed to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India, on the administrative side, for constitution of a three-Judge Bench in light of the judgment dated 22.05.2026,” the Bench said. The May 22 reference arose from divergent interpretations by coordinate Benches of the law governing bail under the UAPA. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and P.B. Varale had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. The court permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier. Subsequently, on May 18, a Bench comprising Justices B. V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan, while granting bail to an accused in a narco-terrorism case, expressed reservations about the January 5 judgment, observing that it had failed to correctly apply the binding principles laid down in the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K. A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights. Following this, Justices Kumar and Varale referred the matter to the CJI on May 22 for the constitution of a larger Bench to ensure “parity and consistency” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. The Bench, however, granted six months’ interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, observing that they “cannot be made to suffer” merely because a question of law awaited authoritative settlement. Also read | The continued custody in Delhi Riots cases is an injustice https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/lead/the-continued-custody-in-delhi-riots-cases-is-an-injustice/article70510629.ece ‘Conflicting interpretations’ At the outset of Wednesday’s hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, urged the court to consider their pleas for interim bail, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. Mr. Dave argued that the prayer for interim relief was distinct from the larger question of law referred to the CJI on May 22. “Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, seeking an early hearing. The CJI, however, said he would have to first examine the conflicting interpretations of the Najeeb ruling, which he had authored. “…in the light of the conflict of observation, I have to apply my mind. It was my judgment (Najeeb case) which is being discussed. So, I am feeling a little embarrassed. One bench says Najeeb means this; another bench says it does not mean… I am being told what I have said,” the CJI remarked. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi Police, pointed out that the May 22 reference had arisen from bail proceedings involving other accused in the same conspiracy case. The right to a fair trial at the crossroads The right to a fair trial at the crossroads As proceedings in the 2020 Delhi riots cases show, endless imprisonment without trial raises urgent questions about liberty and justice The right to a fair trial at the crossroads opinion 1 ‘Unjustified delay’ The two activists have challenged a September 30 ruling of the Delhi High Court rejecting their fresh bail pleas, contending that the case remains at the stage of framing of charges and that the trial is yet to commence. A Division Bench of the High Court had held that judicial discipline prevented it from modifying the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in its January 5 judgment. “These two conditions would show that the specific liberty is clear and conditional, and this Court would not be in a position to modify the condition,” a Bench comprising Justices Prathiba M. Singh and Dinesh Bhatt had said. In his petition filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, Mr. Imam pointed out that despite his incarceration for over six years, not one of the more than 900 prosecution witnesses named in the case had been examined. Of these, 47 are protected witnesses. Delhi court restores Umar Khalid’s two weekly video meetings with family Delhi court restores Umar Khalid’s two weekly video meetings with family Counsel for Umar Khalid submitted that he had been permitted two weekly e-mulakats since the beginning of his incarceration and that the number had been reduced to one without any stated reason, despite there being no breach of prison rules on his part Delhi court restores Umar Khalid’s two weekly video meetings with family storyline 1 Given the pace of proceedings, he contended, “On no fair assessment can examination of protected witnesses be expected to commence, much less to conclude, before January 5, 2027, or for a considerable period thereafter.” Mr. Imam further argued that his continued detention had ceased to serve a procedural purpose and had become “punitive by reason of unreasonable and unjustified delay”. Of the 18 accused in the conspiracy case, five, including Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, remain in custody. Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmed were granted bail on January 5. The Delhi Police have booked the accused under the UAPA and various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), alleging that they conspired to orchestrate the communal violence that broke out in northeast Delhi on February 23, 2020, amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. The riots left 53 people dead and hundreds injured. Mr. Imam was initially arrested on January 28, 2020, before the riots, while Mr. Khalid was taken into custody in September that year.
