headline: Punjab declares November 28 Public Holiday in 3 Municipal Areas; Check Details
content: Chandigarh, November 25, 2026: The Punjab Government has declared November 28 (Saturday) a public holiday in the areas under the Municipal Corporation, Patiala, and Municipal Councils of Bagha Purana and Dharamkot, where municipal general and bye-elections will be held. The elections will cover 30 wards in Patiala, 15 wards in Bagha Purana and seven wards in Dharamkot. The holiday will also apply under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The government has also allowed eligible voters employed in Punjab government offices, boards, corporations and educational institutions to avail themselves of special leave to cast their votes. Employees will have to present their voter cards to the competent authority to avail of the leave, which will not be deducted from their regular leave account.

headline: Punjab Government accepts PRTC staff’s demand after fresh stir threat
content: In what appeared to be a face-saving exercise to pull the state government out of an embarrassing situation ahead of the Aam Aadmi Party’s rally in Moga, the Transport Department agreed late Wednesday evening to bring around 2,000 outsourced drivers and conductors of the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) under the contract system.The breakthrough came after the employees announced a three-day strike and refused to ferry AAP supporters to the party’s rally in Moga on Thursday. With around 2,600 buses of the PRTC and Punjab Roadways requisitioned to transport supporters from villages across Punjab, the government was left scrambling for alternative arrangements.Though the employees’ demand had been pending for a long time, their decision to withdraw from the rally duty put the government under considerable pressure. General managers of PRTC depots issued orders around 9 pm on Wednesday, agreeing to shift the outsourced employees to the contractual system.A meeting between employee representatives and officials of the Transport Department was held on Wednesday afternoon. However, the employees refused to call off their agitation merely on assurances, insisting that they would resume duty only after receiving written orders.Once the orders were issued, the drivers and conductors took their buses to the villages assigned to them to ferry AAP supporters to the Moga rally on Thursday morning.An official order issued by the PRTC’s Faridkot depot on November 25, a copy of which is available with The Tribune, confirmed the transition of 120 listed employees (73 conductors and 47 drivers) to contractual engagement under the Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Act, 2026.Earlier, employee representatives had said the government had already passed a resolution in the Vidhan Sabha to bring outsourced employees under the contractual system. The Transport Minister had also issued directions to the officials concerned, but the PRTC management had failed to implement the decision, they alleged.The employees had initially announced the three-day strike but deferred it following assurances from the government. However, with no concrete orders forthcoming, they went ahead with their agitation on Wednesday.The employees had also objected to being assigned duties for a political rally, alleging that they were being asked to reach designated villages on Wednesday evening, stay overnight and ferry supporters to Moga the next morning.The strike threat had put the government’s arrangements for transporting thousands of AAP supporters from across the state in jeopardy, forcing the authorities to concede the employees’ long-pending demand.

headline: Register live-in relationship or face jail, recommends Haryana law commission
content: Mandatory registration of live-in relationships, prohibition of multiple marriages and uniform provisions governing divorce, maintenance and succession are among the key recommendations of the Haryana State Law Commission in its report on the proposed Uniform Civil Code (UCC).The report, submitted at the Haryana Government's request, proposes that partners in a live-in relationship must submit a declaration to the Registrar or Sub-Registrar having jurisdiction over their place of residence. Following a summary inquiry, the declaration will be entered in a prescribed register and a certificate issued. A copy will also be sent to the local police station. If either partner is below 21 years of age, their parents or guardians will be informed.Commission chairperson Justice HS Bhalla confirmed that the report had been submitted. Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi said on Thursday that the government would seek the opinions of the Advocate General and the Legal Remembrancer before proceeding further.Under the recommendations, registration of a live-in relationship will be refused if either partner is already married, is in another live-in relationship or is a minor. Relationships involving consent obtained through force, coercion, fraud, misrepresentation or undue influence will also be ineligible for registration.Either or both partners can terminate the relationship by submitting a prescribed declaration. Staying in a live-in relationship for more than a month without submitting the mandatory statement could attract imprisonment of up to three months, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both. Obtaining consent through force or fraud could invite imprisonment of up to five years and a fine.The report also provides for a woman to seek maintenance from a competent court if deserted by her live-in partner.Marriage and divorceThe proposed code prohibits polygamy by allowing marriage only when neither partner has a living spouse. It also makes marriage registration mandatory and prohibits marriages between first cousins on both maternal and paternal sides. Exceptions to other prohibited relationships may be allowed where recognised customs permit them, subject to public policy and morality.A marriage may be annulled on grounds including non-consummation, forced or fraudulent consent, and misrepresentation of identity. Divorce may be granted on grounds of adultery, cruelty, desertion for at least two years and conversion to another religion. Existing polygamous marriages solemnised before the UCC comes into force have also been addressed in the proposed provisions.The report proposes permanent alimony and maintenance based on the financial circumstances of both parties or their mutual agreement. 'Mahr, dower, streedhan' and other property given to the wife would be additional to her maintenance claim.It also allows divorced spouses to remarry each other without any condition requiring either to marry a third person first.The proposed code would override conflicting personal laws, customs and traditions, with violations of its divorce provisions attracting imprisonment of up to three years and a fine. Scheduled Tribes have been exempted.Uttarakhand and Goa already have a Uniform Civil Code in force, while Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh have taken steps towards similar legislation. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday that all BJP-ruled states would implement the UCC. The state government’s next step will be to examine the Law Commission's recommendations and obtain legal opinion. The proposals are recommendations and have not yet become law.

headline: Haryana in grip of gangsters, alleges Congress after Rohtak killings
content: The Congress on Thursday condemned the killing of four people by unidentified assailants at Milan Dhaba near Kharawar village, alleging that Haryana was in the grip of gangsters while the government remained absent.Reacting to Wednesday night’s incident, Rohtak Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda alleged that the law and order situation in Haryana had “completely collapsed”, with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini having “no time for the state”.Describing the killings as horrific, he said such incidents had become routine in the state.“Haryana is now in the grip of extortion, gun violence and gangster rule. People are living in fear while criminals continue to roam freely without fear,” Deepender told mediapersons in Rohtak.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala also slammed the state’s BJP government.“Today, Haryana is under criminal rule. Gangs are running Haryana, while the government is missing,” he said in a social media post.“Ransom, indiscriminate gunfire, kidnappings — this is now everyday life in Haryana. The latest evidence is the shooting at Milan Dhaba, just 50 steps from the Kharawar police post in Rohtak…” he added.“Chief Minister Nayab Saini, if you can spare a moment from your jokes and trips to Punjab, spare a little concern for the lives of Haryanvis too,” he said.Three of the four deceased — Rinku (28), Vineet (22) and Yash (22) — belonged to Dighal village in neighbouring Jhajjar district.An uneasy calm prevailed in the village after news of the murders reached residents, as it has already witnessed two killings stemming from personal enmity this year.Some residents, particularly those engaged in the financing business, have also received extortion threats from gangsters operating from abroad.In view of the prevailing security concerns, police checkpoints have already been set up in the village.Meanwhile, Jhajjar Commissioner of Police Simardeep Singh said the preliminary investigation suggested that the killings at Milan Dhaba were a case of inter-gang rivalry.“The investigation is ongoing, and we expect to track down those responsible soon. A significant number of rounds were fired. We are verifying a post that appeared on social media and are also examining the angle of inter-gang rivalry. At least four to five shooters appear to have been involved in the crime,” he said.

headline: Himachal: Tanda hospital cuts stent prices by up to 57%
content: In a major relief to patients undergoing cardiac treatment, Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College and Hospital, Tanda, has substantially reduced stent prices following a competitive tender process. The cost of different brands of stents, earlier priced at Rs 41,000, has been reduced to Rs 21,500 and Rs 17,500, depending on the brand.The revised rates are expected to ease the financial burden on patients requiring stent implantation and other cardiac interventions. The reduction follows a competitive tendering process in which several vendors participated.Principal of Tanda Medical College, Dr Milap Sharma, told The Tribune that the revised prices had been finalised after completion of the tender process. He said vendors, including Hari Om Traders, Atulya Surgical, Niccos and Ramdial, among others, had participated in the process.Dr Sharma clarified that the revised rates would apply uniformly to all patients, irrespective of their mode of payment. Patients availing themselves of treatment under the Himcare and Ayushman Bharat health insurance schemes, as well as those paying in cash, would benefit from the reduced prices.The decision is particularly significant for economically weaker patients, for whom the cost of cardiac treatment can be a major financial burden. The reduction in stent prices is expected to make treatment more affordable and improve access to essential cardiac procedures.The hospital administration has appealed to patients and their attendants to remain informed about the revised rates and avail themselves of the facility.The move is being viewed as a step towards reducing out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure at one of Himachal Pradesh’s major government tertiary-care institutions. By introducing lower rates through a competitive tender process, the medical college administration aims to make essential cardiac treatment more affordable.Tanda Medical College had earlier come under scrutiny after stents were found stored illegally in a cupboard in its Cardiology Department, raising concerns over alleged irregularities in the department.Dr Sharma said an inquiry into allegations of overcharging for stents in the past was underway. He said the Chief Minister had taken the matter seriously and senior officials of the state Health Department were investigating it.Cardiac scrutinyStents were found stored illegally in a cupboard in the Cardiology Department at Tanda Medical College, triggering scrutiny over alleged irregularitiesPatients had allegedly been overcharged for stents in the past, prompting an inquiry into the matterThe Chief Minister has taken the allegations seriously, with senior Health Department officials investigating the caseThe inquiry into the alleged overcharging is still underway

headline: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
content: NEW DELHI The Election Commission of India on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) directed that any incorrect or erroneous entries flagged in the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) would be corrected using Form 8 after comparing the entries with the corresponding information collected during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/special-intensive-revision-of-electoral-rolls/ All the changes would be made after verification by the concerned officials and not through automated matching. Form 8 is the ECI application for correction in voter details. Also Read | Hear pleas by deleted voters first, Supreme Court directs Bengal SIR tribunals https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/west-bengal-sir-supreme-court-orders-eci-calcutta-high-court-to-increase-tribunals-hearing-appeals/article71734188.ece The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists. The directive was given to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and UTs where the SIR has been completed and SSR is on. The States and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Island, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya. The ECI had ordered the SSR of electoral rolls with reference to January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date in these States/UTs through letters on October 15, November 4 and November 11. In its directive on Wednesday, the poll body said: “In order to identify and rectify any probable incorrect or erroneous entries in the particulars of electors (such as name, relation name or type, date of birth, mobile number, photograph, etc.) in the existing electoral rolls during the ongoing SSR, the existing electoral particulars of the concerned electors shall be compared with the corresponding information collected during the SIR.” “Wherever any mismatch is noticed, the same shall be flagged for verification and for taking necessary corrective action,” it said. In respect of such flagged entries, the BLOs shall visit the concerned electors during the ongoing SSR to verify their particulars and obtain a duly filled-in and signed Form 8, wherever is required. The AERO/ERO shall examine and dispose of such applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The commission order said that though the above exercise shall be carried out through the relevant BLO/AERO/ERO modules on the ECINet portal, “no changes shall be made solely on the basis of automated identification”. “... Since the exercise involves updating the demographic particulars of electors, all corrections shall be effected only through Form 8, duly signed by the concerned elector and subject to the prescribed verification and approval by the competent authority”, it said.

headline: Chandigarh, birthplace of SAD-BJP alliance, to test its revival after 30 years
content: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), once a formidable electoral partnership in Chandigarh and Punjab, are returning to the city where their alliance was forged and first proved its electoral potential. But as they prepare for the December 23 Municipal Corporation elections, the political landscape is markedly different from the one in which they joined hands three decades ago.The alliance was first tested in the 1996 Chandigarh Lok Sabha election, which BJP candidate Satya Pal Jain won with SAD support. He retained the seat in 1998, becoming the first major electoral beneficiary of the partnership in the city. The two parties then jointly contested Chandigarh’s maiden Municipal Corporation election in December 1996, winning 15 of the 20 seats — 13 for the BJP and two for the SAD. The Congress won one seat and others four.In a goodwill gesture, the BJP gave the Deputy Mayor’s post to the SAD despite the latter having won only two of the four seats it contested. The gesture reflected the political understanding between the partners and helped consolidate the alliance in its first municipal house.The two consecutive victories in Chandigarh — first in the Lok Sabha election and then in the MC polls — impressed SAD patriarch and former Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal. He spoke to Narendra Modi, then BJP general secretary in charge of Chandigarh and Punjab, and the partnership was taken from Chandigarh to Punjab for the February 1997 Assembly elections. It resonated across the state, with the alliance winning a record 93 of 117 seats — 75 for the SAD and 18 for the BJP — securing a two-thirds majority and ending Congress rule. The Congress was decimated to 14 seats from its 1992 tally of 87.The success also drew praise from then Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee at a BJP Parliamentary Party meeting. Hailing the victories in Chandigarh and the formation of the alliance government in Punjab, he said: “Pehli baar Chandigarh aur Punjab se koi achhi khabar aayi hai...” The remark recognised both the electoral breakthrough and the role of Modi and Badal in building the partnership.The alliance subsequently won 44 Assembly seats in 2002, 67 in 2007 and 68 in 2012, when the SAD secured 56 and the BJP 12. But after a decade in power, it was reduced to 18 seats in 2017 — 15 for the SAD and three for the BJP — as the Congress returned to power with 77. Its fortunes in Punjab’s Lok Sabha elections also fluctuated: the alliance won 11 seats in 1998, three in 1999, 11 in 2004, five in 2009, six in 2014 and four in 2019. The SAD quit the NDA in September 2020 over the Centre’s three farm laws, ending the 24-year-old partnership. Contesting separately, the parties managed only five Assembly seats in 2022 — three for the SAD and two for the BJP. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SAD won one seat while the BJP failed to open its account in Punjab.Chandigarh’s results underline the changed equation. The alliance won 21 seats in the 2016 MC election. When the parties fought separately in 2021, the AAP emerged as the largest party with 14 seats, followed by the BJP with 12, the Congress with eight and the SAD with one. Their combined tally of 13 would still have been one short of the AAP’s count, although a joint contest cannot be assessed simply by adding separate results.Former BJP MP Satya Pal Jain, who won Chandigarh in 1996 and 1998, told The Tribune that Modi played a key role in bringing the parties together through discussions with Badal. The partnership was projected as a symbol of Hindu-Sikh unity through the slogan “Hindu-Sikh bhai-bhai”. Badal described it as “nauh maas da rishta” — a bond as inseparable as nail and flesh.For the BJP, the SAD offers access to its Sikh and Punjabi support base; for the SAD, the BJP brings a stronger urban organisation. But the AAP’s rise in Chandigarh and Punjab, along with the Congress’s continuing presence, makes the contest very different from the one that produced the alliance’s historic victories.The December 23 election will test whether the two parties can rebuild the vote transfer and political chemistry that once made them dominant — and whether a partnership born in Chandigarh can again become a force in Punjab ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: Deepam row: Tamil Nadu govt apologises to Supreme Court, blames temple board for not lighting lamp at 'deepathoon'
content: New Delhi: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday tendered an apology to the Supreme Court for failing to light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at the disputed Deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hill, pinning the blame squarely on the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple’s Board of Trustees.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi earlier declined to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings but left the door open, stating the registry would examine any formal contempt petition and decide on listing it later this week..Deepam row: BJP accuses TVK government of displaying hostility towards Sanatan Dharma and Tamil culture.Despite the apex court’s November 20 order permitting the lighting of the lamp at the stone pillar as a one-time measure, the Deepam was lit only at the traditional Uchipillayar mandapam on Monday. Petitioners alleged deliberate non-compliance and urged the court to act.In a detailed status report, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna said the district administration had completed all logistical arrangements in coordination with the police, ASI and temple officials. A restricted team of up to 10 persons authorised by the Devasthanam was to perform the ritual between 6 pm and 6.30 pm on November 24. Extensive security, involving nearly 5,800 personnel and prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, was put in place amid intelligence inputs of possible mobilisation by opposing groups..BJP, RSS trying to divide Tamil Nadu over Thirupparankundram deepam row: Manickam Tagore.However, the temple’s Board of Trustees refused to authorise the proposed team and instead resolved to stick to the customary practice of lighting the lamp at the traditional site. The collector asserted there was no wilful disobedience on his part and that every effort had been made to secure the required authorisation.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the state, placed the report before the court and described the outcome as “unfortunate.” Counsel for Hindu Dharma Parishad termed the developments “most unfortunate” and accused authorities of circumvention.Subsequently, during the day, a contempt petition was also filed, as per the Supreme Court's website.The controversy centres on the long-standing dispute over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam. For decades the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes. Hindu groups had sought permission to light it at the Deepathoon, located higher up and about 50 metres from a dargah. The dargah side has claimed ownership of the hilltop and opposed the move.
